declarations.docstring:
**Artin's Conjecture on Primitive Roots**, first half.
Let $a$ be an integer that is not a square number and not $−1$. Then the set $S(a)$
of primes $p$ such that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ has a positive asymptotic
density inside the set of primes. In particular, $S(a)$ is infinite.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artin%27s_conjecture_on_primitive_roots)
[A85397](https://oeis.org/A85397)
[LMS14](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.4816) Lenstra, H.W. et al. "Character sums for primitive root densities" _arXiv:1112.4816_ [math.NT] (2014).
[Ho67] Hooley, C. "On Artin's conjecture." _Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik_ 225 (1967): 209-220.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (a : ℤ), ¬IsSquare a → a ≠ -1 → ∃ x > 0, (ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.S a).HasDensity x {p | Nat.Prime p}

declarations.docstring:
**Artin's Conjecture on Primitive Roots**, second half.
Write $a = a_0 b^2$ where $a_0$ is squarefree. Under the conditions that $a$ is not a perfect
power and $a_0\not\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ (sequence A85397 in the OEIS), the density of the set
$S(a)$ of primes $p$ such that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ is independent of $a$ and
equals Artin's constant.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artin%27s_conjecture_on_primitive_roots)
[A85397](https://oeis.org/A85397)
[LMS14](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.4816) Lenstra, H.W. et al. "Character sums for primitive root densities" _arXiv:1112.4816_ [math.NT] (2014).
[Ho67] Hooley, C. "On Artin's conjecture." _Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik_ 225 (1967): 209-220.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a a_0 b : ℤ),
  a = a_0 * b ^ 2 →
    (∀ (n : ℤ) (m : ℕ), m ≠ 1 → a ≠ n ^ m) →
      Squarefree a_0 →
        ¬a_0 ≡ 1 [ZMOD 4] →
          (ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.S a).HasDensity ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.ArtinConstant {p | Nat.Prime p}

declarations.docstring:
**Artin's Conjecture on Primitive Roots**, second half, power version
If $a = b^m$ is a perfect power of a number $b$ whose squarefree part $b_0\equiv 1 \pmod{4}$,
then the density of the set $S(a)$ of primes $p$ such that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$
is given by
$$C \left(\prod_{p \mid m} \frac{p(p-2)}{(p ^ 2 - p - 1)}\right)
\left(1 - \prod_{p \mid \gcd(b_0, m)} \frac{1}{2 - p}
\prod_{p \mid b_0, p\nmid m} \frac{1}{(1 + p - p ^ 2)}\right),$$
where $C$ is Artin's constant.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artin%27s_conjecture_on_primitive_roots)
[A85397](https://oeis.org/A85397)
[LMS14](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.4816) Lenstra, H.W. et al. "Character sums for primitive root densities" _arXiv:1112.4816_ [math.NT] (2014).
[Ho67] Hooley, C. "On Artin's conjecture." _Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik_ 225 (1967): 209-220.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a m b : ℕ),
  a = b ^ m →
    (∀ (u v : ℕ), 1 < u → b ≠ v ^ u) →
      1 < m →
        Odd m →
          b.squarefreePart ≡ 1 [MOD 4] →
            (ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.S ↑a).HasDensity
              (ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.ArtinConstant * ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.powCorrectionFactor m *
                ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.entanglementFactor b m)
              {p | Nat.Prime p}

declarations.docstring:
**Artin's Conjecture on Primitive Roots**, second half, power version
If $a = b^m$ is a perfect odd power of a number $b$ whose squarefree part
$b_0\not\equiv 1 \pmod{4}$, then the density of the set $S(a)$ of primes $p$ such that
$a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ is given by
$$C\prod_{p \mid m} \frac{p(p - 2)}{p^2 - p - 1}$$,
where $C$ is Artin's constant.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artin%27s_conjecture_on_primitive_roots)
[A85397](https://oeis.org/A85397)
[LMS14](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.4816) Lenstra, H.W. et al. "Character sums for primitive root densities" _arXiv:1112.4816_ [math.NT] (2014).
[Ho67] Hooley, C. "On Artin's conjecture." _Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik_ 225 (1967): 209-220.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a m b : ℕ),
  a = b ^ m →
    (∀ (u v : ℕ), 1 < u → b ≠ v ^ u) →
      1 < m →
        Odd m →
          ¬b.squarefreePart ≡ 1 [MOD 4] →
            (ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.S ↑a).HasDensity
              (ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.ArtinConstant * ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.powCorrectionFactor m)
              {p | Nat.Prime p}

declarations.docstring:
**Artin's Conjecture on Primitive Roots**, second half, different residue version
If $a$ is a square number or $a = −1$, then the density of the set $S(a)$ of primes
$p$ such that $a$ is a primitive root modulo $p$ is $0$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artin%27s_conjecture_on_primitive_roots)
[A85397](https://oeis.org/A85397)

[Ho67] Hooley, C. "On Artin's conjecture." _Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik_ 225 (1967): 209-220.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (a : ℤ), IsSquare a ∨ a = -1 → (ArtinPrimitiveRootsConjecture.S a).HasDensity 0 {p | Nat.Prime p}

declarations.docstring:
**Borsuk's conjecture**, open range: every bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ with at least two
points can be partitioned into $n + 1$ sets of strictly smaller diameter, for
$4 \leq n \leq 62$.

The conjecture is known to be true for $n \leq 3$ and false for $n \geq 63$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borsuk%27s_conjecture)

[Pe47] Perkal, J. (1947). *Sur la subdivision des ensembles en parties de diamètre inférieur*. Colloquium Mathematicum 2, 45.
[Eg55] Eggleston, H. G. (1955). *Covering a three-dimensional set with sets of smaller diameter*. Journal of the London Mathematical Society 30, 11–24. https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms/s1-30.1.11

**Partial result in dimension $4$**: every bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^4$ with at least two
points can be partitioned into $8$ sets of strictly smaller diameter. Claimed by Tolmachev and
Voronov [TV26] via computer-assisted partitions of a truncated Lassak cover, with floating-point

declarations.docstring:
**Brocard's Conjecture**
For every `n ≥ 2`, between the squares of the `n`-th and `(n+1)`-th primes,
there are at least four prime numbers.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brocard%27s_conjecture)
[Luan Alberto Ferreira, *Real exponential sums over primes and prime gaps*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08725)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ),
  1 ≤ n → 4 ≤ (Finset.filter Nat.Prime (Finset.Ioo (Nat.nth Nat.Prime n ^ 2) (Nat.nth Nat.Prime (n + 1) ^ 2))).card

declarations.docstring: Ferreira proved that Brocard's conjecture is true for sufficiently large n.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brocard%27s_conjecture)
[Luan Alberto Ferreira, *Real exponential sums over primes and prime gaps*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.08725)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
  4 ≤ (Finset.filter Nat.Prime (Finset.Ioo (Nat.nth Nat.Prime n ^ 2) (Nat.nth Nat.Prime (n + 1) ^ 2))).card

declarations.docstring:
**Bunyakovsky conjecture**
If a polynomial $f$ over integers satisfies both Schinzel and Bunyakovsky conditions,
there exist infinitely many natural numbers $m$ such that $f(m)$ is prime.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunyakovsky_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : Polynomial ℤ),
  BunyakovskyCondition f ∧ SchinzelCondition {f} → Infinite ↑{n | Nat.Prime (Polynomial.eval (↑n) f).natAbs}

declarations.docstring:
In Theorem 6 in [F1998], Kevin Ford proves that the smallest counterexample to
Carmichael's totient function conjecture must be $≥ 10 ^ (10 ^ 10)$
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmichael%27s_totient_function_conjecture)
[F1998] Kevin Ford. The distribution of totients. https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3264
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → n < 10 ^ 10 ^ 10 → CarmichaelTotient.CarmichaelTotientFor n

references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmichael%27s_totient_function_conjecture)
[F1998] Kevin Ford. The distribution of totients. https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3264
declarations.type_pretty: ¬CarmichaelTotient.CarmichaelTotientFor 0

declarations.docstring: For every odd number $n$, $φ(2n) = φ(n)$
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmichael%27s_totient_function_conjecture)
[F1998] Kevin Ford. The distribution of totients. https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3264
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n : ℕ}, Odd n → CarmichaelTotient.CarmichaelTotientFor n

declarations.docstring:
*Carmichael's totient function conjecture*: For every positive natural number $n$,
there exists a natural number $m$ with $m ≠ n$, such that $φ(n) = φ(m)$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmichael%27s_totient_function_conjecture)
[F1998] Kevin Ford. The distribution of totients. https://arxiv.org/abs/1104.3264
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ ⦃n : ℕ⦄, 0 < n → CarmichaelTotient.CarmichaelTotientFor n

declarations.docstring:
There are infinitely many real quadratic fields `ℚ(√d)` with class number one,
where `d > 1` is a squarefree integer.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_number_problem)
declarations.type_pretty: {d | Squarefree d ∧ d > 1 ∧ ClassNumberProblem.IsClassNumberOne d}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
**Stark–Heegner theorem** : For any squarefree integer `d < 0`, the class number of the imaginary
quadratic field Q(√d) is one if and only if `d ∈ {-1, -2, -3, -7, -11, -19, -43, -67, -163}`.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_number_problem)
declarations.type_pretty: {d | Squarefree d ∧ d < 0 ∧ ClassNumberProblem.IsClassNumberOne d} = {-1, -2, -3, -7, -11, -19, -43, -67, -163}

declarations.docstring:
**Dickson's conjecture**
If a finite set of linear integer forms $f_i(n) = a_i n+b_i$ satisfies Schinzel condition,
there exist infinitely many natural numbers $m$ such that $f_i(m)$ are primes for all $i$.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture)
[PrimePages glossary](https://t5k.org/glossary/xpage/DicksonsConjecture.html)
[OEIS Wiki](https://oeis.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture)
[MathWorld](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/DicksonsConjecture.html)
[Leonard Eugene Dickson, *History of the Theory of Numbers, Vol. I: Divisibility and Primality*](https://archive.org/details/historyoftheoryo01dickuoft)
[Arxiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.3850)

declarations.docstring:
**The generalized twin-prime conjecture**
For any positive integer $k$ there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p + 2k$ is prime.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture)
[PrimePages glossary](https://t5k.org/glossary/xpage/DicksonsConjecture.html)
[OEIS Wiki](https://oeis.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture)
[MathWorld](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/DicksonsConjecture.html)
[Leonard Eugene Dickson, *History of the Theory of Numbers, Vol. I: Divisibility and Primality*](https://archive.org/details/historyoftheoryo01dickuoft)
[Arxiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.3850)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 0 < k → Infinite ↑{p | Nat.Prime p ∧ Nat.Prime (p + 2 * k)}

declarations.docstring:
**The infinitude of cousin primes**
There are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p + 4$ is prime.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture)
[PrimePages glossary](https://t5k.org/glossary/xpage/DicksonsConjecture.html)

[Arxiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.3850)
declarations.type_pretty: Infinite ↑{p | Prime p ∧ Prime (p + 4)}

declarations.docstring:
**The infinitude of Sophie Germain primes**
There are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $2p + 1$ is prime.
references: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture)
[PrimePages glossary](https://t5k.org/glossary/xpage/DicksonsConjecture.html)

[Arxiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.3850)
declarations.type_pretty: Infinite ↑{p | Prime p ∧ Prime (2 * p + 1)}

declarations.docstring:

declarations.docstring:
Is there some $k$ such that every integer is the sum of a prime and at most $k$
powers of $2$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/10](https://www.erdosproblems.com/10)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ k, Erdos10.sumPrimeAndTwoPows k = Set.univ \ {0, 1}

declarations.docstring:
Gallagher [Ga75] has shown that for any $ϵ > 0$ there exists $k(ϵ)$
such that the set of integers which are the sum of a prime and at most $k(ϵ)$
many powers of $2$ has lower density at least $1 - ϵ$.

Ref: Gallagher, P. X., _Primes and powers of 2_.
references: [erdosproblems.com/10](https://www.erdosproblems.com/10)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∃ k, 1 - ε ≤ (Erdos10.sumPrimeAndTwoPows k).lowerDensity

declarations.docstring:
Granville and Soundararajan [GrSo98] have conjectured that at most $3$
powers of $2$ suffice for all odd integers, and hence at most $4$ powers of $2$
suffice for all even integers.

declarations.docstring:
For any $0<\alpha<1$, let $f(\alpha,n)=\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}(\tfrac{1}{2}-
\{ \alpha k\})$. Does $f(\alpha,n)$ have an asymptotic distribution function?

In other words, is there a non-decreasing function $g$ such that $g(-\infty)=0$, $g(\infty)=1$,
and $\lim_{n\to \infty}\lvert \{ \alpha\in (0,1): f(\alpha,n)\leq c\}\rvert=g(c)$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/1002](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1002)
[Ke60] Kesten, Harry, Uniform distribution {${\rm mod}\,1$}. Ann. of Math. (2) (1960), 445--471.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ g,
  Monotone g ∧
    Filter.Tendsto g Filter.atBot (nhds 0) ∧
      Filter.Tendsto g Filter.atTop (nhds 1) ∧
        ∀ (c : ℝ),
          Filter.Tendsto
            (fun n =>
              (MeasureTheory.volume
                  {α |
                    α ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1 ∧
                      (fun α n => 1 / Real.log ↑n * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, (1 / 2 - Int.fract (α * ↑k))) α n ≤
                        c}).toReal)
            Filter.atTop (nhds (g c))

declarations.docstring:
Kesten [Ke60] proved that if $f(\alpha,\beta,n)=\frac{1}{\log n}\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}(\tfrac{1}{2}-
\{\beta+\alpha k\})$ then $f(\alpha,\beta,n)$ has asymptotic distribution function
$g(c)=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\rho c}\frac{1}{1+t^2}\mathrm{d}t$, where $\rho>0$ is an explicit
constant.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1002](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1002)
[Ke60] Kesten, Harry, Uniform distribution {${\rm mod}\,1$}. Ann. of Math. (2) (1960), 445--471.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ ρ > 0,
  have g := fun c => 1 / Real.pi * ∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Iic (ρ * c), 1 / (1 + t ^ 2);
  ∀ (c : ℝ),
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n =>
        (MeasureTheory.volume
            {(α, β) |
              α ∈ Set.Icc 0 1 ∧
                β ∈ Set.Icc 0 1 ∧ 1 / Real.log ↑n * ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 n, (1 / 2 - Int.fract (β + α * ↑k)) ≤ c}).toReal)
      Filter.atTop (nhds (g c))

declarations.docstring:
Are there infinitely many solutions to $\phi(n) = \phi(n+1)$, where $\phi$ is the Euler totient
function?
references: [erdosproblems.com/1003](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1003)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ {n | n.totient = (n + 1).totient}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er85e] says that, presumably, for every $k \geq 1$ the equation
$$\phi(n) = \phi(n+1) = \cdots = \phi (n+k)$$ has infinitely many solutions.

[Er85e] Erdős, P., _Some problems and results in number theory_. Number theory and combinatorics. Japan 1984 (Tokyo, Okayama and Kyoto, 1984) (1985), 65-87.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1003](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1003)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, {n | ∀ i ∈ Set.Icc 1 k, n.totient = (n + i).totient}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Erdős, Pomerance, and Sárközy [EPS87] proved that for all large $x$, the number
of $n \leq x$ with $\phi(n) = \phi(n+1)$ is at most $$\frac{x}{\exp((\log x)^{1/3})}$$.

[EPS87] Erd\H os, Paul and Pomerance, Carl and S\'ark\"ozy, Andr\'as, _On locally repeated values of certain arithmetic functions_. {II}. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1987), 1--7.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1003](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1003)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, ↑{n | ↑n ≤ x ∧ n.totient = (n + 1).totient}.ncard ≤ x / Real.exp (Real.log x ^ (1 / 3))

declarations.docstring:
For any fixed c > 0, if x is sufficiently large then there exists n ≤ x such that
the values of φ(n+k) are all distinct for 1 ≤ k ≤ (log x)^c.
This is an open problem.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1004](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1004)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (x : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ n ≤ x, Erdos1004.IsDistinctTotientRun n ⌊Real.log ↑x ^ c⌋₊

declarations.docstring:
Erdős, Pomerance, and Sárközy [EPS87] proved that if φ(n+k) are all distinct for 1 ≤ k ≤ K then
K ≤ n / exp(c (log n)^{1/3}) for some constant c > 0.
Here we state the existence of such a constant c.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1004](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1004)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c,
  ∃ (_ : c > 0),
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (K : ℕ), Erdos1004.IsDistinctTotientRun n K → ↑K ≤ ↑n / Real.exp (c * Real.log ↑n ^ (1 / 3))

declarations.docstring:
Let $c > 0$ and let $h_c(n)$ be such that for any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with at least
$cn^2$ lines that each contain more than three of the points, some line contains $h_c(n)$ of
the points. Is it true that, for fixed $c > 0$, $h_c(n) \to \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/102)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ c > 0, ∀ (M : ℕ), ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑M ≤ Erdos102.h c n

declarations.docstring: It is not known whether $h_c(n) \geq 5$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/102)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, 5 ≤ Erdos102.h c n

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er95] suggested that perhaps $h_c(n) \gg_c n^{1/2}$. Zach Hunter pointed out that this is
false: the points of $\{1, \dots, m\}^d$ with $n \approx m^d$, randomly projected to
$\mathbb{R}^2$, meet every line in $\ll_d n^{1/d}$ points and determine $\gg_d n^2$ lines with
more than three points. This gives $h_c(n) \ll n^{1 / \log(1/c)}$; we state the underlying form:
for every $d \geq 1$ there is $c > 0$ with $h_c(n) \ll_d n^{1/d}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/102)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (d : ℕ), 1 ≤ d → ∃ c > 0, ∃ C, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos102.h c n ≤ ↑⌈C * ↑n ^ (1 / ↑d)⌉₊

declarations.docstring:
It is easy to see that $h_c(n) \ll_c n^{1/2}$: for all sufficiently small $c > 0$ there are
admissible configurations (e.g. grids) in which no line contains more than $C_c n^{1/2}$ points.
references: [erdosproblems.com/102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/102)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c₀ > 0, ∀ c ∈ Set.Ioc 0 c₀, ∃ C, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos102.h c n ≤ ↑⌈C * √↑n⌉₊

declarations.docstring: The plane contains a line.
references: [erdosproblems.com/102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/102)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ L, EuclideanGeometry.IsLine L

declarations.docstring:
`M ≤ h c n` exactly when every admissible configuration of $n$ points has a line that
contains at least `M` of its points.
references: [erdosproblems.com/102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/102)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (c : ℝ) (n M : ℕ),
  ↑M ≤ Erdos102.h c n ↔
    ∀ (P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
      Erdos102.Admissible c n P → ∃ L, EuclideanGeometry.IsLine L ∧ M ≤ Erdos102.pointsOn P L

declarations.docstring: `M ≤ maxCollinear P` exactly when some line contains at least `M` points of `P`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/102)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) (M : ℕ),
  M ≤ Erdos102.maxCollinear P ↔ ∃ L, EuclideanGeometry.IsLine L ∧ M ≤ Erdos102.pointsOn P L

declarations.docstring: The statement $h_c(n) \to \infty$, written without $h_c$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/102)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (c : ℝ),
  (∀ (M : ℕ), ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑M ≤ Erdos102.h c n) ↔
    ∀ (M : ℕ),
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
        ∀ (P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),

            c * ↑n ^ 2 ≤ ↑(Erdos102.richLineCount P) → ∃ L, EuclideanGeometry.IsLine L ∧ M ≤ Erdos102.pointsOn P L

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n;r,k)$ be the maximal number of edges in an $r$-uniform hypergraph which contains no set of $k$ many independent edges.

For all $r\geq 3$, $$f(n;r,k)=\max\left(\binom{rk-1}{r}, \binom{n}{r}-\binom{n-k+1}{r}\right).$$

Note: the source states the formula with no range on `n` or `k`, but some restriction
is needed: e.g. for `r = 3`, `k = 2`, `n = 4` no two disjoint triples fit in `4`
vertices, so the left-hand side is `4.choose 3 = 4` while the right-hand side is
`5.choose 3 = 10`. We require `k ≥ 1` and `n ≥ r*k - 1`: this is the smallest `n`
accommodating the construction counted by the first term (all `r`-subsets of a fixed
`(r*k - 1)`-set), and at `n = r*k - 1` the equality holds trivially, since the complete
`r`-uniform hypergraph has no `k`-matching. The source's commentary likewise calls the
case `n < k*r` trivial.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1020](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1020)
[BDE76] Bollobás, B. and Daykin, D. E. and Erdős, P., *Sets of independent edges of a hypergraph*. Quart. J. Math. Oxford Ser. (2) (1976), 25--32.
[Er65d] Erdős, P., *A problem on independent {$r$}-tuples*. Ann. Univ. Sci. Budapest. Eötvös Sect. Math. (1965), 93--95.
[ErGa59] Erdős, P. and Gallai, T., *On maximal paths and circuits of graphs*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1959), 337-356 (unbound insert).
[FLM12] Frankl, Peter and Łuczak, Tomasz and Mieczkowska, Katarzyna, *On matchings in hypergraphs*. Electron. J. Combin. (2012), Paper 42, 5.

[FRR12] Frankl, Peter and Rödl, Vojtech and Ruciński, Andrzej, *On the maximum number of edges in a triple system not containing a disjoint family of a given size*. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2012), 141--148.
[Fr17] Frankl, Peter, *Proof of the {E}rdős matching conjecture in a new range*. Israel J. Math. (2017), 421--430.
[Fr87] Frankl, Peter, *The shifting technique in extremal set theory*. (1987), 81--110.
[HLS12] Huang, Hao and Loh, Po-Shen and Sudakov, Benny, *The size of a hypergraph and its matching number*. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2012), 442--450.
[Kl68] Kleitman, Daniel J., *Maximal number of subsets of a finite set no {$k$} of which are pairwise disjoint*. J. Combinatorial Theory (1968), 157--163.
[KoKu23] Kolupaev, Dmitriy and Kupavskii, Andrey, *Erdős matching conjecture for almost perfect matchings*. Discrete Math. (2023), Paper No. 113304, 9.
[LuMi14] Łuczak, Tomasz and Mieczkowska, Katarzyna, *On {E}rdős' extremal problem on matchings in hypergraphs*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2014), 178--194.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  3 ≤ r →
    ∀ (n k : ℕ),
      0 < k → r * k - 1 ≤ n → Erdos1020.f n r k = max ((r * k - 1).choose r) (n.choose r - (n - k + 1).choose r)

declarations.docstring:
If $R(k)$ is the Ramsey number for $K_k$, the minimal $n$ such that every $2$-colouring of the edges
of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $K_k$, then
$$\frac{R(k)}{k2^{k/2}}\to \infty.$$

In [Er93] Erdős offers $100 for a proof of this and $1000 for a disproof, but says 'this last offer
is to some extent phoney: I am sure that this is true (but I have been wrong before).'
references: [erdosproblems.com/1029](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1029)
[Er93] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory. Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
[ErSz35] Erdős, P. and Szekeres, G., A combinatorial problem in geometry. Compos. Math. (1935), 463-470.
[Sp75] Spencer, J., Ramsey's theorem - a new lower bound. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1975), 108-115.
declarations.type_pretty: Filter.Tendsto (fun k => ↑(SimpleGraph.diagonalRamsey k) / (↑k * 2 ^ (↑k / 2))) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Let $h(n)$ count the number of incongruent sets of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ which minimise
the diameter subject to the constraint that $d(x,y)\geq 1$ for all points $x\neq y$. Is it true
that $h(n)\to \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/103](https://www.erdosproblems.com/103)
declarations.type_pretty: Filter.Tendsto Erdos103.h Filter.atTop (nhds ⊤)

declarations.docstring: It is not even known whether $h(n)\geq 2$ for all large $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/103](https://www.erdosproblems.com/103)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, 2 ≤ Erdos103.h n

declarations.docstring:
Let $R(k,l)$ be the usual Ramsey number: the smallest $n$ such that if the edges of $K_n$ are
coloured red and blue then there exists either a red $K_k$ or a blue $K_l$.

Prove the existence of some $c>0$ such that
$$\lim_{k\to \infty}\frac{R(k+1,k)}{R(k,k)}> 1+c.$$

A problem of Erdős and Sós.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1030](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1030)
[BEFS89] Burr, S. and Erdős, P. and Faudree, R. J. and Schelp, R. H., On the difference between consecutive Ramsey numbers. Utilitas Math. (1989), 115-118.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c > 0,
  ∃ L,
    Filter.Tendsto (fun k => ↑(SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey (k + 1) k) / ↑(SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey k k)) Filter.atTop
        (nhds L) ∧
      L > 1 + c

declarations.docstring:
Is there a constant $c > 0$ such that every graph on $2^n$ vertices with minimum degree
$> (1-c) \cdot 2^n$ contains the $n$-dimensional hypercube $Q_n$?

This is Erdős's question [Er93, p. 345].

See also [576] for the extremal number of edges that guarantee a $Q_n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1035](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1035)
[Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*. Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c > 0,
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 ^ n))) [inst : DecidableRel G.Adj],
    (∀ (v : Fin (2 ^ n)), ↑(G.degree v) > (1 - c) * 2 ^ n) → (SimpleGraph.hypercube n).IsContained G

declarations.docstring:
What is the infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such
that all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]`?
references: [erdosproblems.com/1038](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1038)
[Tao25] Tao, Terence. Sublevel Sets of Logarithmic Potentials. Terry Tao’s Blog, Dec. 2025 (https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/erdos-1038-1.pdf)
[EHP58] Erdős, P., Herzog, F., Piranian, G. Metric properties of polynomials. J. Analyse Math. 6 (1958), 125--148.
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos1038.erdos_1038.parts.i.answer = ⨅ f, MeasureTheory.volume {x | |Polynomial.eval x ↑f| < 1}

declarations.docstring:
The supremum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all monic polynomials `f` such that
all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]` is `2 * 2 ^ (1 / 2)`. This is proved in
[Tao25].
references: [erdosproblems.com/1038](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1038)
[Tao25] Tao, Terence. Sublevel Sets of Logarithmic Potentials. Terry Tao’s Blog, Dec. 2025 (https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/erdos-1038-1.pdf)
[EHP58] Erdős, P., Herzog, F., Piranian, G. Metric properties of polynomials. J. Analyse Math. 6 (1958), 125--148.
declarations.type_pretty: 2 * 2 ^ (1 / 2) = ⨆ f, MeasureTheory.volume {x | |Polynomial.eval x ↑f| < 1}

declarations.docstring:
The infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such that
all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]` is `≥ 2 ^ (4 / 3) - 1`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1038](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1038)
[Tao25] Tao, Terence. Sublevel Sets of Logarithmic Potentials. Terry Tao’s Blog, Dec. 2025 (https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/erdos-1038-1.pdf)
[EHP58] Erdős, P., Herzog, F., Piranian, G. Metric properties of polynomials. J. Analyse Math. 6 (1958), 125--148.
declarations.type_pretty: 2 ^ (4 / 3) - 1 ≤ ⨅ f, MeasureTheory.volume {x | |Polynomial.eval x ↑f| < 1}

declarations.docstring:
The infimum in `erdos_1038.parts.i` is strictly less than $2$, as observed in [EHP58]:
for $f(x)=(x+1)(x-1)^3$ the sublevel set $\{x : |f(x)| < 1\}$ is contained in
$(-1.108,-0.835)\cup(0,1.718)$, whose total length is $1.991$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1038](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1038)
[Tao25] Tao, Terence. Sublevel Sets of Logarithmic Potentials. Terry Tao’s Blog, Dec. 2025 (https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/erdos-1038-1.pdf)
[EHP58] Erdős, P., Herzog, F., Piranian, G. Metric properties of polynomials. J. Analyse Math. 6 (1958), 125--148.
declarations.type_pretty: ⨅ f, MeasureTheory.volume {x | |Polynomial.eval x ↑f| < 1} < 2

declarations.docstring:
The infimum of `|{x ∈ ℝ : |f x| < 1}|` over all nonconstant monic polynomials `f` such that
all of its roots are real and contained in `[-1,1]` is `< 1.835`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1038](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1038)
[Tao25] Tao, Terence. Sublevel Sets of Logarithmic Potentials. Terry Tao’s Blog, Dec. 2025 (https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/erdos-1038-1.pdf)
[EHP58] Erdős, P., Herzog, F., Piranian, G. Metric properties of polynomials. J. Analyse Math. 6 (1958), 125--148.
declarations.type_pretty: ⨅ f, MeasureTheory.volume {x | |Polynomial.eval x ↑f| < 1} < 1.835

declarations.docstring:
The admissible quadratic $x^2-1$, with roots $-1$ and $1$, attains the supremum
value $2\sqrt{2}$ in [Tao25].
references: [erdosproblems.com/1038](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1038)
[Tao25] Tao, Terence. Sublevel Sets of Logarithmic Potentials. Terry Tao’s Blog, Dec. 2025 (https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/erdos-1038-1.pdf)
[EHP58] Erdős, P., Herzog, F., Piranian, G. Metric properties of polynomials. J. Analyse Math. 6 (1958), 125--148.
declarations.type_pretty: MeasureTheory.volume {x | |x ^ 2 - 1| < 1} = ENNReal.ofReal (2 * √2)

declarations.docstring:
For a monic quadratic with roots at distance at most two, the sublevel measure
is $2\sqrt{1+d^2}$, where $2|d|$ is the distance between the roots. This gives
the degree-two case of the sublevel-set problem in [Tao25].
references: [erdosproblems.com/1038](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1038)
[Tao25] Tao, Terence. Sublevel Sets of Logarithmic Potentials. Terry Tao’s Blog, Dec. 2025 (https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/erdos-1038-1.pdf)
[EHP58] Erdős, P., Herzog, F., Piranian, G. Metric properties of polynomials. J. Analyse Math. 6 (1958), 125--148.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (m d : ℝ), |d| ≤ 1 → MeasureTheory.volume {x | |(x - m) ^ 2 - d ^ 2| < 1} = ENNReal.ofReal (2 * √(1 + d ^ 2))

declarations.docstring:
The degree-two case of the supremum bound in [Tao25]: if $a,b\in[-1,1]$,
the sublevel set of $(x-a)(x-b)$ has measure at most $2\sqrt{2}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1038](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1038)
[Tao25] Tao, Terence. Sublevel Sets of Logarithmic Potentials. Terry Tao’s Blog, Dec. 2025 (https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/erdos-1038-1.pdf)
[EHP58] Erdős, P., Herzog, F., Piranian, G. Metric properties of polynomials. J. Analyse Math. 6 (1958), 125--148.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (a b : ℝ), |a| ≤ 1 → |b| ≤ 1 → MeasureTheory.volume {x | |(x - a) * (x - b)| < 1} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 * √2)

declarations.docstring:
The lower half of `erdos_1038.parts.ii`: the supremum is at least $2\sqrt{2}$, because the
admissible polynomial $x^2-1$ has sublevel measure exactly $2\sqrt{2}$. The matching upper bound
is proved in [Tao25].
references: [erdosproblems.com/1038](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1038)
[Tao25] Tao, Terence. Sublevel Sets of Logarithmic Potentials. Terry Tao’s Blog, Dec. 2025 (https://terrytao.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/erdos-1038-1.pdf)
[EHP58] Erdős, P., Herzog, F., Piranian, G. Metric properties of polynomials. J. Analyse Math. 6 (1958), 125--148.
declarations.type_pretty: 2 * 2 ^ (1 / 2) ≤ ⨆ f, MeasureTheory.volume {x | |Polynomial.eval x ↑f| < 1}

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(z)=\prod_{i=1}^n(z-z_i)\in\mathbb{C}[x]$ where $\lvert z_i\rvert\leq 1$ for all $i$.
If $\Lambda(f)$ is the maximum of the lengths of the boundaries of the connected components of
$$
\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert<1\}
$$
then determine the infimum of $\Lambda(f)$.

A problem of Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian [EHP58].

This has been resolved by Tang, who proved that the infimum of $\Lambda(f)$ over all such $f$
is $2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1044](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1044)
[EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., *Metric properties of polynomials*. J. Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
[Ta26] Tang, Quanyu, *On Erdős Problem 1044* (2026), [github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-1044](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-1044).
declarations.type_pretty: IsGLB {L | ∃ f, Erdos1044.IsAdmissible f ∧ Erdos1044.maxBoundaryLength f = L} Erdos1044.erdos_1044.answer

declarations.docstring:
Tang also suggests that, if the degree $n$ is fixed, then the infimum over all such $f$ of
degree $n$ is attained by $f_n(z)=z^n-1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1044](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1044)
[EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., *Metric properties of polynomials*. J. Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
[Ta26] Tang, Quanyu, *On Erdős Problem 1044* (2026), [github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-1044](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-1044).

  0 < n →

      (Erdos1044.maxBoundaryLength (Polynomial.X ^ n - 1))

Tang also suggests that, if the degree $n$ is fixed, then the infimum over all such $f$ of
degree $n$ is attained by $f_n(z)=z^n-1$ (and proves this for $n=1$ and $n=2$).
references: [erdosproblems.com/1044](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1044)

∀ (n : ℕ),

      (Erdos1044.maxBoundaryLength (Polynomial.X ^ n - 1))

declarations.docstring:
This has been resolved by Tang, who proved that the infimum of $\Lambda(f)$ over all such $f$
is $2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1044](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1044)

[Ta26] Tang, Quanyu, *On Erdős Problem 1044* (2026), [github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-1044](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-1044).

declarations.docstring:
Let $t>1$ be a rational number. Is
$\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{1}{t^n-1}=\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\tau(n)}{t^n}$ irrational, where
$\tau(n)$ counts the divisors of $n$?

A conjecture of Chowla.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1049](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1049)

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 1050.** The series $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{2^n - 3}$ is irrational.

The source sum runs over $n \ge 1$; as a `tsum` over `ℕ` (which starts at $0$) it is reindexed
$n \mapsto n + 1$, i.e. $\sum_{n=0}^\infty 1/(2^{n+1} - 3)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1050](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1050)
[Bo91] Borwein, Peter B., On the irrationality of {$\sum(1/(q^n+r))$}. J. Number Theory (1991), 253--259.
[Bo92] Borwein, Peter B., On the irrationality of certain series. Math. Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. (1992), 141--146.
[Er48] Erdős, P., On arithmetical properties of Lambert series. J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1948), 63-66.
[Er88c] Erdős, P., On the irrationality of certain series: problems and results. New advances in transcendence theory (Durham, 1986) (1988), 102-109.

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 1050, variant [Bo91].** Borwein's general theorem: for every integer $q \ge 2$
and rational $r \ne 0$ with $r \ne -q^n$ for all $n \ge 1$, the series $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{q^n + r}$
is irrational. Problem 1050 is the case $q = 2$, $r = -3$; the [Er48] variant is $q = 2$, $r = -1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1050](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1050)
[Bo91] Borwein, Peter B., On the irrationality of {$\sum(1/(q^n+r))$}. J. Number Theory (1991), 253--259.
[Bo92] Borwein, Peter B., On the irrationality of certain series. Math. Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. (1992), 141--146.
[Er48] Erdős, P., On arithmetical properties of Lambert series. J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1948), 63-66.
[Er88c] Erdős, P., On the irrationality of certain series: problems and results. New advances in transcendence theory (Durham, 1986) (1988), 102-109.

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 1050, variant [Er88c] (open).** Erdős conjectured that
$\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{2^n + t}$ is *transcendental* for every integer $t \ne 0$ — strictly
stronger than the irrationality established by Borwein [Bo91]. This remains open.

Two exclusions make the series well-posed and the claim non-vacuous, exactly as in Borwein's theorem:
$t \ne -2^n$ for all $n \ge 1$ (so no denominator vanishes), and $t \ne 0$ (at $t = 0$ the series is
the rational $\sum_{n \ge 1} 2^{-n} = 1$, hence not transcendental).
references: [erdosproblems.com/1050](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1050)
[Bo91] Borwein, Peter B., On the irrationality of {$\sum(1/(q^n+r))$}. J. Number Theory (1991), 253--259.
[Bo92] Borwein, Peter B., On the irrationality of certain series. Math. Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. (1992), 141--146.
[Er48] Erdős, P., On arithmetical properties of Lambert series. J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.) (1948), 63-66.
[Er88c] Erdős, P., On the irrationality of certain series: problems and results. New advances in transcendence theory (Durham, 1986) (1988), 102-109.

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 1050, variant [Er48].** Erdős proved that the related series
$\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{2^n - 1}$ (which equals the Lambert series $\sum_n \frac{\tau(n)}{2^n}$,
where $\tau$ is the divisor function) is irrational. This is the $q = 2$, $r = -1$ case of Borwein's
general theorem `Erdos1050.erdos_1050.variants.borwein` below.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1050](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1050)

declarations.docstring:
Call a number $k$-perfect if $\sigma(n)=kn$, where $\sigma(n)$ is the sum of the divisors
of $n$. Must $k=o(\log\log n)$?

A question of Erdős, as reported in problem B2 of Guy's collection [Gu04].
The little-$o$ relation is taken as $n \to \infty$ within the positive integers for which
$\sigma(n) = kn$ for some $k$; on this set, $\sigma(n)/n$ is precisely that multiplier $k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1053](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1053)
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. Springer-Verlag, New York (2004).

declarations.docstring:
Estimate $n_k$ by finding a better upper bound than Cambie's
$n_k \leq k \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dotsc, k-1)$.

The comparator takes its least common multiple in `ℕ` and casts the result. Writing the
ascription as `((… ).lcm (fun n : ℕ => n) : ℝ)` instead puts it on the `Finset.lcm`
application, so the coercion lands on `n` and the `lcm` is taken in `ℝ`, where `lcm` of
non-zero elements is `1` and the whole comparator collapses to `k`.

declarations.docstring:
[Cambie observed](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1063) the improved bound
$n_k \le k \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dotsc, k - 1)$.

The hypothesis `3 ≤ k` is necessary here too. At $k = 2$ the right hand side is
$2 \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(1) = 2$, while $n_2 = 4$.

The source writes the bound as $k[2, 3, \dotsc, k-1]$. That agrees with the range used here,
because including $1$ does not change a least common multiple.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1063](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1063)

declarations.docstring:
Monier observed that $n_k \le k!$ for $k \ge 3$ ([Mo85]), since $\binom{k!}{k}$ is divisible
by $k! - i$ for $1 \le i < k$.

The hypothesis `3 ≤ k` is necessary. At $k = 2$ the bound is false: $n_2 = 4$ and $2! = 2$.

An improved upper bound
$n_k \ll \exp\left(\frac{k}{\log k}(\log \log k + \log \log \log k + \log 2)\right)$,
which is $o\bigl(k \cdot \operatorname{lcm}(1, \dotsc, k - 1)\bigr)$, was formally proved in
Lean 4 by the LEAP prover agent [Ku+26] (see the linked `formal_proof`).
This is an improvement over another upper bound propsed [here](https://github.com/pw/erdos1063-upper-bound/blob/a28481f5b4bda374086533397269c5b550c759b8/README.md).
references: [erdosproblems.com/1063](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1063)
[ErSe83] Erdos, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Problem 6447. Amer. Math. Monthly (1983), 710.

  Real.exp (↑k / Real.log ↑k * (Real.log (Real.log ↑k) + Real.log (Real.log (Real.log ↑k)) + Real.log 2));
(fun k => ↑(Erdos1063.n k)) =O[Filter.atTop] upper_bound ∧

declarations.docstring:
Let $G$ be a graph given by $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, where any two distinct points are at
least distance $1$ apart, and we draw an edge between two points if they are distance $1$ apart.

Let $g(n)$ be maximal such that any such graph always has an independent set on at least $g(n)$
vertices. Estimate $g(n)$, or perhaps $\lim \frac{g(n)}{n}$.

We ask for $\lim g(n)/n$. The limit exists by Fekete's lemma, since placing two configurations far
apart shows $g(a+b) \leq g(a)+g(b)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1066](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1066)
[Cs98] Csizmadia, G., *On the independence number of minimum distance graphs*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 20 (1998), 179-187.
[Er87b] Erdős, P., *Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry*. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
[PaTo96] Pach, J. and Tóth, G., *On the independence number of coin graphs*. Geombinatorics 6 (1996), 30-33.
[Po85] Pollack, R., *Increasing the minimum distance of a set of points*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 40 (1985), 450.
[Sw02] Swanepoel, K. J., *Independence numbers of planar contact graphs*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 28 (2002), 649-670.
declarations.type_pretty: Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos1066.g n) / ↑n) Filter.atTop (nhds Erdos1066.erdos_1066.answer)

declarations.docstring:
Pollack [Po85] also reports a letter from Erdős which poses the more general problem of, given
$n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with minimum distance $1$, let $g_d(n)$ be maximal such that there
always exist at least $g_d(n)$ many points which have minimum distance $>1$. Is it true that
$g_d(n) \gg n/d$ in general?

We read this with a constant independent of $d$ and $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1066](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1066)
[Cs98] Csizmadia, G., *On the independence number of minimum distance graphs*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 20 (1998), 179-187.
[Er87b] Erdős, P., *Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry*. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
[PaTo96] Pach, J. and Tóth, G., *On the independence number of coin graphs*. Geombinatorics 6 (1996), 30-33.
[Po85] Pollack, R., *Increasing the minimum distance of a set of points*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 40 (1985), 450.
[Sw02] Swanepoel, K. J., *Independence numbers of planar contact graphs*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 28 (2002), 649-670.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c > 0, ∀ (d n : ℕ), 1 ≤ d → c * ↑n / ↑d ≤ ↑(Erdos1066.gDim d n)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős initially thought that $g(n)=n/3$, but Chung and Graham, and independently Pach, gave a
construction that shows $g(n)\leq \frac{6}{19}n$. Pach and Tóth [PaTo96] improved this to
$g(n)\leq \frac{5}{16}n$.

Since $g(1) = 1$, the bound cannot hold for all $n$, so it is stated for infinitely many $n$,
with $5/16$ replaced by $5/16+\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1066](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1066)
[Cs98] Csizmadia, G., *On the independence number of minimum distance graphs*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 20 (1998), 179-187.
[Er87b] Erdős, P., *Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry*. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
[PaTo96] Pach, J. and Tóth, G., *On the independence number of coin graphs*. Geombinatorics 6 (1996), 30-33.
[Po85] Pollack, R., *Increasing the minimum distance of a set of points*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 40 (1985), 450.
[Sw02] Swanepoel, K. J., *Independence numbers of planar contact graphs*. Discrete Comput. Geom. 28 (2002), 649-670.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ ε > 0, ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos1066.g n) ≤ (5 / 16 + ε) * ↑n

declarations.docstring:
Such graphs are always planar. Pollack [Po85] noted that the Four colour theorem implies
$g(n)\geq n/4$, since the graph is planar.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1066](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1066)

declarations.docstring:

$$
  2^{n-2} + 1 ≤ f(n) ≤ \binom{2n-4}{n-2} + 1
$$
([ErSz60] and [ErSz35] respectively).

[ErSz60] Erdős, P. and Szekeres, G., _On some extremum problems in elementary geometry_.
  Ann. Univ. Sci. Budapest. Eötvös Sect. Math. (1960/61), 53-62.

[ErSz35] Erdős, P. and Szekeres, G., _A combinatorial problem in geometry_.
  Compos. Math. (1935), 463-470.

$$

  _Two extensions of the Erdős-Szekeres problem_. J. Eur. Math. Soc. (JEMS) (2020), 3981-3995.

[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happy_ending_problem)

Regarding the first question, Hardy and Subbarao computed all EHS numbers up to $2^{10}$, and
write "...if this trend conditions we expect [the limit] to be around 0.5, if it exists. The
frequency with which the EHS numbers occur - most often in long sequences of consecutive integers -
makes us believe that their asymptotic density exists and is unity. Erdős, though initially
hesitant, later agreed with this view." That is, the conjecture is that $S$ has density $1$.

declarations.docstring:
Let $r\geq 3$. There exists $c_r>r^{-r}$ such that, for any $\epsilon>0$, if $n$ is sufficiently
large, the following holds. Any $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with at least
$(1+\epsilon)(n/r)^r$ many edges contains a subgraph on $m$ vertices with at least $c_rm^r$ edges,
where $m=m(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1075](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1075)
[Er64f] Erdős, P., On extremal problems of graphs and generalized graphs. Israel J. Math. (1964), 183--190.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  3 ≤ r →
    ∃ c,
      (↑r)⁻¹ ^ r < c ∧
        ∀ (ε : ℝ),
          0 < ε →
            ∃ m,
              Filter.Tendsto m Filter.atTop Filter.atTop ∧
                ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
                  ∀ (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
                    H.IsUniform r →
                      (1 + ε) * (↑n / ↑r) ^ r ≤ ↑H.card →
                        ∃ S, S.card = m n ∧ c * ↑S.card ^ r ≤ ↑(H.hypergraphInduce S).card

declarations.docstring:

contains a subgraph of girth ≥ r and chromatic number ≥ k?

declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ r ≥ 4,
    ∀ k ≥ 2,
      ∃ f,
        ∀ (V : Type u) (G : SimpleGraph V),
          Nonempty V → ↑f ≤ G.chromaticNumber → ∃ H, H.coe.girth ≥ r ∧ H.coe.chromaticNumber ≥ ↑k

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points with no three on a line.
Does $A$ determine at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ distinct distances?
references: [erdosproblems.com/1082](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1082)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))), EuclideanGeometry.NonTrilinear ↑A → A.card / 2 ≤ distinctDistances A

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points with no three on a line.
Must there exist a single point from which there are at least $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ distinct
distances?

This question has been answered negatively by Xichuan in the
[comments](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/1082), who gave a set of $42$ points in
$\mathbb{R}^2$, with no three on a line, such that each point determines only $20$ distinct distances.

A smaller counterexample has been formalised here: it comprised of $8$ points, where each point only
determines $3$ distances.

This counterexample has originally been found by Heiko Harborth.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1082](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1082)
declarations.type_pretty:
False ↔
  ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
    A.Nonempty → EuclideanGeometry.NonTrilinear ↑A → ∃ a, ∃ (_ : a ∈ A), A.card / 2 ≤ distinctDistancesFrom A a - 1

[Er46b] Erdős, P., *On sets of distances of {$n$} points*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1946), 248--250.

Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains at most $f(n)$
many sets of four points which are 'degenerate' in the sense that some pair are the same distance
apart. Estimate $f(n)$ - in particular, is it true that $f(n)\leq n^{3+o(1)}$?

Here a set of four points is degenerate if two of its six pairwise distances are equal, and
$f(n)\leq n^{3+o(1)}$ is read as $f(n) \ll n^{3+\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$.

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(N)$ be the size of the largest subset $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that
every $n\in A+A$ is squarefree. Estimate $f(N)$. In particular, is it true that
$f(N)\leq N^{o(1)}$, or even $f(N) \leq (\log N)^{O(1)}$?

This theorem formalizes the subpolynomial bound as `f(N) = O(N^ε)` for every `ε > 0`.

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 111** (Erdős, Hajnal, Szemerédi [EHS82]):

If $G$ is a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$, is it true that $h_G(n)/n \to \infty$?

Formally: for every graph $G$ (on a type $V$) with chromatic cardinal $\aleph_1$, the ratio
$h_G(n)/n$ tends to infinity: for every constant $C$, all sufficiently large $n$ satisfy
$h_G(n) > C \cdot n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/111](https://www.erdosproblems.com/111)
[Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved. (1981)
[EHS82] Erdős, P., Hajnal, A., and Szemerédi, E., On almost bipartite large chromatic graphs. Theory and practice of combinatorics (1982), 117–123.
[Er87] Erdős, P., Some problems on finite and infinite graphs. (1987)
[Er90] Erdős, P., Some of my favourite unsolved problems. (1990)
[Er97d] Erdős, P., Some recent problems and results in graph theory. (1997)
[Er97f] Erdős, P., Some unsolved problems. (1997)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V),
  G.chromaticCardinal = Cardinal.aleph 1 → Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos111.hG G n) / ↑n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Erdős conjectured [Er81] that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there is a graph $G$ with
$\chi(G) = \aleph_1$ such that $h_G(n) \ll n^{1+\varepsilon}$.
The graph is chosen after $\varepsilon$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/111](https://www.erdosproblems.com/111)
[Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved. (1981)
[EHS82] Erdős, P., Hajnal, A., and Szemerédi, E., On almost bipartite large chromatic graphs. Theory and practice of combinatorics (1982), 117–123.
[Er87] Erdős, P., Some problems on finite and infinite graphs. (1987)
[Er90] Erdős, P., Some of my favourite unsolved problems. (1990)
[Er97d] Erdős, P., Some recent problems and results in graph theory. (1997)
[Er97f] Erdős, P., Some unsolved problems. (1997)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (ε : ℝ),
  0 < ε →
    ∃ V G, G.chromaticCardinal = Cardinal.aleph 1 ∧ (fun n => ↑(Erdos111.hG G n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n ^ (1 + ε)

declarations.docstring:
**Linear lower bound (ZFC, [EHS82])**: Every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ has
$h_G(n) \geq c \cdot n$ for some positive constant $c > 0$ and all sufficiently large $n$
(i.e., the *linear* lower bound $h_G(n) \gg n$ is known).

This follows from the fact that every graph with uncountable chromatic number contains
$\aleph_1$ vertex-disjoint odd cycles of some fixed odd length $\ell$: any induced subgraph
on $n$ vertices containing $\gg n / \ell$ such cycles requires removing $\gg n$ edges to
become bipartite.

This is a *strictly weaker* statement than the headline `erdos_111`, which asks for
$h_G(n)/n \to \infty$ (i.e., $h_G(n)$ grows *super-linearly* — the constant `c` could be
taken arbitrarily large for a fixed graph $G$). Whether the linear lower bound can be
improved to super-linear remains the open question.
references: [erdosproblems.com/111](https://www.erdosproblems.com/111)
[Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved. (1981)
[EHS82] Erdős, P., Hajnal, A., and Szemerédi, E., On almost bipartite large chromatic graphs. Theory and practice of combinatorics (1982), 117–123.
[Er87] Erdős, P., Some problems on finite and infinite graphs. (1987)
[Er90] Erdős, P., Some of my favourite unsolved problems. (1990)
[Er97d] Erdős, P., Some recent problems and results in graph theory. (1997)
[Er97f] Erdős, P., Some unsolved problems. (1997)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V),
  G.chromaticCardinal = Cardinal.aleph 1 → ∃ c, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, c * ↑n ≤ ↑(Erdos111.hG G n)

declarations.docstring:
**Upper bound existence (Erdős-Hajnal-Szemerédi [EHS82])**: There exists a graph $G$ with
chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such that $h_G(n) \ll n^{3/2}$, i.e., there is a constant $C > 0$
with $h_G(n) \leq C \cdot n^{3/2}$ for all $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/111](https://www.erdosproblems.com/111)
[Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved. (1981)
[EHS82] Erdős, P., Hajnal, A., and Szemerédi, E., On almost bipartite large chromatic graphs. Theory and practice of combinatorics (1982), 117–123.
[Er87] Erdős, P., Some problems on finite and infinite graphs. (1987)
[Er90] Erdős, P., Some of my favourite unsolved problems. (1990)
[Er97d] Erdős, P., Some recent problems and results in graph theory. (1997)
[Er97f] Erdős, P., Some unsolved problems. (1997)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ V G, G.chromaticCardinal = Cardinal.aleph 1 ∧ (fun n => ↑(Erdos111.hG G n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n ^ (3 / 2)

declarations.docstring:
Let $p>q\geq 2$ be two coprime integers. We call $n$ representable if it is the sum of
integers of the form $p^kq^l$, none of which divide each other.

If $\{p,q\}\neq \{2,3\}$ then what can be said about the density of non-representable
numbers? Are there infinitely many coprime non-representable numbers, that is, an infinite
family of pairwise coprime non-representable integers?
references: [Erdős Problem 1110](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1110)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (p q : ℕ),
  q < p →
    2 ≤ q →
      p.Coprime q →
        ¬(p = 3 ∧ q = 2) → ∃ A, A.Infinite ∧ A.Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧ ∀ n ∈ A, ¬Erdos1110.Representable p q n

declarations.docstring: Anticomplete sets stay anticomplete when the two sets are swapped.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1111](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1111)
[ElEr85] El-Zahar, M. and Erdős, P., *On the existence of two non-neighboring subgraphs in a graph*. Combinatorica 5 (1985), 295-300.
[NSS24] Nguyen, T., Scott, A. and Seymour, P., *On a problem of El-Zahar and Erdős*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 165 (2024), 211-222. [arXiv:2303.13449](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13449)
[Wa80b] Wagon, S., *A bound on the chromatic number of graphs without certain induced subgraphs*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 29 (1980), 345-346.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V} {A B : Set V}, Erdos1111.Anticomplete G A B → Erdos1111.Anticomplete G B A

declarations.docstring:
If $G$ is a finite graph and $A,B$ are disjoint sets of vertices then we call $A,B$ anticomplete
if there are no edges between $A$ and $B$.

If $t,c\geq 1$ then there exists $d\geq 1$ such that if $\chi(G)\geq d$ and $\omega(G)<t$ then
there are anticomplete sets $A,B$ with $\chi(A)\geq \chi(B)\geq c$.

El-Zahar and Erdős [ElEr85] pose this as a question. Here $\chi(A)$ is the chromatic number of
the induced subgraph $G[A]$. Swapping $A$ and $B$, the conclusion says that both $\chi(A)$ and
$\chi(B)$ are at least $c$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1111](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1111)
[ElEr85] El-Zahar, M. and Erdős, P., *On the existence of two non-neighboring subgraphs in a graph*. Combinatorica 5 (1985), 295-300.
[NSS24] Nguyen, T., Scott, A. and Seymour, P., *On a problem of El-Zahar and Erdős*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 165 (2024), 211-222. [arXiv:2303.13449](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13449)
[Wa80b] Wagon, S., *A bound on the chromatic number of graphs without certain induced subgraphs*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 29 (1980), 345-346.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (t c : ℕ),
  1 ≤ t →
    1 ≤ c →
      ∃ d,
        1 ≤ d ∧
          ∀ (V : Type u_1) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
            ↑d ≤ G.chromaticNumber →
              G.CliqueFree t →
                ∃ A B,
                  Erdos1111.Anticomplete G A B ∧
                    ↑c ≤ (SimpleGraph.induce A G).chromaticNumber ∧ ↑c ≤ (SimpleGraph.induce B G).chromaticNumber

declarations.docstring: El-Zahar and Erdős [ElEr85] proved the case $c = 3$: $d(t,3)$ exists for every $t$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1111](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1111)
[ElEr85] El-Zahar, M. and Erdős, P., *On the existence of two non-neighboring subgraphs in a graph*. Combinatorica 5 (1985), 295-300.
[NSS24] Nguyen, T., Scott, A. and Seymour, P., *On a problem of El-Zahar and Erdős*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 165 (2024), 211-222. [arXiv:2303.13449](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13449)
[Wa80b] Wagon, S., *A bound on the chromatic number of graphs without certain induced subgraphs*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 29 (1980), 345-346.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (t : ℕ),
  1 ≤ t →
    ∃ d,
      1 ≤ d ∧
        ∀ (V : Type u_1) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
          ↑d ≤ G.chromaticNumber →
            G.CliqueFree t →
              ∃ A B,
                Erdos1111.Anticomplete G A B ∧
                  3 ≤ (SimpleGraph.induce A G).chromaticNumber ∧ 3 ≤ (SimpleGraph.induce B G).chromaticNumber

declarations.docstring:
Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour [NSS24] prove that if $t,c\geq 1$ then there exists $d\geq 1$ such
that if $\chi(G)\geq d$ and $\omega(G)<t$ then there are anticomplete sets $A,B$ with
$\chi(B)\geq c$ and such that the minimum degree of the induced graph on $A$ is at least $c$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1111](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1111)
[ElEr85] El-Zahar, M. and Erdős, P., *On the existence of two non-neighboring subgraphs in a graph*. Combinatorica 5 (1985), 295-300.
[NSS24] Nguyen, T., Scott, A. and Seymour, P., *On a problem of El-Zahar and Erdős*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 165 (2024), 211-222. [arXiv:2303.13449](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13449)
[Wa80b] Wagon, S., *A bound on the chromatic number of graphs without certain induced subgraphs*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 29 (1980), 345-346.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (t c : ℕ),
  1 ≤ t →
    1 ≤ c →
      ∃ d,
        1 ≤ d ∧
          ∀ (V : Type u_1) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
            ↑d ≤ G.chromaticNumber →
              G.CliqueFree t →
                ∃ A B,
                  Erdos1111.Anticomplete G A B ∧
                    A.Nonempty ∧
                      (∀ v ∈ A, c ≤ (A ∩ G.neighborSet v).ncard) ∧ ↑c ≤ (SimpleGraph.induce B G).chromaticNumber

declarations.docstring: El-Zahar and Erdős [ElEr85] proved $d(3,3)\leq 8$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1111](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1111)
[ElEr85] El-Zahar, M. and Erdős, P., *On the existence of two non-neighboring subgraphs in a graph*. Combinatorica 5 (1985), 295-300.
[NSS24] Nguyen, T., Scott, A. and Seymour, P., *On a problem of El-Zahar and Erdős*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 165 (2024), 211-222. [arXiv:2303.13449](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13449)
[Wa80b] Wagon, S., *A bound on the chromatic number of graphs without certain induced subgraphs*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 29 (1980), 345-346.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (V : Type u_1) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
  8 ≤ G.chromaticNumber →
    G.CliqueFree 3 →
      ∃ A B,
        Erdos1111.Anticomplete G A B ∧
          3 ≤ (SimpleGraph.induce A G).chromaticNumber ∧ 3 ≤ (SimpleGraph.induce B G).chromaticNumber

declarations.docstring:
El-Zahar and Erdős note that a result of Wagon [Wa80b] implies $d(t,2)\leq \binom{t}{2}+1$, where
$d(t,c)$ is the minimal $d$ in the problem.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1111](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1111)
[ElEr85] El-Zahar, M. and Erdős, P., *On the existence of two non-neighboring subgraphs in a graph*. Combinatorica 5 (1985), 295-300.
[NSS24] Nguyen, T., Scott, A. and Seymour, P., *On a problem of El-Zahar and Erdős*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 165 (2024), 211-222. [arXiv:2303.13449](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.13449)
[Wa80b] Wagon, S., *A bound on the chromatic number of graphs without certain induced subgraphs*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 29 (1980), 345-346.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (t : ℕ) (V : Type u_1) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
  ↑(t.choose 2 + 1) ≤ G.chromaticNumber →
    G.CliqueFree t →
      ∃ A B,
        Erdos1111.Anticomplete G A B ∧
          2 ≤ (SimpleGraph.induce A G).chromaticNumber ∧ 2 ≤ (SimpleGraph.induce B G).chromaticNumber

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 1113.** Do there exist Sierpiński numbers that possess no finite covering set
of primes?

Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] conjectured that the answer is yes. A negative answer would imply
that there are infinitely many Fermat primes.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1113](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1113)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L., Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory. Monographie de l'Enseignement Mathématique, No. 28 (1980).
[Si60] Sierpiński, W., Elementary Theory of Numbers. Państwowe Wydawnictwo Naukowe, Warsaw (1960).
[FFK08] Filaseta, M., Finch, C., and Kozek, M., On powers associated with Sierpiński numbers, Riesel numbers and Polignac's conjecture. Journal of Number Theory 128 (2008), 1916–1940.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ k, k.IsSierpinskiNumber ∧ ¬Erdos1113.HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet k

declarations.docstring:
**Filaseta–Finch–Kozek conjecture (2008).** Every Sierpiński number is either a perfect power
or possesses a finite covering set of primes.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1113](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1113)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L., Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory. Monographie de l'Enseignement Mathématique, No. 28 (1980).
[Si60] Sierpiński, W., Elementary Theory of Numbers. Państwowe Wydawnictwo Naukowe, Warsaw (1960).
[FFK08] Filaseta, M., Finch, C., and Kozek, M., On powers associated with Sierpiński numbers, Riesel numbers and Polignac's conjecture. Journal of Number Theory 128 (2008), 1916–1940.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), k.IsSierpinskiNumber → k.IsPerfectPower ∨ Erdos1113.HasFinitePrimeCoveringSet k

declarations.docstring:
Sierpiński [Si60] proved that there are infinitely many Sierpiński numbers, using covering
systems to construct suitable covering sets for any $k$ satisfying a certain congruence.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1113](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1113)

declarations.docstring:
For $c \geq 0$ the function $c \log n$ is additive and $A$ is empty, so it satisfies the
hypotheses of `erdos_1122`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1122](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1122)
[Er46](https://doi.org/10.2307/2305092) Erdős, P., *On the distribution function of additive functions*. Annals of Math. (1946), 1-20.
[Ma22] Mangerel, Alexander P., *Additive functions in short intervals, gaps and a conjecture of Erdős*. Ramanujan J. (2022), 1023--1090.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (c : ℝ),
  0 ≤ c →
    ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
      (∀ (n : ℕ), f n = c * Real.log ↑n) →
        (∀ a > 0, ∀ b > 0, a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) ∧ {n | 1 ≤ n ∧ f (n + 1) < f n}.HasDensity 0

declarations.docstring:
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{R}$ be an additive function (i.e. $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$ whenever
$(a,b)=1$). Let
$$A=\{ n \geq 1: f(n+1)< f(n)\}.$$
If $\lvert A\cap [1,X]\rvert =o(X)$ then must $f(n)=c\log n$ for some $c\in \mathbb{R}$?

The condition $\lvert A\cap [1,X]\rvert =o(X)$ says that $A$ has natural density $0$.

Partial progress was made by Mangerel [Ma22], who proved that this is true for completely
additive $f$ if
$$\lvert A\cap [1,X]\rvert \ll \frac{X}{(\log X)^{2+c}}$$
for some $c>0$, and if $f(p)$ does not have very large values (in a certain technical sense).

See also `erdos_491`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1122](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1122)
[Er46](https://doi.org/10.2307/2305092) Erdős, P., *On the distribution function of additive functions*. Annals of Math. (1946), 1-20.
[Ma22] Mangerel, Alexander P., *Additive functions in short intervals, gaps and a conjecture of Erdős*. Ramanujan J. (2022), 1023--1090.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
  (∀ a > 0, ∀ b > 0, a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    {n | 1 ≤ n ∧ f (n + 1) < f n}.HasDensity 0 → ∃ c, ∀ n > 0, f n = c * Real.log ↑n

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er46] proved that $f(n)=c\log n$ for some $c\in\mathbb{R}$ if $A$ is empty, that is, if
$f(n) \leq f(n+1)$ for all $n \geq 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1122](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1122)

[Ma22] Mangerel, Alexander P., *Additive functions in short intervals, gaps and a conjecture of Erdős*. Ramanujan J. (2022), 1023--1090.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
  (∀ a > 0, ∀ b > 0, a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    (∀ n ≥ 1, f n ≤ f (n + 1)) → ∃ c, ∀ n > 0, f n = c * Real.log ↑n

declarations.docstring: Erdős [Er46] proved that $f(n)=c\log n$ for some $c\in\mathbb{R}$ if $f(n+1)-f(n)=o(1)$.

declarations.docstring:
Let $d_n=p_{n+1}-p_n$, where $p_n$ denotes the $n$th prime. Is it true that
$$\frac{\max_{n < x}d_{n}d_{n-1}}{(\max_{n < x}d_n)^2}\to 0$$ as $x\to \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/1137](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1137)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun x => ↑((Finset.range x).sup fun n => primeGap n * primeGap (n - 1)) / ↑((Finset.range x).sup primeGap) ^ 2)
    Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

declarations.docstring:
Let $1\leq u_1 < u_2 < \cdots$ be the sequence of integers with at most $2$ prime factors.
Is it true that $$\limsup_{k \to \infty} \frac{u_{k+1}-u_k}{\log k}=\infty?$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/1139](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1139)
declarations.type_pretty:
Filter.limsup
    (fun k =>
      (↑↑(Nat.nth (fun n => 0 < n ∧ ArithmeticFunction.cardFactors n ≤ 2) (k + 1)) -
          ↑↑(Nat.nth (fun n => 0 < n ∧ ArithmeticFunction.cardFactors n ≤ 2) k)) /
        ↑(Real.log (↑k + 1)))
    Filter.atTop =
  ⊤

declarations.docstring:
If $p(z) \in \mathbb{C}[z]$ is a monic polynomial of degree $n$, is the length of the curve
$\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \lvert p(z)\rvert = 1\}$ maximised when $p(z) = z^n - 1$?

We require $n \geq 1$. For $n = 0$ the only monic polynomial is $1$, whose level set is all of
$\mathbb{C}$, while $z^0 - 1 = 0$ has an empty level set.

Let $K_{t}(r)$ be the complete $t$-partite $t$-uniform hypergraph with $r$ vertices in each class.
Is it true that
$$\mathrm{ex}_t(n,K_t(r)) \geq n^{t-r^{1-t}-o(1)}$$
for all $t,r\geq 2$? The restriction $r\geq 2$ excludes forbidding a single edge.

declarations.docstring:
Determine whether there exists a constant $C>1$ such that the following holds.

Let $P$ be a finite [projective plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Projective_plane). Must there exist a set of points $S$ such that $1\leq \lvert S\cap \ell\rvert \leq C$ for all lines $\ell$?

[ESS83] Erdős, P. and Silverman, R. and Stein, A., *Intersection properties of families containing sets of nearly the same size*. Ars Combin. (1983), 247--259.
[Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*. Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C,
  1 < C ∧
    ∀ (P L : Type) (x : Membership P L) (x_1 : Fintype P) (x_2 : Fintype L) (x_3 : Configuration.ProjectivePlane P L),
      ∃ S, ∀ (l : L), 1 ≤ (S ∩ {p | p ∈ l}).ncard ∧ (S ∩ {p | p ∈ l}).ncard ≤ C

declarations.docstring:
Give an asymptotic formula for the number of subgroups of $S_n$. Is there a statistical theorem
on their order?

A problem of Erdős and Turán [Va99, 5.73]. We state the first question: `erdos_1162.answer` is a
function asymptotically equivalent to the number $f(n)$ of subgroups of $S_n$ (an explicit
formula is intended, not $f$ itself). The second question is too vague to state.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1162](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1162)

$$\log f(n)=\left(\frac{1}{16}+o(1)\right)n^2.$$
Here $\log$ is the logarithm to base $2$, as in [RoTr25].

$\alpha>0$ and $\beta$ such that for all integers $n>1$
$$2^{n^2/16+\alpha n\log n}\leq f(n)\leq 2^{n^2/16+\beta n^{3/2}},$$
where $\log$ is the logarithm to base $2$. This implies the previous variant.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1162](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1162)
