declarations.docstring: The partition relation $\mu \to (\nu)^r_1$ with a single color is equivalent to $\nu \le \mu$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1167](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1167)
[EHMR84] P. Erdős, A. Hajnal, A. Máté and R. Rado, *Combinatorial set theory: partition relations for cardinals*. Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics 106, North-Holland (1984).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (μ : Cardinal.{u}) (r : ℕ) (ν : Ordinal.ToType 1 → Cardinal.{u}),
  Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel μ r 1 ν ↔ μ ≥ ν Erdos1167.i0

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 1167.** Let $r \geq 2$ be finite, $\gamma \geq 2$, and $\lambda$ be an infinite
cardinal. Let $\kappa_\alpha > r$ be cardinals for all $\alpha < \gamma$. Is it true
that
$$2^\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha + 1)_{\alpha < \gamma}^{r+1}$$
implies
$$\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha < \gamma}^r?$$
Here $+$ means cardinal addition, so that $\kappa_\alpha + 1 = \kappa_\alpha$
if $\kappa_\alpha$ is infinite.

A problem of Erdős, Hajnal, and Rado.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1167](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1167)
[EHMR84] P. Erdős, A. Hajnal, A. Máté and R. Rado, *Combinatorial set theory: partition relations for cardinals*. Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics 106, North-Holland (1984).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  2 ≤ r →
    ∀ (lam : Cardinal.{u}),
      Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ lam →
        ∀ (γ : Ordinal.{u}),
          2 ≤ γ →
            ∀ (κ : γ.ToType → Cardinal.{u}),
              (∀ (α : γ.ToType), ↑r < κ α) →
                (Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel (2 ^ lam) (r + 1) γ fun α => κ α + 1) →
                  Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel lam r γ κ

declarations.docstring:
The unrestricted version of Erdős Problem 1167 (without the condition $\gamma \geq 2$ from the
original Erdős–Hajnal list) is false. Taking $\gamma = 1$, $\kappa_0 = \aleph_1$, $\lambda =
\aleph_0$: the premise $2^{\aleph_0} \to (\aleph_1 + 1)^3_1$ holds since $2^{\aleph_0} \geq
\aleph_1$, but the conclusion $\aleph_0 \to (\aleph_1)^2_1$ fails since $\aleph_0 < \aleph_1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1167](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1167)
[EHMR84] P. Erdős, A. Hajnal, A. Máté and R. Rado, *Combinatorial set theory: partition relations for cardinals*. Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics 106, North-Holland (1984).
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∀ (r : ℕ),
    2 ≤ r →
      ∀ (lam : Cardinal.{u}),
        Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ lam →
          ∀ (γ : Ordinal.{u}) (κ : γ.ToType → Cardinal.{u}),
            (Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel (2 ^ lam) (r + 1) γ fun α => κ α + 1) →
              Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel lam r γ κ

declarations.docstring: **Binary-color case.** The $\gamma = 2$ specialization (two color classes).
references: [erdosproblems.com/1167](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1167)
[EHMR84] P. Erdős, A. Hajnal, A. Máté and R. Rado, *Combinatorial set theory: partition relations for cardinals*. Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics 106, North-Holland (1984).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  2 ≤ r →
    ∀ (lam : Cardinal.{u}),
      Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ lam →
        ∀ (κ : Ordinal.ToType 2 → Cardinal.{u}),
          (∀ (α : Ordinal.ToType 2), ↑r < κ α) →
            (Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel (2 ^ lam) (r + 1) 2 fun α => κ α + 1) →
              Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel lam r 2 κ

declarations.docstring:
**Finite-target case.** When all $\kappa_\alpha$ are finite, $\kappa_\alpha + 1$
is the ordinary natural-number successor. Special case of `erdos_1167`.

This case was proved by Erdős, Hajnal, Máté and Rado [EHMR84], using the Erdős–Rado tree
argument and the negative stepping-up lemma. The statement omits the condition $n_\alpha > r$.
This is harmless, since a colouring that witnesses
$\lambda \not\to (n_\alpha)^r_{\alpha < \gamma}$ can only use colours $\alpha$ with $n_\alpha > r$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1167](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1167)
[EHMR84] P. Erdős, A. Hajnal, A. Máté and R. Rado, *Combinatorial set theory: partition relations for cardinals*. Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics 106, North-Holland (1984).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  2 ≤ r →
    ∀ (lam : Cardinal.{u}),
      Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ lam →
        ∀ (γ : Ordinal.{u}),
          2 ≤ γ →
            ∀ (n : γ.ToType → ℕ),
              (Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel (2 ^ lam) (r + 1) γ fun α => ↑(n α) + 1) →
                Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel lam r γ fun α => ↑(n α)

declarations.docstring:
**Infinite-target case.** When all $\kappa_\alpha \geq \aleph_0$ are infinite and bounded by
$\lambda$, $\kappa_\alpha + 1 = \kappa_\alpha$, so the hypothesis simplifies to a "pure"
stepping-down lemma:
$$2^\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha<\gamma}^{r+1} \implies
   \lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha<\gamma}^r.$$
The condition $\kappa_\alpha \leq \lambda$ is needed to avoid a size obstruction: without it, the
conclusion would require a subset of $\lambda$ of size $\kappa_\alpha > \lambda$, which is impossible
(see `infinite_targets_needs_bound`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/1167](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1167)
[EHMR84] P. Erdős, A. Hajnal, A. Máté and R. Rado, *Combinatorial set theory: partition relations for cardinals*. Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics 106, North-Holland (1984).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  2 ≤ r →
    ∀ (lam : Cardinal.{u}),
      Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ lam →
        ∀ (γ : Ordinal.{u}),
          2 ≤ γ →
            ∀ (κ : γ.ToType → Cardinal.{u}),
              (∀ (i : γ.ToType), Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ κ i) →
                (∀ (i : γ.ToType), κ i ≤ lam) →
                  Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel (2 ^ lam) (r + 1) γ κ →
                    Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel lam r γ κ

declarations.docstring:
The `infinite_targets` variant without the bound $\kappa_\alpha \leq \lambda$ is false.
Taking $\gamma = 1$, $\kappa_0 = 2^{\aleph_0}$, $\lambda = \aleph_0$: the premise
$2^{\aleph_0} \to (2^{\aleph_0})^3_1$ holds since $2^{\aleph_0} \leq 2^{\aleph_0}$, but the
conclusion $\aleph_0 \to (2^{\aleph_0})^2_1$ fails by Cantor's theorem.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1167](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1167)
[EHMR84] P. Erdős, A. Hajnal, A. Máté and R. Rado, *Combinatorial set theory: partition relations for cardinals*. Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics 106, North-Holland (1984).
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∀ (r : ℕ),
    2 ≤ r →
      ∀ (lam : Cardinal.{u}),
        Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ lam →
          ∀ (γ : Ordinal.{u}) (κ : γ.ToType → Cardinal.{u}),
            (∀ (i : γ.ToType), Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ κ i) →
              Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel (2 ^ lam) (r + 1) γ κ → Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel lam r γ κ

declarations.docstring:
**$r = 2$ case.** The stepping-down from 3-uniform to 2-uniform partition
relations: $2^\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha + 1)_{\alpha<\gamma}^3$ implies
$\lambda \to (\kappa_\alpha)_{\alpha<\gamma}^2$. Generalises the classical
Erdős–Rado stepping-up/down theorem for pairs.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1167](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1167)
[EHMR84] P. Erdős, A. Hajnal, A. Máté and R. Rado, *Combinatorial set theory: partition relations for cardinals*. Studies in Logic and the Foundations of Mathematics 106, North-Holland (1984).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (lam : Cardinal.{u}),
  Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ lam →
    ∀ (γ : Ordinal.{u}),
      2 ≤ γ →
        ∀ (κ : γ.ToType → Cardinal.{u}),
          (∀ (α : γ.ToType), 2 < κ α) →
            (Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel (2 ^ lam) 3 γ fun α => κ α + 1) →
              Combinatorics.cardinalPartitionRel lam 2 γ κ

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 1168.** Prove that
$$\aleph_{\omega+1} \not\to (\aleph_{\omega+1}, \underbrace{3, 3, \ldots}_{\aleph_0})^2_{\aleph_0}$$
without assuming the generalized continuum hypothesis.

A problem of Erdős, Hajnal, and Rado [EHR65]: the negative arrow is known under GCH;
the open problem asks for a ZFC proof. Here `ω = Ordinal.omega0`, so `ℵ_ (ω + 1)` is
the successor cardinal of the singular `ℵ_ω`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1168](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1168)
[EHR65] Erdős, P., Hajnal, A. and Rado, R., *Partition relations for cardinal numbers*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1965), pp. 93–196.
declarations.type_pretty: ¬CardinalCountableColorRamsey (Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega0 + 1))

declarations.docstring:
**GCH implies `2^(ℵ_ω) = ℵ_{ω+1}`** — the arithmetic fact used in the
Erdős–Hajnal–Rado [EHR65] proof. Direct from the Jech-style formulation of GCH.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1168](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1168)
[EHR65] Erdős, P., Hajnal, A. and Rado, R., *Partition relations for cardinal numbers*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1965), pp. 93–196.
declarations.type_pretty: Cardinal.GCH → 2 ^ Cardinal.aleph Ordinal.omega0 = Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega0 + 1)

declarations.docstring: `ℵ_{ω+1} = Order.succ (ℵ_ω)`: a structural fact used in partition calculus.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1168](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1168)
[EHR65] Erdős, P., Hajnal, A. and Rado, R., *Partition relations for cardinal numbers*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1965), pp. 93–196.
declarations.type_pretty: Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega0 + 1) = Order.succ (Cardinal.aleph Ordinal.omega0)

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős–Hajnal–Rado theorem under GCH** [EHR65]: the negative partition relation
$\aleph_{\omega+1} \not\to (\aleph_{\omega+1}, 3, 3, \ldots)^2_{\aleph_0}$ holds
assuming GCH.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1168](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1168)
[EHR65] Erdős, P., Hajnal, A. and Rado, R., *Partition relations for cardinal numbers*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1965), pp. 93–196.
declarations.type_pretty: Cardinal.GCH → ¬CardinalCountableColorRamsey (Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega0 + 1))

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that $\omega_1^2 \not\to (\omega_1^2, 3)^2$?

A problem of Erdős and Hajnal. Hajnal [Ha71] proved this assuming the continuum hypothesis.
The source's displayed relation has blue target $3$; its introductory $k$ does not occur
in that relation. See also [erdosproblems.com/592](https://www.erdosproblems.com/592).
references: [erdosproblems.com/1169](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1169)
declarations.type_pretty: ¬OrdinalRamsey (Ordinal.omega 1 ^ 2) (Ordinal.omega 1 ^ 2) 3

declarations.docstring:
The finite-blue-target form asks whether $\omega_1^2 \not\to (\omega_1^2, k)^2$
for every $k \ge 3$. The restriction excludes $k \le 2$, where the positive relation holds.
A colouring witnessing the negative relation with blue target $3$ also witnesses this form.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1169](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1169)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → ¬OrdinalRamsey (Ordinal.omega 1 ^ 2) (Ordinal.omega 1 ^ 2) ↑k

declarations.docstring:
**Hajnal (1971), assuming CH.** Under the Continuum Hypothesis,
$\omega_1^2 \not\to (\omega_1^2, k)^2$ holds for every finite $k \ge 3$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1169](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1169)
declarations.type_pretty: Cardinal.continuum = Cardinal.aleph 1 → ∀ (k : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → ¬OrdinalRamsey (Ordinal.omega 1 ^ 2) (Ordinal.omega 1 ^ 2) ↑k

declarations.docstring:
**Monotonicity in the blue side.** If the ordinal Ramsey relation holds with blue
target $\gamma$, it holds with any smaller blue target $\gamma' \le \gamma$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1169](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1169)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {α β γ γ' : Ordinal.{u}}, OrdinalRamsey α β γ → γ' ≤ γ → OrdinalRamsey α β γ'

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 1171.** Is it true that for all finite $k < \omega$,
$$\omega_1^2 \to (\omega_1 \cdot \omega, \underbrace{3, \ldots, 3}_{k})^2_{k+1}?$$

In any $(k+1)$-coloring of the pairs of the complete graph on $\omega_1^2$, either
there is a color-0 set of order type $\omega_1 \cdot \omega$, or there is a
monochromatic triangle $K_3$ in some non-zero color. The case $k = 1$
(`erdos_1171.variants.k_one`) is the Erdős–Hajnal theorem [EH74].
references: [erdosproblems.com/1171](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1171)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), OrdinalMultiColorRamsey (Ordinal.omega 1 ^ 2) (Ordinal.omega 1 * Ordinal.omega0) 3 k

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős–Hajnal theorem** [EH74]: the case $k = 1$,
$\omega_1^2 \to (\omega_1 \cdot \omega, 3)^2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1171](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1171)
declarations.type_pretty: OrdinalMultiColorRamsey (Ordinal.omega 1 ^ 2) (Ordinal.omega 1 * Ordinal.omega0) 3 1

declarations.docstring:
`OrdinalMultiColorRamsey` is monotone in the number of non-zero colors:
a witness for the `k`-color version yields one for any `j ≤ k`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1171](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1171)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {j k : ℕ},
  j ≤ k →
    OrdinalMultiColorRamsey (Ordinal.omega 1 ^ 2) (Ordinal.omega 1 * Ordinal.omega0) 3 k →
      OrdinalMultiColorRamsey (Ordinal.omega 1 ^ 2) (Ordinal.omega 1 * Ordinal.omega0) 3 j

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős–Hajnal Problem 1173** [EH74]. Assume GCH. Let
$f : \omega_{\omega+1} \to [\omega_{\omega+1}]^{\leq \aleph_\omega}$
be a set mapping such that $|f(\alpha) \cap f(\beta)| < \aleph_\omega$ for all
$\alpha \neq \beta$. Does there exist a free set of cardinality $\aleph_{\omega+1}$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/1173](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1173)
declarations.type_pretty:
Cardinal.GCH →
  ∀ (f : (Ordinal.omega (Ordinal.omega0 + 1)).ToType → Set (Ordinal.omega (Ordinal.omega0 + 1)).ToType),
    Erdos1173.IsSetMapping f → ∃ Y, Erdos1173.IsFreeSet f Y ∧ Cardinal.mk ↑Y = Cardinal.aleph (Ordinal.omega0 + 1)

`ℵ_ω < ℵ_{ω+1}`: free-set size is strictly above the image-bound, making
the problem non-trivial.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1173](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1173)

∀ (f : (Ordinal.omega (Ordinal.omega0 + 1)).ToType → Set (Ordinal.omega (Ordinal.omega0 + 1)).ToType),

∀ (f : (Ordinal.omega (Ordinal.omega0 + 1)).ToType → Set (Ordinal.omega (Ordinal.omega0 + 1)).ToType)

references: [erdosproblems.com/1173](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1173)

∀ (f : (Ordinal.omega (Ordinal.omega0 + 1)).ToType → Set (Ordinal.omega (Ordinal.omega0 + 1)).ToType),

declarations.docstring:
The empty graph on $\mathbb{N}$ is trivially $K_4$-free but fails the colouring
property of part (i): it has no triangles at all, so the $K_4$-free condition alone
is not enough.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1174](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1174)
[Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999), problem 7.91.

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 1174, part (i)** [Va99, 7.91]. A problem of Erdős and Hajnal:
does there exist a graph $G$ with no $K_4$ such that every edge colouring of $G$
with countably many colours contains a monochromatic $K_3$?

For simplicity the colourings are given on all unordered pairs $\operatorname{Sym}_2(V)$;
only the values on the edges of $G$ matter, since a monochromatic triangle is witnessed by
edges alone.

Shelah proved that a graph with this property can consistently exist, so the
problem is not disprovable in ZFC; whether such a graph exists outright remains open.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1174](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1174)
[Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999), problem 7.91.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ V G,
  G.CliqueFree 4 ∧
    ∀ (c : Sym2 V → ℕ), ∃ x y z, G.Adj x y ∧ G.Adj y z ∧ G.Adj x z ∧ c s(x, y) = c s(y, z) ∧ c s(y, z) = c s(x, z)

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 1174, part (ii)** [Va99, 7.91]. A problem of Erdős and Hajnal:
does there exist a graph $G$ with no $K_{\aleph_1}$ (that is, every clique of $G$
is countable) such that every edge colouring of $G$ with countably many colours
contains a monochromatic $K_{\aleph_0}$ (an infinite clique all of whose edges
receive the same colour)?

For simplicity the colourings are given on all unordered pairs $\operatorname{Sym}_2(V)$;
only the values on the edges of $G$ matter.

Shelah proved that a graph with this property can consistently exist, so the
problem is not disprovable in ZFC; whether such a graph exists outright remains open.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1174](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1174)
[Va99] Various, *Some of Paul's favorite problems*. Booklet produced for the conference "Paul Erdős and his mathematics", Budapest, July 1999 (1999), problem 7.91.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ V G,
  (∀ (S : Set V), G.IsClique S → Cardinal.mk ↑S ≤ Cardinal.aleph0) ∧
    ∀ (c : Sym2 V → ℕ), ∃ S, G.IsClique S ∧ S.Infinite ∧ ∃ k, ∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, x ≠ y → c s(x, y) = k

declarations.docstring:
Let $\kappa$ be an uncountable cardinal. Must there exist a cardinal $\lambda$ such that every
graph with chromatic number $\lambda$ contains a triangle-free subgraph with chromatic number
$\kappa$?

Shelah proved that a negative answer is consistent when
$\kappa = \lambda = \aleph_1$ (see `erdos_1175.variants.shelah_consistency`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/1175](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1175)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (κ : Cardinal.{u_1}),
    Cardinal.aleph0 < κ →
      ∃ μ,
        ∀ (V : Type u_1) (G : SimpleGraph V),
          G.chromaticCardinal = μ → ∃ H, H.coe.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.coe.chromaticCardinal = κ

declarations.docstring:
Every graph has a triangle-free subgraph: the bottom subgraph (with no edges)
witnesses triangle-freeness, so the existential
`∃ H : G.Subgraph, H.coe.CliqueFree 3` in `erdos_1175` is non-vacuous.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1175](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1175)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (V : Type u_1) (G : SimpleGraph V), ∃ H, H.coe.CliqueFree 3

declarations.docstring:
The threshold variant `threshold_formulation` is stronger than the exact-equality
form `erdos_1175`: if every graph with `chromaticCardinal ≥ μ` has the desired
triangle-free subgraph, then in particular every graph with `chromaticCardinal = μ`
does too.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1175](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1175)
declarations.type_pretty:
(∀ (κ : Cardinal.{0}),
    Cardinal.aleph0 < κ →
      ∃ μ,
        ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V),
          μ ≤ G.chromaticCardinal → ∃ H, H.coe.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.coe.chromaticCardinal = κ) →
  ∀ (κ : Cardinal.{0}),
    Cardinal.aleph0 < κ →
      ∃ μ,
        ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V),
          G.chromaticCardinal = μ → ∃ H, H.coe.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.coe.chromaticCardinal = κ

declarations.docstring:
**Shelah's consistency result**: it is consistent with ZFC that there exists a graph $G$ with
chromatic number $\aleph_1$ such that every triangle-free subgraph of $G$ has chromatic number
strictly less than $\aleph_1$.

This shows that a negative answer to Problem 1175 (with $\kappa = \lambda = \aleph_1$) is
consistent, so the main statement `erdos_1175` is not provable in ZFC.

**Formalization caveat (consistency placeholder).** Shelah's result is a *consistency*
statement — it asserts the existence of a model of ZFC, not a ZFC theorem. Lean operates
inside a single (fixed) model of its set theory, so we cannot directly express "consistent
with ZFC" without leaving ZFC. Rather than pretend that Shelah's theorem is a bare ZFC
negation, we record it here as an explicit `answer(sorry)` consistency placeholder: the
intended conjecture is the model-theoretic statement, and any concrete formalisation must
either appeal to an explicit extra axiom (such as Shelah's specific forcing extension)
or to a meta-theoretic consistency proof. Until such a wrapper exists in `FormalConjectures`,
we leave the body as `sorry`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1175](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1175)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ¬∀ (V : Type u_1) (G : SimpleGraph V),
      G.chromaticCardinal = Cardinal.aleph 1 → ∃ H, H.coe.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.coe.chromaticCardinal = Cardinal.aleph 1

declarations.docstring:
**Threshold reformulation variant.** Replaces `chromaticCardinal = λ` in the hypothesis
of `erdos_1175` with `λ ≤ chromaticCardinal` (a graph of chromatic number ≥ λ has a
triangle-free subgraph of chromatic number κ). This is a strengthening of `erdos_1175`
(see `erdos_1175.test.threshold_implies_exact`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/1175](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1175)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (κ : Cardinal.{u_1}),
    Cardinal.aleph0 < κ →
      ∃ μ,
        ∀ (V : Type u_1) (G : SimpleGraph V),
          μ ≤ G.chromaticCardinal → ∃ H, H.coe.CliqueFree 3 ∧ H.coe.chromaticCardinal = κ

declarations.docstring:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$. Is it true that there is a colouring of the
edges with $\aleph_1$ many colours such that, in any countable colouring of the vertices, there
exists a vertex colour containing all edge colours?

A problem of Erdős, Galvin, and Hajnal. The consistency of this was proved by Hajnal and Komjáth.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1176](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1176)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {V : Type u_1} (G : SimpleGraph V),
  G.chromaticCardinal = Cardinal.aleph 1 →
    ∃ EColor,
      ∃ (_ : Cardinal.mk EColor = Cardinal.aleph 1),
        ∃ c_edge,
          ∀ (VColor : Type),
            Cardinal.mk VColor ≤ Cardinal.aleph 0 →
              ∀ (c_vert : V → VColor),
                ∃ vc,
                  ∀ (ec : EColor), ∃ u v, ∃ (h : G.Adj u v), c_vert u = vc ∧ c_vert v = vc ∧ c_edge ⟨s(u, v), h⟩ = ec

declarations.docstring:
For $r\geq 3$ let $d_r(e)$ be the minimal $d$ such that
$$\mathrm{ex}_r(n,\mathcal{F})=o(n^2),$$
where $\mathcal{F}$ is the family of $r$-uniform hypergraphs on $d$ vertices with $e$ edges. Prove
that
$$d_r(e)=(r-2)e+3$$
for all $r,e\geq 3$.

declarations.docstring:
Let $\epsilon>0$. Does there exist a constant $C_\epsilon$ such that, for all primes $p$, every
residue modulo $p$ is the sum of at most $C_\epsilon$ many elements of
$$\{ n^{-1} : 1\leq n\leq p^\epsilon\}$$
where $n^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $n$ modulo $p$?

The original question was answered in the affirmative by Shparlinski [Sh02], who proved that
$\ll \epsilon^{-3}$ summands suffice for all sufficiently large primes. This was improved to
$\ll \epsilon^{-2}$ by Glibichuk [Gl06]. It is trivial that at least $\gg \epsilon^{-1}$
summands are required, and it may be that $C_\epsilon\leq \epsilon^{-1-o(1)}$ is possible.

See also [540](https://www.erdosproblems.com/540).
references: [erdosproblems.com/1180](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1180)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh02] Shparlinski, Igor E., *On a question of Erdős and Graham*. Arch. Math. (Basel) (2002), 445-448.
[Gl06] Glibichuk, A. A., *Combinatorial properties of sets of residues modulo a prime and the Erdős-Graham problem*. Mat. Zametki (2006), 384-395.

declarations.docstring:
Let $\delta_k$ be such that in any $2$-colouring of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ there exist at least
$(\delta_k+o(1))n^2$ many monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progressions. Give reasonable bounds
(or even an asymptotic formula) for $\delta_k$.

We read "reasonable bounds" as determining the order of magnitude of $\delta_k$ as $k \to \infty$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1186](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1186)

[PRS08] Parrilo, Pablo A. and Robertson, Aaron and Saracino, Dan, *On the asymptotic minimum number of monochromatic 3-term arithmetic progressions*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2008), 185-192. [arXiv:math/0609532](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0609532)

declarations.docstring:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ a covering set if there is a choice of
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of these
congruences. A set is an irreducible covering set if no proper subset is a covering set.

How many irreducible covering sets of size $k$ are there?

This is the first part of the questions of Erdős [Er80, p. 95]. We read "how many" as asking for
the asymptotics of $\log I(k)$, where $I(k)$ is the number of irreducible covering sets of size
$k$; this is the scale on which the number of minimal covering systems is known [BBMST24].
references: [erdosproblems.com/1189](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1189)
[Er80] Erdős, P., *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)
[Si85] Simpson, R. J., *Regular coverings of the integers by arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. 45 (1985), 145-152.
[Su07] Sun, Z.-W., *On covering numbers*. Combinatorial Number Theory, de Gruyter (2007), 443-453. [arXiv:math/0601017](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601017)

[BBMST24] Balister, P., Bollobás, B., Morris, R., Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., *The structure and number of Erdős covering systems*. J. Eur. Math. Soc. 26 (2024), 75-109. [arXiv:1904.04806](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04806)
declarations.type_pretty:
Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun k => Real.log ↑(Erdos1189.irreducibleCount k))
  Erdos1189.erdos_1189.parts.i.answer

declarations.docstring:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ a covering set if there is a choice of
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of these
congruences. A set is an irreducible covering set if no proper subset is a covering set.

What is the minimum and maximum that $n_k$ can be?

This is the second part. Here $n_k$ is the largest element of an irreducible covering set of
size $k$. The answer is a pair (minimum, maximum), stated for each $k$ for which an irreducible
covering set of size $k$ exists.

∀ (k : ℕ),
  (∃ M, Erdos1189.IsIrreducibleCoveringSet M ∧ M.card = k) →

declarations.docstring:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ a covering set if there is a choice of
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of these
congruences. A set is an irreducible covering set if no proper subset is a covering set.

Determine or estimate $\max \sum\frac{1}{n_i}$, where the maximum ranges over all irreducible
covering sets of size $k$.

This is the third part. We read "determine or estimate" as an estimate up to constant factors.
In [Er80, p. 95] the maximum is taken over the irreducible covering sets
$1<n_1<\cdots<n_k\leq x$, as a function of $x$; we follow the problem page, which takes it over
the irreducible covering sets of size $k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1189](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1189)
[Er80] Erdős, P., *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)
[Si85] Simpson, R. J., *Regular coverings of the integers by arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. 45 (1985), 145-152.
[Su07] Sun, Z.-W., *On covering numbers*. Combinatorial Number Theory, de Gruyter (2007), 443-453. [arXiv:math/0601017](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601017)

[BBMST24] Balister, P., Bollobás, B., Morris, R., Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., *The structure and number of Erdős covering systems*. J. Eur. Math. Soc. 26 (2024), 75-109. [arXiv:1904.04806](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04806)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos1189.maxReciprocalSum =Θ[Filter.atTop] Erdos1189.erdos_1189.parts.iii.answer

declarations.docstring:
Call a set of distinct integers $1<n_1<\cdots<n_k$ a covering set if there is a choice of
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ such that every integer satisfies at least one of these
congruences. A set is an irreducible covering set if no proper subset is a covering set.

Are there infinitely many $n$ such that the divisors of $n$ (which are $>1$) form an irreducible
covering set?

This is the fourth part. Sun [Su07, Theorem 1.4(i) and Corollary 1.3] proved that the answer is
yes: see `erdos_1189.variants.sun`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1189](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1189)
[Er80] Erdős, P., *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)
[Si85] Simpson, R. J., *Regular coverings of the integers by arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. 45 (1985), 145-152.
[Su07] Sun, Z.-W., *On covering numbers*. Combinatorial Number Theory, de Gruyter (2007), 443-453. [arXiv:math/0601017](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601017)

[BBMST24] Balister, P., Bollobás, B., Morris, R., Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., *The structure and number of Erdős covering systems*. J. Eur. Math. Soc. 26 (2024), 75-109. [arXiv:1904.04806](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04806)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | Erdos1189.IsIrreducibleCoveringSet ({x ∈ n.divisors | 1 < x})}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Let $I(k)$ count the number of irreducible covering sets of size $k$. Balister, Bollobás, Morris,
Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba [BBMST24] proved that
$$I(k) \leq \exp\left((c+o(1))\frac{k^{3/2}}{(\log k)^{1/2}}\right)$$
by proving that the right-hand side is an asymptotic for the number of minimal covering systems
on $k$ moduli.

Here $c = 4\sqrt{\tau}/3$ [BBMST24, Theorem 1.1]. The bound for $I(k)$ follows because each
irreducible covering set is the set of moduli of a minimal covering system. The $o(1)$ is stated
with an arbitrary $\varepsilon > 0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1189](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1189)
[Er80] Erdős, P., *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)
[Si85] Simpson, R. J., *Regular coverings of the integers by arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. 45 (1985), 145-152.
[Su07] Sun, Z.-W., *On covering numbers*. Combinatorial Number Theory, de Gruyter (2007), 443-453. [arXiv:math/0601017](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601017)

[BBMST24] Balister, P., Bollobás, B., Morris, R., Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., *The structure and number of Erdős covering systems*. J. Eur. Math. Soc. 26 (2024), 75-109. [arXiv:1904.04806](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04806)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (ε : ℝ),
  0 < ε →
    ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ↑(Erdos1189.irreducibleCount k) ≤ Real.exp ((4 * √Erdos1189.bbmstTau / 3 + ε) * (↑k ^ (3 / 2) / √(Real.log ↑k)))

declarations.docstring:
Simpson [Si85] proved $n_k\leq 2^{k-1}$.

Here $n_k$ is the largest element of an irreducible covering set of size $k$. The bound follows
from Simpson's theorem [Si85] (see [BBMST24, Theorem 2.4]), as stated in [BBMST24, Section 1].
references: [erdosproblems.com/1189](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1189)
[Er80] Erdős, P., *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)
[Si85] Simpson, R. J., *Regular coverings of the integers by arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. 45 (1985), 145-152.
[Su07] Sun, Z.-W., *On covering numbers*. Combinatorial Number Theory, de Gruyter (2007), 443-453. [arXiv:math/0601017](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601017)

[BBMST24] Balister, P., Bollobás, B., Morris, R., Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., *The structure and number of Erdős covering systems*. J. Eur. Math. Soc. 26 (2024), 75-109. [arXiv:1904.04806](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04806)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (M : Finset ℕ), Erdos1189.IsIrreducibleCoveringSet M → ∀ n ∈ M, n ≤ 2 ^ (M.card - 1)

declarations.docstring:
The divisors of $12$ (which are $>1$) are an example of an irreducible covering set. Sun [Su07]
proved more generally that, for any odd prime $p$, the divisors (which are $>1$) of $2^{p-1}p$
form an irreducible covering set, settling the final question.

That $n=12$ is an example is already noted in [Er80, p. 95].
references: [erdosproblems.com/1189](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1189)
[Er80] Erdős, P., *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)
[Si85] Simpson, R. J., *Regular coverings of the integers by arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. 45 (1985), 145-152.
[Su07] Sun, Z.-W., *On covering numbers*. Combinatorial Number Theory, de Gruyter (2007), 443-453. [arXiv:math/0601017](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601017)

[BBMST24] Balister, P., Bollobás, B., Morris, R., Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., *The structure and number of Erdős covering systems*. J. Eur. Math. Soc. 26 (2024), 75-109. [arXiv:1904.04806](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04806)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → Odd p → Erdos1189.IsIrreducibleCoveringSet ({x ∈ (2 ^ (p - 1) * p).divisors | 1 < x})

declarations.docstring: The empty set is not a covering set, since the integer `0` satisfies no congruence.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1189](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1189)
[Er80] Erdős, P., *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89-115. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf)
[Si85] Simpson, R. J., *Regular coverings of the integers by arithmetic progressions*. Acta Arith. 45 (1985), 145-152.
[Su07] Sun, Z.-W., *On covering numbers*. Combinatorial Number Theory, de Gruyter (2007), 443-453. [arXiv:math/0601017](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0601017)

[BBMST24] Balister, P., Bollobás, B., Morris, R., Sahasrabudhe, J. and Tiba, M., *The structure and number of Erdős covering systems*. J. Eur. Math. Soc. 26 (2024), 75-109. [arXiv:1904.04806](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.04806)
declarations.type_pretty: ¬Erdos1189.IsCoveringSet ∅

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ be an infinite Sidon set. Is it true that
$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^{1/2}=0?$$

Here $x$ runs over $\mathbb{N}$ and the $\liminf$ is taken in `ℝ≥0∞`, so that it is $\infty$
rather than $0$ when the sequence tends to infinity.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1191](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1191)
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.
[HaRo66] Halberstam, H. and Roth, K. F., *Sequences. Vol. I*. (1966), xx+291.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (A : Set ℕ),
  A.Infinite →
    IsSidon A →
      Filter.liminf (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x).ncard / ↑x ^ (1 / 2) * Real.log ↑x ^ (1 / 2)))
          Filter.atTop =
        0

declarations.docstring:
Does there exist an infinite Sidon set $A$ such that
$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^c>0$$
for some $c>0$?

A positive answer would also give a positive answer to Erdős Problem 39.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1191](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1191)
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.
[HaRo66] Halberstam, H. and Roth, K. F., *Sequences. Vol. I*. (1966), xx+291.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ A,
  A.Infinite ∧
    IsSidon A ∧
      ∃ c > 0,
        0 <
          Filter.liminf (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x).ncard / ↑x ^ (1 / 2) * Real.log ↑x ^ c))
            Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Erdős proved (see for example [HaRo66]) that if $A$ is an infinite Sidon set then
$$\liminf_{x\to \infty} \frac{\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert}{x^{1/2}}(\log x)^{1/2}\leq c$$
for some constant $c>0$. See also `erdos_158.variants.isSidon'`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1191](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1191)
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.
[HaRo66] Halberstam, H. and Roth, K. F., *Sequences. Vol. I*. (1966), xx+291.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {A : Set ℕ},
  A.Infinite →
    IsSidon A →
      ∃ c > 0,
        Filter.liminf (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x).ncard / ↑x ^ (1 / 2) * Real.log ↑x ^ (1 / 2)))
            Filter.atTop ≤
          ENNReal.ofReal c

declarations.docstring:
Does there exist, for all $r\geq 2$, a basis $A$ of order $r$ (so that $f_r(n)>0$ for all
large $n$) such that $$\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x$$ for all $x$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/1192](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1192)
[Ru90] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A just basis. Monatsh. Math. (1990), 145--151.
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89--115.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ r ≥ 2,
    ∃ A,
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos1192.f_r A r n > 0) ∧
        (fun x => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (x + 1), ↑(Erdos1192.f_r A r n) ^ 2) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑x

declarations.docstring: With an empty set, there are no valid $r$-tuples for $r \geq 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1192](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1192)
[Ru90] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A just basis. Monatsh. Math. (1990), 145--151.
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89--115.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (r n : ℕ), Erdos1192.f_r ∅ (r + 1) n = 0

declarations.docstring: $f_1(\{0\}, 1) = 0$: can't represent $1$ with a single element from $\{0\}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1192](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1192)
[Ru90] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A just basis. Monatsh. Math. (1990), 145--151.
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89--115.

declarations.docstring: For $r = 1$, $f_1(\{n\}, n) = 1$: the only $1$-tuple from $\{n\}$ summing to $n$ is $(n)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1192](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1192)
[Ru90] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A just basis. Monatsh. Math. (1990), 145--151.
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89--115.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), Erdos1192.f_r {n} 1 n = 1

declarations.docstring: The empty sum ($r = 0$) gives exactly one representation of $0$: the empty tuple.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1192](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1192)
[Ru90] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A just basis. Monatsh. Math. (1990), 145--151.
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89--115.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (A : Set ℕ), Erdos1192.f_r A 0 0 = 1

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Rényi proved by the probabilistic method that there exists a set $A$ such that
$$\sum_{n\leq x}f_r(n)^2 \ll x$$ and $$\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert\gg x^{1/r}$$ for all $x$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1192](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1192)
[Ru90] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A just basis. Monatsh. Math. (1990), 145--151.
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89--115.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ r ≥ 2,
  ∃ A,
    ((fun x => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (x + 1), ↑(Erdos1192.f_r A r n) ^ 2) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑x) ∧
      (fun x => ↑x ^ (1 / ↑r)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑(Nat.count (fun x => x ∈ A) x)

declarations.docstring: Ruzsa [Ru90] proved that the answer is yes for $r=2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1192](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1192)
[Ru90] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A just basis. Monatsh. Math. (1990), 145--151.
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math. 6 (1980), 89--115.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ A,
  (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos1192.f_r A 2 n > 0) ∧
    (fun x => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (x + 1), ↑(Erdos1192.f_r A 2 n) ^ 2) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑x

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that in any 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exists an infinite set $A$
such that all elements of $A+A$ are the same colour?

A conjecture of Owings [Ow74].
references: [erdosproblems.com/1199](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1199)
[Hi79] Hindman, Neil, Partitions and sums of integers with repetition. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1979), 19--32.
[Ow74] J. Owings, E2494. Amer. Math. Monthly (1974), 902.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (color : ℕ → Fin 2), ∃ A, A.Infinite ∧ ∀ n ∈ A + A, ∀ m ∈ A + A, color n = color m

declarations.docstring: Hindman [Hi79] has shown that this is false for 3-colourings.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1199](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1199)
[Hi79] Hindman, Neil, Partitions and sums of integers with repetition. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1979), 19--32.
[Ow74] J. Owings, E2494. Amer. Math. Monthly (1974), 902.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ color, ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.Infinite → ∃ n ∈ A + A, ∃ m ∈ A + A, color n ≠ color m

declarations.docstring:
Let $A$ be an infinite set such that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$
such that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$. Is there such an $A$ with
$\liminf \frac{|A \cap \{1, \dotsc, N\}|}{N^{1/2}} > 0$ ?

The DeepMind prover agent has found a formal proof of this statement.
references: [erdosproblems.com/12](https://www.erdosproblems.com/12)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ A, Erdos12.IsGood A ∧ 0 < Filter.liminf (fun N => ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 N).ncard / √↑N) Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Let $A$ be an infinite set such that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$
such that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$. Does there exist some absolute constant $c > 0$
such that there are always infinitely many $N$
with $|A \cap \{1, \dotsc, N\}| < N^{1−c}$?

The DeepMind prover agent has found a formal disproof of this statement.
references: [erdosproblems.com/12](https://www.erdosproblems.com/12)
declarations.type_pretty: ¬∃ c > 0, ∀ (A : Set ℕ), Erdos12.IsGood A → {N | ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 N).ncard < ↑N ^ (1 - c)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Let $A$ be an infinite set such that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$
such that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$. Is it true that $∑_{n \in A} \frac{1}{n} < \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/12](https://www.erdosproblems.com/12)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (A : Set ℕ), Erdos12.IsGood A → Summable fun n => 1 / ↑↑n

declarations.docstring:
Let $A$ be a set of natural numbers with the property that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$ such
that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$. If all elements in $A$ are pairwise coprime then
$$\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \ll N^{2/3}/\log N$$
for infinitely many $N$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/12](https://www.erdosproblems.com/12)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (A : Set ℕ),
  Erdos12.IsGood A →
    A.Pairwise Nat.Coprime → ∃ C > 0, {N | ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 N).ncard ≤ C * ↑N ^ (2 / 3) / Real.log ↑N}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Given any function $f(x)\to \infty$ as $x\to \infty$ there exists a set $A$ with the property
that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$ such that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$, such that there are
infinitely many $N$ such that $$\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert > \frac{N}{f(N)}.
references: [erdosproblems.com/12](https://www.erdosproblems.com/12)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ),
  Filter.Tendsto f Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    ∃ A, Erdos12.IsGood A ∧ {N | ↑N / ↑(f N) < ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 N).ncard}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Sárközy proved that such an $A$ must have density 0.
[ErSa70] Erd\H os, P. and Sárk\"ozi, A., On the divisibility properties of sequences of integers.
    Proc. London Math. Soc. (3) (1970), 97-101
references: [erdosproblems.com/12](https://www.erdosproblems.com/12)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (A : Set ℕ), Erdos12.IsGood A → A.HasDensity 0

declarations.docstring:
An example of an $A$ with the property that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$ such that
$a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$ and such that
$$\liminf \frac{\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert}{N^{1/2}}\log N > 0$$
is given by the set of $p^2$, where $p\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is prime.
references: [erdosproblems.com/12](https://www.erdosproblems.com/12)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (A : Set ℕ),
  A = {x | ∃ p, ∃ (_ : Nat.Prime p) (_ : p ≡ 3 [MOD 4]), p ^ 2 = x} →
    Erdos12.IsGood A ∧ 0 < Filter.liminf (fun N => ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 N).ncard * Real.log ↑N / √↑N) Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Let $A$ be a set of natural numbers with the property that there are no distinct $a,b,c \in A$ such
that $a \mid (b+c)$ and $b,c > a$. If all elements in $A$ are pairwise coprime then
$$\lvert A\cap\{1,\ldots,N\}\rvert \ll N^{2/3}$$
for infinitely many $N$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/12](https://www.erdosproblems.com/12)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (A : Set ℕ),
  Erdos12.IsGood A → A.Pairwise Nat.Coprime → ∃ C > 0, {N | ↑(A ∩ Set.Icc 1 N).ncard ≤ C * ↑N ^ (2 / 3)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
The set of $p ^ 2$ where $p \cong 3 \mod 4$ is prime is an example of a good set.
Formal proof provided by AlphaProof
references: [erdosproblems.com/12](https://www.erdosproblems.com/12)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos12.IsGood {x | ∃ p, ∃ (_ : p ≡ 3 [MOD 4]) (_ : Nat.Prime p), p ^ 2 = x}

declarations.docstring:
Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be an infinite set. Must there be a set $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$
of positive measure which does not contain any set of the shape $a * A + b$
for some $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $a \neq 0$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/120](https://www.erdosproblems.com/120)
[St20](http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/fm/fm1/fm1111.pdf) Steinhaus, Hugo, Sur les distances des points dans les ensembles de measure positive. Fund. Math. (1920), 93-104.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (A : Set ℝ), A.Infinite → Erdos120.Erdos120For A

declarations.docstring: Steinhaus [St20] has proved Erdős 120 to be false whenever $A$ is a finite set.
references: [erdosproblems.com/120](https://www.erdosproblems.com/120)
[St20](http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/fm/fm1/fm1111.pdf) Steinhaus, Hugo, Sur les distances des points dans les ensembles de measure positive. Fund. Math. (1920), 93-104.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {A : Set ℝ}, A.Finite → ¬Erdos120.Erdos120For A

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that for every $\epsilon,\eta>0$ there exists a $k$ such that the density of $n$
for which $P(n(n+1)\cdots(n+k))>n^{1-\epsilon}$ is at least $1-\eta$ (where $P(m)$ is the greatest
prime divisor of $m$)?
references: [erdosproblems.com/1201](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1201)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ ε > 0,
  ∀ η > 0,
    ∃ k, Filter.liminf (fun x => ↑↑(Nat.count (fun x => x ∈ Erdos1201.Erdos1201Set ε k) x) / ↑↑x) Filter.atTop ≥ 1 - η

declarations.docstring: Erdős wrote he could prove this for $\epsilon=1/2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/1201](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1201)
declarations.type_pretty:

congruence class modulo every prime $p$. Estimate

declarations.docstring:
Let $A=\{a_1<a_2<\cdots\}$ be a sequence of integers which tends to infinity sufficiently fast.
If there is an $n$ such that all $n+a_k$ are primes then must there exist infinitely many such $n$?

Erdős [Er80] wrote 'unless I overlook a trivial way of getting a counterexample these questions
are quite hopeless'. There is indeed a trivial counterexample (a variant of the construction in
[erdosproblems.com/429]): define $a_1=2$ and for $k\geq 2$ let $a_k>a_{k-1}$ be a prime such that
$a_k+k\equiv 0\pmod{q_k}$, where $q_k$ is some prime not dividing $k$. This sequence can be made to
grow arbitrarily fast

See also [erdosproblems.com/429] and [erdosproblems.com/1102].
references: [erdosproblems.com/429](https://www.erdosproblems.com/429)
[erdosproblems.com/1102](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1102)
[erdosproblems.com/1209](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1209)
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.
declarations.type_pretty:

  ∃ f,
    ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
      StrictMono a →
        (∀ (k : ℕ), f k ≤ a k) → (∃ n, ∀ (k : ℕ), Nat.Prime (n + a k)) → {n | ∀ (k : ℕ), Nat.Prime (n + a k)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Are there $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is always a prime?

ebarschkis and GPT have proved that there are no $n$ such that $n+2^{2^k}$ is always prime: let
$n\geq 3$ be any odd integer. If $k$ is chosen sufficiently large, and $p=n+2^{2^{k}}$ is prime,
then the multiplicative order of $2^{2^k}\pmod{p}$, say $m$ is odd, and hence if $l$ is chosen such
that $2^l\equiv 1\pmod{m}$ then $p\mid n+2^{2^{k+rl}}$ for all $r\geq 1$.

This was formalized in Lean by Barschkis using ChatGPT.
references: [erdosproblems.com/429](https://www.erdosproblems.com/429)

[Er80] Erdős, Paul, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory. Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.

declarations.docstring:
Let $a, b, c$ be three integers which are pairwise coprime. Is every large integer
the sum of distinct integers of the form $a^k b^l c^m$ ($k, l, m ≥ 0$), none of which
divide any other?

Equivalently: is the set $\{a^k b^l c^m : k, l, m \geq 0\}$ d-complete?

Note: For this not to reduce to the two-integer case, we need the integers
to be greater than one and distinct.

The prize of \$250 is offered by Erdős in [Er97] and [Er97e] for a 'proof or disproof'.

The main problem was resolved in the affirmative by GPT 5.6 (prompted by Snyder).

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev.

[ChYu23b] Chen, Yong-Gao and Yu, Wang-Xing, On {$d$}-complete sequences of integers, {II}. Acta Arith. (2023), 161--181.
[Er92b] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics. Matematiche (Catania) (1992), 231-240.

  ∀ b > 1,
    ∀ c > 1,
      Erdos123.PairwiseCoprime a b c →
        Erdos123.IsDComplete (↑(Submonoid.powers a) * ↑(Submonoid.powers b) * ↑(Submonoid.powers c))

declarations.docstring:
A simpler case: the set of numbers of the form $2^k 3^l$ ($k, l ≥ 0$) is d-complete.

This was initially conjectured by Erdős in 1992, who called it a "nice and difficult"
problem, but it was quickly proven by Jansen and others using a simple inductive argument:
- If $n = 2m$ is even, apply the inductive hypothesis to $m$ and double all summands.
- If $n$ is odd, let $3^k$ be the largest power of $3$ with $3^k ≤ n$, and apply the
  inductive hypothesis to $n - 3^k$ (which is even).
references: [erdosproblems.com/123](https://www.erdosproblems.com/123)

$0, 1$ when written in base $d_i$. Then
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$

Can all sufficiently large integers be written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$
where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ is divisible by $d_i ^ k$ and has only the digits $0, 1$ when
written in base $d_i$?

declarations.docstring:
Let  $3 \le d_1 < d_2 < \dots < d_r$ be integers such that
$$\sum_{1 \le i \le r}\frac 1{d_i - 1} \ge 1.$$
Can all sufficiently large integers be written as a sum of the shape $\sum_i c_ia_i$
where $c_i \in \{0, 1\}$ and $a_i$ has only the digits $0, 1$ when written in base $d_i$?

Conjectured by Erdős [Er97], solved by Boris Alexeev using Aristotle.
references: [erdosproblems.com/124](https://www.erdosproblems.com/124)
[BEGL96] Burr, S. A. and Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Li, W. Wen-Ching, Complete sequences of sets of integer powers. Acta Arith. (1996), 133-138.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (D : Finset ℕ),
    (∀ d ∈ D, 3 ≤ d) →
      1 ≤ ∑ d ∈ D, (↑d - 1)⁻¹ → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, n ∈ ∑ d ∈ D, Erdos124.sumsOfDistinctPowers d 0

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ has $|A| = n$ then
$\prod_{a\neq b\in A}(a + b)$ has at least $f(n)$ distinct prime factors.
Is it true that $\frac{f(n)}{\log n} \to\infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/126](https://www.erdosproblems.com/126)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ),
    Erdos126.IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f → Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(f n) / Real.log ↑n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Turán proved [ErTu34] in their first joint paper that
$$
  \log n \ll f(n) \ll \frac{n}{\log n}
$$

[ErTu34] Erdős, Paul and Turan, Paul, _On a Problem in the Elementary Theory of Numbers_. Amer. Math. Monthly (1934), 608-611.
references: [erdosproblems.com/126](https://www.erdosproblems.com/126)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ),
  Erdos126.IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f →
    ((fun n => Real.log ↑n) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑(f n)) ∧
      (fun n => ↑(f n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n / Real.log ↑n

declarations.docstring: Erdős says that $f(n) = o(\frac{n}{\log n})$ has never been proved.
references: [erdosproblems.com/126](https://www.erdosproblems.com/126)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ), Erdos126.IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f → (fun n => ↑(f n)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n / Real.log ↑n

declarations.docstring:
Let G be a graph with n vertices such that every induced subgraph on ≥ $n/2$
vertices has more than $n^2/50$ edges. Must G contain a triangle?
references: [erdosproblems.com/128](https://www.erdosproblems.com/128)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
    (∀ (V' : Set V),
        2 * V'.ncard + 1 ≥ Fintype.card V → 50 * (SimpleGraph.induce V' G).edgeSet.ncard > Fintype.card V ^ 2) →
      ¬G.CliqueFree 3

declarations.docstring:
If $A \subseteq \{1, ..., N\}$ is a set with no $a, b, c \in A$ such that $a | (b+c)$ and
$a < \min(b,c)$, then $|A| \le N/3 + O(1)$. This has been solved by Bedert [Be23].

[Be23] Bedert, B., _On a problem of Erdős and Sárközy about sequences with no term dividing
the sum of two larger terms_. arXiv:2301.07065 (2023).
references: [erdosproblems.com/13](https://www.erdosproblems.com/13)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C, ∀ (N : ℕ), ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, Erdos13.IsForbiddenTripleFree A → ↑A.card ≤ ↑N / 3 + C

declarations.docstring:
A general version asks, for a fixed $r \in \mathbb{N}$, if a set
$A \subseteq \{1, ..., N\}$ has no $a \in A$ and $b_1, ..., b_r \in A$ such that
$a | (b_1 + ... + b_r)$ and $a < \min(b_1, ..., b_r)$, then is it true that
$|A| \le N/(r+1) + O(1)$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/13](https://www.erdosproblems.com/13)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  ∃ C,
    ∀ (N : ℕ),
      ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N,
        (∀ a ∈ A, ∀ (b : Fin r → ℕ), (∀ (i : Fin r), b i ∈ A) → (∀ (i : Fin r), a < b i) → ¬a ∣ ∑ i, b i) →
          ↑A.card ≤ ↑N / (↑r + 1) + C

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that every triangle-free graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and diameter
$2$ contains a vertex with degree $\geq f(n)$. What is the order of growth of $f(n)$? Does
$f(n)/\sqrt{n}\to \infty$?

Asked by Erdős and Pach. The lower bound $f(n)\geq (1-o(1))\sqrt{n}$ follows from the fact that
a graph with maximum degree $d$ and diameter $2$ has at most $1+d+d(d-1)=d^2+1$ many vertices.

Hanson and Seyffarth [HaSe84] proved that $f(n)\leq (\sqrt{2}+o(1))\sqrt{n}$ using a Cayley graph
on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, with the generating set given by some symmetric complete sum-free set
of size $\sim \sqrt{n}$. An alternative construction of such a complete sum-free set was given by
Haviv and Levy [HaLe18]. Füredi and Seress [FuSe94] proved that
$f(n)\leq (\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+o(1))\sqrt{n}$. In particular $f(n)/\sqrt{n}\not\to\infty$.

The precise asymptotics of $f(n)$ are unknown; Alon believes that the truth is $f(n)\sim \sqrt{n}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/133](https://www.erdosproblems.com/133)
[Er97b] Erdős, Paul, *Some old and new problems in various branches of combinatorics*. Discrete Math. (1997), 227-231.
[HaSe84] Hanson, D. and Seyffarth, K., *$k$-saturated graphs of prescribed maximum degree*. Congr. Numer. (1984), 169-182.
[FuSe94] Füredi, Zoltán and Seress, Ákos, *Maximal triangle-free graphs with restrictions on the degrees*. J. Graph Theory (1994), 11-24.
[HaLe18] Haviv, Ishay and Levy, Dan, *Symmetric complete sum-free sets in cyclic groups*. Israel J. Math. (2018), 931-956.
declarations.type_pretty: ¬Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos133.f n) / √↑n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Let $k\geq 3$. Can the product of any $k$ consecutive integers $N$ ever be powerful? That is,
must there always exist a prime $p\mid N$ such that $p^2\nmid N$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/137](https://www.erdosproblems.com/137)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 3, ∀ (n : ℕ), ¬(∏ x ∈ Finset.Ioc n (n + k), x).Powerful

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er82c] conjectures that, if $k$ is fixed, then for all $n$ sufficiently large and all
positive integers $m$, there must be at least $k$ distinct primes $p$ such that
$p\mid m(m+1)\cdots (m+n)$ and yet $p^2$ does not divide the right hand side.

[Er82c] Erdős, Paul, "Miscellaneous problems in number theory". Congr. Numer. (1982), 25-45.,
references: [erdosproblems.com/137](https://www.erdosproblems.com/137)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (m : ℕ),
      0 < m →
        ∃ P,
          P.card = k ∧ ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p ∧ p ∣ ∏ x ∈ Finset.Icc m (m + n), x ∧ ¬p ^ 2 ∣ ∏ x ∈ Finset.Icc m (m + n), x

declarations.docstring:
Let $k\geq 2$. Erdős and Selfridge [ES75] proved that the product of any $k$ consecutive
integers $N$ cannot be a perfect power.

[ES75] P. Erdös, J. L. Selfridge, "The product of consecutive integers is never a power",
  Illinois J. Math. 19(2): 292-301, 1975
references: [erdosproblems.com/137](https://www.erdosproblems.com/137)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ k ≥ 2, ∀ (n x l : ℕ), 2 ≤ l → ∏ x ∈ Finset.Ioc n (n + k), x ≠ x ^ l

declarations.docstring:
In [Er80] Erdős asks whether
$$ \lim_{k \to \infty} (W(k))^{1/k} = \infty $$

Yes. This was proved by an internal OpenAI model in September 2026 [OAI26], which shows
$W(k) > k^{k/100000}$ for all large $k$; see the linked Lean proof.
references: [erdosproblems.com/138](https://www.erdosproblems.com/138)

In [Er80] Erdős asks whether $W(k)/2^k\to \infty$.

Campos, Fox and Schildkraut [CFS26] independently prove $W(k) \geq (1 - o(1)) k 2^{k-1}$, which
implies this; they report that their proof was generated with ChatGPT. (The related variant
`erdos_138.variants.difference`, $W(k+1) - W(k) \to \infty$, was solved separately in
[arxiv/2605.22763].)

[facebookresearch/atlas-lean](https://github.com/facebookresearch/atlas-lean), is linked in
`formal_proof`.

declarations.docstring:
If $H$ is bipartite with minimum degree $r$ then there exists $\epsilon=\epsilon(H)>0$ such that
$$\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \gg n^{2-\frac{1}{r-1}+\epsilon}.$$

Conjectured by Erdős and Simonovits [ErSi84]. A probabilistic argument shows that there exists
some $\epsilon=\epsilon(H)>0$ such that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \gg n^{2-\frac{2}{r}+\epsilon}$.

This conjecture was disproved by Janzer [Ja23] for even $r\geq 4$. The case $r=3$ was disproved
by Janzer [Ja23b], who constructed, for any $\epsilon>0$, a $3$-regular bipartite graph $H$ such
that $\mathrm{ex}(n;H)\ll n^{\frac{4}{3}+\epsilon}$.

In [Ja23] Janzer conjectures that the above lower bound is sharp, in that for any $r\geq 3$ and
$\epsilon>0$ there exists an $r$-regular graph $H$ such that
$\mathrm{ex}(n;H) \ll n^{2-\frac{2}{r}+\epsilon}$. Janzer's result proves this for even
$r\geq 4$.

See also [113](https://www.erdosproblems.com/113), [146](https://www.erdosproblems.com/146), and
[714](https://www.erdosproblems.com/714).

The conjecture is stated for minimum degree $r \geq 2$ (for $r = 1$ the exponent
$2 - \frac{1}{r-1}$ is not meaningful).
references: [erdosproblems.com/147](https://www.erdosproblems.com/147)
[ErSi84] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Cube-supersaturated graphs and related problems*. Progress in graph theory (Waterloo, Ont., 1982) (1984), 203-218.
[Er93] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite solved and unsolved problems in graph theory*. Quaestiones Math. (1993), 333-350.
[Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul Erdős, I (1997), 47-67.
[Ja23] Janzer, Oliver, *Rainbow Turán number of even cycles, repeated patterns and blow-ups of cycles*. Israel J. Math. (2023), 813--840.
[Ja23b] Janzer, Oliver, *Disproof of a conjecture of Erdős and Simonovits on the Turán number of graphs with minimum degree 3*. Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN (2023), 8478--8494.
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] [Nonempty V] (H : SimpleGraph V) [inst_2 : DecidableRel H.Adj],
    H.IsBipartite →
      2 ≤ H.minDegree →
        ∃ ε,
          0 < ε ∧
            (fun n => ↑n ^ (2 - 1 / (↑H.minDegree - 1) + ε)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑(SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n H)

declarations.docstring:
The current best bounds known are
$$2^{c^{\frac{k}{\log k}}}\leq F(k) \leq c_0^{(\frac{1}{5}+o(1))2^k},$$
where $c>0$ is some absolute constant and $c_0=1.5979102\ldots$ is the square of the 'Vardi
constant' $1.26408\cdots$. The lower bound is due to Konyagin [Ko14] and the upper bound to
Elsholtz and Planitzer [ElPl21]. (erdosproblems.com gives $c_0=1.26408\cdots$;
[ElPl21, Remark 3] gives $c_0=1.5979102\ldots$.)

[Ko14, Theorem 1] states the lower bound in the explicit form
$$F(k) \geq \exp\left(\exp\left(\left(\frac{(\log 2)(\log 3)}{3}+o(1)\right)
\frac{k}{\log k}\right)\right) \quad (k \to \infty),$$
which is the statement formalised here.
references: [erdosproblems.com/148](https://www.erdosproblems.com/148)
[ElPl21] Elsholtz, Christian and Planitzer, Stefan, *Sums of four and more unit fractions and approximate parametrizations*. Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. (2021), 695-709.
[Ko14] Konyagin, S. V., *Double exponential lower bound for the number of representations of unity by Egyptian fractions*. Math. Notes (2014), 277-281.
[OEIS A006585](https://oeis.org/A006585)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ o,
  o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧
    ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      Real.exp (Real.exp ((Real.log 2 * Real.log 3 / 3 + o k) * (↑k / Real.log ↑k))) ≤ ↑(Erdos148.F k)

declarations.docstring:
The current best bounds known are
$$2^{c^{\frac{k}{\log k}}}\leq F(k) \leq c_0^{(\frac{1}{5}+o(1))2^k},$$
where $c>0$ is some absolute constant and $c_0=1.5979102\ldots$ is the square of the 'Vardi
constant' $1.26408\cdots$. The lower bound is due to Konyagin [Ko14] and the upper bound to
Elsholtz and Planitzer [ElPl21]. (erdosproblems.com gives $c_0=1.26408\cdots$;
[ElPl21, Remark 3] gives $c_0=1.5979102\ldots$.)

[ElPl21, Corollary 3(2)] shows that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all $k \geq k(\varepsilon)$,
the number $f_k(1,1) \geq F(k)$ of solutions with $n_1 \leq \cdots \leq n_k$ is less than
$c_0^{(\frac{2}{5}+\varepsilon)2^{k-1}} = c_0^{(\frac{1}{5}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2})2^k}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/148](https://www.erdosproblems.com/148)
[ElPl21] Elsholtz, Christian and Planitzer, Stefan, *Sums of four and more unit fractions and approximate parametrizations*. Bull. Lond. Math. Soc. (2021), 695-709.
[Ko14] Konyagin, S. V., *Double exponential lower bound for the number of representations of unity by Egyptian fractions*. Math. Notes (2014), 277-281.
[OEIS A006585](https://oeis.org/A006585)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ o, o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos148.F k) ≤ Erdos148.c₀ ^ ((1 / 5 + o k) * 2 ^ k)

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that $\sum_{n=1}^\infty(-1)^n\frac{n}{p_n}$ converges,
where $p_n$ is the sequence of primes?

Note: In the problem statement, $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime, indexed such that $p_1=2, p_2=3, \ldots$.
We 0-index here to reflect how Nat.nth works.

Note: convergence here is convergence of the sequence of partial sums, which is what the
problem asks about. `Summable` would be the wrong notion: it is unconditional summability,
equivalent over $\mathbb{R}$ to absolute convergence, and $\sum_n n/p_n$ diverges.
references: [erdosproblems.com/15](https://www.erdosproblems.com/15)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ l,
  Filter.Tendsto (fun N => ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, (-1) ^ (k + 1) * (↑k + 1) / ↑(Nat.nth Nat.Prime k)) Filter.atTop
    (nhds l)

declarations.docstring:
For a graph $G$, let $\tau(G)$ denote the minimal number of vertices that include at least one
from each maximal clique of $G$ on at least two vertices. Let $H(n)$ be maximal such that every
triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices contains an independent set on $H(n)$ vertices.

If $G$ is a graph on $n$ vertices, is $\tau(G)\leq n-H(n)$?

Erdős remarked that this is perhaps completely wrongheaded [Er88].
references: [erdosproblems.com/151](https://www.erdosproblems.com/151)
[Er88] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and graph theory*. Discrete Math. (1988), 81-92.
[EGT92] Erdős, P. and Gallai, T. and Tuza, Zs., *Covering the cliques of a graph with vertices*. Discrete Math. (1992), 279-289.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), Erdos151.cliqueTransversalNumber G ≤ n - Erdos151.H n

declarations.docstring: Erdős and Gallai made no progress on the question even when $G$ is $K_4$-free [Er88].
references: [erdosproblems.com/151](https://www.erdosproblems.com/151)
[Er88] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and graph theory*. Discrete Math. (1988), 81-92.
[EGT92] Erdős, P. and Gallai, T. and Tuza, Zs., *Covering the cliques of a graph with vertices*. Discrete Math. (1992), 279-289.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G.CliqueFree 4 → Erdos151.cliqueTransversalNumber G ≤ n - Erdos151.H n

declarations.docstring:
If $G$ is triangle-free, then $\tau(G)\leq n-H(n)$: the complement of an independent set meets
every edge.
references: [erdosproblems.com/151](https://www.erdosproblems.com/151)
[Er88] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and graph theory*. Discrete Math. (1988), 81-92.
[EGT92] Erdős, P. and Gallai, T. and Tuza, Zs., *Covering the cliques of a graph with vertices*. Discrete Math. (1992), 279-289.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G.CliqueFree 3 → Erdos151.cliqueTransversalNumber G ≤ n - Erdos151.H n

declarations.docstring:
It is easy to see that $\tau(G)\leq n-\sqrt{n}$. We state this with $\lfloor\sqrt{n}\rfloor$:
with the real square root the bound fails for a single edge ($n = 2$, $\tau = 1$).
references: [erdosproblems.com/151](https://www.erdosproblems.com/151)
[Er88] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and graph theory*. Discrete Math. (1988), 81-92.
[EGT92] Erdős, P. and Gallai, T. and Tuza, Zs., *Covering the cliques of a graph with vertices*. Discrete Math. (1992), 279-289.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), Erdos151.cliqueTransversalNumber G ≤ n - n.sqrt

declarations.docstring:
Let $A$ be a finite Sidon set and $A+A=\{s_1<\cdots<s_t\}$. Is it true that
$$\frac{1}{t}\sum_{1\leq i<t}(s_{i+1}-s_i)^2 \to \infty$$
as $\lvert A\rvert\to \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/153](https://www.erdosproblems.com/153)
[ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number Theory (1994), 329-347.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Filter.Tendsto Erdos153.f Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that for every $k \geq 1$ we have
$$
F(N + k) \leq F(N) + 1
$$
for all sufficiently large $N$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/155](https://www.erdosproblems.com/155)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 1, ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos155.F (N + k) ≤ Erdos155.F N + 1

declarations.docstring:
Does there exist a maximal Sidon set $A\subset \{1,\ldots,N\}$ of size $O(N^{1/3})$?

A question of Erdős, Sárközy, and Sós [ESS94].
references: [erdosproblems.com/156](https://www.erdosproblems.com/156)
[ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number Theory (1994), 329-347.
[Ru98b] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A small maximal Sidon set. Ramanujan J. (1998), 55-58.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ (fun N => ↑(Erdos156.minMaximalSidonSet N)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑N ^ (1 / 3)

declarations.docstring:
It is easy to prove that the greedy construction of a maximal Sidon set in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has size
$\gg N^{1/3}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/156](https://www.erdosproblems.com/156)

declarations.docstring: Ruzsa [Ru98b] constructed a maximal Sidon set of size $\ll (N\log N)^{1/3}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/156](https://www.erdosproblems.com/156)
[ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number Theory (1994), 329-347.
[Ru98b] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A small maximal Sidon set. Ramanujan J. (1998), 55-58.
declarations.type_pretty: (fun N => ↑(Erdos156.minMaximalSidonSet N)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => (↑N * Real.log ↑N) ^ (1 / 3)

references: [erdosproblems.com/156](https://www.erdosproblems.com/156)
[ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number Theory (1994), 329-347.
[Ru98b] Ruzsa, Imre Z., A small maximal Sidon set. Ramanujan J. (1998), 55-58.

declarations.docstring: Let `A` be an infinite `B₂[2]` set. Must `liminf |A ∩ {1, ..., N}| * N ^ (- 1 / 2) = 0`?
references: [erdosproblems.com/158](https://www.erdosproblems.com/158)
[ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number Theory (1994), 329-347.

True ↔

    A.Infinite → Erdos158.B2 2 A → Filter.liminf (fun N => ↑(A ∩ Set.Iio N).ncard * ↑N ^ (-1 / 2)) Filter.atTop = 0

As a corollary of `erdos_158.isSidon'`, we can prove that
`liminf |A ∩ {1, ..., N}| * N ^ (- 1 / 2) = 0` for any infinite Sidon set `A`.

[ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number Theory (1994), 329-347.

declarations.docstring:
Let `A` be an infinite Sidon set. Then
`liminf |A ∩ {1, ..., N}| * N ^ (- 1 / 2) * (log N) ^ (1 / 2) < ∞`. This is proved in [ESS94].
references: [erdosproblems.com/158](https://www.erdosproblems.com/158)
[ESS94] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, A. and Sós, T., On Sum Sets of Sidon Sets, I. Journal of Number Theory (1994), 329-347.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {A : Set ℕ},
  A.Infinite →
    IsSidon A →
      Filter.liminf (fun N => ENNReal.ofReal (↑(A ∩ Set.Iio N).ncard * ↑N ^ (-1 / 2) * Real.log ↑N ^ (1 / 2)))
          Filter.atTop <
        ⊤

declarations.docstring:
There exists some constant $c>0$ such that
$$R(C_4,K_n) \ll n^{2-c}.$$

The prize of $100 is offered in [Er78] for a proof or disproof.

This problem is #17 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.

[Er78] Erdős, P., Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number theory. Proc. Ninth Southeastern Conf. Combinatorics, Graph Theory and Computing (1978), 29-40.
[Sp77] Spencer, J., Asymptotic lower bounds for Ramsey functions. Discrete Math. (1977), 69-76.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c,
  ∃ (_ : 0 < c),
    ∃ C,
      ∀ (n : ℕ),
        1 ≤ n → ↑((SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4).graphRamsey (SimpleGraph.completeGraph (Fin n))) ≤ C * ↑n ^ (2 - c)

declarations.docstring:
Let $\alpha\in[0,1/2)$ and $n,t\geq 1$. Let $F^{(t)}(n,\alpha)$ be the smallest $m$ such that we can
$2$-colour the edges of the complete $t$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices such that if $X\subseteq
[n]$ with $\lvert X\rvert \geq m$ then there are at least $\alpha \binom{\lvert X\rvert}{t}$ many
$t$-subsets of $X$ of each colour. For fixed $n,t$ as we change $\alpha$ from $0$ to $1/2$ does
$F^{(t)}(n,\alpha)$ increase continuously or are there jumps? Only one jump?

Here growth is compared up to constant factors as $n\to\infty$. At $\alpha=0$,
each color must occur, following the source's Ramsey convention.
references: [erdosproblems.com/161](https://www.erdosproblems.com/161)
[CFS11] Conlon, David and Fox, Jacob and Sudakov, Benny, Large almost monochromatic subsets in hypergraphs. Israel J. Math. (2011), 423--432.
[Er90b] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on graphs and hypergraphs: similarities and differences . Mathematics of Ramsey theory (1990), 12-28.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (t : ℕ),
  1 ≤ t →
    {p |
        p.1 ∈ Set.Ico 0 (1 / 2) ∧
          p.2 ∈ Set.Ico 0 (1 / 2) ∧
            (fun n => ↑(Hypergraph.balancedColoringThreshold n t p.1)) =Θ[Filter.atTop] fun n =>
              ↑(Hypergraph.balancedColoringThreshold n t p.2)} =
      Erdos161.erdos_161.parts.i.answer t

declarations.docstring: For fixed $t\geq 3$, do all positive densities below $1/2$ give the same asymptotic order?
references: [erdosproblems.com/161](https://www.erdosproblems.com/161)
[CFS11] Conlon, David and Fox, Jacob and Sudakov, Benny, Large almost monochromatic subsets in hypergraphs. Israel J. Math. (2011), 423--432.
[Er90b] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on graphs and hypergraphs: similarities and differences . Mathematics of Ramsey theory (1990), 12-28.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (t : ℕ),
  3 ≤ t →
    ∀ (α β : ℝ),
      0 < α →
        α < 1 / 2 →
          0 < β →
            β < 1 / 2 →
              (fun n => ↑(Hypergraph.balancedColoringThreshold n t α)) =Θ[Filter.atTop] fun n =>
                ↑(Hypergraph.balancedColoringThreshold n t β)

declarations.docstring: $F(n, \alpha)$ is at most `n + 1`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/162](https://www.erdosproblems.com/162)
[Er90b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on graphs and hypergraphs: similarities and differences*. Mathematics of Ramsey theory (1990), 12-28.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ) (α : ℝ), Erdos162.F n α ≤ n + 1

declarations.docstring:
Let $\alpha > 0$ and $n \geq 1$. Let $F(n,\alpha)$ be the largest $k$ such that there exists some
2-colouring of the edges of $K_n$ in which any induced subgraph $H$ on at least $k$ vertices
contains more than $\alpha\binom{|H|}{2}$ many edges of each colour.

Prove that for every fixed $0 \leq \alpha \leq 1/2$, as $n \to \infty$,
$F(n,\alpha) \sim c_\alpha \log n$ for some constant $c_\alpha$.

We require $\alpha < 1/2$: at $\alpha = 1/2$ no colouring works for any `k ≤ n`
(see `erdos_162.variants.half`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/162](https://www.erdosproblems.com/162)
[Er90b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on graphs and hypergraphs: similarities and differences*. Mathematics of Ramsey theory (1990), 12-28.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (α : ℝ),
  0 ≤ α → α < 1 / 2 → ∃ c, Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ↑(Erdos162.F n α)) fun n => c * Real.log ↑n

declarations.docstring:
It is easy to show with the probabilistic method that there exist $c_1(\alpha), c_2(\alpha)$ such
that $c_1(\alpha)\log n < F(n,\alpha) < c_2(\alpha)\log n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/162](https://www.erdosproblems.com/162)
[Er90b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on graphs and hypergraphs: similarities and differences*. Mathematics of Ramsey theory (1990), 12-28.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (α : ℝ),
  0 ≤ α →
    α < 1 / 2 →
      ∃ c₁ c₂,
        0 < c₁ ∧
          c₁ < c₂ ∧
            ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, c₁ * Real.log ↑n < ↑(Erdos162.F n α) ∧ ↑(Erdos162.F n α) < c₂ * Real.log ↑n

declarations.docstring:
At $\alpha = 1/2$ the two colour counts in $H$ add up to $\binom{|H|}{2}$, so both cannot exceed
half of it. Hence $F(n, 1/2) = n + 1$, and the claim fails at $\alpha = 1/2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/162](https://www.erdosproblems.com/162)
[Er90b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on graphs and hypergraphs: similarities and differences*. Mathematics of Ramsey theory (1990), 12-28.

declarations.docstring: `k = n + 1` always works, since no vertex set has more than `n` elements.
references: [erdosproblems.com/162](https://www.erdosproblems.com/162)
[Er90b] Erdős, Paul, *Problems and results on graphs and hypergraphs: similarities and differences*. Mathematics of Ramsey theory (1990), 12-28.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ) (α : ℝ) (c : Sym2 (Fin n) → Bool), Erdos162.IsBalancedAbove n α c (n + 1)

declarations.docstring:
Sanity check: if `S` is a maximal non ternary subset of `{1,..., N}` then `F N` is given by the
cardinality of `S`
references: [erdosproblems.com/168](https://www.erdosproblems.com/168)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (N : ℕ),
  ∀ S ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N,
    Erdos168.NonTernary S →
      (∀ T ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, Erdos168.NonTernary T → S.card ≤ T.card → T.card = S.card) → Erdos168.F N = S.card

declarations.docstring: **Erdős Problem 17.** Are there infinitely many cluster primes?
references: [erdosproblems.com/17](https://www.erdosproblems.com/17)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ {p | Erdos17.IsClusterPrime p}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
In 1999 Blecksmith, Erdős, and Selfridge [BES99] proved the upper bound
$$\pi^{\mathcal{C}}(x) \ll_A x(\log x)^{-A}$$ for every real $A > 0$.

[BES99] Blecksmith, Richard and Erd\H os, Paul and Selfridge, J. L., Cluster primes. Amer. Math. Monthly (1999), 43--48.
references: [erdosproblems.com/17](https://www.erdosproblems.com/17)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {A : ℝ}, 0 < A → (fun x => ↑(Erdos17.clusterPrimeCount x)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑x / Real.log ↑x ^ A

declarations.docstring:
In 2003, Elsholtz [El03] refined the upper bound to
$$\pi^{\mathcal{C}}(x) \ll x\,\exp\!\bigl(-c(\log\log x)^2\bigr)$$
for every real $0 < c < 1/8$.

[El03] Elsholtz, Christian, On cluster primes. Acta Arith. (2003), 281--284.
references: [erdosproblems.com/17](https://www.erdosproblems.com/17)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C,
  0 < C ∧
    ∀ c ∈ Set.Ioo 0 (1 / 8),
      Asymptotics.IsBigOWith C Filter.atTop (fun x => ↑(Erdos17.clusterPrimeCount x)) fun x =>
        ↑x * Real.exp (-c * Real.log (Real.log ↑x) ^ 2)

declarations.docstring: $97$ is the smallest prime that is not a cluster prime.
references: [erdosproblems.com/17](https://www.erdosproblems.com/17)
declarations.type_pretty: IsLeast {p | Nat.Prime p ∧ ¬Erdos17.IsClusterPrime p} 97

The existence of the limit has been proved by Erdős and Gál [ErGa48].
