declarations.docstring:
In any $2$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^2$, for all but at most one triangle $T$ (up to
congruence), there is a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$.

The colouring is arbitrary. No measurability is assumed. `≅` compares vertices with the same
label, so the conclusion allows a relabelling `σ`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/173](https://www.erdosproblems.com/173)
[Sh76] Shader, L. E., *All right triangles are Ramsey in $E^2$!*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1976), 385-389.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (c : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → Fin 2) (T₁ T₂ : Affine.Triangle ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
  ¬Erdos173.HasMonochromaticCopy c T₁ → ¬Erdos173.HasMonochromaticCopy c T₂ → ∃ σ, Congruent (T₁.points ∘ ⇑σ) T₂.points

declarations.docstring:
The exceptional triangle can exist: colouring the plane in alternating half-open strips of
suitable width gives no monochromatic copy of some equilateral triangle.
references: [erdosproblems.com/173](https://www.erdosproblems.com/173)
[Sh76] Shader, L. E., *All right triangles are Ramsey in $E^2$!*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1976), 385-389.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c T,
  dist (T.points 0) (T.points 1) = dist (T.points 1) (T.points 2) ∧
    dist (T.points 1) (T.points 2) = dist (T.points 2) (T.points 0) ∧ ¬Erdos173.HasMonochromaticCopy c T

declarations.docstring:
Shader [Sh76] proved that in any $2$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^2$, every right-angled triangle
has a monochromatic congruent copy.
references: [erdosproblems.com/173](https://www.erdosproblems.com/173)
[Sh76] Shader, L. E., *All right triangles are Ramsey in $E^2$!*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1976), 385-389.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (c : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → Fin 2) (T : Affine.Triangle ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
  EuclideanGeometry.angle (T.points 0) (T.points 1) (T.points 2) = Real.pi / 2 → Erdos173.HasMonochromaticCopy c T

declarations.docstring:
A finite set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is called Ramsey if, for any $k\geq 1$, there exists some
$d=d(A,k)$ such that in any $k$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^d$ there exists a monochromatic copy
of $A$. Characterise the Ramsey sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

A copy of $A$ is a set congruent to $A$, as in [EGMRSS73, p. 344].
references: [erdosproblems.com/174](https://www.erdosproblems.com/174)

[EGMRSS73] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Montgomery, P. and Rothschild, B. L. and Spencer, J. and Straus, E. G., *Euclidean Ramsey Theorems I*. J. Comb. Th. A (1973), 341-363. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1973-08.pdf)
[Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*. Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-25.pdf)
[FrRo90] Frankl, P. and Rödl, V., *A partition property of simplices in Euclidean space*. J. Amer. Math. Soc. (1990), 1-7.
[Kr92] Kříž, Igor, *All trapezoids are Ramsey*. Discrete Math. (1992), 59-62.
[LRW12] Leader, Imre and Russell, Paul A. and Walters, Mark, *Transitive sets in Euclidean Ramsey theory*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2012), 382-396. [arXiv:1012.1350](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.1350)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), {A | Erdos174.IsRamsey A} = Erdos174.erdos_174.answer n

Sets known to be Ramsey include vertices of $k$-dimensional rectangles [EGMRSS73].

This is the case of the vertices `{x | ∀ i, x i = 0 ∨ x i = a i}` of a rectangular
parallelepiped [EGMRSS73, Cor. 21]; some $a_i$ may be $0$ [EGMRSS73, Cor. 22].

Leader, Russell, and Walters [LRW12] have alternatively conjectured that a set is Ramsey if and
only if it is 'subtransitive': it can be embedded in some higher-dimensional set on which
rotations act transitively.

We use the definition of [LRW12]: a subset of a finite set whose symmetry group acts
transitively.

Sets known to be Ramsey include trapezoids [Kr92].

We state it for isosceles trapezoids with vertices $(\pm s, 0)$ and $(\pm t, h)$, $h\neq 0$.
A trapezoid that is not isosceles is not spherical, so it is not Ramsey by [EGMRSS73].

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős's Theorem.**
Erdős proved that $h(n!) < n$ for all $n \ge 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/18](https://www.erdosproblems.com/18)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. (1980). Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos18.practicalH n.factorial < n

declarations.docstring:
**Vose's Theorem.**
Vose proved the existence of infinitely many practical numbers $m$ such that
$h(m) \ll (\log m)^{1/2}$. This gives a positive answer to a weaker form of Conjecture 1.
references: [erdosproblems.com/18](https://www.erdosproblems.com/18)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. (1980). Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∃ᶠ (m : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, m.IsPractical ∧ ↑(Erdos18.practicalH m) < C * Real.log ↑m ^ (1 / 2)

declarations.docstring:
**Conjecture 1.**
Are there infinitely many practical numbers $m$ such that $h(m) < (\log \log m)^{O(1)}$?

More precisely: does there exist a constant $C > 0$ such that for infinitely many
practical numbers $m$, we have $h(m) < (\log \log m)^C$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/18](https://www.erdosproblems.com/18)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. (1980). Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∃ᶠ (m : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, m.IsPractical ∧ ↑(Erdos18.practicalH m) < Real.log (Real.log ↑m) ^ C

declarations.docstring:
**Conjecture 2.**
Is it true that $h(n!) < n^{o(1)}$? That is, for all $\varepsilon > 0$,
is $h(n!) < n^\varepsilon$ for sufficiently large $n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/18](https://www.erdosproblems.com/18)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. (1980). Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos18.practicalH n.factorial) < ↑n ^ ε

declarations.docstring:
**Conjecture 3.**
Or perhaps even $h(n!) < (\log n)^{O(1)}$?

Erdős offered \$250 for a proof or disproof.
references: [erdosproblems.com/18](https://www.erdosproblems.com/18)

declarations.docstring:
If $\mathbb{R}^2$ is finitely coloured then must there exist some colour class which contains the
vertices of a rectangle of every area?

Graham, "On Partitions of 𝔼ⁿ", Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series A 28, 89-91 (1980).
(See "Concluding Remarks" on page 96.)

Solved (with answer `False`, as formalised below) in:
Vjekoslav Kovač, "Coloring and density theorems for configurations of a given volume", 2023
https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.09973
In fact, Kovač's colouring is even Jordan measurable (the topological boundary of each
monochromatic region is Lebesgue measurable and has measure zero).

This was formalized in Lean by Alexeev and Kovac using Aristotle.

declarations.docstring:
What is the largest $k$ such that in any permutation of $\mathbb{Z}$ there must exist a
monotone $k$-term arithmetic progression $x_1 < \cdots < x_k$?

Here a permutation of $\mathbb{Z}$ is a one-sided arrangement $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ of the
integers, i.e. a bijection $\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}$, and a monotone $k$-term arithmetic
progression is a subsequence $a_{i_1}, \ldots, a_{i_k}$ with $i_1 < \cdots < i_k$ forming an
increasing or decreasing arithmetic progression.
references: [erdosproblems.com/195](https://www.erdosproblems.com/195)

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that all sufficiently large $n$ can be written as $2^k+m$ for some $k\geq 0$, where
$\Omega(m)<\log\log m$? (Here $\Omega(m)$ is the number of prime divisors of $m$ counted with
multiplicity.)

Barreto and Leeham, using ChatGPT and Aristotle, have proved a negative answer, which was
quantified by Tao and Alexeev (see the comments): in fact there are infinitely many $n$ such that,
for all $k$ with $2^k<n$, $n-2^k$ has at least
$$\gg \left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)^{1/2}$$
many prime factors.
references: [erdosproblems.com/205](https://www.erdosproblems.com/205)
[Er80] Erdős, Paul, *A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory*. Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.
[Ro34] Romanoff, N. P., *Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie*. Math. Ann. (1934), 668-678.

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that there is an intersecting family $\mathcal{F}$ of sets of size $n$
(so $A\cap B\neq\emptyset$ for all $A,B\in \mathcal{F}$) with $\lvert \mathcal{F}\rvert=f(n)$
such that any set $S$ with $\lvert S\rvert \leq n-1$ is disjoint from at least one
$A\in \mathcal{F}$.

Is it true that
$$f(n) \ll n?$$

Conjectured by Erdős and Lovász [ErLo75], who proved that
$$\frac{8}{3}n-3\leq f(n) \ll n^{3/2}\log n$$
for all $n$. The upper bound was improved by Kahn [Ka92b] to $f(n) \ll n\log n$. (The upper
bound constructions in both cases are formed by taking a random set of lines from a projective
plane of order $n-1$, assuming $n-1$ is a prime power.)

This problem was solved by Kahn [Ka94] who proved the upper bound $f(n) \ll n$. The Erdős-Lovász
lower bound of $\frac{8}{3}n-O(1)$ has not been improved, and it has been speculated (see e.g.
[Ka94]) that the correct answer is $3n+O(1)$.

It is trivial that $f(1)=1$ and $f(2)=3$. The values $f(3)=6$ and $f(4)=9$ were established by
Tripathi [Tr14]. Barát and Wanless [BaWa21] proved that $f(5)=13$, and that $13\leq f(6)\leq 18$.

declarations.docstring: The quadratic special case follows with twice the constant in the main bound.
references: [erdosproblems.com/211](https://www.erdosproblems.com/211)
[Be83] Beck, József, *On the lattice property of the plane and some problems of Dirac, Motzkin and Erdős in combinatorial geometry*. Combinatorica (1983), 281-297.
[SzTr83] Szemerédi, Endre and Trotter, Jr., William T., *Extremal problems in discrete geometry*. Combinatorica (1983), 381-392.
[Er84] Erdős, P., *Research problems*. Period. Math. Hungar. (1984), 101-103.
[BGS74] Burr, Stefan A. and Grünbaum, Branko and Sloane, N. J. A., *The orchard problem*. Geometriae Dedicata (1974), 397-424.
[FuPa84] Füredi, Z. and Palásti, I., *Arrangements of lines with a large number of triangles*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1984), 561-566.
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos211.MainBound → Erdos211.QuadraticBound

declarations.docstring: The real-valued form of the preceding bound, including empty configurations.
references: [erdosproblems.com/211](https://www.erdosproblems.com/211)
[Be83] Beck, József, *On the lattice property of the plane and some problems of Dirac, Motzkin and Erdős in combinatorial geometry*. Combinatorica (1983), 281-297.
[SzTr83] Szemerédi, Endre and Trotter, Jr., William T., *Extremal problems in discrete geometry*. Combinatorica (1983), 381-392.
[Er84] Erdős, P., *Research problems*. Period. Math. Hungar. (1984), 101-103.
[BGS74] Burr, Stefan A. and Grünbaum, Branko and Sloane, N. J. A., *The orchard problem*. Geometriae Dedicata (1974), 397-424.
[FuPa84] Füredi, Z. and Palásti, I., *Arrangements of lines with a large number of triangles*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1984), 561-566.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {s : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))},
  (∀ (L : AffineSubspace ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))), EuclideanGeometry.IsLine L → {p ∈ s | p ∈ L}.card ≤ 3) →
    ↑s.card * (↑s.card - 1) / 6 ≤ ↑(Erdos211.determinedLines s).card

declarations.docstring:
With at most three points on each line, double counting gives the sharp
leading coefficient $1/6$ in a quadratic lower bound.
references: [erdosproblems.com/211](https://www.erdosproblems.com/211)
[Be83] Beck, József, *On the lattice property of the plane and some problems of Dirac, Motzkin and Erdős in combinatorial geometry*. Combinatorica (1983), 281-297.
[SzTr83] Szemerédi, Endre and Trotter, Jr., William T., *Extremal problems in discrete geometry*. Combinatorica (1983), 381-392.
[Er84] Erdős, P., *Research problems*. Period. Math. Hungar. (1984), 101-103.
[BGS74] Burr, Stefan A. and Grünbaum, Branko and Sloane, N. J. A., *The orchard problem*. Geometriae Dedicata (1974), 397-424.
[FuPa84] Füredi, Z. and Palásti, I., *Arrangements of lines with a large number of triangles*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (1984), 561-566.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {s : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))},
  (∀ (L : AffineSubspace ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))), EuclideanGeometry.IsLine L → {p ∈ s | p ∈ L}.card ≤ 3) →
    s.card * (s.card - 1) ≤ 6 * (Erdos211.determinedLines s).card

declarations.docstring:
Is there a dense subset of ℝ^2 such that all pairwise distances
are rational?
references: [erdosproblems.com/212](https://www.erdosproblems.com/212)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ u, Dense u ∧ u.Pairwise fun c₁ c₂ => dist c₁ c₂ ∈ Set.range Rat.cast

declarations.docstring:
Let $n \geq 4$. Are there $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no three on a line and no four on a circle,
such that all pairwise distances are integers?
references: [erdosproblems.com/213](https://www.erdosproblems.com/213)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ n ≥ 4, Erdos213.Erdos213For n

declarations.docstring: The best construction to date, due to Kreisel and Kurz, has $n = 7$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/213](https://www.erdosproblems.com/213)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos213.Erdos213For 7

declarations.docstring:
For which $n$ do there exist $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no three on a line and no four on
a circle, that determine $n-1$ distinct distances whose multiplicities are
$1,2,\ldots,n-1$? The condition $n>0$ excludes the empty configuration, since the
requested number $n-1$ of distances is nonnegative.
references: [Erdős Problem 217](https://www.erdosproblems.com/217)
declarations.type_pretty:
Erdos217.erdos_217.answer =
  {n |
    0 < n ∧
      ∃ P,
        P.card = n ∧
          EuclideanGeometry.InGeneralPosition ↑P ∧
            (distanceSet P).card = n - 1 ∧ Finset.image (distanceMultiplicity P) (distanceSet P) = Finset.Icc 1 (n - 1)}

declarations.docstring:
The set of indices $n$ for which a prime gap is preceded by a larger or equal prime gap has a
natural density of $\frac 1 2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/218](https://www.erdosproblems.com/218)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | primeGap (n + 1) ≤ primeGap n}.HasDensity (1 / 2)

declarations.docstring:
There are infinitely many indices $n$ such that the prime gap at $n$ is equal to the prime gap
at $n+1$. This is equivalent to the existence of infinitely many arithmetic progressions of
length $3$, see `erdos_141.variants.infinite_three`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/218](https://www.erdosproblems.com/218)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | primeGap n = primeGap (n + 1)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
The set of indices $n$ for which a prime gap is followed by a larger or equal prime gap has a
natural density of $\frac 1 2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/218](https://www.erdosproblems.com/218)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | primeGap n ≤ primeGap (n + 1)}.HasDensity (1 / 2)

declarations.docstring:
The blow-up of $C_5$ shows that the bound $n^2$ in Erdős Problem 23 is tight:
any bipartite subgraph must omit at least $n^2$ edges.
references: [erdosproblems.com/23](https://www.erdosproblems.com/23)
[OEIS A389646](https://oeis.org/A389646)
[Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky, Max Cuts in Triangle-free Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14179)
[McKay, Extremal graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs](https://users.cecs.anu.edu.au/~bdm/data/graphs.html)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ),
  0 < n → ∀ H ≤ Erdos23.blowupC5 n, H.IsBipartite → n ^ 2 ≤ ((Erdos23.blowupC5 n).edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card

declarations.docstring: Can every triangle-free graph on $5n$ vertices be made bipartite by deleting at most $n^2$ edges?
references: [erdosproblems.com/23](https://www.erdosproblems.com/23)
[OEIS A389646](https://oeis.org/A389646)
[Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky, Max Cuts in Triangle-free Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14179)
[McKay, Extremal graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs](https://users.cecs.anu.edu.au/~bdm/data/graphs.html)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V],
    Fintype.card V = 5 * n →
      ∀ (G : SimpleGraph V), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ H ≤ G, H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ n ^ 2

declarations.docstring:
Every triangle-free graph on $5$ vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most $1$ edge.
This is the $n = 1$ case of Erdős Problem 23.
references: [erdosproblems.com/23](https://www.erdosproblems.com/23)
[OEIS A389646](https://oeis.org/A389646)
[Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky, Max Cuts in Triangle-free Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14179)
[McKay, Extremal graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs](https://users.cecs.anu.edu.au/~bdm/data/graphs.html)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 5)), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ H ≤ G, H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ 1

declarations.docstring:
There exists a triangle-free graph on $5$ vertices such that at least $1$ edge must be removed
to make it bipartite. This shows the bound in `erdos_23_n1` is tight.
references: [erdosproblems.com/23](https://www.erdosproblems.com/23)
[OEIS A389646](https://oeis.org/A389646)
[Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky, Max Cuts in Triangle-free Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14179)
[McKay, Extremal graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs](https://users.cecs.anu.edu.au/~bdm/data/graphs.html)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ G, G.CliqueFree 3 ∧ ∀ H ≤ G, H.IsBipartite → 1 ≤ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card

declarations.docstring:
Every triangle-free graph on $25$ vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most $25$
edges.

This is the $n = 5$ case of Erdős Problem 23.  It follows from the high-density range of
Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky together with McKay's complete catalogue of the 23-vertex extremal
graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs.
references: [erdosproblems.com/23](https://www.erdosproblems.com/23)
[OEIS A389646](https://oeis.org/A389646)
[Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky, Max Cuts in Triangle-free Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14179)
[McKay, Extremal graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs](https://users.cecs.anu.edu.au/~bdm/data/graphs.html)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 25)), G.CliqueFree 3 → ∃ H ≤ G, H.IsBipartite ∧ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card ≤ 25

declarations.docstring:
There exists a triangle-free graph on $25$ vertices such that at least $25$ edges must be
removed to make it bipartite.  The balanced blow-up of $C_5$ with five parts of size $5$
witnesses this.
references: [erdosproblems.com/23](https://www.erdosproblems.com/23)
[OEIS A389646](https://oeis.org/A389646)
[Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky, Max Cuts in Triangle-free Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.14179)
[McKay, Extremal graphs for bipartization of triangle-free graphs](https://users.cecs.anu.edu.au/~bdm/data/graphs.html)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ G, G.CliqueFree 3 ∧ ∀ H ≤ G, H.IsBipartite → 25 ≤ (G.edgeFinset \ H.edgeFinset).card

declarations.docstring:
A conjecture by Heath-Brown:
The sum of squares of the first $N$ gaps between consecutive primes behaves like $N * (log N)^2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/233](https://www.erdosproblems.com/233)
[A74741](https://oeis.org/A74741)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cram%C3%A9r%27s_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty: (fun N => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, ↑(primeGap n) ^ 2) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑N * Real.log ↑N ^ 2

declarations.docstring:
The prime number theorem immediately implies a lower bound of $\gg N(\log N)^2$ for the sum of
squares of gaps between consecutive primes.

Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.
references: [erdosproblems.com/233](https://www.erdosproblems.com/233)
[A74741](https://oeis.org/A74741)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cram%C3%A9r%27s_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty: (fun N => ↑N * Real.log ↑N ^ 2) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, ↑(primeGap n) ^ 2

declarations.docstring: Cramér proved an upper bound of $O(N(\log N)^4)$ conditional on the Riemann hypothesis.
references: [erdosproblems.com/233](https://www.erdosproblems.com/233)
[A74741](https://oeis.org/A74741)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cram%C3%A9r%27s_conjecture)
declarations.type_pretty: RiemannHypothesis → (fun N => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, ↑(primeGap n) ^ 2) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑N * Real.log ↑N ^ 4

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that for all `c ≥ 0`, the density `f c` of integers for which
`(p (n + 1) - p n) / log n < c` exists and is a continuous function of `c`?
references: [erdosproblems.com/234](https://www.erdosproblems.com/234)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ f, Continuous f ∧ ∀ (c : NNReal), {n | ↑(primeGap n) / Real.log ↑n < ↑c}.HasDensity (f c)

declarations.docstring: Let $f(n)$ count the number of solutions to $n=p+2^k$ for prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$. Show that $f(n)=o(\log n)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/236](https://www.erdosproblems.com/236)
declarations.type_pretty: (fun n => ↑(Erdos236.f n)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => Real.log ↑n

declarations.docstring:
Let `c₁, c₂ > 0`. Is it true that for any sufficiently large `x`, there exists more than
`c₁ * log x` many consecutive primes `≤ x` such that the difference between any two is `> c₂`?
references: [erdosproblems.com/238](https://www.erdosproblems.com/238)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ c₁ > 0,
    ∀ c₂ > 0,
      ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop,
        ∃ k,
          c₁ * Real.log x < ↑k ∧
            ∃ f m,
              (∀ (i : Fin k), ↑(f i) ≤ x ∧ f i = Nat.nth Nat.Prime (m + ↑i)) ∧
                ∀ (i : Fin (k - 1)), c₂ < primeGap (m + ↑i)

declarations.docstring: It is well-known that the conjecture above is true when `c₁` is sufficiently small.
references: [erdosproblems.com/238](https://www.erdosproblems.com/238)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ c₂ > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (c₁ : ℝ) in nhdsWithin 0 (Set.Ioi 0),
    ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∃ k,
        c₁ * Real.log x < ↑k ∧
          ∃ f m,
            (∀ (i : Fin k), ↑(f i) ≤ x ∧ f i = Nat.nth Nat.Prime (m + ↑i)) ∧ ∀ (i : Fin (k - 1)), c₂ < primeGap (m + ↑i)

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that $f(N)\sim N^{1/3}$?

Originally asked to Erdős by Bose.

This is discussed in problem C11 of Guy's collection [Gu04].
references: [erdosproblems.com/30](https://www.erdosproblems.com/30)
[erdosproblems.com/241](https://www.erdosproblems.com/241)
[BoCh62] Bose, R. C. and Chowla, S., Theorems in the additive theory of numbers. Comment. Math. Helv. (1962/63), 141-147.
[Gr01] Green, Ben, The number of squares and {$B_h[g]$} sets. Acta Arith. (2001), 365-390.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun N => ↑(Erdos241.f N 3)) fun N => ↑N ^ (1 / 3)

declarations.docstring:
More generally, Bose and Chowla [BoCh62] conjectured that the maximum size of
$A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with all $r$-fold sums distinct (aside from the trivial coincidences)
then $\lvert A\rvert \sim N^{1/r}.$
references: [erdosproblems.com/30](https://www.erdosproblems.com/30)
[erdosproblems.com/241](https://www.erdosproblems.com/241)
[BoCh62] Bose, R. C. and Chowla, S., Theorems in the additive theory of numbers. Comment. Math. Helv. (1962/63), 141-147.
[Gr01] Green, Ben, The number of squares and {$B_h[g]$} sets. Acta Arith. (2001), 365-390.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ r ≥ 2, Erdos241.BoseChowlaConjecture r

declarations.docstring:
Bose and Chowla [BoCh62] provided a construction proving one half of this, namely
$(1+o(1))N^{1/3}\leq f(N)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/30](https://www.erdosproblems.com/30)
[erdosproblems.com/241](https://www.erdosproblems.com/241)
[BoCh62] Bose, R. C. and Chowla, S., Theorems in the additive theory of numbers. Comment. Math. Helv. (1962/63), 141-147.
[Gr01] Green, Ben, The number of squares and {$B_h[g]$} sets. Acta Arith. (2001), 365-390.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ ε, (ε =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => 1) ∧ ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (1 + ε N) * ↑N ^ (1 / 3) ≤ ↑(Erdos241.f N 3)

declarations.docstring: This is known only for $r=2$ (see [erdosproblems.com/30]).
references: [erdosproblems.com/30](https://www.erdosproblems.com/30)
[erdosproblems.com/241](https://www.erdosproblems.com/241)
[BoCh62] Bose, R. C. and Chowla, S., Theorems in the additive theory of numbers. Comment. Math. Helv. (1962/63), 141-147.
[Gr01] Green, Ben, The number of squares and {$B_h[g]$} sets. Acta Arith. (2001), 365-390.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos241.BoseChowlaConjecture 2

declarations.docstring:
The best upper bound known to date is due to Green [Gr01], $f(N) \leq ((7/2)^{1/3}+o(1))N^{1/3}$.
(note that $(7/2)^{1/3}\approx 1.519$).
references: [erdosproblems.com/30](https://www.erdosproblems.com/30)
[erdosproblems.com/241](https://www.erdosproblems.com/241)
[BoCh62] Bose, R. C. and Chowla, S., Theorems in the additive theory of numbers. Comment. Math. Helv. (1962/63), 141-147.
[Gr01] Green, Ben, The number of squares and {$B_h[g]$} sets. Acta Arith. (2001), 365-390.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ ε,
  (ε =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => 1) ∧
    ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos241.f N 3) ≤ ((7 / 2) ^ (1 / 3) + ε N) * ↑N ^ (1 / 3)

declarations.docstring:
For every $n>2$ there exist distinct integers $1 ≤ x < y < z$
such that $\frac 4 n = \frac 1 x + \frac 1 y + \frac 1 z$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/242](https://www.erdosproblems.com/242)
[Si56](https://zbmath.org/?q=an%3A0075.03302) Sierpiński, W., Sur les décompositions de nombres rationnels en fractions primaires. Mathesis (1956), 16--32.

declarations.docstring:
Schinzel conjectured (see [Si56]) the generalisation that, for any fixed $a$, if $n$ is sufficiently
large in terms of $a$ then there exist distinct integers $1\leq x < y < z$ such that
$\frac{a}{n} = \frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}+\frac{1}{z}.$
references: [erdosproblems.com/242](https://www.erdosproblems.com/242)
[Si56](https://zbmath.org/?q=an%3A0075.03302) Sierpiński, W., Sur les décompositions de nombres rationnels en fractions primaires. Mathesis (1956), 16--32.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (a : ℕ), 0 < a → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ x y z, 1 ≤ x ∧ x < y ∧ y < z ∧ ↑a / ↑n = 1 / ↑x + 1 / ↑y + 1 / ↑z

declarations.docstring:
Let $a_1 < a_2 < \dots$ be a sequence of integers such that
$\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{a_{n-1}^2} = 1$ and $\sum \frac{1}{a_n} \in \mathbb{Q}$.

Then, for all sufficiently large $n \ge 1$, $a_n = a_{n-1}^2 - a_{n-1} + 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/243](https://www.erdosproblems.com/243)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
  StrictMono a →
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(a n) / ↑(a (n - 1)) ^ 2) Filter.atTop (nhds 1) →
      (Summable fun x => 1 / ↑(a x)) → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, a n = a (n - 1) ^ 2 - a (n - 1) + 1

declarations.docstring:
Let $C > 1$. Does the set of integers of the form $p + \lfloor C^k \rfloor$,
for some prime $p$ and $k\geq 0$, have density $>0$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/244](https://www.erdosproblems.com/244)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ C > 1, 0 < {x | ∃ p k, ∃ (_ : Nat.Prime p), p + ⌊C ^ k⌋₊ = x}.lowerDensity

declarations.docstring:
Romanoff [Ro34] proved that the answer is yes if $C$ is an integer.

[Ro34] Romanoff, N. P., _Über einige Sätze der additiven Zahlentheorie_.
Math. Ann. (1934), 668-678.
references: [erdosproblems.com/244](https://www.erdosproblems.com/244)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {C : ℕ}, 1 < C → 0 < {x | ∃ p k, ∃ (_ : Nat.Prime p), p + ⌊C ^ k⌋₊ = x}.lowerDensity

declarations.docstring:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \cdots$ be a sequence of integers such that
$$
  \limsup \frac{n_k}{k} = \infty.
$$
Is
$$
  \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2^{n_k}}
$$
transcendental?
references: [erdosproblems.com/247](https://www.erdosproblems.com/247)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono n →
      Filter.limsup (fun k => ↑(n k) / ↑k.succ) Filter.atTop = ⊤ → Transcendental ℚ (∑' (k : ℕ), 1 / 2 ^ n k)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős proved the answer is yes under the stronger condition that
$\limsup \frac{n_k}{k^t} = \infty$ for all $t\geq 1$.

[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R.,
_Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory_.
Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
references: [erdosproblems.com/247](https://www.erdosproblems.com/247)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ),
  StrictMono n →
    (∀ t ≥ 1, Filter.limsup (fun k => ↑(↑(n k) / ↑k.succ ^ t)) Filter.atTop = ⊤) →
      Transcendental ℚ (∑' (k : ℕ), 1 / 2 ^ n k)

declarations.docstring:
Is
$$\sum_{n} \frac{\phi(n)}{2^n}$$
irrational? Here $\phi$ is the Euler totient function.
references: [erdosproblems.com/249](https://www.erdosproblems.com/249)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), ↑n.totient / 2 ^ n)

declarations.docstring:
Let $n_1 < n_2 < \dots$ be an arbitrary sequence of integers, each with an associated residue class
$a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Let $A$ be the set of integers $n$ such that for every $i$ either $n < n_i$ or
$n \not\equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$. Must the logarithmic density of $A$ exist?
references: [erdosproblems.com/25](https://www.erdosproblems.com/25)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (seq_n : ℕ → ℕ) (seq_a : ℕ → ℤ),
    (∀ (i : ℕ), 0 < seq_n i) →
      StrictMono seq_n → ∃ d, {x | ∀ (i : ℕ), ↑x < ↑(seq_n i) ∨ ¬↑x ≡ seq_a i [ZMOD ↑(seq_n i)]}.HasLogDensity d

declarations.docstring: Is $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{p_n}{2^n}$ irrational? Here $p_n$ is the $n$-th prime ($p_1=2, p_2=3, \dots$).
references: [erdosproblems.com/251](https://www.erdosproblems.com/251)

declarations.docstring:
Are there infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that there exist some $t \ge 2$ and
distinct integers $a_1, \ldots, a_t \ge 1$ satisfying
$$\frac{n}{2^n} = \sum_{1 \le k \le t} \frac{a_k}{2^{a_k}}?$$

In [Er88c], Erdős notes that Cusick had a simple proof that infinitely many such $n$ exist.
references: [erdosproblems.com/261](https://www.erdosproblems.com/261)
[BoLo90] Borwein, Peter and Loring, Terry A., Some questions of Erdős and Graham on numbers of the form $\sum g_n/2^{g_n}$. Math. Comp. (1990), 377--394.
[Er88c] Erdős, P., On the irrationality of certain series: problems and results. New advances in transcendence theory (Durham, 1986) (1988), 102--109.
[TUZ20] Tengely, Szabolcs and Ulas, Maciej and Zygadlo, Jakub, On a Diophantine equation of Erdős and Graham. J. Number Theory (2020), 445--459.
[PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016&version=1)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | 0 < n ∧ Erdos261.Erdos261Prop n}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Is there a rational number $x$ such that
$$x = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{a_k}{2^{a_k}}$$
has at least $2^{\aleph_0}$ representations by pairwise distinct positive integers $a_k$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/261](https://www.erdosproblems.com/261)
[BoLo90] Borwein, Peter and Loring, Terry A., Some questions of Erdős and Graham on numbers of the form $\sum g_n/2^{g_n}$. Math. Comp. (1990), 377--394.
[Er88c] Erdős, P., On the irrationality of certain series: problems and results. New advances in transcendence theory (Durham, 1986) (1988), 102--109.
[TUZ20] Tengely, Szabolcs and Ulas, Maciej and Zygadlo, Jakub, On a Diophantine equation of Erdős and Graham. J. Number Theory (2020), 445--459.
[PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016&version=1)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ x, Cardinal.continuum ≤ Cardinal.mk ↑{a | Erdos261.Erdos261InfiniteRepresentation x a}

declarations.docstring:
For every positive integer $m$, if $n = 2^{m+1} - m - 2$, then
$$\frac{n}{2^n} = \sum_{n < k \le n + m} \frac{k}{2^k}.$$

This construction is due to Borwein and Loring [BoLo90].
references: [erdosproblems.com/261](https://www.erdosproblems.com/261)
[BoLo90] Borwein, Peter and Loring, Terry A., Some questions of Erdős and Graham on numbers of the form $\sum g_n/2^{g_n}$. Math. Comp. (1990), 377--394.
[Er88c] Erdős, P., On the irrationality of certain series: problems and results. New advances in transcendence theory (Durham, 1986) (1988), 102--109.
[TUZ20] Tengely, Szabolcs and Ulas, Maciej and Zygadlo, Jakub, On a Diophantine equation of Erdős and Graham. J. Number Theory (2020), 445--459.
[PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016&version=1)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (m : ℕ),
  0 < m →
    have n := 2 ^ (m + 1) - m - 2;
    ↑n / 2 ^ n = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Ioc n (n + m), ↑k / 2 ^ k

declarations.docstring:
The Borwein--Loring construction gives the required property when $m \ge 2$. This lower
bound ensures that the representation contains at least two terms.
references: [erdosproblems.com/261](https://www.erdosproblems.com/261)
[BoLo90] Borwein, Peter and Loring, Terry A., Some questions of Erdős and Graham on numbers of the form $\sum g_n/2^{g_n}$. Math. Comp. (1990), 377--394.
[Er88c] Erdős, P., On the irrationality of certain series: problems and results. New advances in transcendence theory (Durham, 1986) (1988), 102--109.
[TUZ20] Tengely, Szabolcs and Ulas, Maciej and Zygadlo, Jakub, On a Diophantine equation of Erdős and Graham. J. Number Theory (2020), 445--459.
[PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016&version=1)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (m : ℕ), 2 ≤ m → Erdos261.Erdos261Prop (2 ^ (m + 1) - m - 2)

declarations.docstring:
Tengely, Ulas, and Zygadlo [TUZ20] verified that every positive integer $n \le 10000$ has
the required property.
references: [erdosproblems.com/261](https://www.erdosproblems.com/261)
[BoLo90] Borwein, Peter and Loring, Terry A., Some questions of Erdős and Graham on numbers of the form $\sum g_n/2^{g_n}$. Math. Comp. (1990), 377--394.
[Er88c] Erdős, P., On the irrationality of certain series: problems and results. New advances in transcendence theory (Durham, 1986) (1988), 102--109.
[TUZ20] Tengely, Szabolcs and Ulas, Maciej and Zygadlo, Jakub, On a Diophantine equation of Erdős and Graham. J. Number Theory (2020), 445--459.
[PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016&version=1)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → n ≤ 10000 → Erdos261.Erdos261Prop n

declarations.docstring:
In [Er88c], Erdős asks the weaker question of whether there exists a rational $x$ with at
least two representations
$$x = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{a_k}{2^{a_k}}$$
by pairwise distinct positive integers $a_k$.

The answer is yes: Z. Rafik (erdosproblems.com forum, 27 Apr 2026) observed that
$4/2^4 = 5/2^5 + 6/2^6$ and $\sum_{m \ge 1} m/2^m = 2$, so $7/4$ is represented both by
$\mathbb{N}_{>0} \setminus \{4\}$ and by $\mathbb{N}_{>0} \setminus \{5, 6\}$. It is generally believed that
"two" here is a misprint for $2^{\aleph_0}$ (see `erdos_261.parts.iii`, which remains open).
references: [erdosproblems.com/261](https://www.erdosproblems.com/261)
[BoLo90] Borwein, Peter and Loring, Terry A., Some questions of Erdős and Graham on numbers of the form $\sum g_n/2^{g_n}$. Math. Comp. (1990), 377--394.
[Er88c] Erdős, P., On the irrationality of certain series: problems and results. New advances in transcendence theory (Durham, 1986) (1988), 102--109.
[TUZ20] Tengely, Szabolcs and Ulas, Maciej and Zygadlo, Jakub, On a Diophantine equation of Erdős and Graham. J. Number Theory (2020), 445--459.
[PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016](https://palomar-registry.org/entry.html?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-11-000016&version=1)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ x, 2 ≤ Cardinal.mk ↑{a | Erdos261.Erdos261InfiniteRepresentation x a}

declarations.docstring: Is $a_n = 2^{2^n}$ an irrationality sequence in the above sense?
references: [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Erdos263.IsIrrationalitySequence fun n => 2 ^ 2 ^ n

declarations.docstring:
Must every irrationality sequence $a_n$ in the above sense
satisfy $a_n^{1/n} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$?

Note: this was answered **false** for the *pre-correction* statement, which did not
require monotonicity — the counterexample sequence is not increasing. The problem
was corrected on erdosproblems.com on 2026-04-02 to require increasing sequences;
for the corrected statement this question is **open**. The earlier formal proof
(for the pre-correction definition) is preserved at
https://github.com/google-deepmind/formal-conjectures/blob/c8cf651906abe91051cf835d4232ad5648412113/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/263.lean#L298
references: [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    Erdos263.IsIrrationalitySequence a → Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(a n) ^ (1 / ↑n)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Koizumi [Ko25] showed that $a_n = \lfloor \alpha^{2^n} \rfloor$ is an irrationality sequence
for all but countably many $\alpha > 1$.

[Ko25] Koizumi, J., Irrationality of the reciprocal sum of doubly exponential sequences,
       arXiv:2504.05933 (2025).
references: [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (α : ℝ) in Filter.cocountable, α > 1 → Erdos263.IsIrrationalitySequence fun n => ⌊α ^ 2 ^ n⌋₊

declarations.docstring:
A folklore result states that any $a_n$ satisfying $\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n^{\frac{1}{2^n}} = \infty$
has $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converging to an irrational number.
references: [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
  Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(a n) ^ (1 / 2 ^ n)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop → Irrational (∑' (n : ℕ), 1 / ↑(a n))

declarations.docstring:
Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] proved that any strictly increasing sequence $a_n$ such that
$\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges and $\lim \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n^2} = 0$ is not
an irrationality sequence in the above sense.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series.
         arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).
references: [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
  StrictMono a →
    (Summable fun n => 1 / ↑(a n)) →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(a (n + 1)) / ↑(a n) ^ 2) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) → ¬Erdos263.IsIrrationalitySequence a

declarations.docstring:
On the other hand, if there exists some $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $a_n$ satisfies
$\liminf \frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n^{2+\varepsilon}} > 0$, then $a_n$ is an irrationality sequence
by the above folklore result `erdos_263.variants.folklore`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/263](https://www.erdosproblems.com/263)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
  (∀ (n : ℕ), a n > 0) →
    StrictMono a →
      (∃ ε > 0, Filter.liminf (fun n => ↑(a (n + 1)) / ↑(a n) ^ (2 + ε)) Filter.atTop > 0) →
        Erdos263.IsIrrationalitySequence a

declarations.docstring:
Is $2^n$ an example of an irrationality sequence? Kovač and Tao proved that it is not [KoTa24]

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series. arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).
references: [erdosproblems.com/264](https://www.erdosproblems.com/264)
declarations.type_pretty: ¬Erdos264.IsIrrationalitySequence fun x => 2 ^ x

declarations.docstring: Is $n!$ an example of an irrationality sequence?
references: [erdosproblems.com/264](https://www.erdosproblems.com/264)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Erdos264.IsIrrationalitySequence Nat.factorial

declarations.docstring: One example is $2^{2^n}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/264](https://www.erdosproblems.com/264)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos264.IsIrrationalitySequence fun n => 2 ^ 2 ^ n

declarations.docstring:
Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] generally proved that any strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
$a_n$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_n}$ converges and
$$
  \liminf_{n \to \infty} (a_n^2 \sum_{k > n} \frac{1}{a_k^2}) > 0
$$
is not an irrationality sequence.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series. arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).
references: [erdosproblems.com/264](https://www.erdosproblems.com/264)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {a : ℕ → ℕ},
  StrictMono a →
    0 ∉ Set.range a →
      (Summable fun x => 1 / ↑(a x)) →
        0 < Filter.liminf (fun n => ↑(a n) ^ 2 * ∑' (k : ↑(Set.Ioi n)), 1 / ↑(a ↑k) ^ 2) Filter.atTop →
          ¬Erdos264.IsIrrationalitySequence a

declarations.docstring:
On the other hand, Kovač and Tao [KoTa24] do prove that for any function $F$ with
$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{F(n + 1)}{F(n)} = \infty$ there exists such an irrationality sequence with $a_n \sim F(n)$.

[KoTa24] Kovač, V. and Tao T., On several irrationality problems for Ahmes series. arXiv:2406.17593 (2024).
references: [erdosproblems.com/264](https://www.erdosproblems.com/264)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {F : ℕ → ℕ},
  Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(F (n + 1)) / ↑(F n)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
    ∃ a, Erdos264.IsIrrationalitySequence a ∧ Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ↑(a n)) fun n => ↑(F n)

$\{a_1 < a_2 < \dots\}$ be the set of positive integers whose prime factors
are all in $P$. Is the sum

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to \infty$. Is it true that
$$\sum_{n\geq 1} \frac{1}{(n+1)\cdots (n+f(n))}$$
is irrational?

Erdős and Graham [ErGr80] write 'the answer is almost surely in the affirmative if $f(n)$ is
assumed to be nondecreasing'. The case $f(n)=n$ was subsequently settled by Crmarić and Kovač
[Ko26]. Hansen [Ha75] has
shown that
$$\sum_n \frac{1}{\binom{2n}{n}}=\sum_n \frac{n!}{(n+1)\cdots (n+n)}=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{2\pi}{3^{5/2}}$$
is transcendental.

Crmarić and Kovač [CrKo25] have shown that the answer to this question is no in a strong sense:
for any $\alpha \in (0,\infty)$ there exists a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that
$f(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and
$$\sum_{n\geq 1} \frac{1}{(n+1)\cdots (n+f(n))}=\alpha.$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/270](https://www.erdosproblems.com/270)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Ha75] Hansen, E. R., *A Table of Series and Products*. Prentice-Hall (1975), 87.
[CrKo25] T. Crmarić and V. Kovač, *On the irrationality of certain super-polynomially decaying series*. arXiv:2504.18712 (2025).
[Ko26] V. Kovač, [solution of the linear case](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/270#post-7469) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty: ¬∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ), Filter.Tendsto f Filter.atTop Filter.atTop → Irrational (Erdos270.series f)

declarations.docstring:
Crmarić and Kovač [CrKo25]: for any $\alpha \in (0,\infty)$ there exists a function
$f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that $f(n)\to \infty$ as $n\to\infty$ and
$$\sum_{n\geq 1} \frac{1}{(n+1)\cdots (n+f(n))}=\alpha.$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/270](https://www.erdosproblems.com/270)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Ha75] Hansen, E. R., *A Table of Series and Products*. Prentice-Hall (1975), 87.
[CrKo25] T. Crmarić and V. Kovač, *On the irrationality of certain super-polynomially decaying series*. arXiv:2504.18712 (2025).
[Ko26] V. Kovač, [solution of the linear case](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/270#post-7469) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (α : ℝ),
  0 < α →
    ∃ f,
      Filter.Tendsto f Filter.atTop Filter.atTop ∧
        HasSum (fun n => (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc (n + 2) (n + 1 + f (n + 1)), ↑i)⁻¹) α

[Ha75] Hansen, E. R., *A Table of Series and Products*. Prentice-Hall (1975), 87.
[CrKo25] T. Crmarić and V. Kovač, *On the irrationality of certain super-polynomially decaying series*. arXiv:2504.18712 (2025).
[Ko26] V. Kovač, [solution of the linear case](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/270#post-7469) (2026).

[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Ha75] Hansen, E. R., *A Table of Series and Products*. Prentice-Hall (1975), 87.

declarations.docstring:
Let $N\geq 1$. What is the largest $t$ such that there are
$A_1,\ldots,A_t\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $A_i\cap A_j$ a non-empty
arithmetic progression for all $i\neq j$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/272](https://www.erdosproblems.com/272)
declarations.type_pretty: Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun N => ↑(Erdos272.maxArithInterCard N)) sorry

declarations.docstring: Simonovits and Sós have shown that $t\ll N^2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/272](https://www.erdosproblems.com/272)
declarations.type_pretty: (fun N => ↑(Erdos272.maxArithInterCard N)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑N ^ 2

$$

declarations.docstring:
If $G$ is a group, can there exist an exact covering of $G$ by more than one coset
of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one of the cosets.)

The conjectured answer is no: in every such exact covering, two of the subgroups have
the same cardinality.
references: [erdosproblems.com/274](https://www.erdosproblems.com/274)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog%E2%80%93Sch%C3%B6nheim_conjecture)
[arXiv:1803.08301](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08301)
[arXiv:1803.03569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03569)
[PMC7247885](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7247885/)
[arXiv:1804.11103](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11103)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G],
    1 < ENat.card G →
      ∀ (ι : Type u_2) [inst_1 : Fintype ι] (P : Erdos274.Group.ExactCovering G ι),
        1 < Fintype.card ι → ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ Cardinal.mk ↥(P.parts i) = Cardinal.mk ↥(P.parts j)

declarations.docstring:
If `G` is a finite abelian group then there cannot exist an exact covering of `G` by more
than one cosets of different sizes? (i.e. each element is contained in exactly one
of the cosets.)
references: [erdosproblems.com/274](https://www.erdosproblems.com/274)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog%E2%80%93Sch%C3%B6nheim_conjecture)
[arXiv:1803.08301](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08301)
[arXiv:1803.03569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03569)
[PMC7247885](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7247885/)
[arXiv:1804.11103](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11103)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype G] [inst_1 : CommGroup G],
  1 < Fintype.card G →
    ∀ {ι : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype ι] (P : Erdos274.Group.ExactCovering G ι),
      1 < Fintype.card ι → ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ Cardinal.mk ↥(P.parts i) = Cardinal.mk ↥(P.parts j)

declarations.docstring:
Let $G$ be a group, and let $A = \{a_1G_1, \dots, a_kG_k\}$ be a finite system of left cosets of
subgroups $G_1, \dots, G_k$ of $G$.

Herzog and Schönheim conjectured that if $A$ forms a partition of $G$ with $k > 1$, then the
indices $[G:G_1], \dots, [G:G_k]$ cannot be distinct.
references: [erdosproblems.com/274](https://www.erdosproblems.com/274)
[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herzog%E2%80%93Sch%C3%B6nheim_conjecture)
[arXiv:1803.08301](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08301)
[arXiv:1803.03569](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.03569)
[PMC7247885](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7247885/)
[arXiv:1804.11103](https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.11103)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {G : Type u_1} [inst : Group G],
  1 < ENat.card G →
    ∀ {ι : Type u_2} [inst_1 : Fintype ι],
      1 < Fintype.card ι →
        ∀ (P : Erdos274.Group.ExactCovering G ι), ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ (P.parts i).index = (P.parts j).index

declarations.docstring:
Is there an infinite Lucas sequence $a_0, a_1, \ldots$ where $a_{n+2} = a_{n+1} + a_n$ for
$n \ge 0$ such that all $a_k$ are composite, and yet no integer has a common factor with every
term of the sequence?
references: [erdosproblems.com/276](https://www.erdosproblems.com/276)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ a, Erdos276.IsLucasSequence a ∧ (∀ (k : ℕ), (a k).Composite) ∧ ∀ n > 1, ∃ k, n.gcd (a k) = 1

declarations.docstring:
Let $k\geq 3$. Is there a choice of congruence classes $a_p\pmod{p}$ for every prime $p$
such that all sufficiently large integers can be written as $a_p+tp$ for some prime $p$
and integer $t\geq k$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/279](https://www.erdosproblems.com/279)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ k ≥ 3, ∃ a N, (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → a p < p) ∧ ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ p, ∃ t ≥ k, Nat.Prime p ∧ n = a p + t * p

declarations.docstring:
If $A ⊆ \mathbb{N}$ is such that $A + A$ contains all but finitely many integers then
$\limsup 1_A ∗ 1_A(n) = \infty$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/28](https://www.erdosproblems.com/28)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (A : Set ℕ), (A + A)ᶜ.Finite → Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑(AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep A n)) Filter.atTop = ⊤

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be an infinite set and consider the following
greedy algorithm for a rational $x\in (0,1)$: choose the minimal $n\in A$ not used
so far such that $n\geq 1/x$ and repeat with $x$ replaced by $x-\frac{1}{n}$. If this
terminates after finitely many steps then this produces a representation of
$x$ as the sum of distinct unit fractions with denominators from $A$.

Does this process always terminate if $x$ has odd denominator and $A$ is the
set of odd numbers?
references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {x : ℚ}, x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1 → Odd x.den → Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem {n | Odd n} x =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] 0

declarations.docstring: In 1202 Fibonacci observed that this process terminates for any $x$ when $A=\mathbb{N}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {x : ℚ}, x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1 → Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem Set.univ x =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] 0

declarations.docstring: More generally, for which pairs $x$ and $A$ does this process terminate?
references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (x : ℚ) (A : Set ℕ),
  Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem A x =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] 0 ↔ (x, A) ∈ Erdos282.erdos_282.variants.general.answer

declarations.docstring:
Graham has shown that $\frac{m}{n}$ is the sum of distinct unit fractions
with denominators $\equiv a\pmod{d}$ if and only if
$$\left(\frac{n}{(n,a,d)},\frac{d}{(a,d)}\right)=1.$$
Does the greedy algorithm always
terminate in such cases?
references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1,
  ∀ (a d : ℕ),
    1 < d →
      (x.den / x.den.gcd (a.gcd d)).gcd (d / a.gcd d) = 1 →
        Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem {n | n ≡ a [MOD d]} x =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] 0

declarations.docstring:
Graham has also shown that $x$ is the sum of distinct unit fractions with
square denominators if and only if $x\in [0,\pi^2/6-1)\cup [1,\pi^2/6)$. Does the
greedy algorithm for this always terminate? Erdős and Graham believe not - indeed, perhaps it
fails to terminate almost always.
references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (x : ℚ),
  ↑x ∈ Set.Ico 0 (Real.pi ^ 2 / 6 - 1) ∪ Set.Ico 1 (Real.pi ^ 2 / 6) →
    Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem {n | IsSquare n} x =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] 0

references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem Set.univ (1 / ↑n) 1 = 0

references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem {n | IsSquare n} 1 0 = 0

references: [erdosproblems.com/282](https://www.erdosproblems.com/282)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), Erdos282.greedyUnitFractionRem Set.univ (1 / ↑n) 0 = 0

declarations.docstring:
Let $k\geq2$. Is it true that, for any distinct integers
$1 < n_1 < \cdots < n_k$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{n_i} = 1$,
we must have $\max(n_{i+1} - n_i) \geq 3$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/287](https://www.erdosproblems.com/287)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ), StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, ⋯⟩ → ∑ i, 1 / ↑(s i) = 1 → 3 ≤ Erdos287.max_gap k s

declarations.docstring:
The example $1 = \frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{6}$ shows that $3$ would be best possible here:
the sequence $(2, 3, 6)$ is a valid Egyptian fraction representation of $1$ with
`max_gap = 3`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/287](https://www.erdosproblems.com/287)
declarations.type_pretty:
have s := ![2, 3, 6];
StrictMono s ∧ 1 < s 0 ∧ ∑ i, 1 / ↑(s i) = 1 ∧ Erdos287.max_gap 3 s = 3

declarations.docstring:
The lower bound of $\geq 2$ is equivalent to saying that $1$ is not the sum of reciprocals of
consecutive integers, proved by Erdős [Er32].
references: [erdosproblems.com/287](https://www.erdosproblems.com/287)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ) (x : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ), StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, ⋯⟩ → ∑ i, 1 / ↑(s i) = 1 → 2 ≤ Erdos287.max_gap k s

declarations.docstring:
For all large $N$, there exists a prime $p \in [N, 2N]$ such that $\frac{p+1}{2}$ is also prime.

This is an open conjecture. If true, it would imply `erdos_287` for all but at most finitely
many exceptions (see `erdos_287.variants.prime_conjecture_implies`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/287](https://www.erdosproblems.com/287)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ N₀, ∀ (N : ℕ), N₀ ≤ N → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ N ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 * N ∧ Nat.Prime ((p + 1) / 2)

declarations.docstring:
The conjecture `erdos_287` would follow for all but at most finitely many exceptions if it were
known that, for all large $N$, there exists a prime $p \in [N, 2N]$ such that $\frac{p+1}{2}$
is also prime.

More precisely: if the prime conjecture holds, then there exists $k_0$ such that for all
$k \geq k_0$, any Egyptian fraction representation of $1$ with $k$ terms and all terms $> 1$
must have $\max(n_{i+1} - n_i) \geq 3$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/287](https://www.erdosproblems.com/287)
declarations.type_pretty:
(True ↔ ∃ N₀, ∀ (N : ℕ), N₀ ≤ N → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ N ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 * N ∧ Nat.Prime ((p + 1) / 2)) →
  ∃ k₀,
    ∀ (k : ℕ),
      k₀ ≤ k →
        ∀ (hk : 2 ≤ k) (s : Fin k → ℕ), StrictMono s → 1 < s ⟨0, ⋯⟩ → ∑ i, 1 / ↑(s i) = 1 → 3 ≤ Erdos287.max_gap k s

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that there are only finitely many pairs of intervals $I_1$, $I_2$ such that
$$
\sum_{n_1 \in I_1} \frac{1}{n_1} + \sum_{n_2 \in I_2} \frac{1}{n_2} \in \mathbb{N}?
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/288](https://www.erdosproblems.com/288)
declarations.type_pretty: {I | ∀ (j : Fin 2), (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧ ∃ n, ∑ j, ∑ nⱼ ∈ (Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2).toFinset, (↑↑nⱼ)⁻¹ = ↑↑n}.Finite

declarations.docstring: Is it true for any $k > 2$ that only finitely many $k$ intervals satisfy this condition?
references: [erdosproblems.com/288](https://www.erdosproblems.com/288)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ k > 2,
  {I | ∀ (j : Fin k), (I j).1 ≤ (I j).2 ∧ ∃ n, ∑ j, ∑ nⱼ ∈ (Set.Icc (I j).1 (I j).2).toFinset, (↑↑nⱼ)⁻¹ = ↑↑n}.Finite

declarations.docstring: This is still open even if $|I_2| = 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/288](https://www.erdosproblems.com/288)
declarations.type_pretty: {(I, n₂) | I.1 ≤ I.2 ∧ ∃ n, ∑ n₁ ∈ (Set.Icc I.1 I.2).toFinset, (↑↑n₁)⁻¹ + (↑↑n₂)⁻¹ = ↑↑n}.Finite

declarations.docstring:
Let $n\geq 1$ and define $L_n$ to be the least common multiple of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and $a_n$ by
$\sum_{1\leq k\leq n}\frac{1}{k}=\frac{a_n}{L_n}$.

Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)=1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
[ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).

[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ {n | (Erdos291.a n).gcd (Erdos291.L n) = 1}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that $(a_n,L_n)>1$ occurs for infinitely many $n$?

Steinerberger has observed that the answer to the second question is trivially yes: for example, any
$n$ which begins with a $2$ in base $3$ has $3\mid (a_n,L_n)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
[ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ {n | (Erdos291.a n).gcd (Erdos291.L n) > 1}.Infinite

$\asymp\frac{x}{\log x}$ for the number of $n\in [1,x]$ such that $(a_n,L_n)=1$.

declarations.docstring:
More generally, if the leading digit of $n$ in base $p$ is $p-1$ then $p\mid (a_n,L_n)$. There is
in fact a necessary and sufficient condition: a prime $p\leq n$ divides $(a_n,L_n)$ if and only if
$p$ divides the numerator of $1+\cdots+\frac{1}{k}$, where $k$ is the leading digit of $n$ in base
$p$. This can be seen by writing $a_n = \frac{L_n}{1}+\cdots+\frac{L_n}{n}$ and observing that the
right-hand side is congruent to $1+\cdots+1/k$ modulo $p$. (The previous claim about $p-1$ follows
immediately from Wolstenholme's theorem.)
references: [erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
[ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n p : ℕ),
  Nat.Prime p →
    p ≤ n →
      have k := n / p ^ Nat.log p n;
      p ∣ (Erdos291.a n).gcd (Erdos291.L n) ↔ ↑p ∣ (∑ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, 1 / ↑i).num

declarations.docstring:
Wu and Yan [WuYa22] have proved, conditional on $\frac{1}{\log p}$ being linearly independent
over $\mathbb{Q}$ for any finite collection of primes $p$ (itself a consequence of Schanuel's
conjecture), that the set of $n$ for which $(a_n,L_n)>1$ has upper density $1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/291](https://www.erdosproblems.com/291)
[ErGr80, p.34] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Sh16] P. Shiu, The denominators of harmonic numbers. arXiv:1607.02863 (2016).
[WuYa22] Wu, Bing-Ling and Yan, Xiao-Hui, On the denominators of harmonic numbers. {IV}. C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris (2022), 53--57.

$N ≤ n_1 < ⋯ < n_k$ with $\frac 1 {n_1} + ... + \frac 1 {n_k} = 1$

Let $f(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that there are no
solutions to
$$\frac{1}{a}= \frac{1}{b}+\frac{1}{c}$$
with distinct $a,b,c\in A$? Estimate $f(N)$.

The colouring version of this is [303], which was solved by Brown and Rödl [BrRo91].
references: [erdosproblems.com/302](https://www.erdosproblems.com/302)
[BrRo91] Brown, Tom C. and Rödl, Voijtech, Monochromatic solutions to equations with unit fractions. Bull. Austral. Math. Soc. (1991), 387-392.

declarations.docstring:
Are there two finite set of primes $P$ and $Q$ such that

$$
1 = \left( \sum_{p \in P} \frac{1}{p} \right) \left( \sum_{q \in Q} \frac{1}{q} \right)
$$
?

Asked by Barbeau [Ba76].

[Ba76] Barbeau, E. J., _Computer challenge corner: Problem 477: A brute force program._
references: [erdosproblems.com/307](https://www.erdosproblems.com/307)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ P Q, (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) ∧ (∀ q ∈ Q, Nat.Prime q) ∧ 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (↑p)⁻¹) * ∑ q ∈ Q, (↑q)⁻¹

declarations.docstring:
A machine-checked **barrier** for Erdős 307 (Bonfioli, 2026): any solution with `Q` nonempty uses at
least 59 primes in total, and `(∏_{p ∈ P} p)² ≥ 4·10¹¹²` — i.e. `∏_{p ∈ P} p ≥ 2·10⁵⁶` (and, by
symmetry, the same for `∏ Q`); so no solution lies below a prime-product of `2.09·10⁵⁶`. The full
`sorry`-free proof is in the linked repository (`Closed.lean`): the left conjunct is `card_ge_59`,
the right is `erdos307_barrier_closed`. Both depend on `propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound` and
nothing further: the evaluation of the first 59 primes is kernel-checked by `decide`, so no
`native_decide` enters this statement.
references: [erdosproblems.com/307](https://www.erdosproblems.com/307)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {P Q : Finset ℕ},
  (∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p) →
    (∀ q ∈ Q, Nat.Prime q) →
      Q.Nonempty → 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (↑p)⁻¹) * ∑ q ∈ Q, (↑q)⁻¹ → 59 ≤ (P ∪ Q).card ∧ 4 * 10 ^ 112 ≤ (∏ p ∈ P, ↑p) ^ 2

declarations.docstring:
Instead of asking for sets of primes, ask only that all elements in the sets be relatively coprime.

Cambie has found several examples when this weakened version is true. For example,
$$
1=\left(1+\frac{1}{5}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}\right)
$$
and
$$
1=\left(1+\frac{1}{41}\right)\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{7}\right).
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/307](https://www.erdosproblems.com/307)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ P Q,
    0 ∉ P ∩ Q ∧
      1 < P.card ∧
        1 < Q.card ∧ (↑P).Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧ (↑Q).Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧ 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (↑p)⁻¹) * ∑ q ∈ Q, (↑q)⁻¹

declarations.docstring: There are no examples known of the weakened coprime version if we insist that $1\not\in P\cup Q$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/307](https://www.erdosproblems.com/307)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ P Q,
    0 ∉ P ∩ Q ∧
      1 ∉ P ∪ Q ∧
        1 < P.card ∧
          1 < Q.card ∧ (↑P).Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧ (↑Q).Pairwise Nat.Coprime ∧ 1 = (∑ p ∈ P, (↑p)⁻¹) * ∑ q ∈ Q, (↑q)⁻¹

declarations.docstring:
Let $N\geq 1$. What is the smallest integer not representable as the sum of distinct unit
fractions with denominators from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$?

This was essentially solved by Croot [Cr99] (see `erdos_308.variants.croot`); in particular,
for all sufficiently large $N$, the smallest such integer is either $m_N$ or $m_N+1$, where
$m_N=\lfloor \sum_{n\leq N}\frac{1}{n}\rfloor$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/308](https://www.erdosproblems.com/308)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., _Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory_. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Cr99] Croot, III, Ernest S., _On some questions of Erdős and Graham about Egyptian fractions_. Mathematika (1999), 359-372.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos308.f N = Erdos308.m N ∨ Erdos308.f N = Erdos308.m N + 1

declarations.docstring:
Let $N\geq 1$. Is it true that the set of integers representable as the sum of distinct unit
fractions with denominators from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has the shape $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ for some $m$?

It follows from Croot's bounds [Cr99] that this holds for all sufficiently large $N$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/308](https://www.erdosproblems.com/308)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., _Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory_. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Cr99] Croot, III, Ernest S., _On some questions of Erdős and Graham about Egyptian fractions_. Mathematika (1999), 359-372.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ m, Erdos308.representable N = Set.Icc 1 m

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for every $N\geq 1$, the set of integers representable as the sum of distinct
unit fractions with denominators from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has the shape $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ for some
$m$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/308](https://www.erdosproblems.com/308)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., _Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory_. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Cr99] Croot, III, Ernest S., _On some questions of Erdős and Graham about Egyptian fractions_. Mathematika (1999), 359-372.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ N ≥ 1, ∃ m, Erdos308.representable N = Set.Icc 1 m

declarations.docstring:
Croot [Cr99] bounded $\eta(N)$, the largest integer such that every integer in
$\{1,\ldots,\eta(N)\}$ is representable; this is $f(N)-1$, so his bounds read
$$\left\lfloor\sum_{n\leq N}\frac{1}{n}-\frac{9}{2}(1+o(1))\frac{(\log\log N)^2}{\log N}
\right\rfloor + 1 \leq f(N)$$
and
$$f(N)\leq \left\lfloor\sum_{n\leq N}\frac{1}{n}-\frac{1}{2}(1+o(1))
\frac{(\log\log N)^2}{\log N}\right\rfloor + 1.$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/308](https://www.erdosproblems.com/308)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., _Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory_. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Cr99] Croot, III, Ernest S., _On some questions of Erdős and Graham about Egyptian fractions_. Mathematika (1999), 359-372.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ o₁ o₂,
  Filter.Tendsto o₁ Filter.atTop (nhds 0) ∧
    Filter.Tendsto o₂ Filter.atTop (nhds 0) ∧
      ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
        ⌊↑(harmonic N) - 9 / 2 * (1 + o₁ N) * Real.log (Real.log ↑N) ^ 2 / Real.log ↑N⌋₊ + 1 ≤ Erdos308.f N ∧
          Erdos308.f N ≤ ⌊↑(harmonic N) - 1 / 2 * (1 + o₂ N) * Real.log (Real.log ↑N) ^ 2 / Real.log ↑N⌋₊ + 1

declarations.docstring:
If $m_N=\lfloor \sum_{n\leq N}\frac{1}{n}\rfloor$, then the set of integers representable is, for
all $N$ sufficiently large, either $\{1,\ldots,m_N-1\}$ or $\{1,\ldots,m_N\}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/308](https://www.erdosproblems.com/308)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., _Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory_. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
[Cr99] Croot, III, Ernest S., _On some questions of Erdős and Graham about Egyptian fractions_. Mathematika (1999), 359-372.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
  Erdos308.representable N = Set.Icc 1 (Erdos308.m N - 1) ∨ Erdos308.representable N = Set.Icc 1 (Erdos308.m N)

declarations.docstring: Since $[1, \ldots, N] = e^{(1+o(1))N}$, the trivial bound gives $\delta(N) \ge e^{-(1+o(1))N}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/311](https://www.erdosproblems.com/311)
[ErGr80] P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980), p. 40.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Real.exp (-(1 + ε) * ↑N) ≤ Erdos311.delta N

declarations.docstring:
The trivial lower bound: every non-zero value of $1 - \sum_{n \in A} 1/n$ is a non-zero rational
with denominator dividing $[1, \ldots, N]$, so $\delta(N) \geq 1/[1,\ldots,N]$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/311](https://www.erdosproblems.com/311)
[ErGr80] P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980), p. 40.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (N : ℕ), 1 / ↑((Finset.Icc 1 N).lcm id) ≤ Erdos311.delta N

declarations.docstring:
For $N = 1$ the only non-zero value is $\lvert 1-0\rvert = 1$ (from $A = \emptyset$),
so $\delta(1) = 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/311](https://www.erdosproblems.com/311)
[ErGr80] P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980), p. 40.
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos311.delta 1 = 1

declarations.docstring:
Let $\delta(N)$ be the minimal non-zero value of $\lvert 1-\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}\rvert$ as $A$
ranges over all subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Is it true that
$$\delta(N)=e^{-(c+o(1))N}$$
for some constant $c\in (0,1)$?

The formulation in [ErGr80] has the additional condition that $A$ contains no $S$ with
$\sum_{n\in S}\frac{1}{n}=1$; Kovac (in the comments on the problem page) showed that the
formulation above is equivalent. We state $\delta(N)=e^{-(c+o(1))N}$ as
$-\log \delta(N) / N \to c$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/311](https://www.erdosproblems.com/311)
[ErGr80] P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980), p. 40.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1, Filter.Tendsto (fun N => -Real.log (Erdos311.delta N) / ↑N) Filter.atTop (nhds c)

declarations.docstring:

$1 - \exp(-(c*K)) < \sum_{n \in S} 1/n \le 1$?

declarations.docstring:
What is the size of the largest $A\subseteq\{1, \dots, N\}$ such that there is a function
$\delta : A \to \{-1, 1\}$ such that
$$
  \sum_{n\in A} \frac{\delta n}{n} = 0
$$
and
$$
  \sum_{n\in A'}\frac{\delta n}{n} \neq 0
$$
for all non-empty $A'\subsetneq A$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/319](https://www.erdosproblems.com/319)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (N : ℕ),
  IsGreatest
    {x |
      ∃ A,
        ∃ (_ : A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N) (_ :
          ∃ δ, ∑ n ∈ A, ↑↑(δ n) / ↑n = 0 ∧ ∀ A' ⊂ A, A'.Nonempty → ∑ n ∈ A', ↑↑(δ n) / ↑n ≠ 0), A.card = x}
    Erdos319.erdos_319.answer

declarations.docstring:
Let $c(N)$ be the size of the largest $A\subseteq\{1, \dots, N\}$ such that there is a function
$\delta : A \to \{-1, 1\}$ such that
$$
  \sum_{n\in A} \frac{\delta n}{n} = 0
$$
and
$$
  \sum_{n\in A'}\frac{\delta n}{n} \neq 0
$$
for all non-empty $A'\subsetneq A$. What is $\Theta(c(N))$?

Trivially $c(N) \leq N$, and `erdos_319.variants.lb` gives $c(N) \geq (1 - \frac{1}{e} + o(1))N$,
so $c(N) = \Theta(N)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/319](https://www.erdosproblems.com/319)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (N : ℕ) (c : ℕ → ℝ),
  (∀ (N : ℕ),
      IsGreatest
        {x |
          ∃ A,
            ∃ (_ : A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N) (_ :
              ∃ δ, ∑ n ∈ A, ↑↑(δ n) / ↑n = 0 ∧ ∀ A' ⊂ A, A'.Nonempty → ∑ n ∈ A', ↑↑(δ n) / ↑n ≠ 0), ↑A.card = x}
        (c N)) →
    c =Θ[Filter.atTop] Erdos319.erdos_319.variants.isTheta.answer

Acta Arith. (2001), 99-114.

        sSup

declarations.docstring:
Does there exist a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that $|A \cap \{1, \ldots, N\}| = o((\log N)^2)$
and every sufficiently large integer can be written as $p + a$ for some prime $p$ and $a \in A$?

declarations.docstring:
Let $R(N)$ be the maximal such size. Results of Bleicher and Erdős from [BlEr75] and [BlEr76b] imply that
$$
\frac{N}{\log N} \prod_{i=3}^{k} \log_i N \le R(N),
$$
valid for any $k \ge 4$ with $\log_k N \ge k$ and any $r \ge 1$ with $\log_{2r} N \ge 1$. (In these bounds $\log_i n$ denotes the $i$-fold iterated logarithm.)

[BlEr75] Bleicher, M. N. and Erdős, P., _The number of distinct subsums of $\sum \sb{1}\spN\,1/i$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 29-42.
[BlEr76b] Bleicher, Michael N. and Erdős, Paul, _Denominators of Egyptian fractions. II_. Illinois J. Math. (1976), 598-613.
references: [erdosproblems.com/321](https://www.erdosproblems.com/321)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (N k : ℕ), 4 ≤ k → ↑k ≤ Real.log^[k] ↑N → ↑N / Real.log ↑N * ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 3 k, Real.log^[i] ↑N ≤ ↑(Erdos321.R N)

declarations.docstring:
Let $R(N)$ be the maximal such size. Results of Bleicher and Erdős from [BlEr75] and [BlEr76b] imply that
$$
R(N) \le \frac{1}{\log 2} \log_r N \left( \frac{N}{\log N} \prod_{i=3}^{r} \log_i N \right),
$$
valid for any $k \ge 4$ with $\log_k N \ge k$ and any $r \ge 1$ with $\log_{2r} N \ge 1$. (In these bounds $\log_i n$ denotes the $i$-fold iterated logarithm.)

Since `Real.log` is defined on all of $\mathbb{R}$, the condition $\log_{2r} N \ge 1$ is
formalised as $\log_i N \ge 1$ for all $i \le 2r$, which is equivalent to it for the
genuine iterated logarithm and ensures that every intermediate iterate is positive.

[BlEr75] Bleicher, M. N. and Erdős, P., _The number of distinct subsums of $\sum \sb{1}\spN\,1/i$_. Math. Comp. (1975), 29-42.
[BlEr76b] Bleicher, Michael N. and Erdős, Paul, _Denominators of Egyptian fractions. II_. Illinois J. Math. (1976), 598-613.
references: [erdosproblems.com/321](https://www.erdosproblems.com/321)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (N r : ℕ),
  1 ≤ r →
    (∀ i ≤ 2 * r, 1 ≤ Real.log^[i] ↑N) →
      ↑(Erdos321.R N) ≤ 1 / Real.log 2 * Real.log^[r] ↑N * ↑N / Real.log ↑N * ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 3 r, Real.log^[i] ↑N

declarations.docstring: Let $k\geq 3$ and $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ be the set of $k$th powers. What is the order of growth of $1_A^{(k)}(n)$, i.e. the number of representations of $n$ as the sum of $k$ many $k$th powers? Does there exist some $c>0$ and infinitely many $n$ such that $$1_A^{(k)}(n) >n^c?$$

[Er36] Erdős, Paul, *On the Representation of an Integer as the Sum of k k-th Powers*. J. London Math. Soc. (1936), 133-136.
[Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
[Ma36] Mahler, Kurt, *Note on Hypothesis K of Hardy and Littlewood*. J. London Math. Soc. (1936), 136-138.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → ∃ c > 0, {n | ↑n ^ c < ↑(Erdos322.representationCount k n)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that $f_{k,k}(x) \gg_\epsilon x^{1-\epsilon}$ for all $\epsilon>0$?

references: [erdosproblems.com/323](https://www.erdosproblems.com/323)

declarations.docstring:
Does there exist $A = \{a_1 < a_2 < \cdots\} \subset \mathbb{N}$ which is a minimal basis of
order $2$ (i.e. every large integer is the sum of $2$ elements from $A$, and no proper subset of
$A$ has this property), such that
$$\lim_{k\to\infty} \frac{a_k}{k^2} = c$$
for some $c \neq 0$?

Erdős and Graham conjectured a negative answer to this question [ErGr80].

"Minimal basis of order $2$" is formalised as `Minimal` for the predicate
`Set.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder · 2` on sets of naturals ordered by inclusion.
references: [erdosproblems.com/326](https://www.erdosproblems.com/326)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980), p. 47.
[Ca57] Cassels, J. W. S., *Über Basen der natürlichen Zahlenreihe*. Abh. Math. Sem. Univ. Hamburg (1957), 247-257.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ a,
  StrictMono a ∧
    Minimal (fun A => A.IsAsymptoticAddBasisOfOrder 2) (Set.range a) ∧
      ∃ c, c ≠ 0 ∧ Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(a n) / ↑n ^ 2) Filter.atTop (nhds c)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős originally asked this for any basis (not necessarily minimal); such a basis was constructed
by Cassels [Ca57].
references: [erdosproblems.com/326](https://www.erdosproblems.com/326)
[ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980), p. 47.
[Ca57] Cassels, J. W. S., *Über Basen der natürlichen Zahlenreihe*. Abh. Math. Sem. Univ. Hamburg (1957), 247-257.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ a,
