declarations.docstring:
**Graph analogue — bipartite graphs are obligatory (Erdős–Galvin–Hajnal [EGH75])**:
For the 2-uniform (graph) case, a graph of chromatic cardinal $> \aleph_0$ must contain all
finite bipartite graphs. Specifically, for every finite bipartite graph `F` and every graph
`G` with chromatic cardinal $> \aleph_0$, there is a graph embedding from `F` into `G`.

This uses `F ⊑ G` (`SimpleGraph.IsContained`, an injective graph homomorphism), aligned with
the injective edge-preserving map used in the hypergraph `Appears` definition. A graph embedding
`F ↪g G` would require an induced copy, which the theorem does not provide.
references: [erdosproblems.com/593](https://www.erdosproblems.com/593)

[EGH75] Erdős, Paul and Galvin, Fred and Hajnal, András, On set-systems having large chromatic number and not containing prescribed subsystems. [EHR73] Erdős, Paul and Hajnal, András and Rothschild, Bruce, On chromatic number of graphs and set-systems. Cambridge Summer School in Mathematical Logic (Cambridge, 1971), Lecture Notes in Math. 337, Springer (1973), 531–538.

contains no cycle of length $k$. This shows the class of obligatory graphs is strictly
smaller than all finite graphs.

be properly colored with a single color, so its chromatic cardinal is at most 1. In
particular, $\chi(H) > \aleph_0$ implies `H` has at least one hyperedge.

declarations.docstring:
**Necessary direction**: every obligatory finite 3-uniform hypergraph is 2-colorable.

This follows from two constructions in [EGH75]. By [EHR73] (see [EGH75, p. 426]) there are
3-uniform hypergraphs of arbitrarily large chromatic number consisting of edge-disjoint
triples, so an obligatory `F` is linear (no two edges share two vertices). By the remark
preceding [EGH75, Theorem 10.9] there are, for every infinite cardinal $\kappa$, 3-uniform
hypergraphs of chromatic number $> \kappa$ all of whose linear sub-hypergraphs are
2-colorable. An obligatory `F` appears in such a hypergraph, hence is 2-colorable.
references: [erdosproblems.com/593](https://www.erdosproblems.com/593)

[EGH75] Erdős, Paul and Galvin, Fred and Hajnal, András, On set-systems having large chromatic number and not containing prescribed subsystems. declarations.docstring:
**Monotonicity of the obligatory property**: If `F₁` appears in `F₂` and `F₂` is obligatory,
then `F₁` is also obligatory.

**Proof:** For any `H` with $\chi(H) > \aleph_0$, since `F₂` is obligatory, `F₂` appears
in `H` via some injection `φ₂`. Since `F₁` appears in `F₂` via `φ₁`, the composition
`φ₂ ∘ φ₁` witnesses that `F₁` appears in `H`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/593](https://www.erdosproblems.com/593)

**Vertices must be uncountable**: Every 3-uniform hypergraph with chromatic cardinal
$> \aleph_0$ must have an uncountable vertex set.

**Proof:** If `V` is countable, there exists an injection `φ : V → ℕ`. Using distinct natural
numbers as colors gives a proper coloring, so $\chi(H) \leq \#\mathbb{N} = \aleph_0$,
contradicting $\chi(H) > \aleph_0$.

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 595 (\$250)**: Is there an infinite graph $G$ which contains no $K_4$ and is
not the union of countably many triangle-free graphs?

A problem of Erdős and Hajnal [Er87].
references: [erdosproblems.com/595](https://www.erdosproblems.com/595)
[Er87] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on set systems and hypergraphs. Extremal problems for finite sets (Visegrád, 1991), Bolyai Soc. Math. Stud. (1994), 217-227.
[Fo70] Folkman, Jon, Graphs with monochromatic complete subgraphs in every edge coloring. SIAM J. Appl. Math. (1970), 19:340-345.

[NeRo75] Nešetřil, Jaroslav and Rödl, Vojtěch, Type theory of partition problems of graphs. Recent advances in graph theory (Proc. Second Czechoslovak Sympos., Prague, 1974), Academia, Prague (1975), 405-412.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ V, ∃ (_ : Infinite V), ∃ G, G.CliqueFree 4 ∧ ¬Erdos595.IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree G

declarations.docstring:
**The complete graph `⊤` on `Fin 4` is not $K_4$-free**: `⊤` on `Fin 4` equals the complete
graph $K_4$, so it contains $K_4$ as a subgraph and is not $K_4$-free.

This sanity check confirms the $K_4$-free hypothesis of Problem 595 is non-trivial.
references: [erdosproblems.com/595](https://www.erdosproblems.com/595)
[Er87] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on set systems and hypergraphs. Extremal problems for finite sets (Visegrád, 1991), Bolyai Soc. Math. Stud. (1994), 217-227.
[Fo70] Folkman, Jon, Graphs with monochromatic complete subgraphs in every edge coloring. SIAM J. Appl. Math. (1970), 19:340-345.

[NeRo75] Nešetřil, Jaroslav and Rödl, Vojtěch, Type theory of partition problems of graphs. Recent advances in graph theory (Proc. Second Czechoslovak Sympos., Prague, 1974), Academia, Prague (1975), 405-412.
declarations.type_pretty: ¬⊤.CliqueFree 4

declarations.docstring:
**The complete graph `⊤` on `ℕ` is a countable union of triangle-free graphs**: we decompose
it into the family of star graphs `{H_m}_{m : ℕ}`, where `H_m` is the graph with edges `{m, n}`
for all `n ≠ m`. Each star is triangle-free (any two non-center vertices share no edge within
the star), and their union covers all edges of `⊤`.

**Proof sketch (star triangle-free):** If `{a, b, c}` were a triangle in `H_m`, then each of
the three edges `{a, b}`, `{a, c}`, `{b, c}` would pass through `m`. In particular, from
`{a, b}` we get `a = m` or `b = m`; from `{b, c}` we get `b = m` or `c = m`. Case analysis
shows that two vertices must equal `m`, contradicting the triangle having three distinct vertices.
references: [erdosproblems.com/595](https://www.erdosproblems.com/595)
[Er87] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on set systems and hypergraphs. Extremal problems for finite sets (Visegrád, 1991), Bolyai Soc. Math. Stud. (1994), 217-227.
[Fo70] Folkman, Jon, Graphs with monochromatic complete subgraphs in every edge coloring. SIAM J. Appl. Math. (1970), 19:340-345.

[NeRo75] Nešetřil, Jaroslav and Rödl, Vojtěch, Type theory of partition problems of graphs. Recent advances in graph theory (Proc. Second Czechoslovak Sympos., Prague, 1974), Academia, Prague (1975), 405-412.
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos595.IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree ⊤

declarations.docstring:
**Folkman–Nešetřil–Rödl (finite version) [Fo70, NeRo75]**: For every `n ≥ 1`, there exists a
graph `G` (on a finite vertex set) that contains no $K_4$ and whose edges cannot be covered by
`n` triangle-free graphs.

More precisely: for every `n : ℕ` with `1 ≤ n`, there exist a finite type `V` and a graph
`G : SimpleGraph V` with:
1. `G.CliqueFree 4` (no $K_4$), and
2. For every family `H : Fin n → SimpleGraph V` of triangle-free graphs, `G ≠ ⨆ i, H i`.

This is the finite analogue of Problem 595. The proofs of Folkman [Fo70] and Nešetřil–Rödl
[NeRo75] give different explicit constructions.
references: [erdosproblems.com/595](https://www.erdosproblems.com/595)
[Er87] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on set systems and hypergraphs. Extremal problems for finite sets (Visegrád, 1991), Bolyai Soc. Math. Stud. (1994), 217-227.
[Fo70] Folkman, Jon, Graphs with monochromatic complete subgraphs in every edge coloring. SIAM J. Appl. Math. (1970), 19:340-345.

[NeRo75] Nešetřil, Jaroslav and Rödl, Vojtěch, Type theory of partition problems of graphs. Recent advances in graph theory (Proc. Second Czechoslovak Sympos., Prague, 1974), Academia, Prague (1975), 405-412.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ),
  1 ≤ n → ∃ V x G, G.CliqueFree 4 ∧ ∀ (H : Fin n → SimpleGraph V), (∀ (i : Fin n), (H i).CliqueFree 3) → G ≠ ⨆ i, H i

declarations.docstring:
**Reformulation via edge colourings**: A graph `G` is a countable union of triangle-free graphs
if and only if there is a colouring of the edges of `G` by `ℕ` such that no monochromatic
triangle exists.

More precisely: `IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree G` is equivalent to the existence of a map
`c : G.edgeSet → ℕ` such that for each `n : ℕ`, the subgraph of edges coloured `n` is triangle-free.
references: [erdosproblems.com/595](https://www.erdosproblems.com/595)
[Er87] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on set systems and hypergraphs. Extremal problems for finite sets (Visegrád, 1991), Bolyai Soc. Math. Stud. (1994), 217-227.
[Fo70] Folkman, Jon, Graphs with monochromatic complete subgraphs in every edge coloring. SIAM J. Appl. Math. (1970), 19:340-345.

[NeRo75] Nešetřil, Jaroslav and Rödl, Vojtěch, Type theory of partition problems of graphs. Recent advances in graph theory (Proc. Second Czechoslovak Sympos., Prague, 1974), Academia, Prague (1975), 405-412.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {V : Type u_1} (G : SimpleGraph V),
  Erdos595.IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree G ↔
    ∃ c, ∀ (n : ℕ), (SimpleGraph.fromEdgeSet {e | ∃ (h : e ∈ G.edgeSet), c ⟨e, h⟩ = n}).CliqueFree 3

declarations.docstring:
**Monotonicity**: If `G` is a countable union of triangle-free graphs and `H ≤ G` (i.e., `H` is
a subgraph of `G`), then `H` is also a countable union of triangle-free graphs.

**Proof**: If `G = ⨆ i, G_i` with each `G_i` triangle-free, then `H = ⨆ i, H ⊓ G_i`.
Each `H ⊓ G_i` is triangle-free because it is a subgraph of `G_i`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/595](https://www.erdosproblems.com/595)
[Er87] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on set systems and hypergraphs. Extremal problems for finite sets (Visegrád, 1991), Bolyai Soc. Math. Stud. (1994), 217-227.
[Fo70] Folkman, Jon, Graphs with monochromatic complete subgraphs in every edge coloring. SIAM J. Appl. Math. (1970), 19:340-345.

[NeRo75] Nešetřil, Jaroslav and Rödl, Vojtěch, Type theory of partition problems of graphs. Recent advances in graph theory (Proc. Second Czechoslovak Sympos., Prague, 1974), Academia, Prague (1975), 405-412.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {V : Type u_1} {G H : SimpleGraph V},
  H ≤ G → Erdos595.IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree G → Erdos595.IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree H

declarations.docstring:
**Triangle-free graphs are trivially countable unions of triangle-free graphs**: if `G` is
already triangle-free, then `G = ⨆ i : ℕ, G_i` where `G_0 = G` and `G_i = ⊥` for `i ≥ 1`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/595](https://www.erdosproblems.com/595)
[Er87] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on set systems and hypergraphs. Extremal problems for finite sets (Visegrád, 1991), Bolyai Soc. Math. Stud. (1994), 217-227.
[Fo70] Folkman, Jon, Graphs with monochromatic complete subgraphs in every edge coloring. SIAM J. Appl. Math. (1970), 19:340-345.

[NeRo75] Nešetřil, Jaroslav and Rödl, Vojtěch, Type theory of partition problems of graphs. Recent advances in graph theory (Proc. Second Czechoslovak Sympos., Prague, 1974), Academia, Prague (1975), 405-412.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {V : Type u_1} (G : SimpleGraph V), G.CliqueFree 3 → Erdos595.IsCountableUnionOfTriangleFree G

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 596** (Erdős–Hajnal, [Er87]). For which graph pairs $(G_1, G_2)$ is it
true that

  (1) for every $n \geq 1$ there is a graph $H$ without a $G_1$ such that any
      $n$-colouring of $H$'s edges contains a monochromatic $G_2$, and yet
  (2) for every graph $H$ without a $G_1$ there is an $\aleph_0$-colouring of $H$'s edges
      with no monochromatic $G_2$?

Erdős and Hajnal originally conjectured that no such pair exists; but $(C_4, C_6)$
witnesses it (Nešetřil–Rödl + Erdős–Hajnal). The full question is to characterise the
class of all such pairs, recorded here as the unknown `erdos_596.answer`.

See Problem 595 for the specific case $(G_1, G_2) = (K_4, K_3)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/596](https://www.erdosproblems.com/596)
[Er87] Erdős, *Some of my favourite problems in various branches of combinatorics*, *Mat. Lapok* 1987.
[NeRo75] Nešetřil and Rödl, *The Ramsey property for graphs with forbidden complete subgraphs*, *J. Combin. Theory* B **20** (1976), 243--249.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {U₁ U₂ : Type} (G₁ : SimpleGraph U₁) (G₂ : SimpleGraph U₂),
  G₁.IsErdosHajnalExceptional G₂ ↔ Erdos596.erdos_596.answer G₁ G₂

cannot be $n$-coloured without a monochromatic $C_6$.

Every $C_4$-free graph is a countable union of trees (Erdős–Hajnal [Er87]); trees are

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 597** [Er87]. Let $G$ be a graph on at most $\aleph_1$
vertices which contains no $K_4$ and no $K_{\aleph_0,\aleph_0}$ (the complete bipartite
graph with $\aleph_0$ vertices in each class). Is it true that
$$\omega_1^2 \to (\omega_1 \omega, G)^2?$$

colouring of the edges of the complete graph on $\omega_1^2$ there is either a red clique
of order type $\omega_1 \cdot \omega$ or a blue triangle.

Let $m$ be an infinite cardinal and $\kappa$ be the successor cardinal of $2^{\aleph_0}$.
Can one colour the countable subsets of $m$ using $\kappa$ many colours so that every
$X \subseteq m$ with $|X| = \kappa$ contains subsets of all possible colours?

declarations.docstring:
Does every graph on $n$ vertices with $>\mathrm{ex}(n;C_4)$ edges contain $\gg n^{1/2}$ many
copies of $C_4$?

[HeMaYa21] He, J. and Ma, J. and Yang, T., *Some extremal results on 4-cycles*. Journal of Combinatorial Theory B (2021).

  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) [inst : DecidableRel G.Adj],
      SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card →
        c * √↑n ≤ ↑{H' | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4)}.ncard

declarations.docstring:
He, Ma, and Yang [HeMaYa21] proved the conjecture when $n = q^2 + q + 1$ for some $q = 2^k$: they
showed that for large even $q$ every graph on $q^2 + q + 1$ vertices with
$\frac{1}{2}q(q+1)^2 + 1$ edges contains at least $q - 1$ copies of $C_4$, and
$\mathrm{ex}(q^2 + q + 1; C_4) = \frac{1}{2}q(q+1)^2$ when $q = 2^k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/60](https://www.erdosproblems.com/60)
[HeMaYa21] He, J. and Ma, J. and Yang, T., *Some extremal results on 4-cycles*. Journal of Combinatorial Theory B (2021).

∃ c > 0,
  ∀ (q : ℕ),

      ∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin (q ^ 2 + q + 1))) [inst : DecidableRel G.Adj],
        SimpleGraph.extremalNumber (q ^ 2 + q + 1) (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4) < G.edgeFinset.card →
          c * √(↑q ^ 2 + ↑q + 1) ≤ ↑{H' | Nonempty (H'.coe ≃g SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4)}.ncard

declarations.docstring: Let $r \geq 2$. Is it true that $e(n,r+1) - e(n,r) \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$?

[erdosproblems.com/80](https://www.erdosproblems.com/80)

True ↔

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 601** ($500 prize).

For which limit ordinals $\alpha$ does `HasPathOrIndepSetOfType α` hold?
references: [erdosproblems.com/601](https://www.erdosproblems.com/601)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (α : Ordinal.{0}), Order.IsSuccLimit α → (Erdos601.HasPathOrIndepSetOfType α ↔ Erdos601.erdos_601.answer α)

declarations.docstring:
**Base case $\alpha = \omega$**: `HasPathOrIndepSetOfType ω` holds.

Every countably infinite graph on vertex set $\omega$ either contains an infinite path or
has an infinite independent set (and an infinite set has order type $\omega$). Follows from
Ramsey-theoretic arguments (or directly from the Erdős–Hajnal–Milner result since
$\omega < \omega_1^{\omega+2}$).
references: [erdosproblems.com/601](https://www.erdosproblems.com/601)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos601.HasPathOrIndepSetOfType Ordinal.omega0

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős–Hajnal–Milner (1970)** [EHM70]: For all limit ordinals $\alpha < \omega_1^{\omega+2}$,
every graph on $\alpha.\mathrm{ToType}$ has either an infinite path or an independent set of
order type $\alpha$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/601](https://www.erdosproblems.com/601)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (α : Ordinal.{0}),
  Order.IsSuccLimit α → α < Ordinal.omega 1 ^ (Ordinal.omega0 + 2) → Erdos601.HasPathOrIndepSetOfType α

**Erdős–Hajnal–Milner conjecture at $\omega_1^{\omega+2}$** [Er81, Section VII]: every
graph on $\omega_1^{\omega+2}$ contains an infinite path or an independent set of that
order type. Erdős conjectured the positive answer. This is the first limit ordinal not
covered by the Erdős–Hajnal–Milner theorem.
references: [erdosproblems.com/601](https://www.erdosproblems.com/601)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos601.HasPathOrIndepSetOfType (Ordinal.omega 1 ^ (Ordinal.omega0 + 2))

**Erdős–Hajnal–Milner conjecture** [Er81, Section VII]: every graph on a limit ordinal
$\alpha$ contains an infinite path or an independent set of order type $\alpha$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/601](https://www.erdosproblems.com/601)

declarations.docstring:
Formal disproof of `disjoint_without_infinite_claim`.

**Counterexample:** Take `α = ℕ`, `I = Fin 2`, with `A 0 = {0}` and `A 1 = {1}`.
These are pairwise disjoint, satisfying the only hypothesis. But singleton sets
are vacuously monochromatic under any colouring: the only pair `(x, y) ∈ {0} × {0}`
is `(0, 0)`, and `f 0 = f 0` trivially. So any colouring makes `A 0` monochromatic,
meaning `HasPropertyB` fails.
references: [erdosproblems.com/602](https://www.erdosproblems.com/602)
declarations.type_pretty: ¬Erdos602.disjoint_without_infinite_claim

declarations.docstring:
Does every almost-disjoint family of countably infinite sets whose pairwise
intersections all have size ≠ 1 have Property B?

Formally: let `α` be any type, let `(A_i)_{i ∈ I}` be a family of countably infinite subsets
of `α` such that for all `i ≠ j`, the intersection `A_i ∩ A_j` is finite and
`|A_i ∩ A_j| ≠ 1`. Does there exist a 2-colouring `f : α → Fin 2` such that no `A_i` is
monochromatic?

This is an open question about Property B for almost-disjoint families with a
forbidden intersection size of 1.

**Note:** This generalises the formulation in which the ground set is `ℕ`. Since every
countably infinite set is in bijection with `ℕ`, the two formulations are equivalent, but
working over an arbitrary ground type makes the statement apply immediately to, e.g.,
almost-disjoint families of countable subsets of an uncountable space.
references: [erdosproblems.com/602](https://www.erdosproblems.com/602)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {I : Type u_2} (A : I → Set α),
  (∀ (i : I), (A i).Countable ∧ (A i).Infinite) →
    (∀ (i j : I), i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).Finite) → (∀ (i j : I), i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).ncard ≠ 1) → Erdos602.HasPropertyB I A

declarations.docstring:
**Countable index set case.**

If the index set is countable, the answer is yes, and the intersection
condition is unnecessary. This is Bernstein's Lemma:
every countable system of infinite sets has Property B.
references: [erdosproblems.com/602](https://www.erdosproblems.com/602)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (A : ℕ → Set α),
  (∀ (i : ℕ), (A i).Countable ∧ (A i).Infinite) →
    (∀ (i j : ℕ), i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).Finite) → (∀ (i j : ℕ), i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).ncard ≠ 1) → Erdos602.HasPropertyB ℕ A

declarations.docstring:
**Trivial case: pairwise disjoint families.**

If the `A_i` are pairwise disjoint (all intersections are empty, which in
particular satisfies `|A_i ∩ A_j| ≠ 1`), then Property B holds trivially.

**Proof sketch:** Since each `A_i` is infinite, it has (at least) two distinct elements
`a_i` and `b_i`. We can define a colouring that assigns colour 0 to `a_i` and colour 1
to `b_i` for each `i` (using disjointness, these choices don't conflict), and extend
arbitrarily elsewhere. Then no `A_i` is monochromatic.
references: [erdosproblems.com/602](https://www.erdosproblems.com/602)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {I : Type u_2} (A : I → Set α),
  (∀ (i : I), (A i).Infinite) → (∀ (i j : I), i ≠ j → Disjoint (A i) (A j)) → Erdos602.HasPropertyB I A

declarations.docstring:
**Empty index set.**

If the index set `I` is empty (has no elements), then Property B holds vacuously:
any 2-colouring works, since there are no sets to be made non-monochromatic.
references: [erdosproblems.com/602](https://www.erdosproblems.com/602)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (A : PEmpty.{u_2 + 1} → Set α),
  (∀ (i : PEmpty.{u_2 + 1}), (A i).Infinite) → Erdos602.HasPropertyB PEmpty.{u_2 + 1} A

declarations.docstring:
**Intersections of size ≥ 2 suffice.**

For a single countably infinite set `A ⊆ α`, there trivially exists a 2-colouring
of `α` that makes `A` non-monochromatic: since `A` is infinite, it has two distinct
elements, so any colouring that assigns them different colours works.
references: [erdosproblems.com/602](https://www.erdosproblems.com/602)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (A : Set α), A.Infinite → ∃ f, ¬Erdos602.IsMonochromatic f A

declarations.docstring:
**Two infinite sets with pairwise intersection of size ≠ 1.**

If the family consists of exactly two countably infinite sets `A₀` and `A₁` with
`|A₀ ∩ A₁| ≠ 1` (and finite), then Property B holds.

**Proof sketch:**
- If `A₀ ∩ A₁ = ∅`: the sets are disjoint. Pick distinct `a, b ∈ A₀` and distinct
  `c, d ∈ A₁`. Colour `b` and `c` with 1, everything else with 0. Then `A₀` has
  `a` (colour 0) and `b` (colour 1), and `A₁` has `c` (colour 1) and `d` (colour 0),
  so neither is monochromatic.
- If `|A₀ ∩ A₁| ≥ 2`: the intersection contains two distinct points `x` and `y`.
  Assign `x` colour 0 and `y` colour 1. Both `A₀` and `A₁` contain `x` and `y`,
  so neither is monochromatic.
references: [erdosproblems.com/602](https://www.erdosproblems.com/602)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {α : Type u_1} (A : Fin 2 → Set α),
  (∀ (i : Fin 2), (A i).Infinite) → (A 0 ∩ A 1).Finite → (A 0 ∩ A 1).ncard ≠ 1 → Erdos602.HasPropertyB (Fin 2) A

declarations.docstring:
**Unique index set.**

If the index set has exactly one element (i.e., `[Unique I]`), then Property B holds:
any 2-colouring that makes the single set `A (default : I)` non-monochromatic works.
This follows from the single-set case.
references: [erdosproblems.com/602](https://www.erdosproblems.com/602)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {α : Type u_1} (I : Type u_2) [Unique I] (A : I → Set α), (∀ (i : I), (A i).Infinite) → Erdos602.HasPropertyB I A

declarations.docstring:
Given $n$ distinct points $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$, must there be a point $x\in A$ such that
$$\#\{ d(x,y) : y \in A\} \gg n^{1-o(1)}?$$

This is the pinned distance problem, a stronger form of Problem 89. Here $n^{1-o(1)}$ means: for
every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all large $n$, the bound is at least $n^{1-\varepsilon}$. We do not
count the distance $d(x, x) = 0$; this changes the count by one.

This weak formulation was proved by OpenAI [OAI26].

Let $d(x)$ be the number of distinct distances from $x$ to the other points of $A$. Erdős [Er75f]
conjectured that
$$\sum_{x\in A}d(x) \gg \frac{n^2}{\sqrt{\log n}}$$
for every set $A\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of $n$ points.

The sum is at most $n$ times the largest $d(x)$, so this conjecture implies a positive answer to
`Erdos604.erdos_604.variants.sqrt_log`.

The integer grid shows that $\frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}$ would be best possible: there are sets of
$n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ in which every point has $O(\frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}})$ distinct
distances to the other points. This follows from the bound of Erdős [Er46] on the total number of
distinct distances in the grid (see Erdős Problem 89), since the number of distances from one point
is at most the total number of distances. For $n$ that is not a square, take $n$ points of the
smallest square grid with at least $n$ points.

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n,k)$ be minimal such that there is a graph with $n$ vertices and $f(n,k)$ edges
where every set of $k+2$ vertices induces a subgraph with maximum degree at least $k$.
Determine $f(n,k)$.

[A problem on sparse induced subgraphs](https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~erdosproblems/erdos/newproblems/SparseInducedSubgraphs.html)

  IsLeast
    {m |
      ∃ G,
        G.edgeFinset.card = m ∧ ∀ (s : Finset (Fin n)), s.card = k + 2 → ∃ v, k ≤ (SimpleGraph.induce (↑s) G).degree v}

declarations.docstring:
Let $r\geq 3$. For an $r$-uniform hypergraph $G$ let $\tau(G)$ denote the covering number (or
transversal number), the minimum size of a set of vertices which includes at least one from each
edge in $G$. Determine the best possible $t$ such that, if $G$ is an $r$-uniform hypergraph $G$
where every subgraph $G'$ on at most $3r-3$ vertices has $\tau(G')\leq 1$, we have $\tau(G)\leq t$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/616](https://www.erdosproblems.com/616)
[EHT91] Erdős, Paul and Hajnal, András and Tuza, Zsolt, Local constraints ensuring small representing sets. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1991), 78-84.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (r : ℕ), 3 ≤ r → Hypergraph.localTransversalBound r (3 * r - 3) 1 = Erdos616.erdos_616.answer r

declarations.docstring:
Let $r\geq 3$. If the edges of $K_{r^2+1}$ are $r$-coloured then there exist $r+1$ vertices with at
least one colour missing on the edges of the induced $K_{r+1}$.

In other words, there is no balanced colouring.

A conjecture of Erdős and Gyárfás [ErGy99].
references: [erdosproblems.com/617](https://www.erdosproblems.com/617)
[ErGy99](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0012-365X(98)00323-9) Erdős, Paul and Gyárfás, András, Split and balanced colorings of complete graphs. Discrete Math. (1999), 79-86.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ r ≥ 3,
  ∀ {V : Type} [inst : Fintype V] [DecidableEq V],
    Fintype.card V = r ^ 2 + 1 →
      ∀ (coloring : Sym2 V → Fin r), ∃ S k, S.card = r + 1 ∧ ∀ u ∈ S, ∀ v ∈ S, u ≠ v → coloring s(u, v) ≠ k

declarations.docstring:
Let $X$ be a set of cardinality $\aleph_\omega$ and $f$ be a function from the finite subsets of
$X$ to $X$ such that $f(A)\not\in A$ for all $A$. Must there exist an infinite $Y\subseteq X$
that is independent - that is, for all finite $B\subset Y$ we have $f(B)\not\in Y$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/623](https://www.erdosproblems.com/623)

∀ (X : Type u),
  Cardinal.mk X = Cardinal.aleph Ordinal.omega0 →
    ∀ (f : Finset X → X), (∀ (A : Finset X), f A ∉ A) → ∃ Y, Y.Infinite ∧ ∀ (B : Finset X), ↑B ⊆ Y → f B ∉ Y

$f:\{A : A\subseteq X\}\to X$ so that for every $Y\subseteq X$ with $\lvert Y\rvert \geq H(n)$

declarations.docstring:
Let $k \geq 4$ and let $g_k(n)$ denote the largest $m$ such that there is a graph on $n$
vertices with chromatic number $k$ and girth $> m$ (i.e. containing no cycle of length
$\leq m$). Does
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{g_k(n)}{\log n}$$
exist?

By `Erdos626.erdos_626.variants.kostochka` and `Erdos626.erdos_626.variants.erdos_upper`, the
limit, if it exists, is a positive real number.
references: [erdosproblems.com/626](https://www.erdosproblems.com/626)
[Er59b] Erdős, P., *Graph theory and probability*. Canadian J. Math. (1959), 34-38.
[Er62b] Erdős, P., *On circuits and subgraphs of chromatic graphs*. Mathematika (1962), 170-175.
[Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
[Ko88] Kostochka, A. V., *Upper bounds on the chromatic number of graphs*. Trudy Inst. Mat. (Novosibirsk) (1988), 204-226, 265.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 4 ≤ k → ∃ L, Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos626.g k n) / Real.log ↑n) Filter.atTop (nhds L)

Let $h^{(m)}(n)$ be the maximal chromatic number of a graph on $n$ vertices with girth $> m$.
Does
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log h^{(m)}(n)}{\log n}$$
exist, and what is its value? The value is asked for in
`Erdos626.erdos_626.variants.h_odd_conjecture` and `Erdos626.erdos_626.variants.h_even_conjecture`.

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er59b] proved that for $k \geq 4$
$$g_k(n) \leq \frac{2}{\log(k-2)}\log n + 1.$$
We state it for all sufficiently large $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/626](https://www.erdosproblems.com/626)
[Er59b] Erdős, P., *Graph theory and probability*. Canadian J. Math. (1959), 34-38.
[Er62b] Erdős, P., *On circuits and subgraphs of chromatic graphs*. Mathematika (1962), 170-175.
[Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
[Ko88] Kostochka, A. V., *Upper bounds on the chromatic number of graphs*. Trudy Inst. Mat. (Novosibirsk) (1988), 204-226, 265.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 4 ≤ k → ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos626.g k n) ≤ 2 * Real.log ↑n / Real.log (↑k - 2) + 1

declarations.docstring:
For even $m$, Erdős had no good guess for the value of the limit, other than that it should
lie in $\left[\frac{2}{m+2}, \frac{2}{m}\right]$. He could not prove this even for $m = 4$.

The existence of the limit is open, so we state the claim for the lower and upper limits: for
every $\varepsilon > 0$, eventually
$n^{2/(m+2) - \varepsilon} \leq h^{(m)}(n) \leq n^{2/m + \varepsilon}$. We require $m \geq 2$,
since $2/m$ is undefined for $m = 0$. The upper half is known: girth $> m$ implies girth
$> m - 1$, so $h^{(m)}(n) \leq h^{(m-1)}(n)$, and `Erdos626.erdos_626.variants.h_upper_odd` for
the odd number $m - 1$ gives the exponent $2/m$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/626](https://www.erdosproblems.com/626)
[Er59b] Erdős, P., *Graph theory and probability*. Canadian J. Math. (1959), 34-38.
[Er62b] Erdős, P., *On circuits and subgraphs of chromatic graphs*. Mathematika (1962), 170-175.
[Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
[Ko88] Kostochka, A. V., *Upper bounds on the chromatic number of graphs*. Trudy Inst. Mat. (Novosibirsk) (1988), 204-226, 265.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (m : ℕ),
  Even m →
    2 ≤ m →
      ∀ ε > 0,
        ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑n ^ (2 / (↑m + 2) - ε) ≤ ↑(Erdos626.h m n) ∧ ↑(Erdos626.h m n) ≤ ↑n ^ (2 / ↑m + ε)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er59b] proved that
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log h^{(m)}(n)}{\log n} \gg \frac{1}{m}.$$
The existence of the limit is open, so we state the lower bound for the lower limit: there is
an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that for every $m \geq 1$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, eventually
$h^{(m)}(n) \geq n^{c/m - \varepsilon}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/626](https://www.erdosproblems.com/626)
[Er59b] Erdős, P., *Graph theory and probability*. Canadian J. Math. (1959), 34-38.
[Er62b] Erdős, P., *On circuits and subgraphs of chromatic graphs*. Mathematika (1962), 170-175.
[Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
[Ko88] Kostochka, A. V., *Upper bounds on the chromatic number of graphs*. Trudy Inst. Mat. (Novosibirsk) (1988), 204-226, 265.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c > 0, ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑n ^ (c / ↑m - ε) ≤ ↑(Erdos626.h m n)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős conjectured that the bound in `Erdos626.erdos_626.variants.h_upper_odd` is sharp: for
odd $m$,
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log h^{(m)}(n)}{\log n} = \frac{2}{m+1}.$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/626](https://www.erdosproblems.com/626)
[Er59b] Erdős, P., *Graph theory and probability*. Canadian J. Math. (1959), 34-38.
[Er62b] Erdős, P., *On circuits and subgraphs of chromatic graphs*. Mathematika (1962), 170-175.
[Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
[Ko88] Kostochka, A. V., *Upper bounds on the chromatic number of graphs*. Trudy Inst. Mat. (Novosibirsk) (1988), 204-226, 265.

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er59b] proved that for odd $m$
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log h^{(m)}(n)}{\log n} \leq \frac{2}{m+1}.$$
The existence of the limit is open, so we state the bound for the upper limit: for every
$\varepsilon > 0$, eventually $h^{(m)}(n) \leq n^{2/(m+1) + \varepsilon}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/626](https://www.erdosproblems.com/626)
[Er59b] Erdős, P., *Graph theory and probability*. Canadian J. Math. (1959), 34-38.
[Er62b] Erdős, P., *On circuits and subgraphs of chromatic graphs*. Mathematika (1962), 170-175.
[Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
[Ko88] Kostochka, A. V., *Upper bounds on the chromatic number of graphs*. Trudy Inst. Mat. (Novosibirsk) (1988), 204-226, 265.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (m : ℕ), Odd m → ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos626.h m n) ≤ ↑n ^ (2 / (↑m + 1) + ε)

declarations.docstring:
Kostochka [Ko88] proved that for $k \geq 4$
$$g_k(n) \geq \frac{1}{4\log k}\log n.$$
Kostochka's theorem gives this lower bound for the girth itself, and $g_k(n)$ is one less than the
largest possible girth, so the inequality above holds only up to $1$. The statement below is a
consequence of his theorem, not the theorem itself: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all
sufficiently large $n$, $g_k(n) \geq \left(\frac{1}{4\log k} - \varepsilon\right)\log n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/626](https://www.erdosproblems.com/626)
[Er59b] Erdős, P., *Graph theory and probability*. Canadian J. Math. (1959), 34-38.
[Er62b] Erdős, P., *On circuits and subgraphs of chromatic graphs*. Mathematika (1962), 170-175.
[Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
[Ko88] Kostochka, A. V., *Upper bounds on the chromatic number of graphs*. Trudy Inst. Mat. (Novosibirsk) (1988), 204-226, 265.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 4 ≤ k → ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (1 / (4 * Real.log ↑k) - ε) * Real.log ↑n ≤ ↑(Erdos626.g k n)

declarations.docstring:
Every cycle has length at least $3$, so for $m \leq 2$ the girth condition is vacuous and
$h^{(m)}(n) = n$.

declarations.docstring:
Let $\omega(G)$ denote the clique number of $G$ and $\chi(G)$ the chromatic number. If $f(n)$ is
the maximum value of $\chi(G)/\omega(G)$, as $G$ ranges over all graphs on $n$ vertices, then
does
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{f(n)}{n/(\log_2n)^2}$$
exist?

Since $f(n) \asymp n/(\log_2 n)^2$ (see `Erdos627.erdos_627.variants.theta`), the limit, if it
exists, is a finite real number.
references: [erdosproblems.com/627](https://www.erdosproblems.com/627)
[AFM25] Araujo, I. and Filipe, R. and Miyazaki, R., *A note on the maximum ratio between chromatic number and clique number*. arXiv:2512.16062 (2025).
[Er61d] Erdős, P., *Graph theory and probability. II*. Canadian J. Math. (1961), 346-352.
[Er67c] Erdős, P., *Some remarks on chromatic graphs*. Colloq. Math. (1967), 253-256.
[Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
[My55] Mycielski, J., *Sur le coloriage des graphs*. Colloquium Mathematicum 3 (1955), 161–162. [doi:10.4064/cm-3-2-161-162](https://doi.org/10.4064/cm-3-2-161-162)
[Zy52] Zykov, A. A., *On some properties of linear complexes*. Amer. Math. Soc. Translation (1952), 33.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ L, Filter.Tendsto (fun n => Erdos627.maxChromaticCliqueRatio n / (↑n / Real.logb 2 ↑n ^ 2)) Filter.atTop (nhds L)

declarations.docstring:
Araujo, Filipe, and Miyazaki [AFM25, Theorem 1.3] improved the upper bound to
$$f(n) \leq (3.71943 + o(1)) \frac{n}{(\log_2 n)^2},$$
using recent improvements in the asymptotics of Ramsey numbers. [AFM25] is an arXiv preprint.

[Er67c] Erdős, P., *Some remarks on chromatic graphs*. Colloq. Math. (1967), 253-256.
[Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
[My55] Mycielski, J., *Sur le coloriage des graphs*. Colloquium Mathematicum 3 (1955), 161–162. [doi:10.4064/cm-3-2-161-162](https://doi.org/10.4064/cm-3-2-161-162)
[Zy52] Zykov, A. A., *On some properties of linear complexes*. Amer. Math. Soc. Translation (1952), 33.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos627.maxChromaticCliqueRatio n ≤ (3.71943 + ε) * (↑n / Real.logb 2 ↑n ^ 2)

declarations.docstring:
Araujo, Filipe, and Miyazaki [AFM25, Theorem 1.2]: suppose that $R(s,t) \leq R(k)$ for all
$s, t, k \in \mathbb{N}$ with $st \leq k^2$ (their Conjecture 1.1), and that
$\lim_{k \to \infty} \frac{\log_2 R(k)}{k}$ exists and equals $\ell$. Then
$$f(n) = (\ell^2 + o(1)) \frac{n}{(\log_2 n)^2},$$
so the limit in `Erdos627.erdos_627` exists and equals $\ell^2$. Here $R(s,t)$ is the
two-colour Ramsey number and $R(k) = R(k,k)$ (see [77]). [AFM25] is an arXiv preprint.
references: [erdosproblems.com/627](https://www.erdosproblems.com/627)
[AFM25] Araujo, I. and Filipe, R. and Miyazaki, R., *A note on the maximum ratio between chromatic number and clique number*. arXiv:2512.16062 (2025).
[Er61d] Erdős, P., *Graph theory and probability. II*. Canadian J. Math. (1961), 346-352.
[Er67c] Erdős, P., *Some remarks on chromatic graphs*. Colloq. Math. (1967), 253-256.
[Er69b] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in chromatic graph theory*. Proof Techniques in Graph Theory (Proc. Second Ann Arbor Graph Theory Conf., Ann Arbor, Mich., 1968) (1969), 27-35.
[My55] Mycielski, J., *Sur le coloriage des graphs*. Colloquium Mathematicum 3 (1955), 161–162. [doi:10.4064/cm-3-2-161-162](https://doi.org/10.4064/cm-3-2-161-162)
[Zy52] Zykov, A. A., *On some properties of linear complexes*. Amer. Math. Soc. Translation (1952), 33.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (ℓ : ℝ),
  (∀ (s t k : ℕ), s * t ≤ k ^ 2 → SimpleGraph.classicalRamsey s t ≤ SimpleGraph.diagonalRamsey k) →
    Filter.Tendsto (fun k => Real.logb 2 ↑(SimpleGraph.diagonalRamsey k) / ↑k) Filter.atTop (nhds ℓ) →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n => Erdos627.maxChromaticCliqueRatio n / (↑n / Real.logb 2 ↑n ^ 2)) Filter.atTop
        (nhds (ℓ ^ 2))

Erdős [Er61d] proved that for every (large) $n$ there is a graph on $n$ vertices with
$\omega(G) = 2$ and
$$\chi(G) \gg \frac{n^{1/2}}{\log n},$$
whence $f(n) \gg n^{1/2}/\log n$.

$\omega(G) = 2$ and $\chi(G) = k$.

We require $k \geq 2$: a graph with $\omega(G) = 2$ has an edge, so $\chi(G) \geq 2$.

declarations.docstring:
Let $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $k$ containing no $K_k$. If $a,b\geq 2$ and $a+b=k+1$
then must there exist two disjoint subgraphs of $G$ with chromatic numbers $\geq a$ and $\geq b$
respectively?
references: [erdosproblems.com/628](https://www.erdosproblems.com/628)
[BKPS09] Balogh, József and Kostochka, Alexandr V. and Prince, Noah and Stiebitz, Michael, *The Erdős-Lovász Tihany conjecture for quasi-line graphs*. Discrete Math. (2009), 3985-3991.
[BrJu69] Brown, W. G. and Jung, H. A., *On odd circuits in chromatic graphs*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1969), 129-134.
[Er68b] Erdős, P., *Problem 2*. Theory of Graphs (1968), 361.
[So22] Song, Zi-Xia, *A survey on the Erdős-Lovász Tihany conjecture*. Adv. Math. (China) (2022), 259--274.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (V : Type u_1) [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ),
  G.chromaticNumber = ↑k →
    G.CliqueFree k →
      ∀ (a b : ℕ),
        a ≥ 2 →
          b ≥ 2 →
            a + b = k + 1 →
              ∃ s, (SimpleGraph.induce s G).chromaticNumber ≥ ↑a ∧ (SimpleGraph.induce sᶜ G).chromaticNumber ≥ ↑b

              b ≥ 2 →
                a + b = k + 1 →

declarations.docstring:
The list chromatic number $\chi_L(G)$ is defined to be the minimal $k$ such that for any
assignment of a list of $k$ colours to each vertex of $G$ (perhaps different lists for different
vertices) a colouring of each vertex by a colour on its list can be chosen such that adjacent
vertices receive distinct colours.

Determine the minimal number of vertices $n(k)$ of a bipartite graph $G$ such that
$\chi_L(G)>k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/629](https://www.erdosproblems.com/629)

[ERT80] Erdős, Paul and Rubin, Arthur L. and Taylor, Herbert, *Choosability in graphs*. Proceedings of the West Coast Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory and Computing (1979), Congress. Numer. XXVI (1980), 125-157. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-07.pdf)
[HMT96] Hanson, Denis and MacGillivray, Gary and Toft, Bjarne, *Choosability of bipartite graphs*. Ars Combin. (1996), 183-192.
[RaSr00] Radhakrishnan, Jaikumar and Srinivasan, Aravind, *Improved bounds and algorithms for hypergraph $2$-coloring*. Random Structures Algorithms (2000), 4-32.
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos629.n = Erdos629.erdos_629.answer

declarations.docstring:
A problem of Erdős, Rubin, and Taylor [ERT80], who proved that
$$2^{k-1}<n(k) <k^22^{k+2}.$$

The chain of inequalities in [ERT80, p. 129] needs $k \geq 2$, since $m(1) = 1 = 2^0$; for
$k = 1$ the claim holds because $n(1) = 2$. The case $k = 0$ is degenerate ($n(0) = 1$).
references: [erdosproblems.com/629](https://www.erdosproblems.com/629)

[ERT80] Erdős, Paul and Rubin, Arthur L. and Taylor, Herbert, *Choosability in graphs*. Proceedings of the West Coast Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory and Computing (1979), Congress. Numer. XXVI (1980), 125-157. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-07.pdf)

Hanson, MacGillivray, and Toft [HMT96] proved
$$n(k) \leq kn(k-2)+2^k.$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/629](https://www.erdosproblems.com/629)

declarations.docstring: Hanson, MacGillivray, and Toft [HMT96] proved $n(3)=14$.

declarations.docstring:
They also prove that if $m(k)$ is the size of the smallest family of $k$-sets without property B
(i.e. the smallest number of $k$-sets in a graph with chromatic number $3$) then
$m(k)\leq n(k)\leq m(k+1)$.

[ERT80, p. 129] prints the upper bound as $2m(k)$; we state that form. Here $m(k)$ is
`Hypergraph.minChromaticEdges k 3`, as in Erdős Problem 901. We assume $k \geq 2$: for $k = 1$
this is `⊤`, since singleton edges admit no proper colouring, whereas $m(1) = 1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/629](https://www.erdosproblems.com/629)

[ERT80] Erdős, Paul and Rubin, Arthur L. and Taylor, Herbert, *Choosability in graphs*. Proceedings of the West Coast Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory and Computing (1979), Congress. Numer. XXVI (1980), 125-157. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-07.pdf)
[HMT96] Hanson, Denis and MacGillivray, Gary and Toft, Bjarne, *Choosability of bipartite graphs*. Ars Combin. (1996), 183-192.
[RaSr00] Radhakrishnan, Jaikumar and Srinivasan, Aravind, *Improved bounds and algorithms for hypergraph $2$-coloring*. Random Structures Algorithms (2000), 4-32.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  2 ≤ k →
    (Hypergraph.minChromaticEdges k 3).toNat ≤ Erdos629.n k ∧
      Erdos629.n k ≤ 2 * (Hypergraph.minChromaticEdges k 3).toNat

declarations.docstring:
The lower bounds on $m(k)$ by Radhakrishnan and Srinivasan [RaSr00] imply that
$$2^k \left(\frac{k}{\log k}\right)^{1/2}\ll n(k).$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/629](https://www.erdosproblems.com/629)

[ERT80] Erdős, Paul and Rubin, Arthur L. and Taylor, Herbert, *Choosability in graphs*. Proceedings of the West Coast Conference on Combinatorics, Graph Theory and Computing (1979), Congress. Numer. XXVI (1980), 125-157. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-07.pdf)

[RaSr00] Radhakrishnan, Jaikumar and Srinivasan, Aravind, *Improved bounds and algorithms for hypergraph $2$-coloring*. Random Structures Algorithms (2000), 4-32.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, c * 2 ^ k * √(↑k / Real.log ↑k) ≤ ↑(Erdos629.n k)

declarations.docstring: Any bipartite graph $G$ on $m$ vertices with $\chi_L(G) > k$ gives $n(k) \leq m$.

Does every finite graph with minimum degree at least $3$
contain a cycle of length $2^k$ for some $k \geq 2$?

declarations.docstring:
For every $k \geq 3$, does there exist $f(k)$ such that every finite graph of chromatic
number at least $f(k)$ has an odd cycle whose vertices induce a graph of chromatic
number at least $k$? The cycle may have chords in the ambient graph.
references: [erdosproblems.com/640](https://www.erdosproblems.com/640)
[Er97d] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent problems and results in graph theory*. Discrete Math. (1997), 81–85, p.84.

∀ (k : ℕ),
  3 ≤ k → ∃ N, ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), ↑N ≤ G.chromaticNumber → Erdos640.HasHighChromaticOddCycle G k

declarations.docstring:
Every finite graph of chromatic number at least $3$ has an odd cycle whose vertices
induce a graph of chromatic number at least $3$.

[Er97d] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent problems and results in graph theory*. Discrete Math. (1997), 81–85, p.84.

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be the maximal number of edges in a graph on $n$ vertices such that all cycles have more
vertices than chords. Is it true that $f(n)\ll n$?

A problem of Hamburger and Szegedy. A chord is an edge between two vertices of the cycle which are
not consecutive in the cycle.
references: [erdosproblems.com/642](https://www.erdosproblems.com/642)

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n;t)$ be minimal such that if a $t$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices contains at least
$f(n;t)$ edges then there must be four edges $A,B,C,D$ such that
$$A\cup B= C\cup D$$
and
$$A\cap B=C\cap D=\emptyset.$$
Estimate $f(n;t)$ - in particular, is it true that for $t\geq 3$
$$f(n;t)=(1+o(1))\binom{n}{t-1}?$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/643](https://www.erdosproblems.com/643)
[Fu84] F\"uredi, Z., Hypergraphs in which all disjoint pairs have distinct unions. Combinatorica (1984), 161--168.
[PiVe09] Pikhurko, Oleg and Verstra\"{e}te, Jacques, The maximum size of hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2009), 637--649.
[HMY26] Huang, Hao, Ma, Jie, and Yang, Tianchi, *Extremal hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles*. [arXiv:2609.37744](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37744) (2026), Theorem 1.2.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (t : ℕ),
  1 ≤ t →
    Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ↑(Erdos643.forcingThreshold n t))
      (Erdos643.erdos_643.parts.i.answer t)

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that $f(n;t)=(1+o(1))\binom{n}{t-1}$ for $t\geq 3$?

For $t\geq4$, Huang, Ma, and Yang [HMY26] prove the exact extremal formula below.
The case $t=3$ remains open.
references: [erdosproblems.com/643](https://www.erdosproblems.com/643)
[Fu84] F\"uredi, Z., Hypergraphs in which all disjoint pairs have distinct unions. Combinatorica (1984), 161--168.
[PiVe09] Pikhurko, Oleg and Verstra\"{e}te, Jacques, The maximum size of hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2009), 637--649.
[HMY26] Huang, Hao, Ma, Jie, and Yang, Tianchi, *Extremal hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles*. [arXiv:2609.37744](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37744) (2026), Theorem 1.2.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (t : ℕ),
  3 ≤ t → Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ↑(Erdos643.forcingThreshold n t)) fun n => ↑(n.choose (t - 1))

declarations.docstring:
Huang, Ma, and Yang [HMY26, Theorem 1.2] determine the maximum size of an avoiding family
for each fixed $t\geq4$ and all sufficiently large $n$:
$$\binom{n-1}{t-1}+\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{t}\right\rfloor.$$
The forcing threshold is one larger.
references: [erdosproblems.com/643](https://www.erdosproblems.com/643)
[Fu84] F\"uredi, Z., Hypergraphs in which all disjoint pairs have distinct unions. Combinatorica (1984), 161--168.
[PiVe09] Pikhurko, Oleg and Verstra\"{e}te, Jacques, The maximum size of hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2009), 637--649.
[HMY26] Huang, Hao, Ma, Jie, and Yang, Tianchi, *Extremal hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles*. [arXiv:2609.37744](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37744) (2026), Theorem 1.2.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (t : ℕ),
  4 ≤ t →
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      (Hypergraph.extremalNumber n t fun H => ¬H.HasRepeatedDisjointUnion) = (n - 1).choose (t - 1) + (n - 1) / t

declarations.docstring: The largest avoiding family attains the value one below the forcing threshold.
references: [erdosproblems.com/643](https://www.erdosproblems.com/643)
[Fu84] F\"uredi, Z., Hypergraphs in which all disjoint pairs have distinct unions. Combinatorica (1984), 161--168.
[PiVe09] Pikhurko, Oleg and Verstra\"{e}te, Jacques, The maximum size of hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2009), 637--649.
[HMY26] Huang, Hao, Ma, Jie, and Yang, Tianchi, *Extremal hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles*. [arXiv:2609.37744](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37744) (2026), Theorem 1.2.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n t : ℕ), ∃ H, H.IsUniform t ∧ ¬H.HasRepeatedDisjointUnion ∧ H.card + 1 = Erdos643.forcingThreshold n t

declarations.docstring: When no edge of size $t$ fits in the ground set, the threshold is one.
references: [erdosproblems.com/643](https://www.erdosproblems.com/643)
[Fu84] F\"uredi, Z., Hypergraphs in which all disjoint pairs have distinct unions. Combinatorica (1984), 161--168.
[PiVe09] Pikhurko, Oleg and Verstra\"{e}te, Jacques, The maximum size of hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2009), 637--649.
[HMY26] Huang, Hao, Ma, Jie, and Yang, Tianchi, *Extremal hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles*. [arXiv:2609.37744](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37744) (2026), Theorem 1.2.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n t : ℕ}, n < t → Erdos643.forcingThreshold n t = 1

declarations.docstring:
A bound is at least the forcing threshold exactly when every uniform family with that
many edges contains the forbidden four-edge configuration.
references: [erdosproblems.com/643](https://www.erdosproblems.com/643)
[Fu84] F\"uredi, Z., Hypergraphs in which all disjoint pairs have distinct unions. Combinatorica (1984), 161--168.
[PiVe09] Pikhurko, Oleg and Verstra\"{e}te, Jacques, The maximum size of hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2009), 637--649.
[HMY26] Huang, Hao, Ma, Jie, and Yang, Tianchi, *Extremal hypergraphs without generalized 4-cycles*. [arXiv:2609.37744](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37744) (2026), Theorem 1.2.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n t m : ℕ),
  Erdos643.forcingThreshold n t ≤ m ↔
    ∀ (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))), H.IsUniform t → m ≤ H.card → H.HasRepeatedDisjointUnion

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(k,r)$ be minimal such that if $A_1,A_2,\ldots$ is a family of sets, all of size $k$, such
that for every collection of $r$ of the $A_is$ there is some pair $\{x,y\}$ which intersects all of
the $A_j$, then there is some set of size $f(k,r)$ which intersects all of the sets $A_i$. Is it
true that
$$f(k,7)=(1+o(1))\frac{3}{4}k?$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/644](https://www.erdosproblems.com/644)
[EFKT92] Erdős, P. and Fon-Der-Flaass, D. and Kostochka, A. V. and Tuza, Zs., Small transversals in uniform hypergraphs. Siberian Adv. Math. (1992), 82-88.
declarations.type_pretty: Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun k => ↑(Hypergraph.subfamilyTransversalBound k 7 2).toNat) fun k => 3 / 4 * ↑k

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that for any $r\geq 3$ there exists some constant $c_r$ such that
$$f(k,r)=(1+o(1))c_rk?$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/644](https://www.erdosproblems.com/644)
[EFKT92] Erdős, P. and Fon-Der-Flaass, D. and Kostochka, A. V. and Tuza, Zs., Small transversals in uniform hypergraphs. Siberian Adv. Math. (1992), 82-88.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  3 ≤ r →
    ∃ c,
      0 < c ∧
        Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun k => ↑(Hypergraph.subfamilyTransversalBound k r 2).toNat) fun k =>
          c * ↑k

declarations.docstring: For $r \geq 3$, the transversal bound satisfies $f(k,r) \leq 2k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/644](https://www.erdosproblems.com/644)
[EFKT92] Erdős, P. and Fon-Der-Flaass, D. and Kostochka, A. V. and Tuza, Zs., Small transversals in uniform hypergraphs. Siberian Adv. Math. (1992), 82-88.

[EFKT92] Erdős, P. and Fon-Der-Flaass, D. and Kostochka, A. V. and Tuza, Zs., Small transversals in uniform hypergraphs. Siberian Adv. Math. (1992), 82-88.

declarations.docstring:
Let $\tau(n)$ count the number of divisors of $n$. Is there some $n > 24$ such that
$$
  \max_{m < n}(m + \tau(m)) \leq n + 2?
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/647](https://www.erdosproblems.com/647)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ n > 24, ⨆ m, ↑m + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 0) ↑m ≤ n + 2

declarations.docstring:
Erdős says it 'seems certain' that for every $k$ there are infinitely many $n$
for which
$$
  \max_{n−k < m < n}(m + \tau(m)) ≤ n + 2.
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/647](https://www.erdosproblems.com/647)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (k : ℕ), {n | ⨆ m, ↑m + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 0) ↑m ≤ n + 2}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Erdős says 'it is extremely doubtful' that there are infinitely many such $n$, and in
fact suggests that
$$
  lim_{n\to\infty} \max_{m < n}(\tau(m) + m − n) = \infty.
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/647](https://www.erdosproblems.com/647)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ⨆ m, (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 0) ↑m + ↑m - n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring: This is true for $n = 24$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/647](https://www.erdosproblems.com/647)
declarations.type_pretty: ⨆ m, ↑m + (ArithmeticFunction.sigma 0) ↑m ≤ 26

declarations.docstring:
Let $P(m)$ denote the greatest prime factor of $m$. Is it true that, for any two primes $p,q$,
there exists some integer $n$ such that $P(n)=p$ and $P(n+1)=q$?

In fact, the answer to this question as written is easily seen to be no, since there are no
solutions to $2^k\equiv -1\pmod{7}$, and hence this fails with $p=2$ and $q=7$. It is possible
that Erdős meant to exclude such obstructions, by amending this to 'odd primes' or 'all
sufficiently large primes' or such.

The statement below assumes $p \neq q$: for $p = q$ no such $n$ exists, because $p$ would divide
both $n$ and $n+1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/649](https://www.erdosproblems.com/649)
[Ma35] Mahler, Kurt, *Über den grössten Primteiler spezieller Polynome zweiten Grades*. Archiv für math. og naturvid (1935).

[Ro64b] Rotkiewicz, André, *Sur les nombres naturels $n$ et $k$ tels que les nombres $n$ et $nk$ sont à la fois pseudopremiers*. Atti Accad. Naz. Lincei Rend. Cl. Sci. Fis. Mat. Nat. (8) (1964), 816-818.
declarations.type_pretty: ¬∀ (p q : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → Nat.Prime q → p ≠ q → ∃ n, n.maxPrimeFac = p ∧ (n + 1).maxPrimeFac = q

declarations.docstring:
The number of solutions is finite for any fixed $p,q$ since the largest prime factor of $n(n+1)$
tends to $\infty$ (Mahler [Ma35] showed that this is $\gg \log\log n$, see
[368](https://www.erdosproblems.com/368)).
references: [erdosproblems.com/649](https://www.erdosproblems.com/649)
[Ma35] Mahler, Kurt, *Über den grössten Primteiler spezieller Polynome zweiten Grades*. Archiv für math. og naturvid (1935).

[Ro64b] Rotkiewicz, André, *Sur les nombres naturels $n$ et $k$ tels que les nombres $n$ et $nk$ sont à la fois pseudopremiers*. Atti Accad. Naz. Lincei Rend. Cl. Sci. Fis. Mat. Nat. (8) (1964), 816-818.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (p q : ℕ), {n | n.maxPrimeFac = p ∧ (n + 1).maxPrimeFac = q}.Finite

declarations.docstring:
In fact, the answer to this question as written is easily seen to be no, since there are no
solutions to $2^k\equiv -1\pmod{7}$, and hence this fails with $p=2$ and $q=7$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/649](https://www.erdosproblems.com/649)
[Ma35] Mahler, Kurt, *Über den grössten Primteiler spezieller Polynome zweiten Grades*. Archiv für math. og naturvid (1935).

[Ro64b] Rotkiewicz, André, *Sur les nombres naturels $n$ et $k$ tels que les nombres $n$ et $nk$ sont à la fois pseudopremiers*. Atti Accad. Naz. Lincei Rend. Cl. Sci. Fis. Mat. Nat. (8) (1964), 816-818.
declarations.type_pretty: ¬∃ n, n.maxPrimeFac = 2 ∧ (n + 1).maxPrimeFac = 7

declarations.docstring:
Problem 6 in the 12th Romanian Master of Mathematics Competitions in 2020 was to prove that there
exist infinitely many odd primes $p$ such that, for every $n$, $P(n)P(n+1)\neq 2p$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/649](https://www.erdosproblems.com/649)
[Ma35] Mahler, Kurt, *Über den grössten Primteiler spezieller Polynome zweiten Grades*. Archiv für math. og naturvid (1935).

[Ro64b] Rotkiewicz, André, *Sur les nombres naturels $n$ et $k$ tels que les nombres $n$ et $nk$ sont à la fois pseudopremiers*. Atti Accad. Naz. Lincei Rend. Cl. Sci. Fis. Mat. Nat. (8) (1964), 816-818.
declarations.type_pretty: {p | Nat.Prime p ∧ Odd p ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), n.maxPrimeFac * (n + 1).maxPrimeFac ≠ 2 * p}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Sampaio independently observed that the answer to Erdős' original problem is no if one of the
primes can be $2$ - for example this is false with $p=19$ and $q=2$, since if $n+1=2^k$ and
$19\mid n$ then (since $2$ is a primitive root modulo $19$) we must have $18\mid k$, and hence
$73\mid 2^{18}-1\mid n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/649](https://www.erdosproblems.com/649)
[Ma35] Mahler, Kurt, *Über den grössten Primteiler spezieller Polynome zweiten Grades*. Archiv für math. og naturvid (1935).

[Ro64b] Rotkiewicz, André, *Sur les nombres naturels $n$ et $k$ tels que les nombres $n$ et $nk$ sont à la fois pseudopremiers*. Atti Accad. Naz. Lincei Rend. Cl. Sci. Fis. Mat. Nat. (8) (1964), 816-818.
declarations.type_pretty: ¬∃ n, n.maxPrimeFac = 19 ∧ (n + 1).maxPrimeFac = 2

declarations.docstring:
Even with such amendments, this problem is false in a strong sense: Alan Tong has provided the
following elegant elementary proof that, for any given prime $p$, there are infinitely many
primes $q$ such that this statement is false: let $m$ be the product of all primes $\leq p$, and
choose a prime $q$ congruent to $-1$ modulo $4m$. If $p$ is the greatest prime divisor of $n$
then, using quadratic reciprocity, every prime divisor of $n$ is a quadratic residue modulo $q$,
and hence $n$ is a quadratic residue modulo $q$. On the other hand, since $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ we
know that $-1$ is not a quadratic residue modulo $q$, and hence $n\not\equiv -1\pmod{q}$, so it
is impossible for $q\mid n+1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/649](https://www.erdosproblems.com/649)
[Ma35] Mahler, Kurt, *Über den grössten Primteiler spezieller Polynome zweiten Grades*. Archiv für math. og naturvid (1935).

[Ro64b] Rotkiewicz, André, *Sur les nombres naturels $n$ et $k$ tels que les nombres $n$ et $nk$ sont à la fois pseudopremiers*. Atti Accad. Naz. Lincei Rend. Cl. Sci. Fis. Mat. Nat. (8) (1964), 816-818.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → {q | Nat.Prime q ∧ ¬∃ n, n.maxPrimeFac = p ∧ (n + 1).maxPrimeFac = q}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Tong asks whether, for any given odd prime $q$, there are infinitely many primes $p$ such that
there is no integer $n$ with $P(n)=p$ and $P(n+1)=q$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/649](https://www.erdosproblems.com/649)
[Ma35] Mahler, Kurt, *Über den grössten Primteiler spezieller Polynome zweiten Grades*. Archiv für math. og naturvid (1935).

[Ro64b] Rotkiewicz, André, *Sur les nombres naturels $n$ et $k$ tels que les nombres $n$ et $nk$ sont à la fois pseudopremiers*. Atti Accad. Naz. Lincei Rend. Cl. Sci. Fis. Mat. Nat. (8) (1964), 816-818.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (q : ℕ), Nat.Prime q → Odd q → {p | Nat.Prime p ∧ ¬∃ n, n.maxPrimeFac = p ∧ (n + 1).maxPrimeFac = q}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices and $kn$ edges, and $a_1<a_2<\cdots$ be the lengths of
cycles in $G$. Assume $n>0$. Is it true that
$$\sum\frac{1}{a_i}\gg \log k?$$

Gyárfás, Komlós, and Szemerédi [GKS84] have proved that this sum is $\gg \log k$, so that only
the second question remains.

The bound is stated for all sufficiently large $k$: [GKS84, Theorem 4'] proves it for $k \geq b$,
where $b$ is a constant. The case of $k$ slightly larger than $1$ is a separate problem, studied
in [GPSV85].
references: [erdosproblems.com/65](https://www.erdosproblems.com/65)
[GKS84] Gyárfás, A., Komlós, J. and Szemerédi, E., On the distribution of cycle lengths in graphs. J. Graph Theory (1984), 441-462.
[GPSV85] Gyárfás, A., Prömel, H. J., Szemerédi, E. and Voigt, B., On the sum of the reciprocals of cycle lengths in sparse graphs. Combinatorica (1985), 41-52.
[LiMo20] Liu, H. and Montgomery, R., A solution to Erdős and Hajnal's odd cycle problem. arXiv:2010.15802 (2020).
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (k : ℝ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      0 < n →
        Fintype.card V = n → ↑G.edgeSet.ncard = k * ↑n → ∑ᶠ (a : ℕ) (_ : a ∈ G.cycleLengths), 1 / ↑a ≥ c * Real.log k

declarations.docstring:
Is the sum $\sum\frac{1}{a_i}$ minimised when $G$ is a complete bipartite graph?

This problem is #65 in Extremal Graph Theory in the graphs problem collection.
references: [erdosproblems.com/65](https://www.erdosproblems.com/65)

declarations.type_pretty:

    ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      0 < n →

          ↑G.edgeSet.ncard = k * ↑n →

                    ∑ᶠ (a : ℕ) (_ : a ∈ G.cycleLengths), 1 / ↑a

declarations.docstring:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ and let $R(x_i)=\#\{ \lvert x_j-x_i\rvert : j\neq i\}$,
where the points are ordered such that
$$R(x_1)\leq \cdots \leq R(x_n).$$
Let $g(n)$ be the maximum number of distinct values the $R(x_i)$ can take. Is it true that
$g(n) \geq (1-o(1))n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/653](https://www.erdosproblems.com/653)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ o,
    o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (1 - o n) * ↑n ≤ ↑(EuclideanGeometry.maximalDistinctDistancesFrom n)

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be such that, given any $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ with no four points on a
circle, there exists some $x_i$ with at least $f(n)$ many distinct distances to the other $x_j$.
Is it true that $f(n) > (1-o(1))n$?

Erdős asks this in [Er97e]. The answer is no: Aletheia [Fe26] constructed, for every $m \geq 10$,
a set of $n = 4m$ points with no four on a circle such that every point has fewer than
$\frac{3}{4}n$ distinct distances to the other points. This gives infinitely many $n$, which is
enough to refute the statement with $\varepsilon = 1/8$. See `Erdos654.erdos_654.variants.feng`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/654](https://www.erdosproblems.com/654)
[Er87b] Erdős, P., *Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry*. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261--269.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Fe26] T. Feng et al, *Semi-Autonomous Mathematics Discovery with Gemini: A Case Study on the Erdős Problems*. arXiv:2601.22401 (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∀ ε > 0,
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
        A.card = n → EuclideanGeometry.NoFourConcyclic ↑A → ∃ x ∈ A, (1 - ε) * ↑n < ↑(distinctDistancesFromOther A x)

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be as in `erdos_654.parts.i`. Is it true that $f(n) > (\frac{1}{3}+c)n$ for some
constant $c>0$ and all large $n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/654](https://www.erdosproblems.com/654)
[Er87b] Erdős, P., *Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry*. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261--269.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Fe26] T. Feng et al, *Semi-Autonomous Mathematics Discovery with Gemini: A Case Study on the Erdős Problems*. arXiv:2601.22401 (2026).

∃ c > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
      A.card = n → EuclideanGeometry.NoFourConcyclic ↑A → ∃ x ∈ A, (1 / 3 + c) * ↑n < ↑(distinctDistancesFromOther A x)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Pach [ErPa90] suggest that the bound $(1-o(1))n$ holds under the assumption that every
circle centred at a point $x_i$ contains at most $2$ other points $x_j$. We state this for points
in general position (no three on a line and no four on a circle [Er87b, p. 167]), the setting in
which [Er87b] and [ErPa90] ask the weaker question. Without the assumption of no three points on a
line the statement is false: the sets of [Fe26] satisfy the circle condition.
references: [erdosproblems.com/654](https://www.erdosproblems.com/654)
[Er87b] Erdős, P., *Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry*. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261--269.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Fe26] T. Feng et al, *Semi-Autonomous Mathematics Discovery with Gemini: A Case Study on the Erdős Problems*. arXiv:2601.22401 (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ ε > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
      A.card = n →
        EuclideanGeometry.InGeneralPosition ↑A →
          Erdos654.AtMostTwoPerCircle A → ∃ x ∈ A, (1 - ε) * ↑n < ↑(distinctDistancesFromOther A x)

declarations.docstring:
Aletheia [Fe26] showed that for every $m \geq 10$ there is a set of $n = 4m$ points in
$\mathbb{R}^2$, no four on a circle, such that every point has fewer than $\frac{3}{4}n = 3m$
distinct distances to the other points.

The construction places $2m$ points on each of two perpendicular lines, so it is not in general
position. Each point has at most $3m - 1$ distinct distances to the other points.
references: [erdosproblems.com/654](https://www.erdosproblems.com/654)
[Er87b] Erdős, P., *Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry*. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261--269.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Fe26] T. Feng et al, *Semi-Autonomous Mathematics Discovery with Gemini: A Case Study on the Erdős Problems*. arXiv:2601.22401 (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (m : ℕ),
  10 ≤ m → ∃ A, A.card = 4 * m ∧ EuclideanGeometry.NoFourConcyclic ↑A ∧ ∀ x ∈ A, distinctDistancesFromOther A x < 3 * m

additional assumption that no three points are on a line. Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ with
no three points on a line and no four points on a circle. Is there some $x_i$ with at least
$(\frac{1}{3}+c)n$ distinct distances to the other $x_j$, for some constant $c>0$ and all large
$n$?

declarations.docstring:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ with no three points on a line and no four points on a
circle. Is there some $x_i$ with at least $(1-o(1))n$ distinct distances to the other $x_j$?

This is the general-position analogue of `Erdos654.erdos_654.parts.i`. The remark on
erdosproblems.com notes that the construction of [Fe26], which has all points on two lines, does
not settle the version in general position.

declarations.docstring:
It is trivial that $f(n) \geq \frac{n-1}{3}$.

In fact every point $x$ has at least $\frac{n-1}{3}$ distinct distances to the other points: a
circle centred at $x$ contains at most three other points, since four would lie on a common
circle.
references: [erdosproblems.com/654](https://www.erdosproblems.com/654)
[Er87b] Erdős, P., *Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry*. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985) (1987), 167-177.
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261--269.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Fe26] T. Feng et al, *Semi-Autonomous Mathematics Discovery with Gemini: A Case Study on the Erdős Problems*. arXiv:2601.22401 (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
  EuclideanGeometry.NoFourConcyclic ↑A → ∀ x ∈ A, (↑A.card - 1) / 3 ≤ ↑(distinctDistancesFromOther A x)

declarations.docstring:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ be such that no circle whose centre is one
of the $x_i$ contains three other points. Are there at least
$$(1+c)\frac{n}{2}$$
distinct distances determined between the $x_i$, for some constant $c>0$ and
all $n$ sufficiently large?

The answer is **no**: as Zach Hunter observed, the regular `n`-gon (`n` points equally spaced on a
circle) is valid and determines only `⌊n/2⌋ < (1+c)n/2` distinct distances, for every `c > 0`.
(In the spirit of related conjectures of Erdős and others, presumably some kind of assumption that
the points are in general position was intended; see `erdos_655.variants.general_position`.)

The disproof — the regular `n`-gon construction together with its supporting lemmas — is formalised
at the linked commit.
references: [erdosproblems.com/655](https://www.erdosproblems.com/655)
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∃ c > 0,
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (X : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
        X.card = n → Erdos655.IsValid X → (1 + c) * ↑n / 2 ≤ ↑(distinctDistances X)

declarations.docstring:
Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ be such that no circle whose centre is one
of the $x_i$ contains three other points. Are there at least$$(1+c)\frac{n}{2}$$
distinct distances determined between the $x_i$, for some constant $c>0$ and
all $n$ sufficiently large?

In the spirit of related conjectures of Erdős and others, presumably
some kind of assumption that the points are in general position
(e.g. no three on a line and no four on a circle) was intended.
references: [erdosproblems.com/655](https://www.erdosproblems.com/655)

    ∀ (X : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
      X.card = n →
        Erdos655.IsValid X → EuclideanGeometry.InGeneralPosition ↑X → (1 + c) * ↑n / 2 ≤ ↑(distinctDistances X)

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that if $A\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is a set of $n$ points such that every subset of $3$
points determines $3$ distinct distances (that is, $A$ has no isosceles triangles, degenerate
ones included) then $A$ determines at least $f(n)n$ distinct distances, for some function $f$
with $f(n)\to \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/657](https://www.erdosproblems.com/657)

[Er73](https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1973-21.pdf) Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.
[Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*. Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261-269.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Du08] Dumitrescu, Adrian, *On distinct distances and λ-free point sets*. Discrete Math. (2008), 6533-6538.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ f,
  Filter.Tendsto f Filter.atTop Filter.atTop ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
      A.card = n → (↑A).IsIsoscelesFree → f n * ↑n ≤ ↑(distinctDistances A)

declarations.docstring:
The question on the real line, which Erdős [Er73] said was open, has a positive answer: there is
a function $f$ with $f(n)\to \infty$ such that every set of $n$ real numbers with no three-term
arithmetic progression determines at least $f(n)n$ distinct distances. This follows from the
lower bound of Dumitrescu [Du08].

On the line, a set has no isosceles triangle exactly when it has no three-term arithmetic
progression.
references: [erdosproblems.com/657](https://www.erdosproblems.com/657)

[Er73](https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1973-21.pdf) Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.
[Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*. Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261-269.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Du08] Dumitrescu, Adrian, *On distinct distances and λ-free point sets*. Discrete Math. (2008), 6533-6538.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ f,
  Filter.Tendsto f Filter.atTop Filter.atTop ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Finset ℝ), A.card = n → (↑A).IsIsoscelesFree → f n * ↑n ≤ ↑(distinctDistances A)

declarations.docstring:
Dumitrescu [Du08] proved that there is a constant $c > 0$ such that, for all large $n$, every set
of $n$ real numbers with no three-term arithmetic progression determines at least
$n(\log n)^c$ distinct distances.
references: [erdosproblems.com/657](https://www.erdosproblems.com/657)

[Er73](https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1973-21.pdf) Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.
[Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*. Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.

[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Du08] Dumitrescu, Adrian, *On distinct distances and λ-free point sets*. Discrete Math. (2008), 6533-6538.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (A : Finset ℝ), A.card = n → (↑A).IsIsoscelesFree → ↑n * Real.log ↑n ^ c ≤ ↑(distinctDistances A)

declarations.docstring:
As noted in [Du08], Behrend's construction of large sets without three-term arithmetic
progressions shows that there is a constant $C > 0$ such that, for all large $n$, some set
of $n$ real numbers with no three-term arithmetic progression determines at most
$n 2^{C\sqrt{\log n}}$ distinct distances.
references: [erdosproblems.com/657](https://www.erdosproblems.com/657)

[Er73](https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1973-21.pdf) Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.
[Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*. Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261-269.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Du08] Dumitrescu, Adrian, *On distinct distances and λ-free point sets*. Discrete Math. (2008), 6533-6538.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ A, A.card = n ∧ (↑A).IsIsoscelesFree ∧ ↑(distinctDistances A) ≤ ↑n * 2 ^ (C * √(Real.log ↑n))

declarations.docstring:
In [Er73] Erdős attributes the problem, more generally in $\mathbb{R}^k$, to himself and Davies:
for every fixed $k \geq 1$, is there a function $f$ with $f(n)\to \infty$ such that every set of
$n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^k$ with no isosceles triangles determines at least $f(n)n$ distinct
distances?

Here the dimension $k$ is fixed and $f$ may depend on $k$.

        ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))),
          A.card = n → (↑A).IsIsoscelesFree → f n * ↑n ≤ ↑(distinctDistances A)

declarations.docstring:
Straus observed that for every $k$ there is a set of $2^k$ points in $\mathbb{R}^k$ with no
isosceles triangles which determines at most $2^k - 1$ distinct distances.

[Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*. Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99-108.

declarations.docstring:
Let $x_1, \ldots, x_n \in \mathbb{R}^3$ be the vertices of a convex polyhedron. Are there at least
$$(1 - o(1)) \frac{n}{2}$$
many distinct distances between the $x_i$?

The $(1 - o(1)) \frac{n}{2}$ lower bound is formalised as: for every $\varepsilon > 0$, every set
of $n$ vertices of a convex polyhedron with $n$ sufficiently large determines at least
$(1 - \varepsilon) \frac{n}{2}$ distinct distances.
references: [erdosproblems.com/660](https://www.erdosproblems.com/660)
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*, The mathematics of Paul Erdős, I (1997), 47–67.
[Al63] Altman, E., *On a problem of P. Erdős*, Amer. Math. Monthly (1963), 148–157.
[Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*, Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99–108.

  0 < ε →
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))),
        P.card = n → Erdos660.IsPolyhedronVertices P → (1 - ε) * (↑n / 2) ≤ ↑(distinctDistances P)
