      P.card = n → Erdos660.IsPolyhedronVertices P → c * ↑n ≤ ↑(distinctDistances P)

declarations.docstring:
For the similar problem in $\mathbb{R}^2$ there are always at least $n/2$ distances, as proved by
Altman [Al63].
references: [erdosproblems.com/660](https://www.erdosproblems.com/660)
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*, The mathematics of Paul Erdős, I (1997), 47–67.
[Al63] Altman, E., *On a problem of P. Erdős*, Amer. Math. Monthly (1963), 148–157.
[Er75f] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems of elementary and combinatorial geometry*, Ann. Mat. Pura Appl. (4) (1975), 99–108.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ) (P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
  P.card = n → ConvexIndependent ℝ Subtype.val → affineSpan ℝ ↑P = ⊤ → n / 2 ≤ distinctDistances P

declarations.docstring:
Are there, for all large $n$, some points $x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$ such that
the number of distinct distances $d(x_i,y_j)$ is
$$o\left(\frac{n}{\sqrt{\log n}}\right)?$$

We require all $2n$ points to be distinct; without any distinctness one could take all points
equal and get a single distance. Writing $F(n)$ for the minimal number of such distances
(`minimalCrossDistances ℝ² n`), the question asks whether $F(n) = o(n / \sqrt{\log n})$. This is
equivalent to the existence, for all large $n$, of configurations whose count is at most $g(n)$
for some fixed $g(n) = o(n / \sqrt{\log n})$, since the infimum is attained.

The source adds that one can also ask this for points in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Taken literally, the
question is easy there, since a cubic grid of $2n$ points determines only $O(n^{2/3})$ distinct
distances, so we do not state it.
references: [erdosproblems.com/661](https://www.erdosproblems.com/661)
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261--269.
[Er92e] Erdős, Pál, *Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics*. Eureka (1992), 44-48.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
[Er46](https://doi.org/10.2307/2305092) Erdős, Paul, *On sets of distances of $n$ points*. Amer. Math. Monthly 53 (1946), 248--250.
declarations.type_pretty: (fun n => ↑(Erdos661.minimalCrossDistances (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) n)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n / √(Real.log ↑n)

declarations.docstring:
Take $2n$ points of the smallest square grid with at least $2n$ points; by [Er46] they determine
$O(n / \sqrt{\log n})$ distinct distances. Splitting them into two halves of $n$ points shows
that $F(n) = O(n / \sqrt{\log n})$. So the question is whether this trivial bound can be
improved by more than a constant factor.
references: [erdosproblems.com/661](https://www.erdosproblems.com/661)
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261--269.
[Er92e] Erdős, Pál, *Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics*. Eureka (1992), 44-48.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
[Er46](https://doi.org/10.2307/2305092) Erdős, Paul, *On sets of distances of $n$ points*. Amer. Math. Monthly 53 (1946), 248--250.
declarations.type_pretty: (fun n => ↑(Erdos661.minimalCrossDistances (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n / √(Real.log ↑n)

declarations.docstring:
Every split of a set of $2n$ points into two halves of $n$ points gives a configuration for
$F(n)$, and the distances between the halves are among the distances of the whole set. Hence
$F(n) \leq f(2n)$, where $f(2n)$ is the minimal number of distinct distances determined by $2n$
points in $\mathbb{R}^2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/661](https://www.erdosproblems.com/661)
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261--269.
[Er92e] Erdős, Pál, *Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics*. Eureka (1992), 44-48.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
[Er46](https://doi.org/10.2307/2305092) Erdős, Paul, *On sets of distances of $n$ points*. Amer. Math. Monthly 53 (1946), 248--250.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ),
  Erdos661.minimalCrossDistances (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) n ≤
    minimalDistinctDistancesIn (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (2 * n)

declarations.docstring:
In $\mathbb{R}^4$ Lenz observed (as stated on erdosproblems.com/661) that for every $n$ there are
$2n$ distinct points $x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n\in \mathbb{R}^4$ with $d(x_i,y_j)=1$ for all
$i,j$: take the $x_i$ on the circle of radius $1/\sqrt{2}$ about the origin in the plane of the
first two coordinates, and the $y_j$ on the circle of radius $1/\sqrt{2}$ about the origin in the
plane of the last two coordinates.
references: [erdosproblems.com/661](https://www.erdosproblems.com/661)
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261--269.
[Er92e] Erdős, Pál, *Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics*. Eureka (1992), 44-48.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527-537.
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
[Er46](https://doi.org/10.2307/2305092) Erdős, Paul, *On sets of distances of $n$ points*. Amer. Math. Monthly 53 (1946), 248--250.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), ∃ A B, A.card = n ∧ B.card = n ∧ Disjoint A B ∧ ∀ x ∈ A, ∀ y ∈ B, dist x y = 1

declarations.docstring:
Let $F(2n)$ be the minimal number of distinct distances $d(x_i, y_j)$ for $2n$ distinct points
$x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_n\in \mathbb{R}^2$, and $f(2n)$ the minimal number of distinct
distances determined by any $2n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$. Is $F = o(f)$?

Here $F(2n)$ of erdosproblems.com is `minimalCrossDistances ℝ² n` (indexed by $n$ points on each
side) and $f(2n)$ is `minimalDistinctDistancesIn ℝ² (2 * n)`. See also Erdős Problem 89.
references: [erdosproblems.com/661](https://www.erdosproblems.com/661)
[ErPa90] Erdős, P. and Pach, J., *Variations on the theme of repeated distances*. Combinatorica (1990), 261--269.

[Er46](https://doi.org/10.2307/2305092) Erdős, Paul, *On sets of distances of $n$ points*. Amer. Math. Monthly 53 (1946), 248--250.
declarations.type_pretty:
(fun n => ↑(Erdos661.minimalCrossDistances (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) n)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun n =>
  ↑(minimalDistinctDistancesIn (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) (2 * n))

declarations.docstring:
Let $k \geq 2$, and let $q(n,k)$ denote the least prime which does not divide
$\prod_{1 \leq i \leq k}(n+i)$. Is it true that, if $k$ is fixed and $n$ is sufficiently
large, then $q(n,k) < (1+o(1))\log n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/663](https://www.erdosproblems.com/663)
[BEGL96] Burr, S. A., Erdős, P., Graham, R. L., and Li, W. W.-C., *Complete sequences of sets of integer powers*. Acta Arith. (1996), 133–138.
[Er97e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*. Math. Japon. (1997), 527–537.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ k ≥ 2,
  ∃ error,
    (error =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => 1) ∧
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
        have P := ∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k, (n + i);
        ∃ q, Nat.Prime q ∧ ¬q ∣ P ∧ (∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → ¬p ∣ P → q ≤ p) ∧ ↑q < (1 + error n) * Real.log ↑n

declarations.docstring:
Let $c<1$ be some constant and $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ be such that
$\lvert A_i\rvert >c\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$ and $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert\leq 1$ for all $i\neq j$.

Must there exist some set $B$ such that $B\cap A_i\neq \emptyset$ and
$\lvert B\cap A_i\rvert \ll_c 1$ for all $i$?

The answer is no, proved by Alon: if $q$ is a large prime power and $n=m=q^2+q+1$ then there
exist $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that
$\lvert A_i\rvert \geq \tfrac{2}{5}\sqrt{n}$ for all $i$ and $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert\leq 1$ for
all $i\neq j$, and yet if $B$ has non-empty intersection with all $A_i$ then there exists $A_j$
such that $\lvert B\cap A_j\rvert \gg \log n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/664](https://www.erdosproblems.com/664)
[Er81] Erdős, P., _On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved_. Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, _Some unsolved problems_. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∀ (c : ℝ),
    0 < c →
      c < 1 →
        ∃ K,
          ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
            (∀ (i : Fin m), c * √↑n < ↑(A i).card) →
              (∀ (i j : Fin m), i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).card ≤ 1) →
                ∃ B, (∀ (i : Fin m), (B ∩ A i).Nonempty) ∧ ∀ (i : Fin m), (B ∩ A i).card ≤ K

declarations.docstring:
In [Er81] the condition $\lvert A_i\cap A_j\rvert\leq 1$ for all $i\neq j$ is replaced by every
two points in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ being contained in exactly one $A_i$, that is,
$A_1,\ldots,A_m$ is a pairwise balanced block design. The bound $\lvert A_i\rvert>c\sqrt{n}$ is
kept, only the condition $c<1$ is omitted. This weaker version remains open, although Alon
conjectures the answer there to also be no.
references: [erdosproblems.com/664](https://www.erdosproblems.com/664)
[Er81] Erdős, P., _On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved_. Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, _Some unsolved problems_. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (c : ℝ),
  0 < c →
    ∃ K,
      ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
        (∀ (i : Fin m), c * √↑n < ↑(A i).card) →
          (∀ (x y : Fin n), x ≠ y → ∃! i, x ∈ A i ∧ y ∈ A i) →
            ∃ B, (∀ (i : Fin m), (B ∩ A i).Nonempty) ∧ ∀ (i : Fin m), (B ∩ A i).card ≤ K

declarations.docstring: Alon's counterexample already works for $c=2/5$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/664](https://www.erdosproblems.com/664)
[Er81] Erdős, P., _On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved_. Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, _Some unsolved problems_. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∃ K,
    ∀ (n m : ℕ) (A : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
      (∀ (i : Fin m), 2 / 5 * √↑n < ↑(A i).card) →
        (∀ (i j : Fin m), i ≠ j → (A i ∩ A j).card ≤ 1) →
          ∃ B, (∀ (i : Fin m), (B ∩ A i).Nonempty) ∧ ∀ (i : Fin m), (B ∩ A i).card ≤ K

declarations.docstring:
A pairwise balanced design for $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is a collection of sets $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq
\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that $2\leq \lvert A_i\rvert <n$ and every pair of distinct elements $x,y\in
\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is contained in exactly one $A_i$. Is there a constant $C>0$ and, for all large $n$,
a pairwise balanced design such that
$$\lvert A_i\rvert > n^{1/2}-C$$
for all $1\leq i\leq m$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/665](https://www.erdosproblems.com/665)
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, Some unsolved problems. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
[ErLa82] Erdős, P. and Larson, J., On pairwise balanced block designs with the sizes of blocks as uniform as possible. Annals of Discrete Mathematics (1982), 129-134.
[ShSi85] S. S. Shrikhande and N. M. Singhi, On a problem of Erdős and Larson. Combinatorica (1985), 351-358.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ H, H.IsPairwiseBalancedDesign ∧ ∀ e ∈ H, e.card < n ∧ √↑n - C < ↑e.card

declarations.docstring:
Let $p, q \geq 1$ be fixed integers. Define $H(n) = H(n; p, q)$ to be the largest $m$ such that any
graph on $n$ vertices where every set of $p$ vertices spans at least $q$ edges must contain a
complete graph on $m$ vertices. Is
$$ c(p, q) = \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{\log H(n)}{\log n} $$
a strictly increasing function of $q$ for $1 \leq q \leq \binom{p-1}{2} + 1$?

A problem of Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp. When $q = 1$ this corresponds exactly to the
classical Ramsey problem, and hence $\tfrac{1}{p-1} \leq c(p, 1) \leq \tfrac{2}{p+1}$ for
$p \geq 3$. It is easy to see that if $q = \binom{p-1}{2} + 1$ then $c(p, q) = 1$.

erdosproblems.com/667 also states that Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau and Schelp showed
$c(p, \binom{p-1}{2}) \leq 1/2$. This cannot hold for all $p$: for $p = 6$, $q = 10$, the
complement of a $(6, 10)$-locally dense graph is $C_6$-free, so Bondy–Simonovits together with
$\alpha(F) \geq n^2 / (2e(F) + n)$ gives $c(6, 10) \geq 2/3$. That remark is therefore not
formalised here.
references: [erdosproblems.com/667](https://www.erdosproblems.com/667)
[Er97f] P. Erdős, _Some unsolved problems_. In: Combinatorics, Geometry and Probability (Cambridge, 1993), Cambridge Univ. Press (1997), 1-10.
[EFRS94] P. Erdős, R. J. Faudree, C. C. Rousseau and R. H. Schelp, _A local density condition for triangles_. Discrete Math. 127 (1994), 153-161.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (p : ℕ), StrictMonoOn (Erdos667.c p) (Set.Icc 1 ((p - 1).choose 2 + 1))

declarations.docstring:
The right endpoint: when $q = \binom{p-1}{2} + 1$ one has $c(p, q) = 1$
(stated as "easy to see" on erdosproblems.com/667).
references: [erdosproblems.com/667](https://www.erdosproblems.com/667)
[Er97f] P. Erdős, _Some unsolved problems_. In: Combinatorics, Geometry and Probability (Cambridge, 1993), Cambridge Univ. Press (1997), 1-10.
[EFRS94] P. Erdős, R. J. Faudree, C. C. Rousseau and R. H. Schelp, _A local density condition for triangles_. Discrete Math. 127 (1994), 153-161.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (p : ℕ), 2 ≤ p → Erdos667.c p ((p - 1).choose 2 + 1) = 1

declarations.docstring:
That $c(p, q)$ is *nondecreasing* in $q$ for fixed $p$ is a straightforward consequence of the
definitions: enlarging $q$ shrinks the family of $(p, q)$-locally dense graphs, which can only
increase the guaranteed clique size $H(n)$, and hence the exponent.
references: [erdosproblems.com/667](https://www.erdosproblems.com/667)
[Er97f] P. Erdős, _Some unsolved problems_. In: Combinatorics, Geometry and Probability (Cambridge, 1993), Cambridge Univ. Press (1997), 1-10.
[EFRS94] P. Erdős, R. J. Faudree, C. C. Rousseau and R. H. Schelp, _A local density condition for triangles_. Discrete Math. 127 (1994), 153-161.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (p : ℕ), MonotoneOn (Erdos667.c p) (Set.Icc 1 ((p - 1).choose 2 + 1))

declarations.docstring:
The case $q = 1$ is the classical Ramsey problem, giving the bounds
$\tfrac{1}{p-1} \leq c(p, 1) \leq \tfrac{2}{p+1}$ for $p \geq 3$. (For $p = 2$ the condition
forces $G$ to be complete, so $c(2, 1) = 1$ and the upper bound fails.)
references: [erdosproblems.com/667](https://www.erdosproblems.com/667)
[Er97f] P. Erdős, _Some unsolved problems_. In: Combinatorics, Geometry and Probability (Cambridge, 1993), Cambridge Univ. Press (1997), 1-10.
[EFRS94] P. Erdős, R. J. Faudree, C. C. Rousseau and R. H. Schelp, _A local density condition for triangles_. Discrete Math. 127 (1994), 153-161.

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that the number of incongruent sets of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ which maximise the
number of unit distances tends to infinity as $n\to\infty$?

The actual maximal number of unit distances is the subject of
[Erdős Problem 90](https://www.erdosproblems.com/90).

Two sets of points are congruent if an isometry of the plane maps one onto the other.
references: [erdosproblems.com/668](https://www.erdosproblems.com/668)
[A385657](https://oeis.org/A385657)
[AMP25] B. Alexeev, D. Mixon, and H. Parshall, *The Erdős unit distance problem for small point sets*. arXiv:2412.11914 (2025).
[EHSVZ25] P. Engel, O. Hammond-Lee, Y. Su, D. Varga, and P. Zsámboki, *Diverse beam search to find densest-known planar unit distance graphs*. arXiv:2406.15317 (2025).
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (m : ℕ),
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ A,
      (∀ (i : Fin m), (A i).card = n ∧ unitDistNum (A i) = Erdos90.maxUnitDistances n) ∧
        ∀ (i j : Fin m), i ≠ j → ¬∃ f, ⇑f '' ↑(A i) = ↑(A j)

declarations.docstring:
Is it always $>1$ for $n>3$?

In fact this is $=1$ also for $n=4$, the unique example given by two equilateral triangles joined
by an edge.

Computational evidence of Engel, Hammond-Lee, Su, Varga, and Zsámboki [EHSVZ25] and Alexeev,
Mixon, and Parshall [AMP25] suggests that this count is $=1$ for various other $5\leq n\leq 21$
(although these calculations were checking only up to graph isomorphism, rather than
congruency).
references: [erdosproblems.com/668](https://www.erdosproblems.com/668)
[A385657](https://oeis.org/A385657)
[AMP25] B. Alexeev, D. Mixon, and H. Parshall, *The Erdős unit distance problem for small point sets*. arXiv:2412.11914 (2025).
[EHSVZ25] P. Engel, O. Hammond-Lee, Y. Su, D. Varga, and P. Zsámboki, *Diverse beam search to find densest-known planar unit distance graphs*. arXiv:2406.15317 (2025).
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.

¬∀ (n : ℕ),
    3 < n →
      ∃ A B,
        A.card = n ∧
          B.card = n ∧
            unitDistNum A = Erdos90.maxUnitDistances n ∧
              unitDistNum B = Erdos90.maxUnitDistances n ∧ ¬∃ f, ⇑f '' ↑A = ↑B

For $n=4$ there is, up to congruence, exactly one set of points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ which maximises
the number of unit distances: two unit equilateral triangles $abc$ and $bcd$ joined by the edge
$bc$, with $a\neq d$.

    dist a b = 1 ∧

declarations.docstring:
Let $F_k(n)$ be minimal such that for any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ there exist at most
$F_k(n)$ many distinct lines passing through at least $k$ of the points, and $f_k(n)$ similarly
but with lines passing through exactly $k$ points.

Estimate $f_k(n)$ and $F_k(n)$ - in particular, determine $\lim F_k(n)/n^2$ and
$\lim f_k(n)/n^2$.

This part asks for $\lim F_k(n)/n^2$ for $k \geq 3$ (the case $k = 2$ is trivial). The
original question [Er97f, Problem 16] asks for the limits "if they exist", so the answer allows
nonexistence: the answer at $k$ is `some x` if the limit exists and equals $x$, and `none`
otherwise.
references: [erdosproblems.com/669](https://www.erdosproblems.com/669)
[BGS74] Burr, Stefan A. and Grünbaum, Branko and Sloane, N. J. A., *The orchard problem*. Geometriae Dedicata (1974), 397-424.

declarations.docstring:
Let $F_k(n)$ be minimal such that for any $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ there exist at most
$F_k(n)$ many distinct lines passing through at least $k$ of the points, and $f_k(n)$ similarly
but with lines passing through exactly $k$ points.

Estimate $f_k(n)$ and $F_k(n)$ - in particular, determine $\lim F_k(n)/n^2$ and
$\lim f_k(n)/n^2$.

This part asks for $\lim f_k(n)/n^2$ for $k \geq 3$ (the case $k = 2$ is trivial). The
original question [Er97f, Problem 16] asks for the limits "if they exist", so the answer allows
nonexistence: the answer at $k$ is `some x` if the limit exists and equals $x$, and `none`
otherwise.
references: [erdosproblems.com/669](https://www.erdosproblems.com/669)
[BGS74] Burr, Stefan A. and Grünbaum, Branko and Sloane, N. J. A., *The orchard problem*. Geometriae Dedicata (1974), 397-424.
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  3 ≤ k →
    ∀ (x : ℝ),
      Erdos669.erdos_669.parts.ii.answer k = some x ↔
        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos669.maxLinesExactly k n) / ↑n ^ 2) Filter.atTop (nhds x)

declarations.docstring:
The problem with $k=3$ is the classical 'Orchard problem' of Sylvester. Burr, Grünbaum, and Sloane
[BGS74] have proved that
$$f_3(n)=\frac{n^2}{6}-O(n)$$
and
$$F_3(n)=\frac{n^2}{6}-O(n).$$

This is the statement for $F_3$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/669](https://www.erdosproblems.com/669)
[BGS74] Burr, Stefan A. and Grünbaum, Branko and Sloane, N. J. A., *The orchard problem*. Geometriae Dedicata (1974), 397-424.
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
declarations.type_pretty: (fun n => ↑(Erdos669.maxLinesAtLeast 3 n) - ↑n ^ 2 / 6) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n

There is a trivial upper bound of $F_k(n) \leq \binom{n}{2}/\binom{k}{2}$, and hence
$$\lim F_k(n)/n^2 \leq \frac{1}{k(k-1)}.$$
See also [101](https://www.erdosproblems.com/101).

Here the limit is assumed to exist and is called `L`.

ordered pair of its points, and there are at most $n^2$ ordered pairs. The set is also nonempty,
since $n$-point sets exist, so the `sSup` in `Erdos669.maxLinesAtLeast` is attained.

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ be a set of $n$ points such that all pairwise distances differ by
at least $1$. Is the diameter of $A$ at least $(1+o(1))n^2$?

The quantifiers in the source are ambiguous. Following the remarks on erdosproblems.com, this is
the regime where $d$ is fixed and the $o(1)$ term tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$, at a rate
which may depend on $d$. The case $d = 1$ was proved by Erdős
(`Erdos670.erdos_670.variants.dim_one`), so the question is open for $d \geq 2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/670](https://www.erdosproblems.com/670)
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
[Ho26] Ho, B. S., *Erdős's diameter conjecture for separated distances fails in high dimensions*. [arXiv:2604.15305](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15305) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (d : ℕ),
  1 ≤ d →
    ∀ ε > 0,
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
        ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))),
          A.card = n → Erdos670.HasSeparatedDistances A → (1 - ε) * ↑n ^ 2 ≤ Metric.diam ↑A

declarations.docstring:
The trivial lower bound: if $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ is a set of $n \neq 2$ points such that all
pairwise distances differ by at least $1$, then the diameter of $A$ is at least $\binom{n}{2}$.

For $n \geq 3$, take a closest pair $a, b$ and a third point $c$. Then
$1 \leq \lvert d(a, c) - d(b, c)\rvert \leq d(a, b)$, so every distance is at least $1$. The
$\binom{n}{2}$ distances are at least $1$ apart, so the largest one is at least $\binom{n}{2}$.
For $n = 2$ the hypothesis is vacuous, and two points at distance $1/2$ show that the bound fails.
references: [erdosproblems.com/670](https://www.erdosproblems.com/670)
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
[Ho26] Ho, B. S., *Erdős's diameter conjecture for separated distances fails in high dimensions*. [arXiv:2604.15305](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15305) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (d : ℕ) (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))),
  Erdos670.HasSeparatedDistances A → A.card ≠ 2 → ↑(A.card.choose 2) ≤ Metric.diam ↑A

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er97f] proved the claim when $d = 1$: if $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is a set of $n$ points
such that all pairwise distances differ by at least $1$, then the diameter of $A$ is at least
$(1+o(1))n^2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/670](https://www.erdosproblems.com/670)
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
[Ho26] Ho, B. S., *Erdős's diameter conjecture for separated distances fails in high dimensions*. [arXiv:2604.15305](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15305) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ ε > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))),
      A.card = n → Erdos670.HasSeparatedDistances A → (1 - ε) * ↑n ^ 2 ≤ Metric.diam ↑A

declarations.docstring:
Ho [Ho26] showed that the claim fails if $n$ grows with $d$: there exist infinitely many $n$
and, with $d = n^2 - n$, a set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of $n$ points such that all pairwise
distances differ by at least $1$, with diameter at most
$$
\left(1-\frac{1}{\pi^2}+o(1)\right)n^2\approx 0.898n^2.
$$
Ho's construction uses $n = q + 1$ points in dimension $q^2 + q = n^2 - n$, for every prime power
$q$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/670](https://www.erdosproblems.com/670)
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
[Ho26] Ho, B. S., *Erdős's diameter conjecture for separated distances fails in high dimensions*. [arXiv:2604.15305](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15305) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ ε > 0,
  ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ A, A.card = n ∧ Erdos670.HasSeparatedDistances A ∧ Metric.diam ↑A ≤ (1 - 1 / Real.pi ^ 2 + ε) * ↑n ^ 2

declarations.docstring:
The version of the problem where the $o(1)$ term must be uniform in the dimension $d$ has a
negative answer. This follows from `Erdos670.erdos_670.variants.ho` (Ho [Ho26]).
references: [erdosproblems.com/670](https://www.erdosproblems.com/670)
[Er97f] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Combinatorics, geometry and probability (Cambridge, 1993) (1997), 1-10.
[Ho26] Ho, B. S., *Erdős's diameter conjecture for separated distances fails in high dimensions*. [arXiv:2604.15305](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.15305) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∀ ε > 0,
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (d : ℕ) (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))),
        A.card = n → Erdos670.HasSeparatedDistances A → (1 - ε) * ↑n ^ 2 ≤ Metric.diam ↑A

declarations.docstring: If `P` contains every prime, then `composedOf P` is the set of all positive integers.
references: [erdosproblems.com/675](https://www.erdosproblems.com/675)
[Er79] Erdős, Paul, *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.
[Ho26] Ho, B. S., *A squarefree lower bound for Erdős Problem 675*. [PDF](https://boonsuan.github.io/erdos675_squarefree.pdf) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos675.composedOf {p | Nat.Prime p} = {m | 0 < m}

declarations.docstring:
A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ has the translation property if, for every $n$, there is an
integer $t_n \geq 1$ such that, for all $1 \leq a \leq n$, $a \in A$ if and only if
$a + t_n \in A$. Does the set of sums of two squares $\{x^2 + y^2 : x, y \in \mathbb{N}\}$
have the translation property?
references: [erdosproblems.com/675](https://www.erdosproblems.com/675)
[Er79] Erdős, Paul, *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.
[Ho26] Ho, B. S., *A squarefree lower bound for Erdős Problem 675*. [PDF](https://boonsuan.github.io/erdos675_squarefree.pdf) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos675.HasTranslationProperty {m | ∃ x y, m = x ^ 2 + y ^ 2}

declarations.docstring:
If we partition all primes into $P\sqcup Q$, such that each set contains $\gg x/\log x$ many
primes $\leq x$ for all large $x$, then can the set of integers only divisible by primes from
$P$ have the translation property?

We read "can" as: is there such a partition for which this set (which contains $1$) has the
translation property?
references: [erdosproblems.com/675](https://www.erdosproblems.com/675)
[Er79] Erdős, Paul, *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.
[Ho26] Ho, B. S., *A squarefree lower bound for Erdős Problem 675*. [PDF](https://boonsuan.github.io/erdos675_squarefree.pdf) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ P ⊆ {p | Nat.Prime p},
  ((fun x => ↑x / Real.log ↑x) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑(P ∩ Set.Iic x).ncard) ∧
    ((fun x => ↑x / Real.log ↑x) =O[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑({p | Nat.Prime p} \ P ∩ Set.Iic x).ncard) ∧
      Erdos675.HasTranslationProperty (Erdos675.composedOf P)

declarations.docstring:
If $A$ is the set of squarefree numbers then how fast does the minimal such $t_n$ grow? Is it
true that $t_n>\exp(n^c)$ for some constant $c>0$?

We ask for the inequality for all sufficiently large $n$, since $t_1 = 1$.

Ho [Ho26] proved that the answer is yes: for every fixed $0 < c < 25/72$, $t_n > \exp(n^c)$ for
all sufficiently large $n$ (Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 3.2); see also the
[forum discussion](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/675#post-6002).
references: [erdosproblems.com/675](https://www.erdosproblems.com/675)
[Er79] Erdős, Paul, *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.
[Ho26] Ho, B. S., *A squarefree lower bound for Erdős Problem 675*. [PDF](https://boonsuan.github.io/erdos675_squarefree.pdf) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Real.exp (↑n ^ c) < ↑(Erdos675.minTranslation {m | Squarefree m} n)

declarations.docstring:
Let $B \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be a set of pairwise coprime integers with
$$\sum_{b \in B,\ b < x} \frac{1}{b} = o(\log \log x).$$
Then $A = \{n : b \nmid n \text{ for all } b \in B\}$ has the translation property.
As remarked on erdosproblems.com, this follows from Brun's sieve, and Erdős did not know what
happens if the condition on the sum is weakened or dropped.
references: [erdosproblems.com/675](https://www.erdosproblems.com/675)
[Er79] Erdős, Paul, *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.
[Ho26] Ho, B. S., *A squarefree lower bound for Erdős Problem 675*. [PDF](https://boonsuan.github.io/erdos675_squarefree.pdf) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (B : Set ℕ),
  B.Pairwise Nat.Coprime →
    ((fun x => ∑ b ∈ Finset.range x with b ∈ B, 1 / ↑b) =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => Real.log (Real.log ↑x)) →
      Erdos675.HasTranslationProperty {n | ∀ b ∈ B, ¬b ∣ n}

declarations.docstring:
Elementary sieve theory implies that the set of squarefree numbers has the translation property
(as remarked on erdosproblems.com).
references: [erdosproblems.com/675](https://www.erdosproblems.com/675)
[Er79] Erdős, Paul, *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.
[Ho26] Ho, B. S., *A squarefree lower bound for Erdős Problem 675*. [PDF](https://boonsuan.github.io/erdos675_squarefree.pdf) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos675.HasTranslationProperty {m | Squarefree m}

declarations.docstring:
The numbers $1, 2, 3$ are squarefree, and $t = 4$ is the least $t \geq 1$ such that
$1 + t$, $2 + t$ and $3 + t$ are all squarefree.
references: [erdosproblems.com/675](https://www.erdosproblems.com/675)
[Er79] Erdős, Paul, *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Math. Mag. (1979), 67-70.
[Ho26] Ho, B. S., *A squarefree lower bound for Erdős Problem 675*. [PDF](https://boonsuan.github.io/erdos675_squarefree.pdf) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos675.minTranslation {m | Squarefree m} 3 = 4

declarations.docstring:
The set $\{1\}$ does not have the translation property: for $n = 1$ it would need
$1 + t \in \{1\}$ for some $t \geq 1$.

declarations.docstring:
Denote by $M(n, k)$ the least common multiple of the finite set $\{n+1, \dotsc, n+k\}$.
Is it true that for all $m \geq n + k$, we get $M(m, k) \neq M(n, k)$?

declarations.docstring:
Let $\epsilon>0$ and $\omega(n)$ count the number of distinct prime factors of $n$.
Are there infinitely many values of $n$ such that
$$\omega(n-k) < (1+\epsilon)\frac{\log k}{\log\log k}$$
for all $k<n$ which are sufficiently large depending on $\epsilon$ only?
references: [erdosproblems.com/679](https://www.erdosproblems.com/679)
[Er79d] P. Erdős, Some unconventional problems in number theory. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 33 (1979), 71–80.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (ε : ℝ),
  0 < ε →
    ∃ K,
      ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
        ∀ (k : ℕ),
          K < k →
            k < n → ↑(ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n - k)) < (1 + ε) * Real.log ↑k / Real.log (Real.log ↑k)

declarations.docstring:
Can one show the stronger version with
$$\omega(n-k) < \frac{\log k}{\log\log k}+O(1)$$
is false?

DottedCalculator disproved this strengthening. For every additive constant $C$ and cutoff $K$,
all sufficiently large $n$ admit $K<k<n$ violating the bound.
references: [erdosproblems.com/679](https://www.erdosproblems.com/679)
[Er79d] P. Erdős, Some unconventional problems in number theory. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 33 (1979), 71–80.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (C : ℝ) (K : ℕ),
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ k < n, K < k ∧ Real.log ↑k / Real.log (Real.log ↑k) + C ≤ ↑(ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n - k))

declarations.docstring:
Let $P(n, k)$ be the largest prime factor of $\binom{n}{k}$.
There exists $c > 0$ such that $P(n, k) \ge \min(n - k + 1, k^{1 + c})$ for all $0 < k \le n/2$.

Erdős stated this for $1 \le k \le n$ with the bound $\min(n-k+1, k^{1+c})$ [Er79d]. The
minimum is needed even for $k \le n/2$: at $n = 2k$ every prime factor of $\binom{2k}{k}$ is at
most $2k$, so $P(n, k) \ge k^{1+c}$ fails for large $k$. The range $k \le n/2$ is natural
(cf. [#961](https://www.erdosproblems.com/961) and the
[discussion](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/discuss/683)).
references: [erdosproblems.com/683](https://www.erdosproblems.com/683)
[Er34] Erdős, Paul, A Theorem of Sylvester and Schur. J. London Math. Soc. (1934), 282--288.
[Er55d] Erdős, P., On consecutive integers. Nieuw Arch. Wisk. (3) (1955), 124--128.
[Er79d] Erdős, P., Some unconventional problems in number theory. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1979), 71-80.

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er55d] improved this to $P(n, k) \gg \min(n - k + 1, k \log k)$ for $k \le n/2$. The
minimum cannot be dropped: at $n = 2k$ one has $P(n, k) \le 2k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/683](https://www.erdosproblems.com/683)
[Er34] Erdős, Paul, A Theorem of Sylvester and Schur. J. London Math. Soc. (1934), 282--288.

declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c > 0, ∀ (n k : ℕ), 0 < k ∧ k ≤ n / 2 → ↑(Erdos683.P n k) ≥ min (↑(n - k + 1)) (c * ↑k * Real.log ↑k)

declarations.docstring:
Let $\epsilon > 0$ and let $n$ be large depending on $\epsilon$. Is it true that for all
$n^{\epsilon} < k \leq n^{1-\epsilon}$ the number of distinct prime divisors of $\binom{n}{k}$ is
$$(1+o(1))\, k \sum_{k < p < n} \frac{1}{p}?$$

The $o(1)$ is uniform in $k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/685](https://www.erdosproblems.com/685)
[Er79d] Erdős, P., *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1979), 71-80.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ ε > 0,
  ∀ δ > 0,
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (k : ℕ),
        ↑n ^ ε < ↑k →
          ↑k ≤ ↑n ^ (1 - ε) →
            |↑(ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n.choose k)) - ↑k * Erdos685.primeRecipSum k n| ≤
              δ * (↑k * Erdos685.primeRecipSum k n)

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for some constant $c > 0$, the number of distinct prime divisors of
$\binom{n}{k}$ is
$$(1+o(1))\, k \sum_{k < p < n} \frac{1}{p}$$
even for all $(\log n)^c \leq k \leq n^{1-\epsilon}$?

Here $\epsilon > 0$ is as in the first question, and the $o(1)$ is uniform in $k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/685](https://www.erdosproblems.com/685)
[Er79d] Erdős, P., *Some unconventional problems in number theory*. Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. (1979), 71-80.

    ∀ δ > 0,
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
        ∀ (k : ℕ),
          Real.log ↑n ^ c ≤ ↑k →
            ↑k ≤ ↑n ^ (1 - ε) →
              |↑(ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n.choose k)) - ↑k * Erdos685.primeRecipSum k n| ≤
                δ * (↑k * Erdos685.primeRecipSum k n)

declarations.docstring:
In particular, can one prove that $Y(x)=o(x^2)$?

Yes: an internal OpenAI model proved $h(k) \ll k^2$ for Jacobsthal's function $h$ [OAI26a]
(see `Erdos970.erdos_970`). Since $Y(x) + 1$ is Jacobsthal's function of $\prod_{p \leq x} p$,
which has $\pi(x) \ll x/\log x$ prime factors, this gives $Y(x) \ll x^2/(\log x)^2$.
The linked Lean proof is by 30k30, from the bound of [OAI26a].

declarations.docstring:
Let $f_\max(n)$ be the largest $m$ such that $\phi(m) = n$, and
$f_\min(n)$ be the smallest such $m$, where $\phi$ is Euler's
totient function. Investigate
$$
  \max_{n\leq x}\frac{f_\max(n)}{f_\min(n)}.
$$

GPT-5.5 Pro (prompted by Price) has proved (see also the comments for a summary) that
$$
\max_{n\leq x}\frac{f_{\max}(n)}{f_{\min}(n)}=(e^\gamma+o(1))\log\log x.
$$

A Lean formalisation of the reduction exists, conditional on Mertens' product theorem and
Linnik's theorem; see the
[formal proof](https://github.com/Shashi456/erdos-formalizations/blob/main/Erdos/P694/Proof.lean).

The extrema are only required on nonempty fibres of the totient (values such as $3$ have no
preimage), and the identity is asked for sufficiently large $x$: at $x = 1$ the maximum is
$f_\max(1) / f_\min(1) = 2$ while $\log \log 1 = 0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/694](https://www.erdosproblems.com/694)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (fmax fmin : ℕ → ℕ),
  (∀ (n : ℕ), (∃ m, m.totient = n) → IsGreatest (Nat.totient ⁻¹' {n}) (fmax n)) →
    (∀ (n : ℕ), (∃ m, m.totient = n) → IsLeast (Nat.totient ⁻¹' {n}) (fmin n)) →
      ∃ o,
        Filter.Tendsto o Filter.atTop (nhds 0) ∧
          ∀ᶠ (x : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
            sSup {x_1 | ∃ n, ∃ (_ : n ≤ x) (_ : ∃ m, m.totient = n), ↑(fmax n) / ↑(fmin n) = x_1} =
              (Real.exp Real.eulerMascheroniConstant + o x) * Real.log (Real.log ↑x)

  ∀ {q : ℕ → ℕ},
    StrictMono q →
      (∀ (i : ℕ), Nat.Prime (q i)) →
        (∀ (i : ℕ), q (i + 1) % q i = 1) → Filter.Tendsto (fun k => ↑(q k) ^ (1 / ↑k)) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:
Is there a sequence of primes $q_1 < q_2 < \cdots$ such that $q_{i + 1} \equiv 1 \pmod{q_i}$ and
$$
q(k) \leq \exp(k (\log k)^{1 + o(1)})?
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/695](https://www.erdosproblems.com/695)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ q,
    StrictMono q ∧
      (∀ (i : ℕ), Nat.Prime (q i)) ∧
        (∀ (i : ℕ), q (i + 1) % q i = 1) ∧
          ∃ o, o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ (k : ℕ), ↑(q k) ≤ Real.exp ((↑k + 1) * Real.log (↑k + 1) ^ (1 + o k))

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 699.** Is it true that for every $1 \le i < j \le n / 2$ there exists a prime
$p \ge i$ with $p \mid \gcd\big(\binom{n}{i}, \binom{n}{j}\big)$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/699](https://www.erdosproblems.com/699)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (n i j : ℕ), 1 ≤ i → i < j → j ≤ n / 2 → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ i ≤ p ∧ p ∣ (n.choose i).gcd (n.choose j)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Szekeres conjectured that, apart from a finite exceptional set of triples `(n, i, j)`,
one can always take `p > i` in the prime divisor statement.
references: [erdosproblems.com/699](https://www.erdosproblems.com/699)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∃ E,
    ∀ (n i j : ℕ),
      1 ≤ i → i < j → j ≤ n / 2 → (n, i, j) ∉ E → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ i < p ∧ p ∣ (n.choose i).gcd (n.choose j)

declarations.docstring: Sylvester and Schur: for $1 \le i \le n/2$ there is a prime $p > i$ dividing `n.choose i`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/699](https://www.erdosproblems.com/699)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n i : ℕ), 1 ≤ i → i ≤ n / 2 → ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ i < p ∧ p ∣ n.choose i

declarations.docstring: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are odd (and greater than 1)?
references: [erdosproblems.com/7](https://www.erdosproblems.com/7)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C, ∀ (i : C.ι), ¬C.moduli i ≤ Ideal.span {2} ∧ C.moduli i ≠ ⊤

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 70**: Let $\mathfrak{c}$ be the order type of the real numbers,
let $\beta$ be a countable ordinal, and let $2 \le n < \omega$.
Is it true that $\mathfrak{c} \to (\beta, n)^3_2$?

Note: The cases $n \le 3$ are trivially true (compare `omega_three`), so the
genuine content of the conjecture begins at $n = 4$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/70](https://www.erdosproblems.com/70)
[ErRa56] Erdős, P. and Rado, R., *A partition calculus in set theory*, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. **62** (1956), 427–489, Theorem 31.
[Er87] Erdős, P., *Some problems on finite and infinite graphs*, Logic and combinatorics (Arcata, Calif., 1985), Contemp. Math. **65** (1987), 223–228.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (β : Ordinal.{0}) (n : ℕ), β.card ≤ Cardinal.aleph0 → 2 ≤ n → Erdos70.RealCardinalRamsey3 β ↑n

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős–Rado partial result**: $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega + n, 4)^3_2$ for any
$2 \le n < \omega$, where $\mathfrak{c}$ is the order type of the real numbers.
Positive partial answer to Problem 70 with $\beta = \omega + n$ and the blue side
fixed at $4$ [ErRa56, Theorem 31].
references: [erdosproblems.com/70](https://www.erdosproblems.com/70)
[ErRa56] Erdős, P. and Rado, R., *A partition calculus in set theory*, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. **62** (1956), 427–489, Theorem 31.
[Er87] Erdős, P., *Some problems on finite and infinite graphs*, Logic and combinatorics (Arcata, Calif., 1985), Contemp. Math. **65** (1987), 223–228.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → Erdos70.RealCardinalRamsey3 (Ordinal.omega0 + ↑n) 4

declarations.docstring:
**The relation at $\omega_1$**: $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega_1, n)^3_2$ for finite $n \ge 2$,
where $\omega_1 = \aleph_1$ is the first uncountable ordinal.

Note that $\omega_1$ is *not* a countable ordinal, so this is not directly an instance of the
main Erdős problem (which asks for *countable* $\beta$). Under CH, $\omega_1 = \mathfrak{c}.\mathrm{ord}$,
making this a self-referential question about $\mathfrak{c}.\mathrm{ord} \to
(\mathfrak{c}.\mathrm{ord}, n)^3_2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/70](https://www.erdosproblems.com/70)
[ErRa56] Erdős, P. and Rado, R., *A partition calculus in set theory*, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. **62** (1956), 427–489, Theorem 31.
[Er87] Erdős, P., *Some problems on finite and infinite graphs*, Logic and combinatorics (Arcata, Calif., 1985), Contemp. Math. **65** (1987), 223–228.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), 2 ≤ n → Erdos70.OrdinalCardinalRamsey3 Cardinal.continuum.ord (Cardinal.aleph 1).ord ↑n

declarations.docstring:
**Trivial boundary case**: $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega, 3)^3_2$, stated for the initial
ordinal $\mathfrak{c}.\mathrm{ord}$ of the cardinality of the continuum.

This is trivially true because in a 3-uniform hypergraph, a \"blue clique of size 3\"
consists of a single 3-element subset ($\binom{3}{3} = 1$), so the blue alternative
merely asks for one blue triple to exist. The proof splits into two cases:
- If any blue triple exists, it is itself a blue-monochromatic set of cardinality 3.
- If no blue triple exists, all triples are red, and since $\omega \le \mathfrak{c}$,
  any subset of order type $\omega$ is red-monochromatic.

The problem becomes non-trivial only for $n \ge 4$; see `omega_times_two_four` for
the simplest genuinely open case.
references: [erdosproblems.com/70](https://www.erdosproblems.com/70)
[ErRa56] Erdős, P. and Rado, R., *A partition calculus in set theory*, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. **62** (1956), 427–489, Theorem 31.
[Er87] Erdős, P., *Some problems on finite and infinite graphs*, Logic and combinatorics (Arcata, Calif., 1985), Contemp. Math. **65** (1987), 223–228.
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos70.OrdinalCardinalRamsey3 Cardinal.continuum.ord Ordinal.omega0 3

declarations.docstring:
**First open case beyond Erdős–Rado**: $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega \cdot 2, 4)^3_2$,
where $\mathfrak{c}$ is the order type of the real numbers.

Erdős and Rado proved $\mathfrak{c} \to (\omega + n, 4)^3_2$ for every finite $n \ge 2$
(see `erdos_rado`), which covers all red ordinals below $\omega \cdot 2 = \omega + \omega$.
This variant asks whether the result extends to $\beta = \omega \cdot 2$, the simplest
countable ordinal not covered by their theorem.
references: [erdosproblems.com/70](https://www.erdosproblems.com/70)
[ErRa56] Erdős, P. and Rado, R., *A partition calculus in set theory*, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. **62** (1956), 427–489, Theorem 31.
[Er87] Erdős, P., *Some problems on finite and infinite graphs*, Logic and combinatorics (Arcata, Calif., 1985), Contemp. Math. **65** (1987), 223–228.
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos70.RealCardinalRamsey3 (Ordinal.omega0 * 2) 4

declarations.docstring:
**Monotonicity of `OrdinalCardinalRamsey3`**:
If `OrdinalCardinalRamsey3 α β c` holds and $\beta' \le \beta$, $c' \le c$, then
`OrdinalCardinalRamsey3 α β' c'` also holds.

This allows us to deduce weaker partition results from stronger ones.
references: [erdosproblems.com/70](https://www.erdosproblems.com/70)
[ErRa56] Erdős, P. and Rado, R., *A partition calculus in set theory*, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. **62** (1956), 427–489, Theorem 31.
[Er87] Erdős, P., *Some problems on finite and infinite graphs*, Logic and combinatorics (Arcata, Calif., 1985), Contemp. Math. **65** (1987), 223–228.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {α β β' : Ordinal.{u}} {c c' : Cardinal.{u}},
  Erdos70.OrdinalCardinalRamsey3 α β c → β' ≤ β → c' ≤ c → Erdos70.OrdinalCardinalRamsey3 α β' c'

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \le n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$ and let $P(n)$ be the largest prime
dividing $n$.

**(a)** Characterise those composite $n$ such that $f(n) = n/P(n)$.

Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78] note that $f(n) = n/P(n)$ when $n$ is a product of two primes
(`erdos_700.variants.prime_mul`), with $n = 30$ a further example. The characterisation itself is
open; we state it as the (unknown) set of all composite `n` with `f n = n / P n`.

This follows the largest-prime reading on erdosproblems.com. In [ErSz78, p. 98], the first prose
line below (7) reads: "where $P(n)$ is the greatest prime power which divides $n$."
The paper's reading is stated with $Q(n)$ in `erdos_700.variants.prime_power_divisor`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/700](https://www.erdosproblems.com/700)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | ¬Nat.Prime n ∧ 1 < n ∧ Erdos700.f n = n / Erdos700.P n} = Erdos700.erdos_700.parts.i.answer

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \le n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$.

**(b)** Are there infinitely many composite $n$ such that $f(n) > n^{1/2}$?

Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78] could not prove this. (Since $f(n) \ge p(n)$, the least prime factor of
$n$, there are infinitely many $n$ — those of the form $p^2$ — with $f(n) \ge n^{1/2}$; the
question asks for the strict inequality.) Here $f(n) > n^{1/2}$ is written as `(f n) ^ 2 > n`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/700](https://www.erdosproblems.com/700)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | ¬Nat.Prime n ∧ 1 < n ∧ Erdos700.f n ^ 2 > n}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n) = \min_{1 < k \le n/2} \gcd(n, \binom{n}{k})$.

**(c)** Is it true that, for every composite $n$, $f(n) \ll_A n/(\log n)^A$ for every $A > 0$?

Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78] prove the weaker bound $f(n) \le (1 + o(1)) n/\log n$ (the case $A = 1$).
Here $f(n) \ll_A n/(\log n)^A$ is spelled out as: for every `A > 0` there is a constant `C`
(depending on `A`) with `f(n) ≤ C · n/(log n)^A` for every composite `n`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/700](https://www.erdosproblems.com/700)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (A : ℝ), 0 < A → ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), ¬Nat.Prime n → 1 < n → ↑(Erdos700.f n) ≤ C * ↑n / Real.log ↑n ^ A

declarations.docstring:
`f(pq) = p` for distinct primes `p < q` (recorded by Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78]); in particular
`pq` is always a "hit" (`f(pq) = pq / P(pq) = p`). Proof via Lucas' theorem:
`p ∤ C(pq,k) ⟹ p ∣ k` (and the same for `q`),
so any `k` with `gcd(pq, C(pq,k)) = 1` must be a multiple of `pq`, of which there are none in
`(1, pq/2]`; the witness `k = q` gives `gcd(pq, C(pq,q)) = p`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/700](https://www.erdosproblems.com/700)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (p q : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → Nat.Prime q → p < q → Erdos700.f (p * q) = p

declarations.docstring:
`f(p^a) = p` for a prime `p` and `a ≥ 2` (recorded by Erdős–Szekeres [ErSz78]). In particular,
since `(p^a) / P(p^a) = p^{a-1}`, the prime power `p^a` is a "hit" (`f(n) = n / P(n)`) if and only
if `a = 2`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/700](https://www.erdosproblems.com/700)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (p a : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → 2 ≤ a → Erdos700.f (p ^ a) = p

declarations.docstring:
Characterise those composite $n$ such that $f(n) = n/Q(n)$, where $Q(n)$ is the largest
prime-power divisor of $n$. This is the reading of part (a) in Erdős–Szekeres
[ErSz78, pp. 98–99](https://combinatorica.hu/~p_erdos/1978-46.pdf).
references: [erdosproblems.com/700](https://www.erdosproblems.com/700)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | ¬Nat.Prime n ∧ 1 < n ∧ Erdos700.f n = n / Erdos700.Q n} = Erdos700.erdos_700.variants.prime_power_divisor.answer

declarations.docstring: `f n` unfolds to the infimum of `fSet n`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/700](https://www.erdosproblems.com/700)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), Erdos700.f n = sInf (Erdos700.fSet n)

declarations.docstring: `f n` is a lower bound: `f n ≤ gcd(n, C(n,k))` for every `1 < k ≤ n/2`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/700](https://www.erdosproblems.com/700)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 1 < k → k ≤ n / 2 → Erdos700.f n ≤ n.gcd (n.choose k)

declarations.docstring: Each `gcd(n, C(n,k))` with `1 < k ≤ n/2` belongs to `fSet n`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/700](https://www.erdosproblems.com/700)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 1 < k → k ≤ n / 2 → n.gcd (n.choose k) ∈ Erdos700.fSet n

declarations.docstring: Lucas (one step): for prime `P ∣ n`, if `P ∤ C(n,k)` then `P ∣ k`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/700](https://www.erdosproblems.com/700)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (P n k : ℕ), Nat.Prime P → P ∣ n → ¬P ∣ n.choose k → P ∣ k

declarations.docstring: At $n = 12$, $f(n) = 3 = n/Q(n)$, whereas $n/P(n) = 4$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/700](https://www.erdosproblems.com/700)

declarations.docstring:
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of sets closed under taking subsets (i.e. if
$B\subseteq A\in\mathcal{F}$ then $B\in \mathcal{F}$). There exists some element $x$ such that
whenever $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq \mathcal{F}$ is an intersecting subfamily we have
$$\lvert \mathcal{F}'\rvert \leq \lvert \{ A\in \mathcal{F} : x\in A\}\rvert.$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/701](https://www.erdosproblems.com/701)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {X : Type} [Nonempty X] [Fintype X] (F : Set (Set X)),
  IsLowerSet F → ∃ x, ∀ F' ⊆ F, F'.Intersecting → Cardinal.mk ↑F' ≤ Cardinal.mk ↑{A | A ∈ F ∧ x ∈ A}

declarations.docstring:
Does $\chi(G_n)$ grow exponentially in $n$?

Yes: Frankl and Wilson [FrWi81] proved an exponential lower bound and Larman and Rogers
[LaRo72] proved an exponential upper bound. Here exponential growth means that there are
constants $1 < c \leq C$ such that $c^n \leq \chi(G_n) \leq C^n$ for all large $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/704](https://www.erdosproblems.com/704)
[Da26] Davies, J., *Measurable obstructions for unmeasurable colourings*. Preprint (2026). [arXiv:2610.12301](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12301)
[Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*. Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
[FrWi81] Frankl, P. and Wilson, R. M., *Intersection theorems with geometric consequences*. Combinatorica (1981), 357-368.
[LaRo72] Larman, D. G. and Rogers, C. A., *The realization of distances within sets in Euclidean space*. Mathematika (1972), 1-24.
[Pr20] Prosanov, R., *A new proof of the Larman-Rogers upper bound for the chromatic number of the Euclidean space*. Discrete Appl. Math. (2020), 115-120.
[Ra00] Raigorodskii, A. M., *On the chromatic number of a space*. Uspekhi Mat. Nauk (2000), 147-148.
declarations.type_pretty:
(∃ c > 1, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ (k : ℕ), (Erdos704.unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k → c ^ n ≤ ↑k) ∧
  ∃ C, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ k, (Erdos704.unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k ∧ ↑k ≤ C ^ n

declarations.docstring:
Let $G_n$ be the unit distance graph in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with two vertices joined by an edge if
and only if the distance between them is $1$. Does
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\chi(G_n)^{1/n}$$
exist?

This generalises the Hadwiger–Nelson problem (Erdős Problem 508), the case $n = 2$. The
chromatic number is finite (see `Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.cube_colouring`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/704](https://www.erdosproblems.com/704)
[Da26] Davies, J., *Measurable obstructions for unmeasurable colourings*. Preprint (2026). [arXiv:2610.12301](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12301)
[Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*. Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
[FrWi81] Frankl, P. and Wilson, R. M., *Intersection theorems with geometric consequences*. Combinatorica (1981), 357-368.
[LaRo72] Larman, D. G. and Rogers, C. A., *The realization of distances within sets in Euclidean space*. Mathematika (1972), 1-24.
[Pr20] Prosanov, R., *A new proof of the Larman-Rogers upper bound for the chromatic number of the Euclidean space*. Discrete Appl. Math. (2020), 115-120.
[Ra00] Raigorodskii, A. M., *On the chromatic number of a space*. Uspekhi Mat. Nauk (2000), 147-148.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ L, Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(Erdos704.unitDistanceGraph n).chromaticNumber.toNat ^ (1 / ↑n)) Filter.atTop (nhds L)

declarations.docstring:
The trivial colouring (by tiling with cubes) gives
$$\chi(G_n) \leq (2 + \sqrt{n})^n.$$
In particular $\chi(G_n)$ is finite for every $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/704](https://www.erdosproblems.com/704)
[Da26] Davies, J., *Measurable obstructions for unmeasurable colourings*. Preprint (2026). [arXiv:2610.12301](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12301)
[Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*. Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
[FrWi81] Frankl, P. and Wilson, R. M., *Intersection theorems with geometric consequences*. Combinatorica (1981), 357-368.
[LaRo72] Larman, D. G. and Rogers, C. A., *The realization of distances within sets in Euclidean space*. Mathematika (1972), 1-24.
[Pr20] Prosanov, R., *A new proof of the Larman-Rogers upper bound for the chromatic number of the Euclidean space*. Discrete Appl. Math. (2020), 115-120.
[Ra00] Raigorodskii, A. M., *On the chromatic number of a space*. Uspekhi Mat. Nauk (2000), 147-148.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), ∃ k, (Erdos704.unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k ∧ ↑k ≤ (2 + √↑n) ^ n

declarations.docstring:
Davies [Da26, Theorem 1.4] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \geq (2 + o(1))^n,$$
improving the bound of Raigorodskii (see `Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.raigorodskii`): for every
$0 < c < 2$ we have $\chi(G_n) \geq c^n$ for all large $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/704](https://www.erdosproblems.com/704)
[Da26] Davies, J., *Measurable obstructions for unmeasurable colourings*. Preprint (2026). [arXiv:2610.12301](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12301)

[Pr20] Prosanov, R., *A new proof of the Larman-Rogers upper bound for the chromatic number of the Euclidean space*. Discrete Appl. Math. (2020), 115-120.
[Ra00] Raigorodskii, A. M., *On the chromatic number of a space*. Uspekhi Mat. Nauk (2000), 147-148.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ c ∈ Set.Ioo 0 2, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ (k : ℕ), (Erdos704.unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k → c ^ n ≤ ↑k

declarations.docstring:
Davies [Da26, Theorem 1.5] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \leq (3\sqrt{3}/2 + o(1))^n,$$
improving the bound of Larman and Rogers (see `Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.larman_rogers`).
(The abstract of [Da26] prints $3\sqrt{3}/4$; Theorem 1.5 has $3\sqrt{3}/2 \approx 2.598$.)
references: [erdosproblems.com/704](https://www.erdosproblems.com/704)
[Da26] Davies, J., *Measurable obstructions for unmeasurable colourings*. Preprint (2026). [arXiv:2610.12301](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12301)

[Ra00] Raigorodskii, A. M., *On the chromatic number of a space*. Uspekhi Mat. Nauk (2000), 147-148.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ C > 3 * √3 / 2, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ k, (Erdos704.unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k ∧ ↑k ≤ C ^ n

declarations.docstring:
Frankl and Wilson [FrWi81] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \geq (1 + o(1)) 1.2^n.$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/704](https://www.erdosproblems.com/704)
[Da26] Davies, J., *Measurable obstructions for unmeasurable colourings*. Preprint (2026). [arXiv:2610.12301](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12301)

declarations.type_pretty: ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ (k : ℕ), (Erdos704.unitDistanceGraph n).Colorable k → (1 - ε) * 1.2 ^ n ≤ ↑k

declarations.docstring:
Larman and Rogers [LaRo72] proved
$$\chi(G_n) \leq (3 + o(1))^n.$$
Prosanov [Pr20] has given an alternative proof of this bound.
references: [erdosproblems.com/704](https://www.erdosproblems.com/704)

declarations.docstring:
Larman and Rogers [LaRo72] conjecture that the truth may be
$$\chi(G_n) = (2^{3/2} + o(1))^n,$$
that is, $\chi(G_n)^{1/n} \to 2^{3/2}$.

This is false: by `Erdos704.erdos_704.variants.davies_upper` [Da26] we have
$\limsup \chi(G_n)^{1/n} \leq 3\sqrt{3}/2 < 2^{3/2}$. Whether the limit exists remains open
(`Erdos704.erdos_704.parts.ii`).

declarations.docstring:
Let $L(r)$ be such that if $G$ is a graph formed by taking a finite set of points $P$ in
$\mathbb{R}^2$ and some set $A\subset (0,\infty)$ of size $r$, where the vertex set is $P$ and
there is an edge between two points if and only if their distance is a member of $A$, then
$\chi(G)\leq L(r)$.

Estimate $L(r)$. In particular, is it true that $L(r)\leq r^{O(1)}$?

The case $r=1$ is the Hadwiger-Nelson problem, for which it is known that
$5\leq L(1)\leq 7$.

See also [508](https://www.erdosproblems.com/508), [704](https://www.erdosproblems.com/704),
and [705](https://www.erdosproblems.com/705).

Here $L(r)\leq r^{O(1)}$ is read as: there is $C$ with $\chi(G)\leq r^C$ for all large $r$. Small
$r$ must be excluded, since $L(1)\geq 5 > 1^C$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/706](https://www.erdosproblems.com/706)
[Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*. Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C,
  ∀ᶠ (r : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))) (A : Finset ℝ),
      A.card = r → (∀ a ∈ A, 0 < a) → (SimpleGraph.DistancePlaneGraph ↑A ↑P).chromaticNumber ≤ ↑(r ^ C)

declarations.docstring:

of size $n$, in any interval $I$ of $f(n)\max(A)$ consecutive integers there exist distinct
$x_1,\ldots,x_n\in I$ such that $a_i\mid x_i$.

We read "good bounds" as determining the order of magnitude of $f(n)$.

such that $k\mid a_k$ for all $1\leq k\leq n$. Obtain an asymptotic formula for $f(n)$.

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Pomerance [ErPo80] proved
$$\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{e}}+o(1)\right)n\left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)^{1/2}
\leq f(n) \leq (1.7398\cdots+o(1))n(\log n)^{1/2}.$$

This is the lower bound [ErPo80, Theorem 2].
references: [erdosproblems.com/710](https://www.erdosproblems.com/710)

[ErPo80] Erdős, P. and Pomerance, C., *Matching the natural numbers up to $n$ with distinct multiples in another interval*. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch. Indag. Math. 42 (1980), 147-161. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-13.pdf)

  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, (2 / √(Real.exp 1) - ε) * ↑n * √(Real.log ↑n / Real.log (Real.log ↑n)) ≤ ↑(Erdos710.f n)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Pomerance [ErPo80] proved
$$\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{e}}+o(1)\right)n\left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)^{1/2}
\leq f(n) \leq (1.7398\cdots+o(1))n(\log n)^{1/2}.$$

This is the upper bound. Here $1.7398\cdots = \sqrt{r}/(1-r)$, where $r$ is the solution of
$e^{-r} = r$ [ErPo80, (11), p. 154].
references: [erdosproblems.com/710](https://www.erdosproblems.com/710)

[ErPo80] Erdős, P. and Pomerance, C., *Matching the natural numbers up to $n$ with distinct multiples in another interval*. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch. Indag. Math. 42 (1980), 147-161. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-13.pdf)

$$\frac{\mathrm{ex}_r(n,K_k^r)}{\binom{n}{r}},$$
where $\mathrm{ex}_r(n,K_k^r)$ is the largest number of $r$-edges which can placed on $n$ vertices
so that there exists no set of $k$ vertices which is covered by all $\binom{k}{r}$ possible
$r$-edges.

[Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved. Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.

        (nhds (Erdos712.erdos_712.answer k r))
