declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for every bipartite graph $G$, there exists some $\alpha\in [1,2)$ and $c>0$ such that $$\mathrm{ex}(n;G)\sim cn^\alpha?$$

The condition that $G$ have at least two edges excludes degenerate forbidden graphs whose
extremal number is eventually zero, for which the displayed asymptotic with $c>0$ is impossible.
references: [erdosproblems.com/713](https://www.erdosproblems.com/713)
[Er67d] Erdős, P., *Some recent results on extremal problems in graph theory. {R}esults*. (1967), 117--123 (English); pp. 124--130 (French).
[ErSi70] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Some extremal problems in graph theory*. Combinatorial theory and its applications, I-III (Proc. Colloq., Balatonfüred, 1969) (1970), 377-390.
[FrFu87] Frankl, P. and Füredi, Z., *Exact solution of some Turán-type problems*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1987), 226--262.
[FuGe21] Füredi, Zoltán and Gerbner, Dániel, *Hypergraphs without exponents*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2021), Paper No. 105517, 9.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (q : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin q)),
  G.IsBipartite →
    2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
      ∃ α c,
        α ∈ Set.Ico 1 2 ∧
          0 < c ∧ Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ↑(SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n G)) fun n => c * ↑n ^ α

declarations.docstring:
Must $\alpha$ be rational?

The same nondegeneracy condition on $G$ is used as in part (i). Rationality means that the real
number $\alpha$ lies in the image of the canonical embedding $\mathbb{Q}\to\mathbb{R}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/713](https://www.erdosproblems.com/713)
[Er67d] Erdős, P., *Some recent results on extremal problems in graph theory. {R}esults*. (1967), 117--123 (English); pp. 124--130 (French).
[ErSi70] Erdős, P. and Simonovits, M., *Some extremal problems in graph theory*. Combinatorial theory and its applications, I-III (Proc. Colloq., Balatonfüred, 1969) (1970), 377-390.
[FrFu87] Frankl, P. and Füredi, Z., *Exact solution of some Turán-type problems*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1987), 226--262.
[FuGe21] Füredi, Zoltán and Gerbner, Dániel, *Hypergraphs without exponents*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (2021), Paper No. 105517, 9.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (q : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin q)),
  G.IsBipartite →
    2 ≤ G.edgeFinset.card →
      ∀ (α c : ℝ),
        α ∈ Set.Ico 1 2 →
          0 < c →
            (Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ↑(SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n G)) fun n => c * ↑n ^ α) →
              α ∈ Set.range Rat.cast

declarations.docstring: Is it true that $$\mathrm{ex}(n; K_{r,r}) \gg n^{2-1/r}?$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/714](https://www.erdosproblems.com/714)
[Br66] Brown, W. G., *On graphs that do not contain a Thomsen graph*. Canad. Math. Bull. (1966), 281-285.
[ERS66] Erdős, P. and Rényi, A. and Sós, V. T., *On a problem of graph theory*. Studia Sci. Math. Hungar. (1966), 215--235.
[KST54] Kövari, T. and Sós, V. T. and Turán, P., *On a problem of K. Zarankiewicz*. Colloq. Math. (1954), 50-57.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  2 ≤ r →
    ∃ c,
      0 < c ∧
        ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
          c * ↑n ^ (2 - 1 / ↑r) ≤ ↑(SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin r) (Fin r)))

declarations.docstring:
Let $r\geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{ex}_r(n;K_{r+1}^r)$ be the maximum number of $r$-edges that can
be placed on $n$ vertices without forming a $K_{r+1}^r$ (the $r$-uniform complete graph on
$r+1$ vertices). Is every
$r$-hypergraph $G$ on $n$ vertices the union of at most $\mathrm{ex}_{r}(n;K_{r+1}^r)$ many copies
of $K_r^r$ and $K_{r+1}^r$, no two of which share a $K_r^r$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/719](https://www.erdosproblems.com/719)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  2 ≤ r →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Finset (Finset (Fin n))),
      H.IsUniform r →
        ∃ D, H.IsCompleteHypergraphDecomposition r D ∧ D.card ≤ Hypergraph.cliqueExtremalNumber n r (r + 1)

declarations.docstring: If there is a finite projective plane of order $n$ then must $n$ be a prime power?
references: [erdosproblems.com/723](https://www.erdosproblems.com/723)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ {P L : Type} (x : Membership P L) (x_1 : Fintype P) (x_2 : Fintype L) (pp : Configuration.ProjectivePlane P L),
    IsPrimePow (Configuration.ProjectivePlane.order P L)

declarations.docstring:
Bruck and Ryser have proved that if $n \equiv 1 (\mod 4)$ or $n \equiv 2 (\mod 4)$ then $n$ must be
the sum of two squares.
references: [erdosproblems.com/723](https://www.erdosproblems.com/723)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {P L : Type} [inst : Membership P L] [Fintype P] [Fintype L] (n : ℕ) (pp : Configuration.ProjectivePlane P L),
  Configuration.ProjectivePlane.order P L = n → n ≡ 1 [MOD 4] ∨ n ≡ 2 [MOD 4] → ∃ a b, n = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2

declarations.docstring: It is open whether there exists a projective plane of order 12.
references: [erdosproblems.com/723](https://www.erdosproblems.com/723)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ P L x x_1 x_2 pp, Configuration.ProjectivePlane.order P L = 12

declarations.docstring: This conjecture has been proved for $n \leq 11$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/723](https://www.erdosproblems.com/723)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {P L : Type} [inst : Membership P L] [Fintype P] [Fintype L] (pp : Configuration.ProjectivePlane P L),
  Configuration.ProjectivePlane.order P L ≤ 11 → IsPrimePow (Configuration.ProjectivePlane.order P L)

declarations.docstring: These always exist if $n$ is a prime power.
references: [erdosproblems.com/723](https://www.erdosproblems.com/723)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), IsPrimePow n → ∃ P L x x_1 x_2 pp, Configuration.ProjectivePlane.order P L = n

declarations.docstring: There are $n!$ Latin rectangles with one row.
references: [erdosproblems.com/725](https://www.erdosproblems.com/725)
[Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*. Combinatorica 1 (1981), 25-42. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-16.pdf)
[ErKa46] Erdős, P. and Kaplansky, I., *The asymptotic number of Latin rectangles*. Amer. J. Math. 68 (1946), 230-236. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1946-12.pdf)
[Ya51] Yamamoto, K., *On the asymptotic number of Latin rectangles*. Jpn. J. Math. 21 (1951), 113-119.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), Erdos725.L 1 n = n.factorial

declarations.docstring:
Give an asymptotic formula for the number of $k\times n$ Latin rectangles.

The formula $F(k,n)$ must satisfy $L(k,n)\sim F(k,n)$ as $n\to\infty$ for every choice of
$k=k(n)\leq n$, so it also covers Latin squares ($k=n$).
references: [erdosproblems.com/725](https://www.erdosproblems.com/725)
[Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*. Combinatorica 1 (1981), 25-42. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-16.pdf)
[ErKa46] Erdős, P. and Kaplansky, I., *The asymptotic number of Latin rectangles*. Amer. J. Math. 68 (1946), 230-236. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1946-12.pdf)
[Ya51] Yamamoto, K., *On the asymptotic number of Latin rectangles*. Jpn. J. Math. 21 (1951), 113-119.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k : ℕ → ℕ),
  (∀ (n : ℕ), k n ≤ n) →
    Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ↑(Erdos725.L (k n) n)) fun n => Erdos725.erdos_725.answer (k n) n

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Kaplansky [ErKa46] proved the count is
$$\sim e^{-\binom{k}{2}}(n!)^k$$
when $k=o((\log n)^{3/2-\epsilon})$.

Here $\epsilon>0$ is fixed.
references: [erdosproblems.com/725](https://www.erdosproblems.com/725)
[Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*. Combinatorica 1 (1981), 25-42. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-16.pdf)
[ErKa46] Erdős, P. and Kaplansky, I., *The asymptotic number of Latin rectangles*. Amer. J. Math. 68 (1946), 230-236. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1946-12.pdf)
[Ya51] Yamamoto, K., *On the asymptotic number of Latin rectangles*. Jpn. J. Math. 21 (1951), 113-119.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (ε : ℝ),
  0 < ε →
    ∀ (k : ℕ → ℕ),
      ((fun n => ↑(k n)) =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => Real.log ↑n ^ (3 / 2 - ε)) →
        Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ↑(Erdos725.L (k n) n)) fun n =>
          Real.exp (-↑((k n).choose 2)) * ↑n.factorial ^ k n

declarations.docstring:
Yamamoto [Ya51] extended this to $k\leq n^{1/3-o(1)}$.

As in [Ya51, p. 113], we assume $k<n^{1/3-\delta}$ with $n^{-\delta}\to 0$, where $\delta$
may be a positive constant or a function of $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/725](https://www.erdosproblems.com/725)
[Er81] Erdős, P., *On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved*. Combinatorica 1 (1981), 25-42. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-16.pdf)
[ErKa46] Erdős, P. and Kaplansky, I., *The asymptotic number of Latin rectangles*. Amer. J. Math. 68 (1946), 230-236. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1946-12.pdf)
[Ya51] Yamamoto, K., *On the asymptotic number of Latin rectangles*. Jpn. J. Math. 21 (1951), 113-119.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (δ : ℕ → ℝ),
  Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑n ^ (-δ n)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0) →
    ∀ (k : ℕ → ℕ),
      (∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(k n) < ↑n ^ (1 / 3 - δ n)) →
        Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ↑(Erdos725.L (k n) n)) fun n =>
          Real.exp (-↑((k n).choose 2)) * ↑n.factorial ^ k n

declarations.docstring:
As $n\to \infty$ ranges over integers
$\sum_{p\leq n}1_{n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}}\frac{1}{p}\sim \frac{\log\log n}{2}$?

A conjecture of Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75].

By $n\in (p/2,p)\pmod{p}$ we mean $n\equiv r\pmod{p}$ for some integer $r$ with $p/2<r<p$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/726](https://www.erdosproblems.com/726)
[EGRS75] Erdős, P., and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., On the prime factors of $(\sp{2n}\sb{n})$. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop
    (fun n => ∑ p ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with Nat.Prime p ∧ ↑p / 2 < ↑n % ↑p, 1 / ↑p) fun n =>
    Real.log (Real.log ↑n) / 2

declarations.docstring: The classical estimate of Mertens states that $\sum_{p\leq n}\frac{1}{p}\sim \log\log n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/726](https://www.erdosproblems.com/726)
[EGRS75] Erdős, P., and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., On the prime factors of $(\sp{2n}\sb{n})$. Math. Comp. (1975), 83-92.
declarations.type_pretty:
Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun n => ∑ p ∈ Finset.range (n + 1) with Nat.Prime p, 1 / ↑p) fun n =>
  Real.log (Real.log ↑n)

declarations.docstring: Let $k ≥ 2$. Does $((n+k)!)^2∣(2n)!$ hold for infinitely many $n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/727](https://www.erdosproblems.com/727)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ k ≥ 2, {n | (n + k).factorial ^ 2 ∣ (2 * n).factorial}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Balakran proved this holds for $k = 1$.

Let $k = 1$. Does $((n+k)!)^2∣(2n)!$ for infinitely many $n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/727](https://www.erdosproblems.com/727)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | (n + 1).factorial ^ 2 ∣ (2 * n).factorial}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus observe that the method of Balakran can be further used to prove
that there are infinitely many $n$ such that $(n+k)!(n+1)!∣(2n)!$
references: [erdosproblems.com/727](https://www.erdosproblems.com/727)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 2 ≤ k → {n | (n + k).factorial * (n + 1).factorial ∣ (2 * n).factorial}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
It is open even for $k = 2$.
Let $k = 2$. Does $((n+k)!)^2∣(2n)!$ hold for infinitely many n?
references: [erdosproblems.com/727](https://www.erdosproblems.com/727)
declarations.type_pretty: {n | (n + 2).factorial ^ 2 ∣ (2 * n).factorial}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Find some reasonable function $f(n)$ such that, for almost all integers $n$, the least integer
$m$ such that $m\nmid \binom{2n}{n}$ satisfies
$$m\sim f(n).$$

Here "almost all" means natural density $1$, and $m \sim f(n)$ means that for every
$\varepsilon>0$ the set of $n$ with $|m/f(n)-1|<\varepsilon$ has density $1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/731](https://www.erdosproblems.com/731)
[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., *On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$*. Math. Comp. 29 (1975), 83-92. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-27.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ ε > 0, {n | |↑(Erdos731.leastNonDivisor n) / Erdos731.erdos_731.answer n - 1| < ε}.HasDensity 1

declarations.docstring:
A problem of Erdős, Graham, Ruzsa, and Straus [EGRS75], who say it is 'not hard to show that',
for almost all $n$, the minimal such $m$ satisfies
$$m=\exp((\log n)^{1/2+o(1)}).$$

[EGRS75, (8), p. 91] states this as: for every $\varepsilon>0$, for all $n$ outside a set of
density $0$, $\exp((\log n)^{1/2-\varepsilon}) < m < \exp((\log n)^{1/2+\varepsilon})$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/731](https://www.erdosproblems.com/731)
[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., *On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$*. Math. Comp. 29 (1975), 83-92. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-27.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ ε > 0,
  {n |
        Real.exp (Real.log ↑n ^ (1 / 2 - ε)) < ↑(Erdos731.leastNonDivisor n) ∧
          ↑(Erdos731.leastNonDivisor n) < Real.exp (Real.log ↑n ^ (1 / 2 + ε))}.HasDensity
    1

declarations.docstring: $A(1)=3$, since $\binom{2}{1}=2$ is divisible by $1$ and $2$ but not by $3$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/731](https://www.erdosproblems.com/731)
[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., *On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$*. Math. Comp. 29 (1975), 83-92. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-27.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos731.leastNonDivisor 1 = 3

declarations.docstring: `leastNonDivisor n` is a positive integer that does not divide $\binom{2n}{n}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/731](https://www.erdosproblems.com/731)
[EGRS75] Erdős, P. and Graham, R. L. and Ruzsa, I. Z. and Straus, E. G., *On the prime factors of $\binom{2n}{n}$*. Math. Comp. 29 (1975), 83-92. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-27.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < Erdos731.leastNonDivisor n ∧ ¬Erdos731.leastNonDivisor n ∣ n.centralBinom

declarations.docstring:
Call a sequence $1< X_1\leq \cdots \leq X_m\leq n$ block-compatible if there is a pairwise balanced
block design $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that $\lvert A_i\rvert=X_i$ for $1\leq
i\leq m$. (A pairwise block design means that every pair in $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ is contained in exactly
one of the $A_i$.) Are there necessary and sufficient conditions for $(X_i)$ to be block-compatible?
Is there some constant $c>0$ such that for all large $n$ there are
$$\geq \exp(c n^{1/2}\log n)$$
many block-compatible sequences for $\{1,\ldots,n\}$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/732](https://www.erdosproblems.com/732)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ) (s : List ℕ), s ∈ Hypergraph.blockSizeProfiles n ↔ Erdos732.erdos_732.parts.i.answer n s

declarations.docstring:
Is there some constant $c>0$ such that for all large $n$ there are at least
$\exp(c n^{1/2}\log n)$ block-compatible sequences?

Alon has proved there are at least $2^{(\frac{1}{2}+o(1))n^{1/2}\log n}$ many sequences
which are block-compatible for $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/732](https://www.erdosproblems.com/732)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Real.exp (c * √↑n * Real.log ↑n) ≤ ↑(Hypergraph.blockSizeProfiles n).card

declarations.docstring:
Find, for all large $n$, a non-trivial pairwise balanced block design $A_1,\ldots,A_m\subseteq
\{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that, for all $t$, there are $O(n^{1/2})$ many $i$ such that $\lvert
A_i\rvert=t$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/734](https://www.erdosproblems.com/734)
[Er81] Erdős, P., On the combinatorial problems which I would most like to see solved. Combinatorica (1981), 25-42.
[dBEr48] de Bruijn, N. G. and Erdős, P., On a combinatorial problem. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch., Proc. (1948), 1277--1279 = Indagationes Math. 10, 421--423.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C,
  0 < C ∧
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∃ H, H.IsPairwiseBalancedDesign ∧ (∀ e ∈ H, e.card < n) ∧ ∀ (t : ℕ), ↑{e ∈ H | e.card = t}.card ≤ C * √↑n

declarations.docstring:
The set of edge distances to a bipartite graph is always non-empty because deleting all edges
from a graph makes it bipartite.
references: [erdosproblems.com/74](https://www.erdosproblems.com/74)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {V : Type u} {G : SimpleGraph V} (A : G.Subgraph), (Erdos74.SimpleGraph.edgeDistancesToBipartite A).Nonempty

declarations.docstring:
The set of minimum edge distances to bipartite for subgraphs of size `n` is bounded above.
A graph on `n` vertices has at most `n choose 2` edges, and deleting all of them
makes the graph bipartite, providing a straightforward upper bound.
references: [erdosproblems.com/74](https://www.erdosproblems.com/74)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {V : Type u} (G : SimpleGraph V) (n : ℕ), BddAbove (Erdos74.SimpleGraph.subgraphEdgeDistsToBipartite G n)

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n)\to \infty$ possibly very slowly.
Is there a graph of infinite chromatic number such that every finite subgraph on $n$
vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most $f(n)$ edges?

The answer is no. A machine-checked disproof constructs a function $f(n) \to \infty$ for which
every graph satisfying this local deletion bound has finite chromatic number.
references: [erdosproblems.com/74](https://www.erdosproblems.com/74)
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ),
    Filter.Tendsto f Filter.atTop Filter.atTop →
      ∃ V G, G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), Erdos74.SimpleGraph.maxSubgraphEdgeDistToBipartite G n ≤ f n

declarations.docstring:
Is there a graph of infinite chromatic number such that every finite subgraph on $n$
vertices can be made bipartite by deleting at most $\sqrt{n}$ edges?
references: [erdosproblems.com/74](https://www.erdosproblems.com/74)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ V G, G.chromaticNumber = ⊤ ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ), ↑(Erdos74.SimpleGraph.maxSubgraphEdgeDistToBipartite G n) ≤ √↑n

declarations.docstring:
Let $\mathfrak{m}$ be an infinite cardinal and $G$ be a graph with chromatic number $\mathfrak{m}$.
Let $r\geq 1$. Must $G$ contain a subgraph of chromatic number $\mathfrak{m}$ which does not contain
any odd cycle of length $\leq r$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/740](https://erdosproblems.com/740)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (V : Type u_1) (G : SimpleGraph V),
  Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ G.chromaticCardinal →
    ∀ (r : ℕ), ∃ H, H.coe.chromaticCardinal = G.chromaticCardinal ∧ Erdos740.NoShortOddCycle H.coe r

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $A+A$ has positive upper density.
Can one always decompose $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ such that $A_1+A_1$ and $A_2+A_2$
both have positive upper density?

This was proved by the DeepMind prover agent.
references: [erdosproblems.com/741](https://www.erdosproblems.com/741)
[Er94b] Erdős, Paul, Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry. Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (A : Set ℕ),
  0 < (A + A).upperDensity →
    ∃ A₁ A₂, A = A₁ ∪ A₂ ∧ Disjoint A₁ A₂ ∧ 0 < (A₁ + A₁).upperDensity ∧ 0 < (A₂ + A₂).upperDensity

declarations.docstring:
Is there a basis $A$ of order $2$ such that if $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ then $A_1+A_1$ and $A_2+A_2$
cannot both have bounded gaps?

This was proved by DeepMind prover agent.
references: [erdosproblems.com/741](https://www.erdosproblems.com/741)
[Er94b] Erdős, Paul, Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry. Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ A,
  (A ∪ {0}).IsAddBasisOfOrder 2 ∧
    ∀ (A₁ A₂ : Set ℕ), A = A₁ ∪ A₂ → Disjoint A₁ A₂ → ¬(IsSyndetic (A₁ + A₁) ∧ IsSyndetic (A₂ + A₂))

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $A+A$ has positive density in the literal sense that its
natural density exists and is positive.
Can one always decompose $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ such that $A_1+A_1$ and $A_2+A_2$
both have positive density in this sense?

This was disproved by the DeepMind prover agent.
references: [erdosproblems.com/741](https://www.erdosproblems.com/741)
[Er94b] Erdős, Paul, Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry. Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    (A + A).HasPosDensity → ∃ A₁ A₂, A = A₁ ∪ A₂ ∧ Disjoint A₁ A₂ ∧ (A₁ + A₁).HasPosDensity ∧ (A₂ + A₂).HasPosDensity

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be such that $A+A$ has positive lower density.
Can one always decompose $A=A_1\sqcup A_2$ such that $A_1+A_1$ and $A_2+A_2$
both have positive lower density?
references: [erdosproblems.com/741](https://www.erdosproblems.com/741)
[Er94b] Erdős, Paul, Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry. Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (A : Set ℕ),
  0 < (A + A).lowerDensity →
    ∃ A₁ A₂, A = A₁ ∪ A₂ ∧ Disjoint A₁ A₂ ∧ 0 < (A₁ + A₁).lowerDensity ∧ 0 < (A₂ + A₂).lowerDensity

declarations.docstring:
The complete bipartite graph $K_{a, b}$ has exactly $a \cdot b$ edges. The bound
$\lfloor n^2 / 4 \rfloor$ in the Murty-Simon conjecture is attained by the balanced
case $K_{\lceil n/2 \rceil, \lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/742](https://www.erdosproblems.com/742)
[Pl75] Plesník, Ján, Critical graphs of given diameter. Acta Fac. Rerum Natur. Univ. Comenian. Math. 30 (1975), 71-93.
[CaHa79] Caccetta, L. and Häggkvist, R., On diameter critical graphs. Discrete Math. 28 (1979), 223-229.
[Fa87] Fan, Genghua, On diameter 2-critical graphs. Discrete Math. 67 (1987), 235-240.
[Fü92] Füredi, Zoltán, The maximum number of edges in a minimal graph of diameter 2. J. Graph Theory 16 (1992), 81-98.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (a b : ℕ), (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin a) (Fin b)).edgeSet.ncard = a * b

declarations.docstring:
**Murty-Simon Conjecture**

Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with diameter $2$ such that deleting any edge increases the
diameter. Is it true that $G$ has at most $\lfloor n^2 / 4 \rfloor$ edges? Equality is conjectured
to hold for the complete balanced bipartite graph $K_{\lceil n/2 \rceil, \lfloor n/2 \rfloor}$.

The conjecture is resolved up to a finite check: Fan [Fa87] verified it for $n \leq 24$ and
$n = 26$, and Füredi [Fü92] proved it for all sufficiently large $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/742](https://www.erdosproblems.com/742)
[Pl75] Plesník, Ján, Critical graphs of given diameter. Acta Fac. Rerum Natur. Univ. Comenian. Math. 30 (1975), 71-93.
[CaHa79] Caccetta, L. and Häggkvist, R., On diameter critical graphs. Discrete Math. 28 (1979), 223-229.
[Fa87] Fan, Genghua, On diameter 2-critical graphs. Discrete Math. 67 (1987), 235-240.

declarations.docstring:
Let $T_2,\ldots,T_n$ be a collection of trees such that $T_k$ has $k$ vertices. Can we always
write $K_n$ as the edge disjoint union of the $T_k$?

A conjecture of Gyárfás, known as the tree packing conjecture. We state it as a packing. For
every $n$ and all trees $T_k$ on the vertex set `Fin k`, $2 \leq k \leq n$, there are injective
maps
$f_k : \{0, \ldots, k - 1\} \to \{0, \ldots, n - 1\}$ such that the graphs $f_k(T_k)$ are
pairwise edge-disjoint (see `IsPacking`). Every tree with $k$ vertices is isomorphic to a tree
on `Fin k`, so this covers every collection of trees.

A tree with $k$ vertices has $k - 1$ edges, and $\sum_{k=2}^{n} (k - 1) = \binom{n}{2}$ is the
number of edges of $K_n$. Hence the copies $f_k(T_k)$ of a packing cover every edge of $K_n$.
So a packing is the same as a decomposition of $K_n$ into copies of $T_2, \ldots, T_n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/743](https://www.erdosproblems.com/743)

Allen, Böttcher, Clemens, Hladký, Piguet, and Taraz [ABCHPT21] proved that this conjecture holds
when all the trees have maximum degree $\leq c\frac{n}{\log n}$ for some constant $c>0$. That is,
there is $c > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$ the following holds. If $T_k$ is a tree
with $k$ vertices and maximum degree at most $cn/\log n$ for $2 \leq k \leq n$, then $K_n$
decomposes into $T_2, \ldots, T_n$.

bounded maximum degree. That is, for every $d$ there is $N$ such that for all $n \geq N$ the

such that the lower density of $A+A$ is at least $1-\epsilon$

then `H` contains an independent set of size `> n ^ (1 - ε)`?
references: [erdosproblems.com/75] (https://www.erdosproblems.com/75)
declarations.type_pretty:

  G.chromaticCardinal = Cardinal.aleph 1 ∧
    Cardinal.mk V = Cardinal.aleph 1 ∧
      ∀ ε > 0,
        ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
          ∀ (H : G.Subgraph), H.verts.ncard = n → ∃ I, ↑I ⊆ H.verts ∧ G.IsIndepSet ↑I ∧ ↑I.card > ↑n ^ (1 - ε)

declarations.docstring: If `Dicolorable G k` holds, then $\delta(G) \leq k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/761](https://www.erdosproblems.com/761)
[ErGi93] Erdős, P. and Gimbel, J., *Some problems and results in cochromatic theory*. Quo vadis, graph theory? (1993), 261-264.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {V : Type u_1} {G : SimpleGraph V} {k : ℕ}, Erdos761.Dicolorable G k → Erdos761.dichromaticNumber G ≤ ↑k

declarations.docstring:
The dichromatic number of $G$, denoted by $\delta(G)$, is the minimum number $k$ of colours
required such that, in any orientation of the edges of $G$, there is a $k$-colouring of the
vertices of $G$ such that there are no monochromatic oriented cycles.

Must a graph with large chromatic number have large dichromatic number?

This question is due to Erdős and Neumann-Lara. We read it for finite graphs: for every $k$ there
is $m$ such that every finite graph with $\chi(G)\geq m$ has $\delta(G)\geq k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/761](https://www.erdosproblems.com/761)
[ErGi93] Erdős, P. and Gimbel, J., *Some problems and results in cochromatic theory*. Quo vadis, graph theory? (1993), 261-264.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  ∃ m, ∀ (V : Type u_1) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V), ↑m ≤ G.chromaticNumber → ↑k ≤ Erdos761.dichromaticNumber G

declarations.docstring:
The cochromatic number of $G$, denoted by $\zeta(G)$, is the minimum number of colours needed to
colour the vertices of $G$ such that each colour class induces either a complete graph or empty
graph.

Must a graph with large cochromatic number contain a graph with large dichromatic number?

This question is due to Erdős and Gimbel. We read it for finite graphs and subgraphs: for every
$k$ there is $m$ such that every finite graph with $\zeta(G)\geq m$ has a subgraph $H$ with
$\delta(H)\geq k$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/761](https://www.erdosproblems.com/761)
[ErGi93] Erdős, P. and Gimbel, J., *Some problems and results in cochromatic theory*. Quo vadis, graph theory? (1993), 261-264.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  ∃ m,
    ∀ (V : Type u_1) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ↑m ≤ G.cochromaticNumber → ∃ H, ↑k ≤ Erdos761.dichromaticNumber H.coe

declarations.docstring:
A positive answer to the second question implies a positive answer to the first via the bound
mentioned in [760].
references: [erdosproblems.com/761](https://www.erdosproblems.com/761)
[ErGi93] Erdős, P. and Gimbel, J., *Some problems and results in cochromatic theory*. Quo vadis, graph theory? (1993), 261-264.
declarations.type_pretty:
(∀ (k : ℕ),
    ∃ m,
      ∀ (V : Type u) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
        ↑m ≤ G.cochromaticNumber → ∃ H, ↑k ≤ Erdos761.dichromaticNumber H.coe) →
  ∀ (k : ℕ),
    ∃ m, ∀ (V : Type u) [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V), ↑m ≤ G.chromaticNumber → ↑k ≤ Erdos761.dichromaticNumber G

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n;k,l)=\min \mathrm{ex}(n;G)$, where $G$ ranges over all graphs with $k$ vertices and $l$
edges.

Give good estimates for $f(n;k,l)$ in the range $k<l\leq k^2/4$.

In [Er64c, p. 33] this question is asked for $f_1(n;k,l)$ (`Erdos766.forcingNumber`), which
forces at least one graph with $k$ vertices and $l$ edges rather than one fixed graph; we follow
the source. The question for the function of erdosproblems.com is
`Erdos766.erdos_766.variants.minExtremalNumber_estimate`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/766](https://www.erdosproblems.com/766)
[Er64c] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in graph theory*. Theory of Graphs and its Applications (Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963) (1964), 29-36. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1964-06.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k l : ℕ),
  k < l →
    l ≤ k ^ 2 / 4 → (fun n => ↑(Erdos766.forcingNumber n k l)) =Θ[Filter.atTop] Erdos766.erdos_766.parts.i.answer k l

declarations.docstring:
For fixed $k$ and large $n$ is $f(n;k,l)$ a strictly monotone function of $l$?

As in `Erdos766.erdos_766.parts.i`, $f$ is $f_1$ of [Er64c], and we use the range
$k<l\leq k^2/4$ in which the question is asked there; here `k ^ 2 / 4` is $\lfloor k^2/4\rfloor$.
The question for the function of erdosproblems.com is
`Erdos766.erdos_766.variants.minExtremalNumber_strictMonoOn`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/766](https://www.erdosproblems.com/766)
[Er64c] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in graph theory*. Theory of Graphs and its Applications (Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963) (1964), 29-36. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1964-06.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, StrictMonoOn (Erdos766.forcingNumber n k) (Set.Ioc k (k ^ 2 / 4))

declarations.docstring:
Dirac and Erdős proved independently that when $l=\lfloor k^2/4\rfloor+1$
$$f(n;k,l)\leq \lfloor n^2/4\rfloor+1.$$

[Er64c, p. 34] states this for every $k \leq n$. We assume $k \geq 3$, since for $k \leq 2$ there
is no graph with $k$ vertices and $\lfloor k^2/4\rfloor+1$ edges.
references: [erdosproblems.com/766](https://www.erdosproblems.com/766)
[Er64c] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in graph theory*. Theory of Graphs and its Applications (Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963) (1964), 29-36. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1964-06.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → k ≤ n → Erdos766.forcingNumber n k (k ^ 2 / 4 + 1) ≤ n ^ 2 / 4 + 1

declarations.docstring:
The estimate question of `Erdos766.erdos_766.parts.i` for the function
$\min \mathrm{ex}(n;G)$ of erdosproblems.com (`Erdos766.minExtremalNumber`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/766](https://www.erdosproblems.com/766)
[Er64c] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in graph theory*. Theory of Graphs and its Applications (Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963) (1964), 29-36. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1964-06.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k l : ℕ),
  k < l →
    l ≤ k ^ 2 / 4 →
      (fun n => ↑(Erdos766.minExtremalNumber n k l).toNat) =Θ[Filter.atTop]
        Erdos766.erdos_766.variants.minExtremalNumber_estimate.answer k l

declarations.docstring:
The monotonicity question of `Erdos766.erdos_766.parts.ii` for the function
$\min \mathrm{ex}(n;G)$ of erdosproblems.com (`Erdos766.minExtremalNumber`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/766](https://www.erdosproblems.com/766)
[Er64c] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in graph theory*. Theory of Graphs and its Applications (Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963) (1964), 29-36. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1964-06.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, StrictMonoOn (Erdos766.minExtremalNumber n k) (Set.Ioc k (k ^ 2 / 4))

declarations.docstring:
If every graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges contains a graph with $k$ vertices and $l$
edges, then $f(n;k,l) \leq m$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/766](https://www.erdosproblems.com/766)
[Er64c] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in graph theory*. Theory of Graphs and its Applications (Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963) (1964), 29-36. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1964-06.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {n k l m : ℕ},
  (∀ (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G.edgeSet.ncard = m → ∃ H, H.edgeSet.ncard = l ∧ H.IsContained G) →
    Erdos766.forcingNumber n k l ≤ m

declarations.docstring:
$f(n;k,l) \leq \mathrm{ex}(n;G) + 1$ for every graph $G$ with $k$ vertices and $l$ edges,
since a graph with more than $\mathrm{ex}(n;G)$ edges contains $G$. Here $\mathrm{ex}(n;G)$ is
`SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n G`, the maximum number of edges of a graph on $n$ vertices with no
copy of $G$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/766](https://www.erdosproblems.com/766)
[Er64c] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in graph theory*. Theory of Graphs and its Applications (Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963) (1964), 29-36. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1964-06.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ) {k l : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin k)),
  G.edgeSet.ncard = l → Erdos766.forcingNumber n k l ≤ SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n G + 1

declarations.docstring:
For $k \leq n$ every graph on $n$ vertices contains the empty graph on $k$ vertices, so
$f(n;k,0) = 0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/766](https://www.erdosproblems.com/766)
[Er64c] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in graph theory*. Theory of Graphs and its Applications (Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963) (1964), 29-36. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1964-06.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n k : ℕ}, k ≤ n → Erdos766.forcingNumber n k 0 = 0

declarations.docstring:
The minimum is at most $\mathrm{ex}(n;G)$ for every graph $G$ with $k$ vertices and $l$
edges.
references: [erdosproblems.com/766](https://www.erdosproblems.com/766)
[Er64c] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in graph theory*. Theory of Graphs and its Applications (Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963) (1964), 29-36. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1964-06.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ) {k l : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin k)),
  G.edgeSet.ncard = l → Erdos766.minExtremalNumber n k l ≤ ↑(SimpleGraph.extremalNumber n G)

declarations.docstring: There is no graph with $0$ vertices and $1$ edge, so the minimum is `⊤`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/766](https://www.erdosproblems.com/766)
[Er64c] Erdős, P., *Extremal problems in graph theory*. Theory of Graphs and its Applications (Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963) (1964), 29-36. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1964-06.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), Erdos766.minExtremalNumber n 0 1 = ⊤

declarations.docstring:
Let $c(n)$ be minimal such that if $k\geq c(n)$ then the $n$-dimensional unit
cube can be decomposed into $k$ homothetic $n$-dimensional cubes. Give good
bounds for $c(n)$ — in particular, is it true that $c(n)\gg n^n$?

The `c(n) \gg n^n` conjecture is **false**: for odd `n`, one can tile the unit
`n`-cube into `k` homothetic cubes for every `k ≥ U(n)` with `U(n)/n^n → 0`, so
`c(n)/n^n → 0` along odd dimensions and no absolute constant lower-bounds it.

Determining good bounds for `c(n)` in general remains open.
references: [erdosproblems.com/769](https://www.erdosproblems.com/769)
declarations.type_pretty: ¬Erdos769.Erdos769LowerBound

declarations.docstring:
What refuting $c(n)\gg n^n$ leaves open: give good bounds for $c(n)$. Asked here on the
scale the problem itself sets, $n^n$: does $c$ have a well-defined order
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log c(n)}{n\log n}?$$
The refuted conjecture would have forced this limit to be at least $1$.
The cutoff condition is restricted to positive dimensions: in dimension zero,
exact coverage permits only one tile, so no cutoff exists.
references: [erdosproblems.com/769](https://www.erdosproblems.com/769)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c,
  (∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → Erdos769.IsCutoff n (c n)) ∧
    ∃ γ, Filter.Tendsto (fun n => Real.log ↑(c n) / (↑n * Real.log ↑n)) Filter.atTop (nhds γ)

declarations.docstring:

declarations.docstring:
Let $R(k)$ be the Ramsey number for $K_k$. Give a constructive proof that $R(k) > C^k$ for some
constant $C > 1$.

Equivalently, give an explicit construction of graphs on $n$ vertices which contain no clique
and no independent set of size $\geq c \log n$, for some constant $c > 0$.

We formalise "explicit" as: the adjacency relation of the graph on $n$ vertices is decided by a
single algorithm that runs in time polynomial in $n$ (see `explicitGraph`). This is the weakest
reasonable notion ("weakly explicit"); even this is open. The strongly explicit version, with time
polynomial in $\log n$, is `erdos_78.variants.strongly_explicit`.

This problem is #4 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.

declarations.docstring:
Do the squares contain arbitrarily long quasi-progressions? That is, does there exist some
constant $C>0$ such that, for any $k$, the squares contain a sequence $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ where, for
some $d$ and all $1\leq i<k$,
$$x_i+d\leq x_{i+1}\leq x_i+d+C.$$

A question of Brown, Erdős, and Freedman [BEF90]. This is the first question. Here $C$ and $d$ are
positive integers; $d\geq 1$ excludes constant sequences.
references: [erdosproblems.com/782](https://www.erdosproblems.com/782)

declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (k : ℕ), Erdos782.ContainsQuasiProgression {n | IsSquare n} C k

declarations.docstring:
Do the squares contain arbitrarily large cubes
$$a+\left\{ \sum_i \epsilon_ib_i : \epsilon_i\in \{0,1\}\right\}?$$

A question of Brown, Erdős, and Freedman [BEF90]. This is the second question. The generators
$b_i$ are nonzero integers, as in [BEU26]. Solymosi [So07] conjectured that the answer is no, and
Cilleruelo and Granville [CiGr07] observed that the answer is no conditional on the
Bombieri-Lang conjecture.

declarations.docstring:
Let $A,B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be infinite sets of positive integers such that $A+B$ contains all
large integers. Let $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert$ and similarly for $B(x)$. Is it true that if
$A(x)B(x)\sim x$ then
$$A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$$
as $x\to \infty$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Danzer. The answer is yes, proved by Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94],
who actually proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$

This was formalized in Lean by van Doorn using Aristotle.

declarations.docstring:
Chen and Fang [ChFa10] proved the stronger statement that $A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$ if $A$ and $B$
are infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers and
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac{5}{4}.$$
They later [ChFa14] improved $5/4$ to $3-\sqrt{3}\approx 1.268$.

declarations.docstring:
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Is there some set $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ of density $> 1 - \epsilon$
such that $a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when
$r = s$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/786](https://www.erdosproblems.com/786)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ ε > 0, ε ≤ 1 → ∃ A δ, 0 ∉ A ∧ 1 - ε < δ ∧ A.HasDensity δ ∧ Erdos786.Set.IsMulCardSet A

declarations.docstring: An example of such a set with density $\frac 1 4$ is given by the integers $\equiv 2\pmod{4}$
references: [erdosproblems.com/786](https://www.erdosproblems.com/786)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A = {n | n % 4 = 2} → A.HasDensity (1 / 4) ∧ Erdos786.Set.IsMulCardSet A

declarations.docstring:
Let $\epsilon > 0$ be given. Then, for a sufficiently large prime `p`, take the sequence of
consecutive primes $p_1 < \cdots < p_k$ such that
$$
\sum_{i=1}^k \frac{1}{p_i} < 1 < \sum_{i=1}^{k + 1} \frac{1}{p_i},
$$
and let $A$ be the set of all naturals divisible by exactly one of $p_1, ..., p_k$ (with
multiplicity $1$). Then $A$ has density $> \frac{1}{e} - \epsilon$ and has the property
that $a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when $r = s$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/786](https://www.erdosproblems.com/786)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (ε : ℝ),
  0 < ε ∧ ε < 1 / Real.exp 1 →
    ∀ᶠ (p : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      Nat.Prime p →
        ∃ k,
          ∑ q ∈ Erdos786.consecutivePrimesFrom p k, 1 / ↑q < 1 ∧
            1 < ∑ q ∈ Erdos786.consecutivePrimesFrom p (k + 1), 1 / ↑q ∧
              ∃ δ,
                1 / Real.exp 1 - ε < δ ∧
                  {n | ∑ q ∈ Erdos786.consecutivePrimesFrom p k, n.factorization q = 1}.HasDensity δ ∧
                    Erdos786.Set.IsMulCardSet {n | ∑ q ∈ Erdos786.consecutivePrimesFrom p k, n.factorization q = 1}

declarations.docstring:

$a_1\cdots a_r = b_1\cdots b_s$ with $a_i, b_j\in A$ can only hold when
$r = s$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/786](https://www.erdosproblems.com/786)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ A f,
  ∃ (_ : f =o[Filter.atTop] 1),
    ∀ (N : ℕ), A N ⊆ Set.Icc 1 (N + 1) ∧ (1 - f N) * ↑N ≤ ↑(A N).ncard ∧ Erdos786.Set.IsMulCardSet (A N)

exists some $B\subseteq A$ of size $\lvert B\rvert\geq g(n)$ such that $b_1+b_2\not\in A$ for all

Here this means that $g(n) \geq (\log n)^{1+c}$ for every $c < 1/68$ and all large $n$
[Be25, Theorem 1.2].

declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n : ℕ}, Erdos80.bookNumber ⊥ = 0

declarations.docstring: A book is counted by triangles, so `bookNumber` is `0` exactly when no edge lies in one.
references: [erdosproblems.com/80](https://www.erdosproblems.com/80)
[erdosproblems.com/600](https://www.erdosproblems.com/600), stated in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/600.lean`
[FoLo12] Fox, Jacob and Loh, Po-Shen, On a problem of Erdős and Rothschild on edges in triangles. Combinatorica (2012), 619--628.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype α] (G : SimpleGraph α) [inst_1 : DecidableRel G.Adj],
  Erdos80.bookNumber G = 0 ↔ ∀ e ∈ G.edgeFinset, G.trianglesContaining e = ∅

declarations.docstring:
Let $c>0$ and let $f_c(n)$ be the maximal $m$ such that every graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and
at least $cn^2$ edges, where each edge is contained in at least one triangle, must contain a
book of size $m$, that is, an edge shared by at least $m$ different triangles. Estimate
$f_c(n)$. In particular, is it true that $f_c(n)>n^\epsilon$ for some $\epsilon>0$?

The answer is no. Fox and Loh [FoLo12] proved that $f_c(n) \leq n^{O(1/\log\log n)}$ for every
fixed $c < 1/4$, so no $\epsilon > 0$ works for, say, $c = 1/8$. For $c > 1/4$ the situation is
different: $f_c(n) \geq n/6$, see [erdosproblems.com/80](https://www.erdosproblems.com/80).

The bound $c < 1/2$ is what makes the hypothesis satisfiable: a simple graph on $n$ vertices
has at most $n(n-1)/2$ edges, so no graph has $cn^2$ of them once $c \geq 1/2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/80](https://www.erdosproblems.com/80)
[erdosproblems.com/600](https://www.erdosproblems.com/600), stated in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/600.lean`
[FoLo12] Fox, Jacob and Loh, Po-Shen, On a problem of Erdős and Rothschild on edges in triangles. Combinatorica (2012), 619--628.
declarations.type_pretty: ¬∀ (c : ℝ), 0 < c → c < 1 / 2 → ∃ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑n ^ ε < ↑(Erdos80.f c n)

declarations.docstring:
The weaker question from the same problem: is $f_c(n) \gg \log n$?

Same feasibility bound on `c` as above.
references: [erdosproblems.com/80](https://www.erdosproblems.com/80)
[erdosproblems.com/600](https://www.erdosproblems.com/600), stated in `FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/600.lean`

declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (c : ℝ), 0 < c → c < 1 / 2 → (fun n => Real.log ↑n) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑(Erdos80.f c n)

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that any $K_r$-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $t$ contains an
independent set on
$$\gg_r \frac{\log t}{t}n$$
many vertices?

A conjecture of Ajtai, Erdős, Komlós, and Szemerédi [AEKS81].
references: [erdosproblems.com/802](https://www.erdosproblems.com/802)
[AEKS81] Ajtai, M. and Erdős, P. and Komlós, J. and Szemerédi, E., *On Turán's theorem for sparse graphs*. Combinatorica (1981), 313-317.
[AKS80] Ajtai, Miklós and Komlós, János and Szemerédi, Endre, *A note on Ramsey numbers*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1980), 354-360.
[Al96b] Alon, Noga, *Independence numbers of locally sparse graphs and a Ramsey type problem*. Random Structures Algorithms (1996), 271-278.
[Sh95] Shearer, James B., *On the independence number of sparse graphs*. Random Structures Algorithms (1995), 269-271.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  ∃ c > 0,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      G.CliqueFree r → c * (Real.log ↑G.averageDegree / ↑G.averageDegree) * ↑n ≤ ↑G.indepNum

declarations.docstring:
Ajtai, Erdős, Komlós, and Szemerédi [AEKS81] proved that any $K_r$-free graph on $n$ vertices
with average degree $t$ contains an independent set on
$$\gg_r \frac{\log\log(t+1)}{t}n$$
many vertices.
references: [erdosproblems.com/802](https://www.erdosproblems.com/802)
[AEKS81] Ajtai, M. and Erdős, P. and Komlós, J. and Szemerédi, E., *On Turán's theorem for sparse graphs*. Combinatorica (1981), 313-317.
[AKS80] Ajtai, Miklós and Komlós, János and Szemerédi, Endre, *A note on Ramsey numbers*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1980), 354-360.
[Al96b] Alon, Noga, *Independence numbers of locally sparse graphs and a Ramsey type problem*. Random Structures Algorithms (1996), 271-278.
[Sh95] Shearer, James B., *On the independence number of sparse graphs*. Random Structures Algorithms (1995), 269-271.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  ∃ c > 0,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      G.CliqueFree r → c * (Real.log (Real.log (↑G.averageDegree + 1)) / ↑G.averageDegree) * ↑n ≤ ↑G.indepNum

declarations.docstring:
Alon [Al96b] proved the conjectured bound under the stronger assumption that the induced graph
on every vertex neighbourhood has chromatic number $\leq r - 2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/802](https://www.erdosproblems.com/802)
[AEKS81] Ajtai, M. and Erdős, P. and Komlós, J. and Szemerédi, E., *On Turán's theorem for sparse graphs*. Combinatorica (1981), 313-317.
[AKS80] Ajtai, Miklós and Komlós, János and Szemerédi, Endre, *A note on Ramsey numbers*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1980), 354-360.
[Al96b] Alon, Noga, *Independence numbers of locally sparse graphs and a Ramsey type problem*. Random Structures Algorithms (1996), 271-278.
[Sh95] Shearer, James B., *On the independence number of sparse graphs*. Random Structures Algorithms (1995), 269-271.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  ∃ c > 0,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      (∀ (v : Fin n), (SimpleGraph.induce (G.neighborSet v) G).Colorable (r - 2)) →
        c * (Real.log ↑G.averageDegree / ↑G.averageDegree) * ↑n ≤ ↑G.indepNum

declarations.docstring:
Ajtai, Komlós, and Szemerédi [AKS80] proved the conjectured bound when $r = 3$: any
triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $t$ contains an independent set on
$$\gg \frac{\log t}{t}n$$
many vertices.
references: [erdosproblems.com/802](https://www.erdosproblems.com/802)
[AEKS81] Ajtai, M. and Erdős, P. and Komlós, J. and Szemerédi, E., *On Turán's theorem for sparse graphs*. Combinatorica (1981), 313-317.
[AKS80] Ajtai, Miklós and Komlós, János and Szemerédi, Endre, *A note on Ramsey numbers*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1980), 354-360.
[Al96b] Alon, Noga, *Independence numbers of locally sparse graphs and a Ramsey type problem*. Random Structures Algorithms (1996), 271-278.
[Sh95] Shearer, James B., *On the independence number of sparse graphs*. Random Structures Algorithms (1995), 269-271.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c > 0,
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
    G.CliqueFree 3 → c * (Real.log ↑G.averageDegree / ↑G.averageDegree) * ↑n ≤ ↑G.indepNum

declarations.docstring:
Shearer [Sh95] proved that any $K_r$-free graph on $n$ vertices with average degree $t$ contains
an independent set on
$$\gg_r \frac{\log t}{\log\log(t+1)t}n$$
many vertices.

We assume $t \geq 2$. For $t + 1$ slightly larger than $e$ the factor $\log\log(t+1)$ is close
to $0$, so the bound blows up and the statement is false without such a restriction.
references: [erdosproblems.com/802](https://www.erdosproblems.com/802)
[AEKS81] Ajtai, M. and Erdős, P. and Komlós, J. and Szemerédi, E., *On Turán's theorem for sparse graphs*. Combinatorica (1981), 313-317.
[AKS80] Ajtai, Miklós and Komlós, János and Szemerédi, Endre, *A note on Ramsey numbers*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1980), 354-360.
[Al96b] Alon, Noga, *Independence numbers of locally sparse graphs and a Ramsey type problem*. Random Structures Algorithms (1996), 271-278.
[Sh95] Shearer, James B., *On the independence number of sparse graphs*. Random Structures Algorithms (1995), 269-271.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (r : ℕ),
  ∃ c > 0,
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
      G.CliqueFree r →
        2 ≤ G.averageDegree →
          c * (Real.log ↑G.averageDegree / (Real.log (Real.log (↑G.averageDegree + 1)) * ↑G.averageDegree)) * ↑n ≤
            ↑G.indepNum

declarations.docstring:
If every set of `m` vertices contains a clique and an independent set of size `k`, so does
every set of `m' ≥ m` vertices. Thus "every induced subgraph on exactly `m` vertices" and "every
set of at least `m` vertices" (the formulation of [ABS21]) agree.
references: [erdosproblems.com/805](https://www.erdosproblems.com/805)
[Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991), 397-406.
[AlSu07] Alon, N. and Sudakov, B., *On graphs with subgraphs having large independence numbers*. J. Graph Theory 56 (2007), 149-157. [arXiv:0706.4099](https://arxiv.org/abs/0706.4099)

[ABS21] Alon, N., Bucić, M. and Sudakov, B., *Large cliques and independent sets all over the place*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 149 (2021), 3145-3157. [arXiv:2004.04718](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04718)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n m m' k : ℕ} {G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)}, Erdos805.IsLocallyRamsey G m k → m ≤ m' → Erdos805.IsLocallyRamsey G m' k

declarations.docstring:
For which functions $g(n)$ with $n>g(n)\geq (\log n)^2$ is there a graph on $n$ vertices in which
every induced subgraph on $g(n)$ vertices contains a clique of size $\geq \log n$ and an
independent set of size $\geq \log n$?

In particular, is there such a graph for $g(n)=(\log n)^3$?

This is the first part. A problem of Erdős and Hajnal [Er91]; see also
[erdosproblems.com/804](https://www.erdosproblems.com/804). The inequalities
on `g` are required for all large `n`, and a graph is required for all large `n`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/805](https://www.erdosproblems.com/805)
[Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991), 397-406.

declarations.docstring:
For which functions $g(n)$ with $n>g(n)\geq (\log n)^2$ is there a graph on $n$ vertices in which
every induced subgraph on $g(n)$ vertices contains a clique of size $\geq \log n$ and an
independent set of size $\geq \log n$?

In particular, is there such a graph for $g(n)=(\log n)^3$?

This is the second part. Erdős and Hajnal thought that there is no such graph for
$g(n)=(\log n)^3$ [AlSu07]; we state the positive proposition, with $g(n)=\lfloor(\log n)^3\rfloor$
and a graph required for all large $n$, as in the first part.
references: [erdosproblems.com/805](https://www.erdosproblems.com/805)
[Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991), 397-406.
[AlSu07] Alon, N. and Sudakov, B., *On graphs with subgraphs having large independence numbers*. J. Graph Theory 56 (2007), 149-157. [arXiv:0706.4099](https://arxiv.org/abs/0706.4099)

[ABS21] Alon, N., Bucić, M. and Sudakov, B., *Large cliques and independent sets all over the place*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 149 (2021), 3145-3157. [arXiv:2004.04718](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04718)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos805.HasRamseyGraphs fun n => ⌊Real.log ↑n ^ 3⌋₊

declarations.docstring:
Alon, Bucić, and Sudakov [ABS21] construct such a graph with
$$g(n)\leq 2^{2^{(\log\log n)^{1/2+o(1)}}}.$$

Here all logarithms are to base $2$, as in [ABS21], so the cliques and independent sets have at
least $\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ vertices; this implies the natural-logarithm version of the problem.
The $o(1)$ is expressed as: for every $0<\varepsilon<1/2$ and all large $n$ there is such a graph
with $g(n)=\lceil 2^{2^{(\log_2\log_2 n)^{1/2+\varepsilon}}}\rceil$. This form, with the rounding,
follows from [ABS21, Theorem 2].
references: [erdosproblems.com/805](https://www.erdosproblems.com/805)
[Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991), 397-406.
[AlSu07] Alon, N. and Sudakov, B., *On graphs with subgraphs having large independence numbers*. J. Graph Theory 56 (2007), 149-157. [arXiv:0706.4099](https://arxiv.org/abs/0706.4099)

[ABS21] Alon, N., Bucić, M. and Sudakov, B., *Large cliques and independent sets all over the place*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 149 (2021), 3145-3157. [arXiv:2004.04718](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04718)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (ε : ℝ),
  0 < ε →
    ε < 1 / 2 →
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
        ∃ G, Erdos805.IsLocallyRamsey G ⌈2 ^ 2 ^ Real.logb 2 (Real.logb 2 ↑n) ^ (1 / 2 + ε)⌉₊ ⌈Real.logb 2 ↑n⌉₊

declarations.docstring:
Alon and Sudakov [AlSu07] proved that there is no such graph with
$$g(n)=\frac{c}{\log\log n}(\log n)^3$$
for some constant $c>0$.

Here `log` is the natural logarithm, as in [AlSu07], and the statement is for all large `n`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/805](https://www.erdosproblems.com/805)
[Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991), 397-406.
[AlSu07] Alon, N. and Sudakov, B., *On graphs with subgraphs having large independence numbers*. J. Graph Theory 56 (2007), 149-157. [arXiv:0706.4099](https://arxiv.org/abs/0706.4099)

[ABS21] Alon, N., Bucić, M. and Sudakov, B., *Large cliques and independent sets all over the place*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 149 (2021), 3145-3157. [arXiv:2004.04718](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04718)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c,
  0 < c ∧
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ¬∃ G, Erdos805.IsLocallyRamsey G ⌊c * Real.log ↑n ^ 3 / Real.log (Real.log ↑n)⌋₊ ⌈Real.log ↑n⌉₊

declarations.docstring:
Let $G$ be a chordal graph on $n$ vertices - that is, $G$ has no induced cycles of
length greater than $3$. Can the edges of $G$ be partitioned into $n^2/6+O(n)$ many cliques?
references: [erdosproblems.com/81](https://www.erdosproblems.com/81)

[CEO94] Chen, Guan-Tao and Erdős, Paul and Ordman, Edward T., *Clique partitions of split graphs*. Combinatorics, graph theory, algorithms and applications (Beijing, 1993) (1994), 21–30.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C, ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G.IsChordal → ∃ P, G.IsCliqueEdgePartition P ∧ ↑P.card ≤ ↑n ^ 2 / 6 + C * ↑n

declarations.docstring:
Chen, Erdős, and Ordman [CEO94] have shown that any split graph can be partitioned
into $\frac{3}{16}n^2+O(n)$ many cliques.
references: [erdosproblems.com/81](https://www.erdosproblems.com/81)
[EOZ93] Erdős, Paul and Ordman, Edward T. and Zalcstein, Yechezkel, *Clique partitions of chordal graphs*. Combin. Probab. Comput. (1993), 409–415.
[CEO94] Chen, Guan-Tao and Erdős, Paul and Ordman, Edward T., *Clique partitions of split graphs*. Combinatorics, graph theory, algorithms and applications (Beijing, 1993) (1994), 21–30.

∃ C,
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
    G.IsSplitGraph → ∃ P, G.IsCliqueEdgePartition P ∧ ↑P.card ≤ 3 * ↑n ^ 2 / 16 + C * ↑n

declarations.docstring:
Let $h(n)$ be minimal such that every graph on $n$ vertices where every set of $7$ vertices
contains a triangle must contain a clique on at least $h(n)$ vertices. Estimate $h(n)$. In
particular, do there exist constants $c_1, c_2 > 0$ such that
$$n^{1/3+c_1} \ll h(n) \ll n^{1/2-c_2}?$$

The lower half has a positive answer (`Erdos813.erdos_813.variants.lower`); the upper half is
`Erdos813.erdos_813.variants.upper`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/813](https://www.erdosproblems.com/813)
[Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991), 397-406.
[BuSu23] Bucić, M. and Sudakov, B., *Large independent sets from local considerations*. Combinatorica 43 (2023), 505-546. [arXiv:2007.03667](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.03667)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c₁ > 0,
  ∃ c₂ > 0,
    ((fun n => ↑n ^ (1 / 3 + c₁)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑(Erdos813.h n)) ∧
      (fun n => ↑(Erdos813.h n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => ↑n ^ (1 / 2 - c₂)

declarations.docstring:
Bucić and Sudakov [BuSu23] proved that $h(n) \gg n^{5/12-o(1)}$. Their result is stated for
graphs in which every $7$ vertices contain an independent set of size $3$; it applies to $h$
by taking complements.
references: [erdosproblems.com/813](https://www.erdosproblems.com/813)
[Er91] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in combinatorial analysis and combinatorial number theory*. Graph theory, combinatorics, and applications, Vol. 1 (Kalamazoo, MI, 1988) (1991), 397-406.

declarations.type_pretty: ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑n ^ (5 / 12 - ε) ≤ ↑(Erdos813.h n)

$$n^{1/3} \ll h(n) \ll n^{1/2}.$$

Sudakov [BuSu23], since $5/12 > 1/3$.

Let $f(N)$ be maximal such that there exists $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$\lvert A\rvert=\lfloor N^{1/2}\rfloor$ such that $\lvert (A+A)\cap [1,N]\rvert=f(N)$.

$$\left(\frac{3}{8}-o(1)\right)N \leq f(N) \leq \left(\frac{1}{2}+o(1)\right)N.$$

This is the lower bound.

Erdős and Freud [ErFr91] proved
$$\left(\frac{3}{8}-o(1)\right)N \leq f(N) \leq \left(\frac{1}{2}+o(1)\right)N.$$

$H(n) = 3$ if and only if $(2^n-1, 3^n-1) = 1$. This holds for every $n$, including
$n = 0$, where both sides are false.

declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ), Erdos820.H n = 3 ↔ (2 ^ n - 1).Coprime (3 ^ n - 1)

declarations.docstring: The first values of $H(n)$, for $1 \leq n \leq 10$, are $3, 3, 3, 6, 3, 18, 3, 6, 3, 12$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/820](https://www.erdosproblems.com/820)
[Er74b] Erdős, P., *Remarks on some problems in number theory*. Math. Balkanica (1974), 197-202.
[OEIS A263647](https://oeis.org/A263647): the $n$ with $(2^n-1, 3^n-1) = 1$.

Erdos820.H 1 = 3 ∧
  Erdos820.H 2 = 3 ∧
    Erdos820.H 3 = 3 ∧
      Erdos820.H 4 = 6 ∧
        Erdos820.H 5 = 3 ∧
          Erdos820.H 6 = 18 ∧ Erdos820.H 7 = 3 ∧ Erdos820.H 8 = 6 ∧ Erdos820.H 9 = 3 ∧ Erdos820.H 10 = 12

declarations.docstring:
For $n \geq 1$ the minimum defining $H(n)$ is attained: there is $k$ with $2 \leq k < H(n)$
and $(k^n-1, H(n)^n-1) = 1$. For $n \geq 2$, the pair $k = 2$, $l = 2^n - 1$ shows that the set
is nonempty. For $n = 1$, take $k = 2$, $l = 3$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/820](https://www.erdosproblems.com/820)
[Er74b] Erdős, P., *Remarks on some problems in number theory*. Math. Balkanica (1974), 197-202.
[OEIS A263647](https://oeis.org/A263647): the $n$ with $(2^n-1, 3^n-1) = 1$.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 1 ≤ n → ∃ k, 2 ≤ k ∧ k < Erdos820.H n ∧ (k ^ n - 1).Coprime (Erdos820.H n ^ n - 1)

declarations.docstring:
Let $H(n)$ be the smallest integer $l$ such that there exists $k < l$ with $(k^n-1, l^n-1) = 1$.
Is it true that $H(n) = 3$ infinitely often? That is, is $(2^n-1, 3^n-1) = 1$ for infinitely
many $n$ (see `Erdos820.H_eq_three_iff`)?

The request to estimate $H(n)$ is open-ended and not formalised; the variants below state the
specific questions that are asked. See also Erdős Problem 770.
references: [erdosproblems.com/820](https://www.erdosproblems.com/820)
[Er74b] Erdős, P., *Remarks on some problems in number theory*. Math. Balkanica (1974), 197-202.
[OEIS A263647](https://oeis.org/A263647): the $n$ with $(2^n-1, 3^n-1) = 1$.
declarations.type_pretty: {n | Erdos820.H n = 3}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er74b] proved that there exists a constant $c > 0$ such that
$$
H(n) > \exp\left(n^{c/(\log\log n)^2}\right)
$$
for infinitely many $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/820](https://www.erdosproblems.com/820)
[Er74b] Erdős, P., *Remarks on some problems in number theory*. Math. Balkanica (1974), 197-202.
[OEIS A263647](https://oeis.org/A263647): the $n$ with $(2^n-1, 3^n-1) = 1$.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c > 0, ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Real.exp (↑n ^ (c / Real.log (Real.log ↑n) ^ 2)) < ↑(Erdos820.H n)

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that there exists some constant $c > 0$ such that, for all $\epsilon > 0$,
$$
H(n) > \exp\left(n^{(c-\epsilon)/\log\log n}\right)
$$
for infinitely many $n$ and
$$
H(n) < \exp\left(n^{(c+\epsilon)/\log\log n}\right)
$$
for all large enough $n$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/820](https://www.erdosproblems.com/820)
[Er74b] Erdős, P., *Remarks on some problems in number theory*. Math. Balkanica (1974), 197-202.
[OEIS A263647](https://oeis.org/A263647): the $n$ with $(2^n-1, 3^n-1) = 1$.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c > 0,
  ∀ ε > 0,
    (∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Real.exp (↑n ^ ((c - ε) / Real.log (Real.log ↑n))) < ↑(Erdos820.H n)) ∧
      ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos820.H n) < Real.exp (↑n ^ ((c + ε) / Real.log (Real.log ↑n)))

declarations.docstring:
Let $K(n)$ be the smallest $k$ such that $(k^n-1, 2^n-1) = 1$. Does a similar upper bound hold
for $K(n)$? That is, is there a constant $c > 0$ such that, for all $\epsilon > 0$,
$$
K(n) < \exp\left(n^{(c+\epsilon)/\log\log n}\right)
$$
for all large enough $n$?

We read "similar" as an upper bound of the same shape, with its own constant $c$, which need
not be the same as in `Erdos820.erdos_820.variants.log_log_exponent`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/820](https://www.erdosproblems.com/820)
[Er74b] Erdős, P., *Remarks on some problems in number theory*. Math. Balkanica (1974), 197-202.
[OEIS A263647](https://oeis.org/A263647): the $n$ with $(2^n-1, 3^n-1) = 1$.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c > 0, ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(Erdos820.K n) < Real.exp (↑n ^ ((c + ε) / Real.log (Real.log ↑n)))

declarations.docstring:
Let $h(x)$ count the number of integers $1\leq a<b<x$ such that $(a,b)=1$ and
$\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)$, where $\sigma$ is the sum of divisors function. Is it true that
$h(x)>x^{2-o(1)}$?

That is, is it true that for every $\epsilon > 0$ we have $h(x) > x^{2-\epsilon}$ for all large
$x$? According to erdosproblems.com, Erdős [Er74b] proved that $\limsup h(x)/x = \infty$ and
claimed a similar proof for this problem.
references: [erdosproblems.com/824](https://www.erdosproblems.com/824)
[Er59c] Erdős, P., *Remarks on number theory. II. Some problems on the $\sigma$ function*. Acta Arith. (1959), 171--177.
[Er74b] Erdős, P., *Remarks on some problems in number theory*. Math. Balkanica (1974), 197-202.
[PoPo16] Pollack, Paul and Pomerance, Carl, *Some problems of Erdős on the sum-of-divisors function*. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B (2016), 1-26.

[LiZh26] Li, Shisheng and Zhuang, Zhong, *Coprime pairs with equal sum of divisors, assuming smooth shifted primes*. Preprint (October 2026). [github.com/daizisheng/erdos-824](https://github.com/daizisheng/erdos-824/blob/b4b7099bb8ab9c1c7fc61dae18a73cdbe503fe5a/paper/erdos824.pdf)

[OpenAI26] OpenAI, *Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers*. OpenAI Math Release preprint (September 2026). [github.com/openai/math](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Weighted-Dilation-Graphs-Smooth-Shifted-Primes-and-Totient-Fibers-September-24-2026/paper.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ (x : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑x ^ (2 - ε) < ↑(Erdos824.h x)

declarations.docstring:

declarations.docstring:
Are there infinitely many $n$ such that, for all $k\geq 1$
$$
  \tau(n + k) \ll k?
$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/826](https://www.erdosproblems.com/826)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C > 0, {n | ∀ k ≥ 1, ↑((ArithmeticFunction.sigma 0) (n + k)) ≤ C * ↑k}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Let $n_k$ be minimal such that if $n_k$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ are in general position then
there exists a subset of $k$ points such that all $\binom{k}{3}$ triples determine circles of
different radii.

Determine $n_k$.

General position means that no three points are collinear and no four are concyclic, as in
[Er75h] (quoted in [MaRo15]).
references: [erdosproblems.com/827](https://www.erdosproblems.com/827)
[Er75h] Erdős, P., *Some problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 2 (1975), 2-3.
[Er78c] Erdős, P., *Some more problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 5 (1978), 52-54.
[MaRo15] Martínez, L. and Roldán-Pensado, E., *Points defining triangles with distinct circumradii*. Acta Math. Hungar. 145 (2015), 136-141. [arXiv:1402.6276](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.6276)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos827.n = Erdos827.erdos_827.answer

declarations.docstring:
In [Er78c] Erdős gave an argument for $n_k \leq k+2\binom{k-1}{2}\binom{k-1}{3}$, but this
argument is incorrect, as explained by Martínez and Roldán-Pensado [MaRo15], who give a corrected
argument that proves $n_k\ll k^9$.

[MaRo15, Theorem 1.1] assumes only that no four points lie on a line or a circle. That class
contains the sets in general position, so the bound holds for $n_k$ as defined here.
references: [erdosproblems.com/827](https://www.erdosproblems.com/827)
[Er75h] Erdős, P., *Some problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 2 (1975), 2-3.
[Er78c] Erdős, P., *Some more problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 5 (1978), 52-54.
[MaRo15] Martínez, L. and Roldán-Pensado, E., *Points defining triangles with distinct circumradii*. Acta Math. Hungar. 145 (2015), 136-141. [arXiv:1402.6276](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.6276)
declarations.type_pretty: (fun k => ↑(Erdos827.n k)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun k => ↑k ^ 9

declarations.docstring: Martínez and Roldán-Pensado [MaRo15, Theorem 1.2] show that $n_5 \leq 37$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/827](https://www.erdosproblems.com/827)
[Er75h] Erdős, P., *Some problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 2 (1975), 2-3.
[Er78c] Erdős, P., *Some more problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 5 (1978), 52-54.
[MaRo15] Martínez, L. and Roldán-Pensado, E., *Points defining triangles with distinct circumradii*. Acta Math. Hungar. 145 (2015), 136-141. [arXiv:1402.6276](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.6276)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos827.n 5 ≤ 37

declarations.docstring: Martínez and Roldán-Pensado [MaRo15, Theorem 1.2] show that $n_4 \leq 9$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/827](https://www.erdosproblems.com/827)
[Er75h] Erdős, P., *Some problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 2 (1975), 2-3.
[Er78c] Erdős, P., *Some more problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 5 (1978), 52-54.
[MaRo15] Martínez, L. and Roldán-Pensado, E., *Points defining triangles with distinct circumradii*. Acta Math. Hungar. 145 (2015), 136-141. [arXiv:1402.6276](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.6276)
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos827.n 4 ≤ 9

declarations.docstring:
If every set of `m` points in general position contains `k` points with pairwise different
circumradii, then $n_k \leq m$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/827](https://www.erdosproblems.com/827)
[Er75h] Erdős, P., *Some problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 2 (1975), 2-3.
[Er78c] Erdős, P., *Some more problems on elementary geometry*. Austral. Math. Soc. Gaz. 5 (1978), 52-54.
[MaRo15] Martínez, L. and Roldán-Pensado, E., *Points defining triangles with distinct circumradii*. Acta Math. Hungar. 145 (2015), 136-141. [arXiv:1402.6276](https://arxiv.org/abs/1402.6276)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ {k m : ℕ},
  (∀ (X : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
      X.card = m → EuclideanGeometry.InGeneralPosition ↑X → ∃ Y ⊆ X, Y.card = k ∧ Erdos827.HasDistinctCircumradii Y) →
    Erdos827.n k ≤ m

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for any $a \in \mathbb{Z}$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$$\phi(n) | n + a$$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/828](https://www.erdosproblems.com/828)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (a : ℤ), {n | ↑n.totient ∣ ↑n + a}.Infinite

declarations.docstring: When $n > 1$, Lehmer conjectured that $\phi(n) | n - 1$ if and only if $n$ is prime.
references: [erdosproblems.com/828](https://www.erdosproblems.com/828)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ n > 1, n.totient ∣ n - 1 ↔ Prime n

declarations.docstring:
It is an easy exercise to show that $\phi(n) | n$ if and only if $n = 0, 1$ or $n = 2^a 3^b$ for
some $a > 0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/828](https://www.erdosproblems.com/828)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {n : ℕ}, n.totient ∣ n ↔ n ≤ 1 ∨ ∃ a > 0, ∃ b, n = 2 ^ a * 3 ^ b

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős Problem 829 (open).**  Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be the set of perfect cubes.  Is
it true that $(1_A \ast 1_A)(n) \ll (\log n)^{O(1)}$?  That is, does there exist a natural
number $C$ such that the number of representations of $n$ as a sum of two cubes is
$O((\log n)^C)$ as $n \to \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ C, (fun n => ↑(AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes n)) =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => Real.log ↑n ^ C

declarations.docstring:
Membership in `cubes` can be witnessed by a bounded cube root, which makes it
decidable for concrete values.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (m : ℕ), m ∈ Erdos829.cubes ↔ ∃ k < m + 1, k ^ 3 = m

declarations.docstring:
The Hardy-Ramanujan taxicab number satisfies $1729 = 1^3 + 12^3 = 9^3 + 10^3$, giving
the four ordered representations $(1, 1728), (1728, 1), (729, 1000), (1000, 729)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes 1729 = 4

declarations.docstring: The integer $3$ is not the sum of two cubes.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes 3 = 0

declarations.docstring: The only ordered pair of cubes summing to $2$ is $(1, 1)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes 2 = 1

declarations.docstring: There is exactly one ordered pair of cubes summing to $0$, namely $(0, 0)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes 0 = 1

declarations.docstring:
Mahler proved $(1_A \ast 1_A)(n) \gg (\log n)^{1/4}$ for infinitely many $n$, where $A$ is
the set of perfect cubes.

[Ma35b] Mahler, K., _On the lattice points on curves of genus 1_. Proc. London Math. Soc.
  (2) (1935), 431-466.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C > 0, ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, C * Real.log ↑n ^ (1 / 4) ≤ ↑(AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes n)

declarations.docstring:
Mordell proved $\limsup_{n \to \infty} (1_A \ast 1_A)(n) = \infty$, where $A$ is the set of
perfect cubes.  Equivalently, the number of representations of $n$ as a sum of two cubes is
unbounded.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑(AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes n)) Filter.atTop = ⊤

declarations.docstring:
Stewart improved Mahler's lower bound to $(1_A \ast 1_A)(n) \gg (\log n)^{11/13}$ for
infinitely many $n$, where $A$ is the set of perfect cubes.

[St08] Stewart, C. L., _Cubic Thue equations with many solutions_. Int. Math. Res. Not.
  IMRN (2008), Art. ID rnn040, 11.
references: [erdosproblems.com/829](https://www.erdosproblems.com/829)
[Er83] Erdős, P. and Dudley, U., _Some remarks and problems in number theory related to the work of Euler_. Math. Mag. (1983), 292-298.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ C > 0, ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, C * Real.log ↑n ^ (11 / 13) ≤ ↑(AdditiveCombinatorics.sumRep Erdos829.cubes n)

declarations.docstring:
**Erdos Problem 830, Part 1**
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$. Are there
infinitely many amicable pairs?
references: [erdosproblems.com/830](https://www.erdosproblems.com/830)
[Er55b] Erdős, P., *On amicable numbers*. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1955), 108-111.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
[Po15] Pomerance, Carl, *On amicable numbers*. (2015), 321-327.
[Po81] Pomerance, Carl, *On the distribution of amicable numbers. II*. J. Reine Angew. Math. (1981), 183-188.
declarations.type_pretty: {(a, b) | IsAmicable a b}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
**Erdos Problem 830, Part 2**
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then is it true that
$$A(x) > x^{1-o(1)}?$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/830](https://www.erdosproblems.com/830)
[Er55b] Erdős, P., *On amicable numbers*. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1955), 108-111.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
[Po15] Pomerance, Carl, *On amicable numbers*. (2015), 321-327.
[Po81] Pomerance, Carl, *On the distribution of amicable numbers. II*. J. Reine Angew. Math. (1981), 183-188.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ o, o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, x ^ (1 - o x) < Erdos830.A x

declarations.docstring:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that $A(x) = o(x)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/830](https://www.erdosproblems.com/830)
[Er55b] Erdős, P., *On amicable numbers*. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1955), 108-111.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
[Po15] Pomerance, Carl, *On amicable numbers*. (2015), 321-327.
[Po81] Pomerance, Carl, *On the distribution of amicable numbers. II*. J. Reine Angew. Math. (1981), 183-188.
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos830.A =o[Filter.atTop] id

declarations.docstring:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that
$A(x) \leq x \exp(-(\log x)^{1/3})$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/830](https://www.erdosproblems.com/830)
[Er55b] Erdős, P., *On amicable numbers*. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1955), 108-111.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
[Po15] Pomerance, Carl, *On amicable numbers*. (2015), 321-327.
[Po81] Pomerance, Carl, *On the distribution of amicable numbers. II*. J. Reine Angew. Math. (1981), 183-188.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, Erdos830.A x ≤ x * Real.exp (-Real.nthRoot 3 (Real.log x))

declarations.docstring:
We say that $a,b\in \mathbb{N}$ are an amicable pair if $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)=a+b$.
If $A(x)$ counts the number of amicable $1\leq a\leq b\leq x$ then one can show that
$A(x) \leq x \exp(-(\tfrac{1}{2}+o(1))(\log x\log\log\log x)^{1/2})$.
(erdosproblems.com has $\log\log x$; [Po15, Theorem 1.1] has $\log\log\log x$.)

[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., *Unsolved problems in number theory*. (2004), xviii+437.
[Po15] Pomerance, Carl, *On amicable numbers*. (2015), 321-327.
[Po81] Pomerance, Carl, *On the distribution of amicable numbers. II*. J. Reine Angew. Math. (1981), 183-188.

∃ o,
  o =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧
    ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop,

declarations.docstring:
It is known that for $3 \leq k \leq 8$, the chromatic number of $J(2k, k)$ is greater than
$k+1$, see [Johnson graphs](https://aeb.win.tue.nl/graphs/Johnson.html).
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {k : ℕ}, 3 ≤ k → k ≤ 8 → ↑k + 1 < (SimpleGraph.johnson (2 * k) k).chromaticNumber

declarations.docstring:
It is also known that for $3 \leq k \leq 203$ odd, the chromatic number of $J(2k, k)$ is
greater than $k+1$, see [Johnson graphs](https://aeb.win.tue.nl/graphs/Johnson.html).
references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)
[MT25](https://github.com/QuanyuTang/erdos-problem-835/blob/main/On_Problem_835.pdf)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ {k : ℕ}, 3 ≤ k → k ≤ 300 → Odd k → ↑k + 1 < (SimpleGraph.johnson (2 * k) k).chromaticNumber

references: [erdosproblems.com/835](https://www.erdosproblems.com/835)

declarations.docstring:
Does there exist a $k>2$ such that the $k$-sized subsets of {1,...,2k} can be coloured with
$k+1$ colours such that for every $A\subset \{1,\ldots,2k\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert=k+1$ all $k+1$
colours appear among the $k$-sized subsets of $A$?
