declarations.docstring:
Let $k\geq 2$ and $A_k\subseteq [0,1]$ be the set of $\alpha$ such that there exists some
$\beta(\alpha)>\alpha$ with the property that, if $G_1,G_2,\ldots$ is a sequence of $k$-uniform
hypergraphs with
$$\liminf \frac{e(G_n)}{\binom{\lvert G_n\rvert}{k}} >\alpha$$
then there exist subgraphs $H_n\subseteq G_n$ such that $\lvert H_n\rvert \to \infty$ and
$$\liminf \frac{e(H_n)}{\binom{\lvert H_n\rvert}{k}} >\beta,$$
and further that this property does not necessarily hold if $>\alpha$ is replaced by $\geq \alpha$.
What is $A_3$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/837](https://www.erdosproblems.com/837)
declarations.type_pretty:
{α | α ∈ Set.Icc 0 1 ∧ ∃ β, α < β ∧ Hypergraph.HasDensityJump 3 α β true ∧ ¬Hypergraph.HasDensityJump 3 α β false} =
  Erdos837.erdos_837.answer

declarations.docstring:
Erdős Problem 839 (Part 1) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\limsup a_n / n = \infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/839](https://www.erdosproblems.com/839)
[Er78f] Erdős, P., *Problems in number theory and combinatorics*, Proc. Sixth Manitoba Conf. on Numerical Math. (1978), 35-58.
[Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1992).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
  (∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ a n) →
    StrictMono a → Erdos839.SumOfConsecutiveFree a → Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑(a n) / ↑n) Filter.atTop = ⊤

declarations.docstring:
Erdős Problem 839 (Part 2, stronger) [Er78f][Er92c]:

Let $1 \leq a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers
such that no $a_i$ is the sum of consecutive $a_j$ for $j < i$.
Is it true that $\lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{1}{\log x} \sum_{a_n < x} \frac{1}{a_n} = 0$?

This is equivalent to asking whether the range $\{a_1,a_2,\ldots\}$ has logarithmic density zero
(see `Set.HasLogDensity`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/839](https://www.erdosproblems.com/839)
[Er78f] Erdős, P., *Problems in number theory and combinatorics*, Proc. Sixth Manitoba Conf. on Numerical Math. (1978), 35-58.
[Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my favourite unsolved problems*, J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1992).
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ), (∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ a n) → StrictMono a → Erdos839.SumOfConsecutiveFree a → (Set.range a).HasLogDensity 0

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(N)$ be the size of the largest quasi-Sidon subset $A\subset\{1,\ldots,N\}$, where we say
that $A$ is quasi-Sidon if
$$\lvert A+A\rvert=(1+o(1))\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}.$$
How does $f(N)$ grow?

Following [Er81h, p. 175], we ask for the largest $c$ such that there are quasi-Sidon sets
$A \subseteq \{1, \ldots, N\}$ with $\lvert A\rvert = (1+o(1))cN^{1/2}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/840](https://www.erdosproblems.com/840)

[Er81h] Erdős, P., *Some problems and results on additive and multiplicative number theory*. Analytic number theory (Philadelphia, Pa., 1980), Lecture Notes in Math. 899 (1981), 171-182. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-33.pdf)
[ErFr91] Erdős, P. and Freud, R., *On sums of a Sidon-sequence*. J. Number Theory 38 (1991), 196-205.
[Pi06] Pikhurko, O., *Dense edge-magic graphs and thin additive bases*. Discrete Math. 306 (2006), 2097-2107.
declarations.type_pretty: IsLUB {c | Erdos840.IsQuasiSidonConstant c} Erdos840.erdos_840.answer

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Freud [ErFr91] proved
$$\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+o(1)\right)N^{1/2} \leq f(N) \leq \left(2+o(1)\right)N^{1/2}.$$
(Although both bounds were already given by Erdős in [Er81h].)

This is the lower bound. The lower bound is taking a genuine Sidon set $B\subset [1,N/3]$ of size
$\sim N^{1/2}/\sqrt{3}$ and taking the union with $\{N-b : b\in B\}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/840](https://www.erdosproblems.com/840)

[Er81h] Erdős, P., *Some problems and results on additive and multiplicative number theory*. Analytic number theory (Philadelphia, Pa., 1980), Lecture Notes in Math. 899 (1981), 171-182. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1981-33.pdf)
[ErFr91] Erdős, P. and Freud, R., *On sums of a Sidon-sequence*. J. Number Theory 38 (1991), 196-205.
[Pi06] Pikhurko, O., *Dense edge-magic graphs and thin additive bases*. Discrete Math. 306 (2006), 2097-2107.
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos840.IsQuasiSidonConstant (2 / √3)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Freud [ErFr91] proved
$$\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}+o(1)\right)N^{1/2} \leq f(N) \leq \left(2+o(1)\right)N^{1/2}.$$
(Although both bounds were already given by Erdős in [Er81h].)

This is the upper bound.

(the constant here is $=1.863\cdots$).

declarations.docstring:
Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $h(x)$ be maximal such that for
some $n < x$ the numbers $d_n, d_{n+1}, \ldots, d_{n+h(x)-1}$ are all distinct [Er85c]. Estimate
$h(x)$. In particular, is it true that
$$h(x) > (\log x)^c$$
for some constant $c > 0$?

The statement avoids defining $h$. Since $h(x)$ is the longest such run, $h(x) > y$ holds exactly
when some $n < x$ starts a run of $H > y$ distinct gaps. We state the question this way, with $x$
real. We read it as asking for one $c > 0$ such that the inequality holds for all large $x$.

The primes are indexed from $p_0 = 2$, as in `primeGap`. Shifting the index by one does not change
the question.
references: [erdosproblems.com/852](https://www.erdosproblems.com/852)
[Er85c] Erdős, P., *On some of my problems in number theory I would most like to see solved*. Number theory (Ootacamund, 1984) (1985), 74-84.
[A001223](https://oeis.org/A001223)
[A053597](https://oeis.org/A053597)
[A078515](https://oeis.org/A078515)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ n, ↑n < x ∧ ∃ H, Real.log x ^ c < ↑H ∧ Erdos852.DistinctGapRun n H

declarations.docstring:
Let $d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n$, where $p_n$ is the $n$th prime. Let $h(x)$ be maximal such that for
some $n < x$ the numbers $d_n, d_{n+1}, \ldots, d_{n+h(x)-1}$ are all distinct [Er85c]. Estimate
$h(x)$. In particular, is it true that
$$h(x) = o(\log x)?$$

The statement avoids defining $h$. It says that for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all large real $x$,
every run of $H$ distinct gaps $d_n, \ldots, d_{n+H-1}$ with $n < x$ satisfies
$H \leq \varepsilon \log x$. This is $h(x) \leq \varepsilon \log x$, because $h(x)$ is the longest
such run.

The indexing is as in `Erdos852.erdos_852.parts.i`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/852](https://www.erdosproblems.com/852)
[Er85c] Erdős, P., *On some of my problems in number theory I would most like to see solved*. Number theory (Ootacamund, 1984) (1985), 74-84.
[A001223](https://oeis.org/A001223)
[A053597](https://oeis.org/A053597)
[A078515](https://oeis.org/A078515)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (ε : ℝ),
  0 < ε → ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ (n : ℕ), ↑n < x → ∀ (H : ℕ), Erdos852.DistinctGapRun n H → ↑H ≤ ε * Real.log x

declarations.docstring:
Brun's sieve implies $h(x) \to \infty$ as $x \to \infty$ (remark on
[erdosproblems.com/852](https://www.erdosproblems.com/852)).

That is, for every $H$ and all large $x$ there is some $n < x$ such that $d_n, \ldots, d_{n+H-1}$
are all distinct. Since more values of $n$ are allowed as $x$ grows, this holds exactly when, for
every $H$, some $n$ has $d_n, \ldots, d_{n+H-1}$ all distinct.

This also follows from `Erdos6.erdos_6.variants.increasing`, because strictly increasing prime
gaps are distinct.
references: [erdosproblems.com/852](https://www.erdosproblems.com/852)
[Er85c] Erdős, P., *On some of my problems in number theory I would most like to see solved*. Number theory (Ootacamund, 1984) (1985), 74-84.
[A001223](https://oeis.org/A001223)
[A053597](https://oeis.org/A053597)
[A078515](https://oeis.org/A078515)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (H : ℕ), ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ n, ↑n < x ∧ Erdos852.DistinctGapRun n H

declarations.docstring:
Let $n_k$ denote the $k$th primorial, i.e. the product of the first $k$ primes.

If $1=a_1<a_2<\cdots <a_{\phi(n_k)}=n_k-1$ is the sequence of integers coprime to $n_k$, then
estimate the smallest even integer not of the form $a_{i+1}-a_i$. Are there
$$\gg \max_i (a_{i+1}-a_i)$$
many even integers of the form $a_{j+1}-a_j$?

This is the first part. A problem of Erdős [Er85c, p. 80], who writes "integer" instead of "even
integer"; all differences $a_{i+1}-a_i$ are even, so only even integers are meaningful. Here
"estimate" is read as $\Theta$. Erdős first thought that for large $k$ every even $t \leq
\max_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)$ is a gap, but [Ob1] reports computations of Lacampagne and Selfridge showing
this fails for $n_6 = 30030$ (OEIS A389839 and A048670 give $20$ and $22$).
references: [erdosproblems.com/854](https://www.erdosproblems.com/854)

[Er85c] Erdős, P., *On some of my problems in number theory I would most like to see solved*. Number theory (Ootacamund, 1984), Lecture Notes in Math. 1122 (1985), 74-84. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-17.pdf)
[Ob1] Erdős, P., *Oberwolfach Mathematical Problems*, Volume 1. Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach.

[OEIS A389839](https://oeis.org/A389839): smallest even number which cannot be written as the difference of two consecutive numbers which are relatively prime to the $n$th primorial. It agrees with `minEvenNonGap k` for $k\geq 3$.
[OEIS A048670](https://oeis.org/A048670): Jacobsthal's function of the product of the first $n$ primes, which is the largest gap.
declarations.type_pretty: (fun k => ↑(Erdos854.minEvenNonGap k)) =Θ[Filter.atTop] Erdos854.erdos_854.parts.i.answer

declarations.docstring:
Let $n_k$ denote the $k$th primorial, i.e. the product of the first $k$ primes.

If $1=a_1<a_2<\cdots <a_{\phi(n_k)}=n_k-1$ is the sequence of integers coprime to $n_k$, then
estimate the smallest even integer not of the form $a_{i+1}-a_i$. Are there
$$\gg \max_i (a_{i+1}-a_i)$$
many even integers of the form $a_{j+1}-a_j$?

This is the second part. We read it as: there is an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that, for all
large $k$, the number of distinct gap values is at least $c$ times the largest gap.
references: [erdosproblems.com/854](https://www.erdosproblems.com/854)

[Er85c] Erdős, P., *On some of my problems in number theory I would most like to see solved*. Number theory (Ootacamund, 1984), Lecture Notes in Math. 1122 (1985), 74-84. [PDF](https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-17.pdf)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős Problem 855 (Segal's conjecture): $\pi(x + y) \le \pi(x) + \pi(y)$
for all sufficiently large $x, y$, i.e. for all $x, y \ge N$ for some $N$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)

declarations.docstring:
Let $k\geq 3$ and $f_k(N)$ be the maximum value of $\sum_{n\in A}\frac{1}{n}$, where $A$ ranges
over all subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ which contain no subset of size $k$ with the same pairwise
least common multiple.

Estimate $f_k(N)$.

This is the question of Erdős [Er70, p. 127]. We read "estimate" as
$f_k(N) = \Theta(\text{answer})$ as $N \to \infty$, for each fixed $k$.

declarations.docstring:

$$f_k(N) \ll \frac{\log N}{\log\log N}.$$

The implied constant depends on $k$.

declarations.docstring:
Tang and Zhang [TaZh25b, Theorem 1.2] proved that, for fixed $k\geq 3$ and as $N\to\infty$,
$$f_k(N) \geq (\log N)^{c_k - o(1)}, \qquad c_k = \frac{k-2}{e\,((k-2)!)^{1/(k-2)}}.$$

The $o(1)$ is stated with an arbitrary $\varepsilon > 0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/856](https://www.erdosproblems.com/856)

    ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, Real.log ↑N ^ (Erdos856.tangZhangExponent k - ε) ≤ Erdos856.f k N

declarations.docstring:

$$(\log N)^{\log(1.551)-o(1)}\leq f_3(N)\ll(\log N)^{\frac{3}{2^{2/3}}-1+o(1)}.$$

This is the lower bound, with the $o(1)$ stated with an arbitrary $\varepsilon > 0$. Since
$\log(1.551) = 0.4389\ldots$, it implies the site's $(\log N)^{0.438}\leq f_3(N)$ for large $N$.

This is the upper bound, with the $o(1)$ and the implied constant absorbed into an arbitrary

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ be a set such that there exists at most one $n$ with more than one
solution to $n=a+b$ (with $a\leq b\in A$). Estimate the maximal possible size of $|A|$. In
particular, is it true that
$$|A| \leq (1+o(1))\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} N^{1/2}?$$

A problem of Erdős and Freud [ErFr91] [Er92c]. For the analogous question with $n=a-b$ they prove
that $\lvert A\rvert\sim N^{1/2}$. This is a weaker form of Erdős Problem 840.

The condition on $A$ is `HasAtMostOneRepeatedSum`. We state the question as follows: for every
$\varepsilon > 0$ and all large $N$, every such set $A$ satisfies
$|A| \leq (1+\varepsilon)\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} N^{1/2}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/864](https://www.erdosproblems.com/864)
[A389182](https://oeis.org/A389182)
[ErFr91] Erdős, P. and Freud, R., *On sums of a Sidon-sequence*. J. Number Theory 38 (1991), 196--205.
[Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*. Hardy-Ramanujan J. 15 (1992), 34-50.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (ε : ℝ),
  0 < ε →
    ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, Erdos864.HasAtMostOneRepeatedSum A → ↑A.card ≤ (1 + ε) * (2 / √3) * √↑N

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Freud [ErFr91] [Er92c] prove that
$$\lvert A\rvert \geq (1+o(1))\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}N^{1/2}.$$
This is shown by taking a genuine Sidon set $B\subset [1,N/3]$ of size $\sim N^{1/2}/\sqrt{3}$
and taking the union with $\{N-b : b\in B\}$.

That is, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ and all large $N$ there is a set $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$
with the property of `Erdos864.erdos_864` and $|A| \geq (1-\varepsilon)\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}N^{1/2}$.
So the constant $2/\sqrt{3}$ there cannot be replaced by a smaller one.
references: [erdosproblems.com/864](https://www.erdosproblems.com/864)
[A389182](https://oeis.org/A389182)
[ErFr91] Erdős, P. and Freud, R., *On sums of a Sidon-sequence*. J. Number Theory 38 (1991), 196--205.
[Er92c] Erdős, P., *Some of my forgotten problems in number theory*. Hardy-Ramanujan J. 15 (1992), 34-50.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (ε : ℝ),
  0 < ε →
    ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∃ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N, Erdos864.HasAtMostOneRepeatedSum A ∧ (1 - ε) * (2 / √3) * √↑N ≤ ↑A.card

declarations.docstring:
There exists a constant $C>0$ such that, for all large $N$, if $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\}$ has
size at least $\frac{5}{8}N+C$ then there are distinct $a,b,c\in A$ such that $a+b,a+c,b+c\in A$.

A problem of Erdős and Sós (also earlier considered by Choi, Erdős, and Szemerédi [CES75], but Erdős
had forgotten this).

This problem was solved in the affirmative by Cipollini and GPT Pro [Ci26].

This is true. The linked proof gives it in the contrapositive and with the constant cleared:
every triple-free $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ satisfies $8\lvert A\rvert\leq 5N+C$ for a fixed
$C$, for every $N$ rather than only for large $N$. It also shows the threshold is sharp, by
exhibiting triple-free sets of size $(5N+16)/8$ for every $N$ divisible by $8$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/865](https://www.erdosproblems.com/865)
[CES75] Choi, S. L. G. and Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., Some additive and multiplicative problems in number theory. Acta Arith. (1975), 37--50.
[Ci26] R. Cipollini, [A sharp $5/8$ bound for an Erdős–Sós pairwise-sums problem](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.29361) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C > 0,
  ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N,
      ↑A.card ≥ 5 / 8 * ↑N + C → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, ∃ c ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ a ≠ c ∧ b ≠ c ∧ a + b ∈ A ∧ a + c ∈ A ∧ b + c ∈ A

It is a classical folklore fact that if $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,2N\}$ has size $\geq N+2$ then
there are distinct $a,b\in A$ such that $a+b\in A$, which establishes the $k=2$ case.
references: [erdosproblems.com/865](https://www.erdosproblems.com/865)
[CES75] Choi, S. L. G. and Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., Some additive and multiplicative problems in number theory. Acta Arith. (1975), 37--50.
[Ci26] R. Cipollini, [A sharp $5/8$ bound for an Erdős–Sós pairwise-sums problem](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.29361) (2026).
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (N : ℕ), ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 (2 * N), A.card ≥ N + 2 → ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ A, a ≠ b ∧ a + b ∈ A

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Sós conjectured that
$f_k(N)\sim \frac{1}{2}\left(1+\sum_{1\leq r\leq k-2}\frac{1}{4^r}\right) N$,
where $f_k(N)$ is the minimal size of a subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ guaranteeing $k$ elements
have all pairwise sums in the set.
references: [erdosproblems.com/865](https://www.erdosproblems.com/865)
[CES75] Choi, S. L. G. and Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., Some additive and multiplicative problems in number theory. Acta Arith. (1975), 37--50.
[Ci26] R. Cipollini, [A sharp $5/8$ bound for an Erdős–Sós pairwise-sums problem](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.29361) (2026).

∀ (k : ℕ),
  2 ≤ k →
    Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun N => ↑(Erdos865.f N k)) fun N =>
      1 / 2 * (1 + ∑ r ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (k - 2), (1 / 4) ^ r) * ↑N

Choi, Erdős, and Szemerédi [CES75] have proved that, for all $k\geq 3$, there exists $\epsilon_k>0$
such that (for large enough $N$) $f_k(N)\leq \left(\frac{2}{3}-\epsilon_k\right)N$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/865](https://www.erdosproblems.com/865)
[CES75] Choi, S. L. G. and Erdős, P. and Szemerédi, E., Some additive and multiplicative problems in number theory. Acta Arith. (1975), 37--50.
[Ci26] R. Cipollini, [A sharp $5/8$ bound for an Erdős–Sós pairwise-sums problem](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.29361) (2026).

declarations.docstring:
Let $0 < \epsilon < 1$. Is it true that, if $k$ is sufficiently large, then
$$R(G) > (1-\epsilon)^k R(k)$$
for every graph $G$ with chromatic number $\chi(G)=k$?

The restriction $\epsilon < 1$ excludes negative bases in $(1-\epsilon)^k$.

This problem is #12 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
references: [erdosproblems.com/87](https://www.erdosproblems.com/87)
[Er95] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry. Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ ε > 0,
  ε < 1 →
    ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ (V : Type) [inst : Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V),

declarations.docstring:
Erdős Problem 872, part (ii) (strong form): for every $\epsilon > 0$, the game length is at
least $(1-\epsilon) \cdot n / 2$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

The forum thread (April-May 2026) records Shortener strategies giving
$L(n) \leq (23/48 + o(1)) \cdot n$ (described in the thread as accepted as correct, with a Lean
formalization in progress) and a claimed $L(n) \leq 0.19 \cdot n$, either of which would answer this
question negatively under the Prolonger-first convention.

The $23/48$ upper bound for `C`-respecting plays (following old-bielefelder's strategy in the
forum thread) was formalized in Lean 4 by Pommeret using Aristotle and Claude Opus 4.7, and
completed to a proof for the full minimax game value `L n` by Ilia Pauzner using Gemini 4 Argon.

declarations.docstring:
Forum-related variant: how small can a maximal primitive subset of $\{2, \dots, n\}$ be?
The set of primes in $\{2, \dots, n\}$ is a maximal primitive subset of size $\pi(n)$, and the forum
thread asks whether this is the smallest possible for all $n \geq 2$. Equivalently: must every
completed play of the saturation game, by both players and regardless of strategy, claim at least
$\pi(n)$ elements? (Terminal positions of the game are exactly the maximal primitive subsets.)

The answer is yes. For each prime $q \le n$, let $q^k$ be the largest power of $q$ that is at most
$n$. Maximality gives an element of $A$ comparable with $q^k$ under divisibility, and no element is
comparable with two such prime powers, so $|A| \ge \pi(n)$. This argument was posted on the forum
by old-bielefelder (May 2026); the statement also appears as Theorem 2.3(i) of
[El23] S. Elsakhawy, *Independence and domination in divisor graph and mod-difference graphs*,
J. Egyptian Math. Soc. 31 (2023).
references: [erdosproblems.com/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/872)
[erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/872)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), Maximal (Erdos872.IsPrimitive n) A → (Finset.filter Nat.Prime (Finset.Icc 2 n)).card ≤ A.card

integers are joined by an edge if they are coprime.

Is it true that if
$$|A| > \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + \lfloor n/3 \rfloor - \lfloor n/6 \rfloor$$
then $G(A)$ contains all odd cycles of length $\leq n/3 + 1$?

A problem of Erdős and Sárközy [ErSa97].
references: [erdosproblems.com/883](https://www.erdosproblems.com/883)
[ErSa97] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, G. N., On cycles in the coprime graph of integers. Electron. J. Combin. (1997), Research Paper 8.
[Sa99] Sárközy, G. N., Complete tripartite subgraphs in the coprime graph of integers. Discrete Math. (1999), 227-238.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ),
  ∀ A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 n,
    n / 2 + n / 3 - n / 6 < A.card →
      ∀ (l : ℕ), Odd l → 3 ≤ l → l ≤ n / 3 + 1 → l ∈ (SimpleGraph.induce (↑A) Erdos883.coprimeGraph).oddCycleLengths

The second question was solved by Sárközy [Sa99], who proved this with
$\ell \gg \log n/\log\log n$.

[ErSa97] Erdős, P. and Sárközy, G. N., On cycles in the coprime graph of integers. Electron. J. Combin. (1997), Research Paper 8.

          (SimpleGraph.completeMultipartiteGraph fun i => Fin (![1, l, l] i)).IsContained
            (SimpleGraph.induce (↑A) Erdos883.coprimeGraph)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős and Rosenfeld ask whether $4$ is the best possible $K$ for the infinitude of $n$
with (at least) $K$ divisors in $(n^{\frac{1}{2}}, n^{\frac{1}{2}} + C n^{\frac{1}{4}})$, for some
constant $C > 0$. The constant cannot be taken to be $1$. Distinct divisors $d > \sqrt{n}$ give
distinct integers $d + n/d$, and a divisor in the interval has
$2\sqrt{n} < d + n/d < 2\sqrt{n} + C^2$, so for $C = 1$ there is at most one such divisor.

The answer is no. In a [forum post](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/887#post-7374)
(July 2026), m-czech showed that for $C = 31$ infinitely many $n$ have $5$ divisors in the
interval. The construction is $n = (x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 4)(x^2 - 16)(x^2 - 49)$ with
$z^2 = 56 x^2 + 65$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/887](https://www.erdosproblems.com/887)
[ErRo97] Erdős, Paul and Rosenfeld, Moshe, The factor-difference set of integers. Acta Arith. (1997), 353--359.
declarations.type_pretty: ¬IsGreatest {K | ∃ C > 0, Infinite ↑{n | K ≤ {d ∈ Finset.Ioo ⌊√↑n⌋₊ ⌈√↑n + C * ↑n ^ (1 / 4)⌉₊ | d ∣ n}.card}} 4

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that
$$\limsup_{n\to \infty}\left(\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\right) \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1,$$
where $\omega$ counts the number of distinct prime factors without restriction?
references: [erdosproblems.com/890](https://www.erdosproblems.com/890)
[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 1,
    Filter.limsup
        (fun n =>
          (∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, ↑(ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n + i))) *
            (↑(Real.log (Real.log ↑n)) / ↑(Real.log ↑n)))
        Filter.atTop =
      1

declarations.docstring:
A question of Erdős and Selfridge [ErSe67], who observe that
$\liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i < k}\omega(n+i)\geq k+\pi(k)-1$ for every $k$. This follows from
Pólya's theorem that the set of $k$-smooth integers has unbounded gaps - indeed,
$n(n+1)\cdots (n+k-1)$ is divisible by all primes $\leq k$ and, provided $n$ is large, all but at
most one of $n,n+1,\ldots,n+k-1$ has a prime factor $>k$ by Pólya's theorem.
references: [erdosproblems.com/890](https://www.erdosproblems.com/890)
[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  Filter.liminf (fun n => ∑ i ∈ Finset.range k, ↑(ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors (n + i))) Filter.atTop ≥
    ↑k + ↑k.primeCounting - 1

declarations.docstring: It is a classical fact that $\limsup_{n\to \infty}\omega(n)\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1.$
references: [erdosproblems.com/890](https://www.erdosproblems.com/890)
[ErSe67] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., Some problems on the prime factors of consecutive integers. Illinois J. Math. (1967), 428--430.

    Filter.atTop =

declarations.docstring:
Let $2=p_1 < p_2 < \cdots$ be the primes and $k\geq 2$. Is it true that, for all sufficiently large
$n$, there must exist an integer in $[n,n+p_1\cdots p_k)$ with $>k$ many prime factors?
references: [erdosproblems.com/891](https://www.erdosproblems.com/891)
[Po18] Pólya, Georg, Zur arithmetischen {U}ntersuchung der {P}olynome. Math. Z. (1918), 143--148.
[Wikipedia] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ k ≥ 2,
    ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∃ m ∈ Finset.Ico n (n + ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, Nat.nth Nat.Prime i), k < ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors m

declarations.docstring:
This is unknown even for $k=2$ - that is, is it true that in every interval of $6$
(sufficiently large) consecutive integers there must exist one with at least $3$ prime factors?
references: [erdosproblems.com/891](https://www.erdosproblems.com/891)
[Po18] Pólya, Georg, Zur arithmetischen {U}ntersuchung der {P}olynome. Math. Z. (1918), 143--148.
[Wikipedia] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture

declarations.docstring:
Schinzel deduced from Pólya's theorem [Po18] (that the sequence of $k$-smooth integers has unbounded
gaps) that this is true with $p_1\cdots p_k$ replaced by $p_1\cdots p_{k-1}p_{k+1}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/891](https://www.erdosproblems.com/891)
[Po18] Pólya, Georg, Zur arithmetischen {U}ntersuchung der {P}olynome. Math. Z. (1918), 143--148.
[Wikipedia] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ k ≥ 2,
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∃ m ∈ Finset.Ico n (n + (∏ i ∈ Finset.range (k - 1), Nat.nth Nat.Prime i) * Nat.nth Nat.Prime k),
      k < ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors m

declarations.docstring:
Weisenberg has observed that Dickson's conjecture implies the answer is no if we replace
$p_1\cdots p_k$ with $p_1\cdots p_k-1$. Indeed, let $L_k$ be the lowest common multiple of all
integers at most $p_1\cdots p_k$. By Dickson's conjecture [Wikipedia], there are infinitely many
$n'$ such that $\frac{L_k}{m}n'+1$ is prime for all $1\leq m < p_1\cdots p_k$. It follows that,
if $n=L_kn'+1$, then all integers in $[n,n+p_1\cdots p_k-1)$ have at most $k$ prime factors.
references: [erdosproblems.com/891](https://www.erdosproblems.com/891)
[Po18] Pólya, Georg, Zur arithmetischen {U}ntersuchung der {P}olynome. Math. Z. (1918), 143--148.
[Wikipedia] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickson%27s_conjecture
declarations.type_pretty:
Erdos891.DicksonConjecture →
  ∀ k ≥ 2,
    ∃ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      ∀ m ∈ Finset.Ico n (n + ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, Nat.nth Nat.Prime i - 1),
        ArithmeticFunction.cardDistinctFactors m ≤ k

declarations.docstring:
Hajnal thought that there is in fact an independent set which is a Hindman set - that is, an
independent set of the shape
$$\left\{ \sum_{i\in S}a_i : S\subseteq \{1,\ldots,k\}\right\}$$
for some $a_1,\ldots,a_k$ (provided $n$ is sufficiently large depending on $k$).

The general question of an independent Hindman set remains open. Here the $a_i$ are taken to be
distinct positive integers and $S$ ranges over the nonempty subsets of $\{1,\ldots,k\}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/895](https://www.erdosproblems.com/895)
[Er95d] Erdős, Paul, *On some problems in combinatorial set theory*. Publ. Inst. Math. (Beograd) (N.S.) (1995), 61-65.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k : ℕ),
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (G : SimpleGraph ↑(Set.Icc 1 n)),
      G.CliqueFree 3 →
        ∃ a, StrictMono a ∧ ∃ I, G.IsIndepSet I ∧ Subtype.val '' I = {m | ∃ S, S.Nonempty ∧ m = ∑ i ∈ S, a i}

declarations.docstring:
Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$ such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n (f(n+1)−f(n))/ \log n = ∞$?

The answer is no; this follows from a construction of Wirsing [Wi81], rediscovered by
Archivara [Ar25] and formalised in Lean by Aristotle [ArWu25].
references: [erdosproblems.com/897](https://www.erdosproblems.com/897)
[Ar25] Archivara Math Research Agent, [An Additive Counterexample: Erdős Problem 897](https://archivara.org/paper/df04f023-6ef0-4c52-bd12-18cdaa8f0741) (2025)
[ArWu25] Aristotle, operated mostly by L. Wu, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 897](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos897.lean) (2025)
[Wi70] E. Wirsing, A characterization of $\log n$ as an additive arithmetic function. Symposia Math. (1970), 45-57.
[Wi81] E. Wirsing, Additive and completely additive functions with restricted growth. Recent progress in analytic number theory, Vol. 2 (Durham, 1979), 231--280 (1981).

¬∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ a > 0, ∀ b > 0, a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
      Filter.limsup
            (fun x =>
              match x with
              | (p, k) => ↑(f (p ^ k)) / ↑(Real.log (↑p ^ k)))
            (Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) | Nat.Prime p}) =
          ⊤ →
        Filter.limsup (fun n => (↑(f (n + 1)) - ↑(f n)) / ↑(Real.log ↑n)) Filter.atTop = ⊤

Let $f(n)$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab)=f(a)+f(b)$
if $(a,b)=1$) such that $\limsup_{p,k} f(p^k) / \log(p^k) = ∞$ and $f(p^k) = f(p)$
or $f(p^k) = kf(p)$.
Is it true that $\limsup_n (f(n+1)−f(n))/ \log n = ∞$?

The known counterexample does not satisfy either of these extra hypotheses, so this variant remains
open.
references: [erdosproblems.com/897](https://www.erdosproblems.com/897)
[Ar25] Archivara Math Research Agent, [An Additive Counterexample: Erdős Problem 897](https://archivara.org/paper/df04f023-6ef0-4c52-bd12-18cdaa8f0741) (2025)
[ArWu25] Aristotle, operated mostly by L. Wu, [Lean formalisation of Erdős problem 897](https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.24.0/ErdosProblems/Erdos897.lean) (2025)
[Wi70] E. Wirsing, A characterization of $\log n$ as an additive arithmetic function. Symposia Math. (1970), 45-57.
[Wi81] E. Wirsing, Additive and completely additive functions with restricted growth. Recent progress in analytic number theory, Vol. 2 (Durham, 1979), 231--280 (1981).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ),
  (∀ a > 0, ∀ b > 0, a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
    Filter.limsup
          (fun x =>
            match x with
            | (p, k) => ↑(f (p ^ k)) / ↑(Real.log (↑p ^ k)))
          (Filter.atTop ⊓ Filter.principal {(p, k) | Nat.Prime p}) =
        ⊤ →
      ((∀ (k p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → f (p ^ k) = f p) ∨ ∀ (k p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → f (p ^ k) = ↑k * f p) →
        Filter.limsup (fun n => (↑(f (n + 1)) - ↑(f n)) / ↑(Real.log ↑n)) Filter.atTop = ⊤

declarations.docstring:
Let $\hat{R}(G)$ denote the size Ramsey number, the minimal number of edges $m$ such that there is
a graph $H$ with $m$ edges that is Ramsey for $G$.

Is there a function $f$ such that $f(x)/x\to \infty$ as $x\to \infty$ such that, for all large $C$,
if $G$ is a graph with $n$ vertices and $e\geq Cn$ edges then
$$\hat{R}(G) > f(C) e?$$

Here $\hat{R}(G)$ is `sizeRamsey G G`, and $G$ has at least one vertex (for $n = 0$ the
inequality fails trivially).
references: [erdosproblems.com/911](https://www.erdosproblems.com/911)
[Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*. (1982), 59--79.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ f,
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => f x / x) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop ∧
    ∃ C₀,
      ∀ C ≥ C₀,
        ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)),
          0 < n → C * ↑n ≤ ↑G.edgeSet.ncard → f C * ↑G.edgeSet.ncard < ↑(G.sizeRamsey G)

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that, for every $r$, there is a $k$ such that
if $I_1,\ldots,I_r$ are disjoint intervals of consecutive integers,
all of length at least $k$, then
$$
  \prod_{1\leq i\leq r}\prod_{m\in I_i}m
$$
is not a perfect power?
references: [erdosproblems.com/930](https://www.erdosproblems.com/930)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ r > 0,
    ∃ k,
      ∀ (I₁ I₂ : Fin r → ℕ),
        (∀ (i : Fin r), 0 < I₁ i ∧ I₁ i + k ≤ I₂ i + 1) →
          (∀ (i j : Fin r), i < j → I₂ i < I₁ j) → ¬Erdos930.IsPower (∏ i, ∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc (I₁ i) (I₂ i), m)

declarations.docstring:
Erdos and Selfridge [ErSe75] proved that the product of
consecutive integers is never a power (establishing the case $r=1$).

Theorem 1 from [ErSe75].

It is implied from `erdos_930.variants.consecutive_strong`.

[ErSe75] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., The product of consecutive integers is never a power. Illinois J. Math. (1975), 292-301.
references: [erdosproblems.com/930](https://www.erdosproblems.com/930)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (n k : ℕ), 0 ≤ n → 2 ≤ k → ¬Erdos930.IsPower (∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc (n + 1) (n + k), m)

declarations.docstring:
Let $k$, $l$, $n$ be integers such that $k \ge 3$, $l \ge 2$ and $n + k \ge p^{(k)}$,
where $p^{(k)}$ is the least prime satisfying $p^{(k)} \ge k$.
Then there is a prime $p \ge k$ for which $l$ does not divide
the multiplicity of the prime factor $p$ in $(n + 1) \ldots (n + k)$.

Theorem 2 from [ErSe75].

[ErSe75] Erdős, P. and Selfridge, J. L., The product of consecutive integers is never a power. Illinois J. Math. (1975), 292-301.
references: [erdosproblems.com/930](https://www.erdosproblems.com/930)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k l n : ℕ),
  3 ≤ k →
    2 ≤ l →
      Erdos930.nextPrime k ≤ n + k →
        ∃ p, k ≤ p ∧ Nat.Prime p ∧ ¬l ∣ (∏ m ∈ Finset.Icc (n + 1) (n + k), m).factorization p

declarations.docstring:
Let $k_1 \geq k_2 \geq 3$. Are there only finitely many $n_2\geq n_1 + k_1$
such that
$$
  \prod_{1\leq i\leq k_1}(n_1 + i)\ \text{and}\ \prod_{1\leq j\leq k_2} (n_2 + j)
$$
have the same prime factors?
references: [erdosproblems.com/931](https://www.erdosproblems.com/931)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (k₁ k₂ : ℕ),
    k₂ ≥ 3 →
      k₂ ≤ k₁ →
        {(n₁, n₂) |
            n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧
              (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Finite

declarations.docstring:
Erdős thought perhaps if the two products have the same factors then
$n_2 > 2(n_1 + k_1)$.
It is an open question whether this is true when allowing a finite number of counterexamples.
references: [erdosproblems.com/931](https://www.erdosproblems.com/931)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (k₁ k₂ : ℕ),
    k₂ ≥ 3 →
      k₂ ≤ k₁ →
        {(n₁, n₂) |
            n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧
              n₂ ≤ 2 * (n₁ + k₁) ∧
                (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Finite

declarations.docstring: In fact there exist counterexamples, like this one found by AlphaProof.
references: [erdosproblems.com/931](https://www.erdosproblems.com/931)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ k₁ k₂,
  ∃ (_ : k₂ ≤ k₁) (_ : 3 ≤ k₂),
    {(n₁, n₂) |
        n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ ∧
          n₂ ≤ 2 * (n₁ + k₁) ∧
            (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors}.Nonempty

declarations.docstring:
Erdős was unable to prove that if the two products have the same factors
then there must exist a prime between $n_1$ and $n_2$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/931](https://www.erdosproblems.com/931)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (k₁ k₂ n₁ n₂ : ℕ),
  k₂ ≤ k₁ →
    3 ≤ k₂ →
      n₁ + k₁ ≤ n₂ →
        (∏ i ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₁, (n₁ + i)).primeFactors = (∏ j ∈ Finset.Icc 1 k₂, (n₂ + j)).primeFactors →
          ∃ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ n₁ ≤ p ∧ p ≤ n₂

declarations.docstring:
If $n(n+1)=2^k3^lm$, where $(m,6)=1$, then is it true that
$\limsup_{n\to \infty} \frac{2^k3^l}{n\log n}=\infty$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/933](https://www.erdosproblems.com/933)

[Er76d] Erdős, P, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ Filter.limsup (fun n => ↑↑(2 ^ Erdos933.k n * 3 ^ Erdos933.l n) / (↑↑n * ↑(Real.log ↑n))) Filter.atTop = ⊤

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er76d] wrote 'it is easy to see' that for infinitely many $n$, $2^k 3^l > n\log n$.

Steinerberger has noted a simple proof of this fact follows from taking $n=2^{3^r}$ for any
integer $r\geq 1$, when $k=3^r$ and $l=r+1$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/933](https://www.erdosproblems.com/933)

[Er76d] Erdős, P, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.
declarations.type_pretty: {n | ↑(2 ^ Erdos933.k n * 3 ^ Erdos933.l n) > ↑n * Real.log ↑n}.Infinite

declarations.docstring: Mahler proved (a more general result that implies in particular) that $2^k3^l<n^{1+o(1)}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/933](https://www.erdosproblems.com/933)

[Er76d] Erdős, P, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions. Proceedings of the Fifth Manitoba Conference on Numerical Mathematics (Univ. Manitoba, Winnipeg, Man., 1975) (1976), 25-44.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c, c =o[Filter.atTop] 1 ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ↑(2 ^ Erdos933.k n * 3 ^ Erdos933.l n) < ↑n ^ (1 + c n)

declarations.docstring:
Let $h_t(d)$ be minimal such that every graph $G$ with $h_t(d)$ edges and maximal degree
$\leq d$ contains two edges whose shortest path between them has length $\geq t$.

Estimate $h_t(d)$.

A problem of Erdős and Nešetřil [Er88]. Erdős wrote 'This problem seems to be interesting only
if there is a nice expression for $h_t(d)$.' We read "estimate" as asking for an exact
expression, as in that remark: `h t d = erdos_934.answer t d` for all `1 ≤ t` and all `d`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/934](https://www.erdosproblems.com/934)

Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, de Joannis de Verclos, and Kang [CCJK22] conjectured that
$h_3(d) \leq d^3-d^2+d+2$ (with equality if $d-1$ is a prime power; the site writes "if and only
if", while [CCJK22, Conjecture 1] says "if"). Kumar, Mohar and Pragada [KMP26, Lemma 3.1]
refute the inequality: the odd graph $KG(7,3)$ has $35$ vertices, is $4$-regular, has $70$ edges
and any two of its edges are at distance less than $3$, so $h_3(4)\geq 71 > 54$.

declarations.docstring:
Cambie has also found solutions when $r=8$.

The source adds that the $r=8$ solution works "even with the sum of $5$ $8$-powerful numbers".
That is a stronger result than this statement, which asks for the $r - 2 = 6$ summands of
`Erdos939Sums`.

declarations.docstring:
Euler had conjectured that the sum of $k - 1$ many $k$-th powers is never a
$k$-th power, but this is false for $k=5$, as Lander and Parkin [LaPa67] found
$$27^5+84^5+110^5+133^5=144^5$$.

The summands must be positive. Without that condition a set containing `0` would count, so the
negation would be satisfied by a sum of fewer than $k-1$ powers and would claim less than the
refutation of Euler's conjecture that this theorem records.
references: [erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/939)
[Ni95] Nitaj, A., _On a conjecture of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers_. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1995), 317-318.
[Co98] Cohn, J. H. E., _A conjecture of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers_. Math. Comp. (1998), 439-440.
[Wa24] Walsh, P., _A question of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers and an elliptic curve analogue of the Ankeny-Artin-Chowla conjecture_. arXiv:2404.03970 (2024).
[LaPa67] Lander, L. J. and Parkin, T. R., _A counterexample to Euler's sum of powers conjecture_. Math. Comp. (1967), 101-103.

Cambie has found several examples of the sum of $r - 2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers being itself
$r$-powerful. For example when $r=5$ we have
$$3^7\cdot 61^5 = 2^8\cdot3^{10}\cdot 5^7 + 2^{12}\cdot 23^6 + 11^5\cdot 13^5$$.

declarations.docstring:
If $r≥4$, are there at most finitely many sums of $r-2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers
that are themselves $r$-powerful?

The answer is no: for every $r \ge 6$ there are infinitely many such sums, see
`erdos_939.variants.infinite_of_six_le`. (For $r = 4$ and $r = 5$ the question is open; for
$r = 4$ no example is known at all, see `erdos_939`.)
A construction in the site's comments, from GPT-5.5 Pro prompted by Price, gives infinitely
many for every $r \ge 6$. This statement quantifies over every $r \ge 4$, so it stays open at
$r = 4$ and $r = 5$. The category is unchanged because the construction is recorded in the
comments and not in the literature.
references: [erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/939)
[Ni95] Nitaj, A., _On a conjecture of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers_. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1995), 317-318.
[Co98] Cohn, J. H. E., _A conjecture of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers_. Math. Comp. (1998), 439-440.
[Wa24] Walsh, P., _A question of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers and an elliptic curve analogue of the Ankeny-Artin-Chowla conjecture_. arXiv:2404.03970 (2024).
[LaPa67] Lander, L. J. and Parkin, T. R., _A counterexample to Euler's sum of powers conjecture_. Math. Comp. (1967), 101-103.
declarations.type_pretty: ¬∀ r ≥ 4, (Erdos939.Erdos939Sums r).Finite

declarations.docstring:
For every $r \ge 6$ there are infinitely many sums of $r - 2$ coprime $r$-powerful numbers that
are themselves $r$-powerful.

A construction, found by GPT-5.5 Pro prompted by Liam Price and recorded in the comments on
[erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/939), expands
$(X+Y)^r = (X-Y)^r + \sum_{j \text{ odd}} 2\binom{r}{j} X^{r-j} Y^j$, splits the $j = 3$ term into
$\lfloor r/2 \rfloor - 2$ distinct pieces to obtain exactly $r - 2$ summands, and takes
$X = q^r$, $Y = B^r$ with $B$ divisible by all primes in the coefficients and $q > B$ a prime not
dividing $B$; varying $q$ gives infinitely many solutions.
references: [erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/939)
[Ni95] Nitaj, A., _On a conjecture of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers_. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1995), 317-318.

[Wa24] Walsh, P., _A question of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers and an elliptic curve analogue of the Ankeny-Artin-Chowla conjecture_. arXiv:2404.03970 (2024).
[LaPa67] Lander, L. J. and Parkin, T. R., _A counterexample to Euler's sum of powers conjecture_. Math. Comp. (1967), 101-103.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ r ≥ 6, (Erdos939.Erdos939Sums r).Infinite

declarations.docstring:
Are there infinitely many triples of coprime $3$-powerful numbers $a, b, c$ such that $a + b = c$?

The answer is yes. Nitaj [Ni95] proved it, with $2^3\cdot 3^5\cdot 73^3 + 271^3 = 919^3$ as an
example. In Nitaj's construction at least two of $a, b, c$ are perfect cubes. Cohn [Co98]
constructed infinitely many triples of which none is a perfect cube, and Walsh [Wa24] gave a
further construction.
references: [erdosproblems.com/939](https://www.erdosproblems.com/939)
[Ni95] Nitaj, A., _On a conjecture of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers_. Bull. London Math. Soc. (1995), 317-318.

[Wa24] Walsh, P., _A question of Erdős on 3-powerful numbers and an elliptic curve analogue of the Ankeny-Artin-Chowla conjecture_. arXiv:2404.03970 (2024).
[LaPa67] Lander, L. J. and Parkin, T. R., _A counterexample to Euler's sum of powers conjecture_. Math. Comp. (1967), 101-103.

declarations.docstring:
Suppose $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ determine a convex polygon and the set of distances between
them is $\{u_1,\ldots,u_t\}$. Suppose $u_i$ appears as the distance between $f(u_i)$ many pairs of
points. Then
$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll n^3.$$

In [Er97c] Erdős claims that Fishburn solved this, but gives no reference.
references: [erdosproblems.com/94](https://www.erdosproblems.com/94)
[Er92e] Erdős, Pál, *Some Unsolved problems in Geometry, Number Theory and Combinatorics*. Eureka (1992), 44-48.
[Er97c] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favorite problems and results*. The mathematics of Paul Erdős, I (1997), 47-67.
[LeTh95] Lefmann, Hanno and Thiele, Torsten, *Point sets with distinct distances*. Combinatorica (1995), 379-408.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C > 0,
  ∀ (P : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
    EuclideanGeometry.ConvexIndep ↑P → ∑ u ∈ distanceSet P, ↑(distanceMultiplicity P u) ^ 2 ≤ C * ↑P.card ^ 3

$$\sum_i f(u_i)^2 \ll n^3$$
under the weaker assumption that no three points are on a line.

declarations.docstring:
Let $r \ge 3$. Are there infinitely many integers which are not the sum of at most $r$-many
$r$-powerful numbers?

declarations.docstring:
Is it true that the set of integers which are the sum of at most three cubes has density $0$?

The cubes are those of non-negative integers, which is what `Multiset ℕ` gives. This choice
decides the question: over `ℤ` a sum of three cubes is conjectured to represent every integer
that is not $\pm 4 \bmod 9$, which is density $7/9$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/940](https://www.erdosproblems.com/940)
[BaBr94] Baker, R. C. and Brüdern, J., _On sums of two squarefull numbers_. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1994), 1-5.
[He88](https://oeis.org/A187054) Heath-Brown, D. R., _Ternary quadratic forms and sums of three square-full numbers_. (1988), 137-163.
declarations.type_pretty: {n | ∃ S, S.card ≤ 3 ∧ n = (Multiset.map (fun x => x ^ 3) S).sum}.HasDensity 0

declarations.docstring:
Heath-Brown [He88] has proved that all large numbers are the sum of at most three
$2$-powerful numbers.

This is the case $r = 2$ of `Erdos1107.erdos_1107`, which asks the same question with $r + 1$
summands, and it is stated there as `Erdos1107.erdos_1107.variants.two`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/940](https://www.erdosproblems.com/940)
[BaBr94] Baker, R. C. and Brüdern, J., _On sums of two squarefull numbers_. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1994), 1-5.
[He88](https://oeis.org/A187054) Heath-Brown, D. R., _Ternary quadratic forms and sums of three square-full numbers_. (1988), 137-163.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ᶠ (x : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ S, S.card ≤ 3 ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, Nat.Full 2 s) ∧ x = S.sum

declarations.docstring:
The set of integers which are the sum of at most two $2$-powerful numbers has density $0$.

Erdős called this 'easy'. Baker and Brüdern [BaBr94] gave the first proof in the literature.
references: [erdosproblems.com/940](https://www.erdosproblems.com/940)

declarations.docstring:
Is there some constant $c > 0$ such that $h(n) < (\log n)^{c + o(1)}$ and, for infinitely many $n$,

declarations.docstring:
Let $k \ge 4$ and $r\ge 1$. Must there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$

declarations.docstring:
Let $k \ge 4$. Must there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$
such that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>1$?

This was conjectured by Dirac in 1970.
references: [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ k ≥ 4, ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G k 1

declarations.docstring:
Dirac's conjecture was proved, for $k=5$: There exists a graph $G$ with chromatic number $5$, such
that every vertex is critical, yet every critical set of edges has size $>1$, or in other words:
has no critical edge.

[Br92] Brown, Jason I., A vertex critical graph without critical edges. Discrete Math. (1992), 99--101
references: [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G 5 1

declarations.docstring: The case $k=4$ and $r=1$ remains open: Are there $4$-critical graphs without any critical edges?
references: [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G 4 1

declarations.docstring:
Jensen [Je02] gave an construction for $k$-critical graphs without any critical edges for all $k ≥ 5$.

[Je02] Jensen, Tommy R., Dense critical and vertex-critical graphs. Discrete Math. (2002), 63--84.
references: [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 5 ≤ k → ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G k 1

declarations.docstring:
Lattanzio [La02] proved there exist $k$-critical graphs without critical edges for all $k$ such that
$k - 1$ is not prime.

[La02] Lattanzio, John J., A note on a conjecture of {D}irac. Discrete Math. (2002), 323--330
references: [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 4 ≤ k → ¬Nat.Prime (k - 1) → ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G k 1

declarations.docstring:
Martinsson and Steiner [MaSt25] proved for every $r \ge 1$ if $k$ is sufficiently large, depending
on $r$, there exist a graph $G$ with chromatic number $k$ such that every vertex is critical,
yet every critical set of edges has size $>r$.

[MaSt25] Martinsson, Anders and Steiner, Raphael, Vertex-critical graphs far from edge-criticality. Combin. Probab. Comput. (2025), 151--157
references: [erdosproblems.com/944](https://www.erdosproblems.com/944)
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (r : ℕ), 1 ≤ r → ∀ᶠ (k : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ V G, Erdos944.SimpleGraph.IsErdos944 G k r

declarations.docstring:
This function was considered by de Bruijn, Erdős, and Turán, who showed that
$\sum_{n<x}f(n)\sim \sum_{n<x}f(n)^2\sim x$. They gave no proofs, but a proof of the (harder) second
claim is given by Gorodetsky here [mathoverflow/508491].
references: [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)
[erdosproblems.com/950](https://www.erdosproblems.com/950)
[Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
[mathoverflow/508491](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/508491)
declarations.type_pretty:
(Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun x => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range x, Erdos950.f n) fun x => ↑x) ∧
  Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun x => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range x, Erdos950.f n ^ 2) fun x => ↑x

declarations.docstring:
The study of $f(p)$ is even harder, and Erdős could not prove that
$\sum_{p<x}f(p)^2\sim \pi(x)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)
[erdosproblems.com/950](https://www.erdosproblems.com/950)
[Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
[mathoverflow/508491](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/508491)
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  Asymptotics.IsEquivalent Filter.atTop (fun x => ∑ p ∈ Finset.range x with Prime p, Erdos950.f p ^ 2) fun x =>
    ↑x.primeCounting

declarations.docstring:
Erdős writes that a 'weaker conjecture which is perhaps not quite inaccessible' is that,
for every $\epsilon>0$, if $x$ is sufficiently large there exists $y<x$ such that
$\pi(x)< \pi(y)+\epsilon \pi(x-y)$. Compare this to [855].
references: [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)
[erdosproblems.com/950](https://www.erdosproblems.com/950)
[Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
[mathoverflow/508491](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/508491)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ (x : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ y < x, ↑x.primeCounting < ↑y.primeCounting + ε * ↑(x - y).primeCounting

declarations.docstring:
He notes that if $\pi(x)< \pi(y)+O\left(\frac{x-y}{\log x}\right)$ for all $y<x-(\log x)^C$ for
some constant $C>0$ then $f(n)\ll \log\log\log n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/855](https://www.erdosproblems.com/855)
[erdosproblems.com/950](https://www.erdosproblems.com/950)
[Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
[mathoverflow/508491](https://mathoverflow.net/questions/508491)
declarations.type_pretty:
(∃ C > 0,
    ∃ K > 0,
      ∀ᶠ (x : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
        ∀ (y : ℕ), ↑y < ↑x - Real.log ↑x ^ C → ↑x.primeCounting < ↑y.primeCounting + K * ((↑x - ↑y) / Real.log ↑x)) →
  Erdos950.f =O[Filter.atTop] fun n => Real.log (Real.log (Real.log ↑n))

declarations.docstring: If `1 < a 0 < ...` has property `Erdos951Prop`, is it true that `#{a i ≤ x} ≤ π x`?
references: [erdosproblems.com/951](https://www.erdosproblems.com/951)
[Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.

True ↔

Beurling conjectured that if the number of Beurling integer in `[1, x]`
is `x + o(log x)`, then `a` must be the sequence of primes.

[Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ., New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.

∀ (a : ℕ → ℝ),
  IsBeurlingPrimes a →
    (fun x => ↑(BeurlingIntegers a ∩ Set.Iic x).ncard - x) =o[Filter.atTop] Real.log → a = Nat.cast ∘ Nat.nth Nat.Prime

declarations.docstring:
If $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ has density $0$ then $s^{-1}(A)$ must also have density $0$.

A conjecture of Erdős, Granville, Pomerance, and Spiro [EGPS90].
references: [erdosproblems.com/955](https://www.erdosproblems.com/955)

[EGPS90] Erdős, P. and Granville, A. and Pomerance, C. and Spiro, C., On the normal behavior of the iterates of some arithmetic functions. Analytic number theory (Allerton Park, IL, 1989) (1990), 165-204.
[Er73b] Erdős, P., Über die Zahlen der Form $\sigma(n) - n$ und $n - \phi(n)$. Elem. Math. (1973), 83--86.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
[PPT18] Pollack, Paul and Pomerance, Carl and Thompson, Lola, Divisor-sum fibers. Mathematika (2018), 330--342.
[Po14b] Pollack, Paul, Some arithmetic properties of the sum of proper divisors and the sum of prime divisors. Illinois J. Math. (2014), 125--147.
[PoPo16] Pollack, Paul and Pomerance, Carl, Some problems of Erdős on the sum-of-divisors function. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B (2016), 1--26.
[Tr15] Troupe, Lee, On the number of prime factors of values of the sum-of-proper-divisors function. J. Number Theory (2015), 120--135.
[Tr20] Troupe, Lee, Divisor sums representable as the sum of two squares. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (2020), 4189--4202.
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (A : Set ℕ), A.HasDensity 0 → {x | Erdos955.s x ∈ A}.HasDensity 0

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er73b] proved that there are sets $A$ of positive density such that $s^{-1}(A)$ is empty.

Here "positive density" means positive lower density: Erdős proved that the set of untouchable
numbers (those not of the form $s(n)$) has positive lower density [Er73b, Satz I]. Pollack and
Pomerance [PoPo16] conjecture that this set has a natural density and give a heuristic for its
value. The same result is stated as `erdos_418.variants.sigma` in Erdős Problem 418.
references: [erdosproblems.com/955](https://www.erdosproblems.com/955)

[EGPS90] Erdős, P. and Granville, A. and Pomerance, C. and Spiro, C., On the normal behavior of the iterates of some arithmetic functions. Analytic number theory (Allerton Park, IL, 1989) (1990), 165-204.
[Er73b] Erdős, P., Über die Zahlen der Form $\sigma(n) - n$ und $n - \phi(n)$. Elem. Math. (1973), 83--86.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
[PPT18] Pollack, Paul and Pomerance, Carl and Thompson, Lola, Divisor-sum fibers. Mathematika (2018), 330--342.
[Po14b] Pollack, Paul, Some arithmetic properties of the sum of proper divisors and the sum of prime divisors. Illinois J. Math. (2014), 125--147.
[PoPo16] Pollack, Paul and Pomerance, Carl, Some problems of Erdős on the sum-of-divisors function. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B (2016), 1--26.
[Tr15] Troupe, Lee, On the number of prime factors of values of the sum-of-proper-divisors function. J. Number Theory (2015), 120--135.
[Tr20] Troupe, Lee, Divisor sums representable as the sum of two squares. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. (2020), 4189--4202.
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ A, 0 < A.lowerDensity ∧ {x | Erdos955.s x ∈ A} = ∅

declarations.docstring:
Pollack, Pomerance, and Thompson [PPT18] prove that if $\epsilon(x)=o(1)$ and $A\subset \mathbb{N}$
has size at most $x^{1/2+\epsilon(x)}$ then $\#\{ n\leq x: s(n)\in A\} =o(x)$ as $x\to \infty$. It
follows that (using $s(n)\ll n\log\log n$) if $A$ grows like
$\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert\leq x^{1/2+o(1)}$ then $s^{-1}(A)$ has density $0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/955](https://www.erdosproblems.com/955)

[EGPS90] Erdős, P. and Granville, A. and Pomerance, C. and Spiro, C., On the normal behavior of the iterates of some arithmetic functions. Analytic number theory (Allerton Park, IL, 1989) (1990), 165-204.
[Er73b] Erdős, P., Über die Zahlen der Form $\sigma(n) - n$ und $n - \phi(n)$. Elem. Math. (1973), 83--86.
[Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
[PPT18] Pollack, Paul and Pomerance, Carl and Thompson, Lola, Divisor-sum fibers. Mathematika (2018), 330--342.

[PoPo16] Pollack, Paul and Pomerance, Carl, Some problems of Erdős on the sum-of-divisors function. Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B (2016), 1--26.

declarations.docstring:
Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of size $n$ and let $\{d_1,\ldots,d_k\}$ be
the set of distinct distances determined by $A$. Let $f(d)$ be the number of times
the distance $d$ is determined, ordered so that
$f(d_1)\geq f(d_2)\geq \cdots \geq f(d_k)$. Estimate
$$\max (f(d_1)-f(d_2)),$$
where the maximum is taken over all $A$ of size $n$ (this is `extremalGap n`).
references: [erdosproblems.com/959](https://www.erdosproblems.com/959)
declarations.type_pretty: (fun n => ↑(Erdos959.extremalGap n)) =Θ[Filter.atTop] Erdos959.erdos_959.answer

declarations.docstring:
A superlinear lower bound: there is a $c>0$ with
$$\text{extremalGap}(n)\geq n^{1 + c/\log\log n}$$
for all large $n$, so $\max (f(d_1)-f(d_2))$ grows faster than any linear function
of $n$. Determining the exact order remains open, which is `erdos_959`.
references: [erdosproblems.com/959](https://www.erdosproblems.com/959)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ c, 0 < c ∧ ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ↑n ^ (1 + c / Real.log (Real.log ↑n)) ≤ ↑(Erdos959.extremalGap n)

declarations.docstring:
Let $1<a_1<\cdots$ be a sequence of integers such that $\sum\frac{1}{a_i}<\infty$. Is it true
that, for every $t\in \mathbb{R}$,
$$1+\sum_{k}\frac{1}{a_k^{1+it}}\neq 0?$$

Yip [Yi25] has proved that this is not always true - in fact, for any real $t\neq 0$, there
exists a sequence of integers $1<a_1<\cdots$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_i}<\infty$ and
$1+\sum_{k}\frac{1}{a_k^{1+it}}=0$.

This was formalized in Lean by Wu using Aristotle.
references: [erdosproblems.com/967](https://www.erdosproblems.com/967)
[ErIn64] Erdős, P. and Ingham, A. E., *Arithmetical Tauberian theorems*. Acta Arith. (1964), 341-356.
[Yi25] Yip, F., *On a problem of Erdős and Ingham*. arXiv:2512.16528 (2025).
declarations.type_pretty:
¬∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
    StrictMono a → 1 < a 0 → (Summable fun k => 1 / ↑(a k)) → ∀ (t : ℝ), 1 + ∑' (k : ℕ), Erdos967.summand t (a k) ≠ 0

declarations.docstring: It remains open whether this is true for every finite sequence of integers.
references: [erdosproblems.com/967](https://www.erdosproblems.com/967)
[ErIn64] Erdős, P. and Ingham, A. E., *Arithmetical Tauberian theorems*. Acta Arith. (1964), 341-356.
[Yi25] Yip, F., *On a problem of Erdős and Ingham*. arXiv:2512.16528 (2025).
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), (∀ n ∈ A, 1 < n) → ∀ (t : ℝ), 1 + ∑ n ∈ A, Erdos967.summand t n ≠ 0

declarations.docstring:
Their interest in this problem arose from their proof that the statement that there are no such
zeros is equivalent to the fact that, for any non-decreasing $f:\mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$
which is bounded on every bounded interval and is $=0$ for $x<1$, the relationship
$$f(x)+\sum_k f(x/a_k)=\left(1+\sum_k \frac{1}{a_k}+o(1)\right)x$$
implies $f(x)=(1+o(1))x$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/967](https://www.erdosproblems.com/967)
[ErIn64] Erdős, P. and Ingham, A. E., *Arithmetical Tauberian theorems*. Acta Arith. (1964), 341-356.
[Yi25] Yip, F., *On a problem of Erdős and Ingham*. arXiv:2512.16528 (2025).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (a : ℕ → ℕ),
  StrictMono a →
    1 < a 0 →
      (Summable fun k => 1 / ↑(a k)) →
        ((∀ (t : ℝ), 1 + ∑' (k : ℕ), Erdos967.summand t (a k) ≠ 0) ↔
          ∀ (f : ℝ → ℝ),
            Monotone f →
              (∀ (x : ℝ), 0 ≤ f x) →
                (∀ x < 1, f x = 0) →
                  (∀ (x y : ℝ), BddAbove (f '' Set.Icc x y)) →
                    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (f x + ∑' (k : ℕ), f (x / ↑(a k))) / x) Filter.atTop
                        (nhds (1 + ∑' (k : ℕ), 1 / ↑(a k))) →
                      Filter.Tendsto (fun x => f x / x) Filter.atTop (nhds 1))

declarations.docstring:
A question of Erdős and Ingham [ErIn64]. The simplest case they could not decide this question
for was the finite sequence $\{2,3,5\}$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/967](https://www.erdosproblems.com/967)

[Yi25] Yip, F., *On a problem of Erdős and Ingham*. arXiv:2512.16528 (2025).
declarations.type_pretty: ∀ (t : ℝ), 1 + ∑ n ∈ {2, 3, 5}, Erdos967.summand t n ≠ 0

declarations.docstring:
Yip [Yi25] has proved that this is not always true - in fact, for any real $t\neq 0$, there
exists a sequence of integers $1<a_1<\cdots$ such that $\sum \frac{1}{a_i}<\infty$ and
$1+\sum_{k}\frac{1}{a_k^{1+it}}=0$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/967](https://www.erdosproblems.com/967)
[ErIn64] Erdős, P. and Ingham, A. E., *Arithmetical Tauberian theorems*. Acta Arith. (1964), 341-356.
[Yi25] Yip, F., *On a problem of Erdős and Ingham*. arXiv:2512.16528 (2025).
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (t : ℝ),
  t ≠ 0 → ∃ a, StrictMono a ∧ 1 < a 0 ∧ (Summable fun k => 1 / ↑(a k)) ∧ 1 + ∑' (k : ℕ), Erdos967.summand t (a k) = 0

declarations.docstring:
Let $Q(x)$ count the squarefree integers in $[1,x]$, and define $E(x)$ by
$$Q(x)=\frac{6}{\pi^2}x+E(x).$$
Determine the order of magnitude of $E(x)$: an upper bound $E(x)=O(g(x))$ with a matching
oscillation bound $E(x)\ne o(g(x))$.
references: [Erdős Problem 969](https://www.erdosproblems.com/969)
Moser, L. and MacLeod, R. A., *The error term for the squarefree integers*. Canadian Mathematical Bulletin **9** (1966), 303–306. https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1966-039-4

declarations.docstring: Evelyn and Linfoot proved $E(x)=\Omega(x^{1/4})$.
references: [Erdős Problem 969](https://www.erdosproblems.com/969)
Moser, L. and MacLeod, R. A., *The error term for the squarefree integers*. Canadian Mathematical Bulletin **9** (1966), 303–306. https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1966-039-4
declarations.type_pretty: ¬(fun x => |Erdos969.squarefreeCountingError x|) =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => ↑x ^ (1 / 4)

declarations.docstring: The prime number theorem implies $E(x)=o(\sqrt{x})$.
references: [Erdős Problem 969](https://www.erdosproblems.com/969)
Moser, L. and MacLeod, R. A., *The error term for the squarefree integers*. Canadian Mathematical Bulletin **9** (1966), 303–306. https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1966-039-4
declarations.type_pretty: (fun x => |Erdos969.squarefreeCountingError x|) =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => √↑x

declarations.docstring: Exactly seven integers in $[1,10]$ are squarefree, including $1$.
references: [Erdős Problem 969](https://www.erdosproblems.com/969)
Moser, L. and MacLeod, R. A., *The error term for the squarefree integers*. Canadian Mathematical Bulletin **9** (1966), 303–306. https://doi.org/10.4153/CMB-1966-039-4
declarations.type_pretty: Erdos969.squarefreeCounting 10 = 7

declarations.docstring: Does every convex polygon have a vertex with no other 4 vertices equidistant from it?
references: [erdosproblems.com/97](https://www.erdosproblems.com/97)
declarations.type_pretty:

declarations.docstring:
Erdős also conjectured that there is a $k$ for which every convex polygon has a vertex
with no other $k$ vertices equidistant from it.
references: [erdosproblems.com/97](https://www.erdosproblems.com/97)

declarations.docstring:
Erdős originally conjectured this (in [Er46b]) with no 3 vertices equidistant,
but Danzer found a convex polygon on 9 points such that every vertex has three
vertices equidistant from it (but this distance depends on the vertex).
Danzer's construction is explained in [Er87b].

[Er46b] Erdős, P., _On sets of distances of $n$ points_. Amer. Math. Monthly (1946), 248-250.
[Er87b] Erdős, P., _Some combinatorial and metric problems in geometry_. Intuitive geometry (Siófok, 1985), 167-177.
references: [erdosproblems.com/97](https://www.erdosproblems.com/97)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ A, A.Nonempty ∧ EuclideanGeometry.ConvexIndep ↑A ∧ Erdos97.HasNEquidistantProperty 3 A

declarations.docstring:
Fishburn and Reeds [FiRe92] have found a convex polygon on 20 points such that
every vertex has three vertices equidistant from it (and this distance is the same for all vertices).

[FiRe92] Fishburn, P. C. and Reeds, J. A., _Unit distances between vertices of a convex polygon_. Comput. Geom. (1992), 81-91.
references: [erdosproblems.com/97](https://www.erdosproblems.com/97)
declarations.type_pretty: ∃ A, A.Nonempty ∧ EuclideanGeometry.ConvexIndep ↑A ∧ Erdos97.HasNUnitDistanceProperty 3 A

declarations.docstring:
Fishburn and Reeds [FiRe92] also proved that the smallest $n$ for which there exists
a convex $n$-gon and a cut $\{A, B\}$ of its vertices such that $|\{b \in B : d(a, b) = 1\}| ≥ 3$
for all $a \in A$, and $|\{a \in A : d(a, b) = 1\}| ≥ 3$ for all $b \in B$, is $n = 20$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/97](https://www.erdosproblems.com/97)
declarations.type_pretty:
sInf
    {n |
      ∃ V A B,
        n = V.card ∧
          EuclideanGeometry.ConvexIndep ↑V ∧
            A.Nonempty ∧
              B.Nonempty ∧
                Erdos97.IsCut V A B ∧ Erdos97.HasNUnitDistancePointsOn 3 B A ∧ Erdos97.HasNUnitDistancePointsOn 3 A B} =
  20

declarations.docstring:
Let `p(a, d)` be the least prime congruent to `a (mod d)`.
Does there exist a constant `c > 0` such that for all large `d`,
`p(a, d) > (1 + c) * φ(d) * log d` for `≫ φ(d)` many values of `a`?
references: [erdosproblems.com/971](https://www.erdosproblems.com/971)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c > 0,
  ∃ C > 0,
    ∀ᶠ (d : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
      C * ↑d.totient ≤
        ↑{a ∈ Finset.Iio d |
              a.Coprime d ∧ ↑(Erdos971.leastCongruentPrime a d) > (1 + c) * ↑d.totient * Real.log ↑d}.card

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er49c] proved that the statement in `erdos_971` holds for infinitely many values of `d`.

[Er49c] Erdős, P., _On some applications of Brun's method_. Acta Univ. Szeged. Sect. Sci. Math.
(1949), 57--63.
references: [erdosproblems.com/971](https://www.erdosproblems.com/971)
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ c > 0,
  ∃ C > 0,
    {d |
        C * ↑d.totient ≤
          ↑{a ∈ Finset.Iio d |
                a.Coprime d ∧ ↑(Erdos971.leastCongruentPrime a d) > (1 + c) * ↑d.totient * Real.log ↑d}.card}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:

[Er49c] Erdős, P., _On some applications of Brun's method_. Acta Univ. Szeged. Sect. Sci. Math.
(1949), 57--63.
references: [erdosproblems.com/971](https://www.erdosproblems.com/971)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ ε > 0,
  ∃ C > 0,
    ∀ᶠ (d : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,

        ↑{a ∈ Finset.Iio d | a.Coprime d ∧ ↑(Erdos971.leastCongruentPrime a d) < ε * ↑d.totient * Real.log ↑d}.card

declarations.docstring:
**Erdős problem 972.**
Let $\alpha > 1$ be irrational. Are there infinitely many primes $p$

declarations.docstring:
For an irreducible polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ with $f(n) \ge 1$ for sufficiently large $n$,
does there exists a constant $c = c(f) > 0$ such that
$\sum_{n \le x} \tau(f(n)) \approx c \cdot x \log x$?

Note that it is unclear whether the polynomial should have integer coefficients or merely be
integer-valued. We assume the former.
references: [erdosproblems.com/975](https://www.erdosproblems.com/975)
[Va39] van der Corput, J. G., Une in\'egalit\'e{} relative au nombre des diviseurs. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch., Proc. (1939), 547--553.
[Er52b] Erd\"os, P., On the sum {$\sum^x_{k=1} d(f(k))$}. J. London Math. Soc. (1952), 7--15.
[Ho63] Hooley, Christopher, On the number of divisors of a quadratic polynomial. Acta Math. (1963), 97--114.
[Mc95] McKee, James, On the average number of divisors of quadratic polynomials. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1995), 389--392.
[Mc97] McKee, James, A note on the number of divisors of quadratic polynomials. (1997), 275--281.
[Mc99] McKee, James, The average number of divisors of an irreducible quadratic polynomial. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1999), 17--22.
[T] T. Tao, Erdos' divisor bound, https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2011/07/23/erdos-divisor-bound/
declarations.type_pretty:

  ∀ (f : Polynomial ℤ),
    f.natDegree ≠ 0 →
      Irreducible f →
        (∀ᶠ (n : ℤ) in Filter.atTop, 1 ≤ Polynomial.eval n f) →
          ∃ c > 0, Filter.Tendsto (fun x => Erdos975.Erdos975Sum f x / (x * Real.log x)) Filter.atTop (nhds c)

declarations.docstring:
Let $f\in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be an irreducible polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$. Let $F_f(n)$ be maximal
such that there exists $1\leq m\leq n$ with $f(m)$ is divisible by a prime $\geq F_f(n)$.
Equivalently, $F_f(n)$ is the greatest prime divisor of
$$\prod_{1\leq m\leq n}f(m).$$
Estimate $F_f(n)$.

We read "estimate" as determining the order of magnitude of $F_f(n)$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/976](https://www.erdosproblems.com/976)
[Er52c] Erdős, P., *On the greatest prime factor of $\prod_{k=1}^x f(k)$*. J. London Math. Soc. 27 (1952), 379-384.
[Er65b] Erdős, P., *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
[Na22] Nagell, T., Abh. Math. Sem. Hamburg 1 (1922), 179-194.
[Ri34] Ricci, G., Annali di Mat. (1934), 295-303.
[Te90] Tenenbaum, G., *Sur une question d'Erdős et Schinzel*. A tribute to Paul Erdős (1990), 405-443.

declarations.docstring:
If $P(m)$ is the greatest prime divisor of $m$, then is it true that
$$\frac{P(2^n-1)}{n}\to \infty$$
as $n\to \infty$?

Schinzel [Sc62] proved that $P(2^n-1)>2n$ for $n>12$. In [Er65b] Erdős also asks about $P(n!+1)$.
Stewart [St74b] proved that this conjecture is true if we restrict $n$ to those integers with
$<\frac{1}{\log 2}\log\log n$ many prime factors.

This was proved in the affirmative by Stewart [St13], who proved that
$P(2^n-1)\gg n^{1+\frac{1}{104\log\log n}}$ for all large $n$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/977](https://www.erdosproblems.com/977)
[Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
[Sc62] Schinzel, A., *On primitive prime factors of $a^n-b^n$*. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1962), 555-562.
[St74b] Stewart, C. L., *The greatest prime factor of $a^n-b^n$*. Acta Arith. (1974/75), 427-433.
[St13] Stewart, Cameron L., *On divisors of Lucas and Lehmer numbers*. Acta Math. (2013), 291-314.
[MuWo02] Murty, Ram and Wong, Siman, *The $ABC$ conjecture and prime divisors of the Lucas and Lehmer sequences*. (2002), 43-54.
[La21] L. Lai, *On the largest prime divisor of $n!+1$*. arXiv:2103.14894 (2021).
declarations.type_pretty: Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(2 ^ n - 1).maxPrimeFac / ↑n) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop

declarations.docstring:

conjecture.

declarations.docstring:
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then some vertex has at least
$\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ different distances to other vertices.
references: [erdosproblems.com/982](https://www.erdosproblems.com/982)
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ),
  3 ≤ n →
    ∀ (p : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)),
      Function.Injective p →
        EuclideanGeometry.IsConvexPolygon p → ∃ i, {d | ∃ j, j ≠ i ∧ d = dist (p i) (p j)}.ncard ≥ n / 2

declarations.docstring: Is it true that, for every prime $p$, there is a prime $q \leq p$ which is a primitive root modulo $p$?
references: [erdosproblems.com/985](https://www.erdosproblems.com/985)
declarations.type_pretty: True ↔ ∀ (p : ℕ), Nat.Prime p → p ≠ 2 → ∃ q, Nat.Prime q ∧ q < p ∧ orderOf ↑q = p - 1

declarations.docstring: Heath-Brown proved that at least one of 2, 3, or 5 is a primitive root for infinitely many primes $p$.
references: [erdosproblems.com/985](https://www.erdosproblems.com/985)
declarations.type_pretty: {p | Nat.Prime p ∧ (orderOf 2 = p - 1 ∨ orderOf 3 = p - 1 ∨ orderOf 5 = p - 1)}.Infinite

declarations.docstring:
For sufficiently large n, is it the case that any set of n points with minimum distance $1$
that minimizes diameter must contain an equilateral triangle of side length 1?
references: [erdosproblems.com/99](https://www.erdosproblems.com/99)
[BeFo99] Bezdek, Andr\'{a}s and Fodor, Ferenc, Minimal diameter of certain sets in the plane. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1999), 105-111.
[Er94b] Erd\H{o}s, Paul, Some problems in number theory, combinatorics and combinatorial geometry. Math. Pannon. (1994), 261-269.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop,
    ∀ (A : Finset (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
      A.card = n →
        Erdos99.HasMinDist1 A →
          IsMinOn (fun B => Metric.diam ↑B) {B | B.card = n ∧ Erdos99.HasMinDist1 B} A →
            ∃ p ∈ A, ∃ q ∈ A, ∃ r ∈ A, Erdos99.FormsEquilateralTriangle p q r

declarations.docstring:
Erdős Problem 995:

For every lacunary sequence $(n_k)$ of integers and every $f \in L^2([0,1])$ with
$\int_0^1 f = 0$, is it true that for almost all $\alpha$,
$$\sum_{k < N} f(\{\alpha n_k\}) = o\!\left(N \sqrt{\log\log N}\right)?$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/995](https://www.erdosproblems.com/995)
[Er49] Erdős, P., On the strong law of large numbers, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. (1949), 329-334.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ),
  IsLacunary n →
    ∀ (f : ℝ → ℝ),
      MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Icc 0 1)) →
        ∫ (x : ℝ) in 0..1, f x = 0 →
          ∀ᵐ (α : ℝ) ∂MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Icc 0 1),
            Erdos995.partialSum n f α =o[Filter.atTop] fun N => ↑N * √(Real.log (Real.log ↑N))

declarations.docstring:
Erdős [Er49] showed the growth cannot be pushed below $N (\log\log N)^{1/2}$ by more than an
arbitrarily small power: there is a lacunary sequence and a mean-zero $f \in L^2([0,1])$ such
that for every $\varepsilon > 0$, for almost all $\alpha$,
$$\limsup_{N \to \infty} \frac{\sum_{k < N} f(\{\alpha n_k\})}{N (\log\log N)^{1/2 - \varepsilon}}
  = \infty.$$
references: [erdosproblems.com/995](https://www.erdosproblems.com/995)
[Er49] Erdős, P., On the strong law of large numbers, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. (1949), 329-334.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ n,
  IsLacunary n ∧
    ∃ f,
      MeasureTheory.MemLp f 2 (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Icc 0 1)) ∧
        ∫ (x : ℝ) in 0..1, f x = 0 ∧
          ∀ ε > 0,
            ∀ᵐ (α : ℝ) ∂MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.Icc 0 1),
              Filter.limsup (fun N => ↑(Erdos995.partialSum n f α N / (↑N * Real.log (Real.log ↑N) ^ (1 / 2 - ε))))
                  Filter.atTop =
                ⊤

declarations.docstring:
Does there exists a positive constant `C` such that for all `f ∈ L²[0,1]` and all lacunary
sequences `n`, if `‖f - fₖ‖₂ = O(1 / log log log k ^ C)`, then for almost every `x`,
`lim ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, f (n k • x)) / N = ∫ t, f t ∂t`?
references: [erdosproblems.com/996](https://www.erdosproblems.com/996)
[Er49d] Erdös, P. "On the strong law of large numbers." Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 67.1 (1949): 51-56.
[Ma66] Matsuyama, Noboru. "On the strong law of large numbers." Tohoku Mathematical Journal, Second Series 18.3 (1966): 259-269.
declarations.type_pretty:
∃ C,
  0 < C ∧
    ∀ (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℂ 2 AddCircle.haarAddCircle)) (n : ℕ → ℕ),
      IsLacunary n →
        ((fun k =>
              (MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (↑↑f - Erdos996.fourierPartial f k) 2
                  AddCircle.haarAddCircle).toReal) =O[Filter.atTop]
            fun k => 1 / Real.log (Real.log (Real.log ↑k)) ^ C) →
          ∀ᵐ (x : AddCircle 1),
            Filter.Tendsto (fun N => (∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, ↑↑f (n k • x)) / ↑N) Filter.atTop
              (nhds (∫ (t : AddCircle 1), ↑↑f t ∂AddCircle.haarAddCircle))

declarations.docstring: The following theorem is proved in [Ma66].
references: [erdosproblems.com/996](https://www.erdosproblems.com/996)
[Er49d] Erdös, P. "On the strong law of large numbers." Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 67.1 (1949): 51-56.
[Ma66] Matsuyama, Noboru. "On the strong law of large numbers." Tohoku Mathematical Journal, Second Series 18.3 (1966): 259-269.
declarations.type_pretty:
∀ (C : ℝ),
  0.5 < C →
    ∀ (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℂ 2 AddCircle.haarAddCircle)) (n : ℕ → ℕ),
      IsLacunary n →
        ((fun k =>
              (MeasureTheory.eLpNorm (↑↑f - Erdos996.fourierPartial f k) 2
                  AddCircle.haarAddCircle).toReal) =O[Filter.atTop]
            fun k => 1 / Real.log (Real.log ↑k) ^ C) →
          ∀ᵐ (x : AddCircle 1),
            Filter.Tendsto (fun N => (∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, ↑↑f (n k • x)) / ↑N) Filter.atTop
              (nhds (∫ (t : AddCircle 1), ↑↑f t ∂AddCircle.haarAddCircle))

The **Generalized Riemann Hypothesis** asserts that all the non-trivial zeros of the
Dirichlet $L$-function $L(\chi, s)$ of a primitive Dirichlet character $\chi$ have real part
$\frac{1}{2}$.
references: [The Clay Institute](https://www.claymath.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/riemann.pdf)
[Wikipedia: Riemann hypothesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riemann_hypothesis)

D. A. Marcus, *Number Fields*, Springer (GTM 81), 1977, Chapter VII.

∀ (q : ℕ) [inst : NeZero q] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ q),

declarations.docstring:
If $A \subset \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is random, $|A| = \sqrt{p}$, can we almost surely cover
$\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ with $100\sqrt{p}$ translates of $A$? [Gr24]
references: [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.39)
[BJR11] Bollobás, Béla, Svante Janson, and Oliver Riordan. "On covering by translates of a set." Random Structures & Algorithms 38.1‐2 (2011): 33-67.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun p =>
      have k := (↑p).sqrt;
      have c := 100 * k;
      ↑(Green39.proportionCoverable (↑p) k c))
    Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

declarations.docstring: "I do not know how to answer this even with 100 replaced by 1.01." [Gr24]"
references: [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.39)
[BJR11] Bollobás, Béla, Svante Janson, and Oliver Riordan. "On covering by translates of a set." Random Structures & Algorithms 38.1‐2 (2011): 33-67.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun p =>
      have k := (↑p).sqrt;
      have c := ⌊1.01 * ↑k⌋₊;
      ↑(Green39.proportionCoverable (↑p) k c))
    Filter.atTop (nhds 1)

declarations.docstring:
Similar questions are interesting with $\sqrt{p}$ replaced by $p^\theta$ for any $\theta \le 1/2$. [Gr24]

NOTE: using $C p^\theta$ translates as stated makes the conjecture trivially false by the pigeonhole
principle. Indeed for a set of size $p^\theta$, we cover at most $C p^{2\theta}$ elements, which is
strictly less than $p$ for $\theta < 1/2$. We interpret the question as asking whether
$O(p^{1-\theta})$ translates suffice. This generalizes the main conjecture where
$\sqrt{p} = p^{1-1/2}$.
references: [Gr24] [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.39)
[BJR11] Bollobás, Béla, Svante Janson, and Oliver Riordan. "On covering by translates of a set." Random Structures & Algorithms 38.1‐2 (2011): 33-67.
declarations.type_pretty:
True ↔
  ∀ (θ : ℝ),
    0 < θ →
      θ ≤ 1 / 2 →
        ∃ C > 1,
          Filter.Tendsto
            (fun p =>
              have k := ⌊↑↑p ^ θ⌋₊;
              have c := ⌊C * ↑↑p ^ (1 - θ)⌋₊;
              ↑(Green39.proportionCoverable (↑p) k c))
            Filter.atTop (nhds 1)
